docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Welcome to the Pandora FMS plugin documentation — guides, integrations, and Discovery modules for the Pandora FMS monitoring platform.

For information about the Pandora FMS product, visit the Pandora FMS product documentation.

This documentation provides guides for plugins and integrations available through the Pandora FMS Marketplace. You can browse and download these resources from the official Pandora FMS Marketplace.

docs.title: Where to find things
docs.text:
• Plugins — standalone/manual plugins, run by hand or as a regular server plugin.
  • Integrations — connectors to external tools (Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat...), mainly used for alerting.
  • Discovery — plugins driven by the Discovery task wizard, which auto-generates agents and modules from their output.
  • Extras — meta content about the site itself, including how to contribute new documentation.

Use the sidebar to browse each section.

docs.title: Amazon CloudWatch Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Amazon CloudWatch Discovery addon turns the results of Amazon CloudWatch queries into Pandora FMS agents and modules. You define the queries yourself, using CloudWatch Metrics Insights or any other MetricDataQueries expression, and you define how each result becomes a module. A single query can produce hundreds of modules, for example one CPU module for each EC2 instance that the query returns.

A Discovery task:

  1. Reads the queries you wrote, each one with its own region and time window.
  2. Runs them against the CloudWatch API with an AWS access key.
  3. Creates one module per result series and places it in the default agent, or in the agent you name in the module configuration.

The agents and modules that appear depend entirely on your configuration; the addon does not create any resource by itself.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.aws.cloudwatch, package version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the AWS CloudWatch API Required The addon calls the CloudWatch API in every region used by your queries AWS access key with the permission listed in AWS permissions Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the AWS API, directly or through an HTTPS proxy.
  2. An AWS access key (access key ID and secret access key) registered in the Pandora FMS credential store as an AWS credential. The credential must provide the keys access_key_id and secret_access_key.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships as a ready-to-run package, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: AWS permissions
docs.text:
The addon performs read-only requests and only uses the CloudWatch GetMetricData operation. The access key needs the following IAM action:

AWS action Used for cloudwatch:GetMetricData Running every query you define 
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "cloudwatch:GetMetricData"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

Attach the policy to a dedicated IAM user created for Pandora FMS and generate an access key for it.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.aws.cloudwatch

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, the package appears in the list of Discovery packages as Amazon Cloudwatch, in the cloud section:

Amazon Cloudwatch is then available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery cloud applications and choose Amazon Cloudwatch. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Cloudwatch base — credentials, default agent and Tentacle destination:

    • AWS Credentials: the AWS credential registered in the credential store.
    • Default agent name: the agent that receives every module whose configuration does not name another agent.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. Cloudwatch detailed — execution, proxy, queries and modules:

    • Max threads: number of parallel workers.
    • Use proxy, Proxy url and Verify proxy SSL: route the AWS requests through an HTTPS proxy.
    • Configure Cloudwatch queries: the queries to run, as described in Query configuration.
    • Configure module data: how each query result becomes a module, as described in Module configuration.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step. The group is applied to the agents the task creates, and the interval is both the execution period and the interval of those agents.

docs.title: Query configuration
docs.text:
The queries field contains a JSON list. Each element is one query block, and the blocks run independently:

[
  {
    "time_frame": "5m",
    "region_name": "us-east-1",
    "MetricDataQueries": [
      {
        "Id": "q1",
        "Expression": "SELECT AVG(CPUUtilization) FROM SCHEMA(\"AWS/EC2\", InstanceId) GROUP BY InstanceId",
        "Label": "avg_cpu",
        "Period": 300
      }
    ]
  }
]
Key Required Default Description time_frame No 15m Window of data requested, counted back from the moment the query runs. A whole number followed by m (minutes) or h (hours), for example 5m, 30m or 1h region_name No us-east-1 AWS region the block queries MetricDataQueries No empty list List of CloudWatch MetricDataQueries items, with the structure of the AWS GetMetricData API (Id, Expression, Label, Period, ReturnData, ...)

The Id of each item links the result to its module configuration. Inner double quotes in a SCHEMA("...") expression may be written either as \" or unescaped, as in the examples of the AWS documentation; the addon escapes them for you. Escape any other double quote inside an expression with \".

docs.title: Module configuration
docs.text:
The module field contains one section per Id defined in the queries, in INI format. Lines that start with # are comments.

[q1]
name = __label__
type = generic_data
description = Average CPU utilization
unit = percent
value = average
min_warning = 75
min_critical = 85
agent = AWS EC2
Key Required Default Description Section name Yes — Must equal the Id of the query item it configures name No module <Id> Module name. __label__ takes the name from the label that CloudWatch returns for each series type Yes — Pandora FMS module type: generic_data (numeric), generic_data_string (string) or async_string value No last How the data points of the series become the module value: last or average (arithmetic mean of the data points returned) description, unit, min_warning, max_warning, min_critical, max_critical No — Module description, unit and warning and critical thresholds agent No Default agent name Agent that receives the module. It is created when it does not exist

Any other key except name, type, value and agent is forwarded to the module definition. Any value other than average is processed as last: max, min and sum are not calculated. Do not use the % character in any value, for example unit = %; use a word such as percent.

A query item without a section in the module configuration, or whose section has no type, produces no module.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: agents that received data.
    • Total modules: modules sent.

    A task that does not complete successfully, or that completes with problems in some query, records the messages in its execution information. See Troubleshoot.

  2. The agents. The default agent, plus every agent named by an agent key.

  3. The modules. One module for each series returned by each query.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Name Notes Default agent Default agent name Receives every module without an agent key Named agent The agent value of the module configuration Created when a module names it. Several modules can name the same agent

Agents are identified by their name: tasks that use the same agent name report to the same agent and keep its history. All agents belong to the task's group and use the task's interval.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
Result of a query item Modules A query that returns one series One module A query that returns several series, for example with GROUP BY One module per series

For each series:

  • The module name is the series label when name = __label__, the fixed name otherwise, or module <Id> when name is not set. With a fixed name, all the series of the query produce modules with the same name in the same agent, so use __label__ for queries that return several series.
  • The module value is the last value or the average of the data points returned, as set by value.
  • A series with no data points in the time window produces no module for that run.

docs.title: How the data is requested
docs.text:
• Each execution requests the data of time_frame back from the execution time.
  • Each query block requests at most 100 data points and the addon does not request further pages, so a query that returns many series with many data points can be truncated. Narrow the query or the time window.
  • The query blocks run in parallel, up to Max threads at the same time.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. It takes three parameters, all required:

./pandora_aws_cloudwatch \
  --creds <BASE64_CREDENTIALS> \
  --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> \
  --query_conf <PATH_TO_QUERY_FILE>
  • --creds: Base64 of the JSON {"access_key_id": "<ACCESS_KEY_ID>", "secret_access_key": "<SECRET_ACCESS_KEY>"}. A value passed as a command-line argument can be exposed in the shell history and in the process list of the operating system. Run it only on a host you control.
  • --conf: the configuration file, which also contains the module configuration after the [CONF] section.
  • --query_conf: a file with the query configuration.

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 3, "Total modules": 25}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the execution information of the task, which shows the messages below.

Message Meaning and action Error: empty creds No credential was selected Error with creds: ... The credential is not valid JSON with the keys access_key_id and secret_access_key Error parsing configuration: ... The queries are not valid JSON, or the module configuration contains an invalid line, for example a value with the % character ClientError AWS: ..., BotoCoreError AWS: ... or Error AWS: ..., followed by Error: query_charge failed for region '<region>' or query '<queries>': ... A query failed. Check the region, the expression syntax, the credential and the cloudwatch:GetMetricData permission. The same message appears when time_frame is not a whole number followed by m or h Empty values or invalid configuration for <Id>, aborting The query returned no data points in the time window. Increase time_frame or check the metric Module '<Id>' is missing 'type' in module_configuration There is no module section for that Id, or the section has no type Total modules lower than expected A query may be truncated by the limit of 100 data points, or its series returned no data Several series overwrite each other The module name is fixed. Use name = __label__ Errors reaching AWS through a proxy Check Proxy url; only HTTPS requests are routed through the proxy

docs.title: Cloudwatch base
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes AWS Credentials _credentials_ credential select (AWS) — Mandatory. Credential registered in the credential store Default agent name _agentName_ string — Optional in the task definition. If left empty, the agent is created with an empty alias Tentacle IP _tentacleIP_ string 127.0.0.1 Server that receives the agent data Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number 41121 Tentacle port Tentacle extra options _tentacleExtraOpt_ string — Optional. This version of the addon does not apply it

docs.title: Cloudwatch detailed
docs.text:
Field Macro Type Default Notes Max threads _threads_ number 1 Optional. Use 1 or more Use proxy _useProxy_ checkbox off Route AWS requests through a proxy Proxy url _proxyUrl_ string — Optional. Shown when Use proxy is on. Applied to HTTPS requests Verify proxy SSL _sslCheck_ checkbox off Shown when Use proxy is on. When off, the addon does not validate TLS certificates in its AWS connections Configure Cloudwatch queries _configQueries_ text area empty Mandatory. See Query configuration Configure module data _configModules_ text area commented template Mandatory. See Module configuration. The commented template mentions max and min for value; they are not calculated

Because Verify proxy SSL is only shown with Use proxy, a task that does not use a proxy always runs with TLS certificate validation disabled. Run such tasks only from a network you trust.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. The [CONF] section holds the options; each additional section is a module configuration section.

Key Default Description agents_group 0 Numeric ID of the group of the generated agents. A value that is not a number is read as 0 agent_name AWS Cloudwatch Default agent name interval 300 Agent interval, in seconds threads 1 Parallel workers. Use 1 or more transfer_mode tentacle Transfer mode of the data files tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle server port use_proxy 0 1 routes AWS requests through the proxy proxy_url empty Proxy URL, applied to HTTPS requests ssl_check 0 1 validates TLS certificates; 0 does not

Example:

[CONF]
agents_group  = 1
agent_name    = AWS General
interval      = 300
threads       = 3
transfer_mode = tentacle
tentacle_ip   = <TENTACLE_SERVER_IP>
tentacle_port = 41121
use_proxy     = 0
ssl_check     = 1

[q1]
name = __label__
type = generic_data
description = Average CPU utilization
unit = percent
value = average
agent = AWS EC2

docs.title: Amazon EC2 Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Amazon EC2 Discovery addon monitors Amazon Web Services EC2 instances and the regions that contain them. It queries the AWS APIs and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: instance state, CPU, disk, IOPS and network performance, volume storage, Elastic IP addresses and, optionally, cost per region.

A Discovery task generates three kinds of agents:

  • A global statistics agent (optional) with the number of instances and the total cost.
  • One agent per monitored region, with summary modules aggregated over the instances of that region.
  • One agent per monitored instance, with its state and performance modules. The instance agent is a child of its region agent.

A region can be selected as a whole, in which case every instance it contains is monitored, including instances created later. Individual instances can also be selected without selecting their region.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.aws.ec2, version 1.5 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the AWS APIs Required The addon calls the AWS EC2, CloudWatch and Cost Explorer APIs AWS access key with the permissions listed in AWS permissions Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the AWS APIs, directly or through an HTTPS proxy.
  2. An AWS access key (access key ID and secret access key) with the permissions described below, registered in the Pandora FMS credential store as an AWS credential.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executables, bin/pandora_aws_ec2 and bin/aws_ec2, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: AWS permissions
docs.text:
The addon performs read-only requests. Which ones it issues depends on the options you enable:

AWS action Used for ec2:DescribeInstances Listing regions and instances (always) cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics CPU, disk, IOPS and network metrics (when Scan and general monitoring is enabled) ec2:DescribeVolumes Storage modules (when Storage is enabled) ec2:DescribeAddresses Elastic IP modules (when Elastic IP Adresses is enabled) ce:GetCostAndUsage Cost modules (when Total cost is enabled)

An IAM policy that grants all of them:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "ec2:DescribeInstances",
        "ec2:DescribeVolumes",
        "ec2:DescribeAddresses",
        "cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics",
        "ce:GetCostAndUsage"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

Attach the policy to a dedicated IAM user created for Pandora FMS and generate an access key for it. Omit the actions of the options you will not enable.

The credential stored in Pandora FMS must provide the keys access_key_id and secret_access_key; the plugin fails with Error while parsing credentials when either is missing.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.aws.ec2

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Amazon EC2 is available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery cloud applications and choose Amazon EC2. The console presents the fields in four steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. EC2 Basic — credentials, execution and agent options:

    • AWS Credentials: the AWS credential registered in the credential store.
    • Max threads: number of groups the monitored regions and instances are divided into.
    • Use proxy, Proxy url and Verify proxy SSL: route the AWS requests through an HTTPS proxy.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where and how the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.
    • Add global stats agent and Stats agent name: create the global agent and optionally name it.
    • Agent autodisable mode: disables the agent when all its modules become unknown until data returns.

  2. EC2 Instances — a tree of regions and instances read from your AWS account with the selected credential. Check a region to monitor it and all of its instances, or check individual instances. Instances are grouped by instance type under each region. Select at least one region or instance; the task fails with list index out of range when the selection is empty.

  3. Instances monitoring — the metrics collected:

    • Scan and general monitoring: enables the CPU, IOPs, disk and network options below.
    • Cpu performance summary, IOPs performance summary, Disk performance summary, Network performance summary: shown only when Scan and general monitoring is enabled.
    • Storage and Elastic IP Adresses: independent of Scan and general monitoring.

  4. EC2 Costs — cost monitoring:

    • Total cost: enables cost modules.
    • Cost by region: regions to query. Shown when Total cost is enabled.
    • Cost interval: period of time the cost covers. Shown when Total cost is enabled.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated, including the global agent when enabled.
    • Zones agents: regions monitored.
    • Instances agents: instances monitored.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One per selected region, one per instance and, when enabled, the global agent. Instance agents are children of their region agent.

  3. The modules. Every instance agent has State and Instance State (bool). Performance modules appear only on running instances; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Parent Notes Global agent The Stats agent name, or Aws when empty None Created only when Add global stats agent is enabled Region agent The region name, for example eu-west-1 The global agent only when a Stats agent name was given One per selected region Instance agent The instance ID Its region agent One per instance, created once even when both the instance and its region are selected. The agent version is the instance type and the address is the public IP address, when it has one

Agent identity does not depend on the task: region agents are identified by the access key and region, and instance agents by the access key and instance ID. Moving a region or instance between tasks that use the same access key keeps reporting to the same agent and preserves its history.

All agents report the operating system name Aws, and ec2 as the operating system version for regions and instances.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Global agent

Module Type Description AWS EC2 Instances count generic_data Instances found in the selected regions and instances AWS EC2 Total cost generic_data Cost of the selected cost regions over the cost interval. Created only when Total cost is enabled

Region agent

Module Condition Description summary.aws.ec2.instances Region selected as a whole Instances in the region cost Total cost enabled, region in Cost by region, and at least one instance in the region Cost of the region over the cost interval summary.aws.ec2.CPUUtilization Scan and general monitoring and Cpu performance summary CPU of the running instances divided by the number of instances in the region summary.aws.ec2.DiskReadBytes, summary.aws.ec2.diskWriteBytes Scan and general monitoring and Disk performance summary Sum over the running instances, in Bytes summary.aws.ec2.DiskReadOps, summary.aws.ec2.DiskWriteOps Scan and general monitoring and IOPs performance summary Sum over the running instances summary.aws.ec2.NetworkPacketsIn, summary.aws.ec2.NetworkPacketsOut Scan and general monitoring and Network performance summary Sum over the running instances, in packets summary.aws.ec2.addresses.count Elastic IP Adresses Elastic IP addresses in the region summary.aws.ec2.storage.count, summary.aws.ec2.storage.size Storage Volumes in the region and their total size in GB

Instance agent

Module Type Condition Description State generic_data_string Always Instance state as reported by AWS Instance State (bool) generic_proc Always 1 when the state is running, 0 otherwise CPUUtilization generic_data Running, Cpu performance summary CPU usage DiskReadBytes, DiskWriteBytes generic_data Running, Disk performance summary Disk bytes read and written, in Bytes DiskReadOps, DiskWriteOps generic_data Running, IOPs performance summary Disk read and write operations NetworkPacketsIn, NetworkPacketsOut generic_data Running, Network performance summary Network packets received and sent, in packets

docs.title: How the values are obtained
docs.text:
• Performance values are the latest five-minute average that AWS CloudWatch returns for the last 150 minutes. When CloudWatch returns no data point in that window, the module value is 0.
  • Performance modules are created only for instances in the running state.
  • The cost modules use the Cost interval as their period and are refreshed at that interval, not at the task interval.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_aws_ec2 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 23, "Zones agents": 5, "Instances agents": 17}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1.

In local transfer mode the data files are moved to data_dir. In tentacle mode the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

A configuration file contains the AWS access key encoded in creds_b64. Protect the file with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • Error while parsing credentials: the credential does not provide access_key_id and secret_access_key, or creds_b64 is not valid base64-encoded JSON.
  • The instance tree is empty or lacks a region: regions whose DescribeInstances request fails are omitted from the tree without an error. Check the ec2:DescribeInstances permission of the key and the status of the region in AWS.
  • Fewer agents than expected: only the regions and instances you checked are monitored. A selected region with no instances still produces its region agent.
  • Error getting cost for <region>: the cost query for that region failed. Check that the access key has ce:GetCostAndUsage; the message includes the error returned by AWS.
  • Performance modules are 0: CloudWatch returned no data point in the last 150 minutes for that instance and metric.
  • No performance modules on an instance: the instance is not running, or Scan and general monitoring is disabled.
  • Error getting volumes for <region> or Error getting addresses for <region>: the key lacks ec2:DescribeVolumes or ec2:DescribeAddresses.
  • Errors reaching AWS through a proxy: check Proxy url; only HTTPS requests are routed through it.

docs.title: Amazon RDS Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Amazon RDS Discovery addon monitors Amazon Web Services RDS database instances and the regions that contain them. It queries the AWS APIs and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: instance state, database connections, CPU, disk, IOPS and network performance.

A Discovery task generates three kinds of agents:

  • A global statistics agent (optional) with the number of instances found.
  • One agent per monitored region, with summary modules aggregated over the instances of that region.
  • One agent per monitored instance, with its state and performance modules. The instance agent is a child of its region agent.

A region can be selected as a whole, in which case every instance it contains is monitored, including instances created later. Individual instances can also be selected without selecting their region.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.aws.rds, version 1.2 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the AWS APIs Required The addon calls the AWS RDS and CloudWatch APIs AWS access key with the permissions listed in AWS permissions Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the AWS APIs, directly or through an HTTPS proxy.
  2. An AWS access key (access key ID and secret access key) with the permissions described below, registered in the Pandora FMS credential store as an AWS credential.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executables, bin/pandora_aws_rds and bin/aws_rds, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: AWS permissions
docs.text:
The addon performs read-only requests:

AWS action Used for rds:DescribeDBInstances Listing the instances of every region (always) cloudwatch:GetMetricData Connection, CPU, disk, IOPS and network metrics (when Scan and general monitoring is enabled)

An IAM policy that grants both:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "rds:DescribeDBInstances",
        "cloudwatch:GetMetricData"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

Attach the policy to a dedicated IAM user created for Pandora FMS and generate an access key for it. Omit cloudwatch:GetMetricData if you will not enable Scan and general monitoring.

The credential stored in Pandora FMS must provide the keys access_key_id and secret_access_key; the addon reports Error while parsing credentials when either is missing.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.aws.rds

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Amazon RDS is available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery cloud applications and choose Amazon RDS. The console presents the fields in three steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. RDS Basic — credentials, execution and agent options:

    • AWS Credentials: the AWS credential registered in the credential store.
    • Max threads: number of groups the monitored regions and instances are divided into.
    • Use proxy, Proxy url and Verify proxy SSL: route the AWS requests through an HTTPS proxy.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where and how the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.
    • Add global stats agent and Stats agent name: create the global agent and optionally name it.
    • Agent autodisable mode: disables the agent when all its modules become unknown until data returns.

  2. RDS Instances — a tree of regions and instances read from your AWS account with the selected credential. Check a region to monitor it and all of its instances, or check individual instances. Instances are listed under their region, under a node for their database engine. Select at least one region or instance.

  3. Instances monitoring — the metrics collected:

    • Scan and general monitoring: enables database connections and the CPU, IOPs, disk and network options below.
    • Cpu performance summary, IOPs performance summary, Disk performance summary, Network performance summary: shown only when Scan and general monitoring is enabled.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated, including the global agent when enabled.
    • Zones agents: regions monitored.
    • Instances agents: instances monitored.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One per selected region, one per instance and, when enabled, the global agent. Instance agents are children of their region agent.

  3. The modules. Every instance agent has State and Instance State (bool). Performance modules appear only on instances in the available state; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Parent Notes Global agent The Stats agent name, or Aws.rds when empty None Created only when Add global stats agent is enabled Region agent The region name, for example eu-west-1 The global agent only when a Stats agent name was given One per selected region Instance agent The instance identifier Its region agent One per instance, created once even when both the instance and its region are selected. The agent version is the instance class and the address is the instance endpoint address. The region agent is created only when the region itself is selected

Agent identity does not depend on the task: region agents are identified by the access key and region, and instance agents by the access key and instance identifier. Moving a region or instance between tasks that use the same access key keeps reporting to the same agent and preserves its history.

Region and instance agents report the operating system name Aws and the operating system version rds. The global agent reports the operating system name Aws.

docs.text:

docs.title: How the values are obtained
docs.text:
• Each performance value is the average that AWS CloudWatch returns, in the AWS/RDS namespace, over a 10-minute period for the last 10 minutes. When CloudWatch returns no data point in that window, the module value is 0. This includes metrics that AWS does not publish for a given instance.
  • Performance modules are created only for instances whose status is available.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_aws_rds --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 5, "Zones agents": 2, "Instances agents": 2}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1.

In local transfer mode the data files are moved to data_dir. In tentacle mode the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

A configuration file contains the AWS access key encoded in creds_b64. Protect the file with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • Error while parsing credentials: the credential does not provide access_key_id and secret_access_key, or creds_b64 is not valid base64-encoded JSON.
  • The instance tree is empty or lacks a region: regions whose DescribeDBInstances request fails are omitted from the tree without an error. Check the rds:DescribeDBInstances permission of the key and the status of the region in AWS.
  • A region agent appears but has no instance agents: the region has no instances, or the instance request for that region failed.
  • Error while running threads: list index out of range: the task has no region or instance selected. Select at least one.
  • Fewer agents than expected: only the regions and instances you checked are monitored.
  • Error getting metric: <metric> : ...: the CloudWatch request failed. Check that the access key has cloudwatch:GetMetricData and that the clock of the Discovery server is correct; the message includes the current date seen by the addon.
  • Performance modules are 0: CloudWatch returned no data point in the last 10 minutes for that instance and metric.
  • No performance modules on an instance: the instance status is not available, or Scan and general monitoring is disabled.
  • Errors reaching AWS through a proxy: check Proxy url; only HTTPS requests are routed through it.

docs.title: Amazon S3 Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Amazon S3 Discovery addon monitors Amazon Web Services S3 buckets. It queries the AWS APIs and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: the number of buckets per region and, for each bucket, its number of objects and its size.

A Discovery task generates two kinds of agents:

  • A global statistics agent (optional) with the number of monitored buckets.
  • One agent per monitored region, with a module for the object count and a module for the size of each monitored bucket.

A region can be selected as a whole, in which case every bucket it contains is monitored, including buckets created later. Individual buckets can also be monitored without selecting their region (see Configuration file).

docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.aws.s3, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the AWS APIs Required The addon calls the AWS S3 API AWS access key with the permissions listed in AWS permissions Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the AWS APIs, directly or through an HTTPS proxy.
  2. An AWS access key (access key ID and secret access key) with the permissions described below, registered in the Pandora FMS credential store as an AWS credential.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executables, bin/pandora_aws_s3 and bin/aws_s3, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: AWS permissions
docs.text:
The addon performs read-only requests:

AWS action Used for s3:ListAllMyBuckets Listing the buckets of the account s3:GetBucketLocation Finding the region of each bucket s3:ListBucket Listing the objects of a bucket to count them and add up their size

An IAM policy that grants all of them:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "s3:ListAllMyBuckets",
        "s3:GetBucketLocation",
        "s3:ListBucket"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

Attach the policy to a dedicated IAM user created for Pandora FMS and generate an access key for it.

The credential stored in Pandora FMS must provide the keys access_key_id and secret_access_key; the addon fails with Error while parsing credentials when either is missing.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.aws.s3

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Amazon S3 is available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery cloud applications and choose Amazon S3. The console presents the fields in three steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. S3 Basic — credentials, execution and agent options:

    • AWS Credentials: the AWS credential registered in the credential store.
    • Max threads: number of groups the monitored regions are divided into.
    • Use proxy, Proxy url and Verify proxy SSL: route the AWS requests through an HTTPS proxy.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where and how the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.
    • Add global stats agent and Stats agent name: create the global agent and optionally name it.

  2. S3 Buckets — a tree of S3 regions read from your AWS account with the selected credential. Check a region to monitor all the buckets it contains.

  3. Bucket monitoring — the metrics collected:

    • S3 Monitoring: enables the bucket modules below.
    • Monitor bucket size and Monitor bucket total items: shown only when S3 Monitoring is enabled.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total buckets: buckets monitored.
    • Total regions: regions with monitored buckets or selected as a whole.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One per selected region and, when enabled, the global agent.

  3. The modules. Each region agent has, for every monitored bucket, bucket.items <bucket> and bucket.size <bucket>; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Parent Notes Global agent The Stats agent name, or Aws when empty None Created only when Add global stats agent is enabled Region agent The region name, for example eu-west-1 The global agent only when a Stats agent name was given One per selected region and per region that contains an individually selected bucket

Buckets do not get their own agent: they are reported as modules of their region agent.

Region agent identity does not depend on the task: it is defined by the access key and the region. Moving a region between tasks that use the same access key keeps reporting to the same agent and preserves its history.

All agents report the operating system name Aws. Region agents report ec2 as the operating system version.

A region agent is created only if it has at least one module. A region selected as a whole always has summary.Aws.ec2.buckets.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_aws_s3 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode:

{"summary": {"Total buckets": 32, "Total regions": 7}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1.

In local transfer mode the data files are moved to data_dir. In tentacle mode the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

A configuration file contains the AWS access key encoded in creds_b64. Protect the file with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • Error while parsing credentials: the credential does not provide access_key_id and secret_access_key, or creds_b64 is not valid base64-encoded JSON.
  • Error while reading configuration file: the file passed to --conf cannot be read.
  • Error while parsing configuration zones or buckets: aws_regions or aws_buckets is not a valid JSON array.
  • Fewer agents than expected: only the regions and buckets you selected are monitored. A selected region with no buckets still produces its region agent.
  • No bucket modules: S3 Monitoring is disabled, or both Monitor bucket size and Monitor bucket total items are.
  • Access errors while listing buckets or objects: check that the access key has the three permissions in AWS permissions. The message includes the error returned by AWS.
  • Errors reaching AWS through a proxy: check Proxy url; only HTTPS requests are routed through it.
  • Tentacle errors: the message is recorded in info prefixed with Tentacle error:. Check Tentacle IP and Tentacle port.
