docs.title: JMX Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The JMX Discovery addon monitors Java applications through Java Management Extensions (JMX). It connects to the JMX endpoint of each target you configure, reads the attributes of the MBeans you choose and turns them into Pandora FMS agents and modules.

A Discovery task generates one agent per JMX target. Each agent contains one module per MBean attribute collected. You choose what is collected in two ways, which can be combined:

  • MBeans selected in the console. The console connects to a reference JMX endpoint and shows the MBeans it exposes. Every attribute of each selected MBean is collected, on every target of the task.
  • Custom metrics. An explicit list of MBean/attribute entries, optionally with thresholds.

The same selection is applied to all the targets of a task, so group in one task only targets that expose the same MBeans.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.jmx, version 1.2 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity A Java runtime available on the Pandora FMS server that runs the task Required The addon starts a Java virtual machine to open the JMX connections Network access from the Discovery server to each JMX endpoint Required The addon opens one JMX connection per target Java runtime versions, Java vendors and application servers Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A Java runtime installed on the Pandora FMS server that runs the Discovery task, available to the user that runs it.
  2. Remote JMX enabled on every monitored Java application, reachable from the Discovery server. See Enable remote JMX.
  3. The JMX service URL of every target, for example service:jmx:rmi:///jndi/rmi://<TARGET_HOST>:<JMX_PORT>/jmxrmi.
  4. JMX credentials, only when the target requires authentication.

docs.title: Enable remote JMX
docs.text:
The monitored application does not need extra software, but it must be started with the JVM options that enable remote JMX. The following set enables it on the local host without authentication or TLS and is meant only for a test environment:

-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=false
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.ssl=false
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.port=<JMX_PORT>
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.rmi.port=<JMX_PORT>
-Djava.rmi.server.hostname=localhost

To require authentication, set -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=true and add the password and access files:

-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.password.file=<PATH_TO_PASSWORD_FILE>
-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.access.file=<PATH_TO_ACCESS_FILE>

To connect from another host, java.rmi.server.hostname must be an address the Discovery server can reach. The exact options for your application and the protection of the password file are defined by the Java application, not by this addon.

docs.title: Credential handling
docs.text:
• The user and password entered in the task are stored with the task definition and sent to the JMX server as the JMX credentials.
  • While the console loads the list of MBeans, it passes the user and password as arguments to the helper executable, so they can be visible in the process list of the Pandora FMS server during that operation.
  • A configuration file used in manual execution contains the password in clear text. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.jmx

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, JMX is available in the Applications section when creating Discovery tasks.

The addon ships its own executables, bin/pandora_jmx and bin/get_jmx_tree.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery applications and choose JMX. The console presents the fields in three steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. JMX Basic — targets and credentials:

    • Instances target strings: the targets to monitor, one or several per line, separated by commas. Each target is a JMX service URL, optionally followed by | and the agent name to use. Lines that start with # are ignored.
    • JMX Url: the reference endpoint used only to list the available MBeans in the next step. It does not define a target.
    • Auth basic, User and Password: credentials for the JMX connections. User and password are shown when Auth basic is enabled.

  2. JMX Mbeans — a tree of the MBeans exposed by the JMX Url endpoint, read with the credentials of the previous step. Select the MBeans to collect. Every attribute of each selected MBean is collected on all the targets.

  3. JMX detailed — execution, naming and filtering options:

    • Max threads: number of targets processed in parallel.
    • Use prefix for modules and Use prefix for agents: prefixes added to the generated module names and agent names.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.
    • Regexp to filter modules and Regexp to discard modules: keep or discard metrics by regular expression.
    • Custom Metrics: explicit MBean/attribute entries with optional thresholds.
    • Rename default modules and Modules names: assign your own module names.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Custom metrics
docs.text:
Write one metric per line using the format <MBean>/<attribute>, optionally followed by thresholds separated by |. Each threshold is a keyword and a value separated by a space. Lines that start with # and empty lines are ignored.

java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount
java.lang:type=Threading/TotalStartedThreadCount|min_warning 30|min_critical 45
java.lang:type=Memory/HeapMemoryUsage/used
  • The thresholds supported by the addon are min_warning, max_warning, min_critical and max_critical.
  • To read one field of a composite attribute, append its name after the attribute, as in java.lang:type=Memory/HeapMemoryUsage/used.
  • If you reference a composite attribute without a field, a module is created for each of its fields; thresholds are not applied to those modules.

docs.title: Rename modules
docs.text:
Module names default to <MBean>/<attribute>, for example java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount. To replace a name, enter one line in Modules names with the original name, a | and the new name:

java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount | Threads.count

The original name must match the default name exactly, without the module prefix. When Use prefix for modules is enabled, the prefix is added after the renaming.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports Total agents, the number of agents generated. Errors and warnings are recorded in the task's execution information.

  2. The agents. One per target, in the group of the task. The agent alias is the agent name given after | in the target, or the JMX service URL when none is given, with the agent prefix when one is configured.

  3. The modules. One per collected attribute. Check that the attributes you selected or listed as custom metrics appear and have values.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Item Value Agents One per target in Instances target strings Alias The text after | in the target, or the target itself when there is none; preceded by the agent prefix when configured Agent name An identifier derived from the alias, including the prefix. The same alias reports to the same agent across runs and tasks Description Created by JMX plugin Group and interval The group and interval of the Discovery task

Changing the agent name or the agent prefix of a target creates a different agent, so keep them stable to preserve the history.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
Each collected attribute produces one module. Its type depends on the value read:

Value read Module type Value Integer, long, float or double number generic_data The number Boolean generic_proc 1 for true and 0 for false Any other value generic_data_string The value as text

A module whose text value is True or False is not created. Attributes that cannot be read, because they do not exist on a target or are unavailable, produce a warning in the execution information and no module.

The attributes of the selected MBeans are filtered by the regular expressions of the task; the custom metrics are also filtered by them. Thresholds in custom metrics are set on the generated module.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task with three files:

./pandora_jmx --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --target_instances <PATH_TO_TARGETS> [--target_metrics <PATH_TO_METRICS>]
  • --conf: configuration file described in Configuration file. Mandatory.
  • --target_instances: the targets, in the same format as Instances target strings. Mandatory.
  • --target_metrics: the custom metrics, in the same format as Custom Metrics. Optional.

It prints a JSON document with the summary (Total agents) and, when there are messages, an info field, and sends one data file per agent with Tentacle. The exit code is 1 when the configuration or targets file cannot be read.

docs.title: Execution tuning
docs.text: Max threads (threads) is the number of worker processes. Each worker takes targets from a shared queue, so more workers than targets add no benefit. Each worker starts its own Java virtual machine, which consumes memory on the Pandora FMS server.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the execution information of the task (the info field in manual execution).

  • Failed to connect: <error>: the connection to a target failed. Check the JMX service URL, the network path, the JMX port and the credentials, and that the application was started with remote JMX enabled.
  • Failed processing <url>: <error>: an error occurred while collecting a target.
  • [WARNING] Failed to read attributes from <MBean>: <error>: a selected MBean could not be read on a target, for example because it does not exist there.
  • [WARNING] Could not read '<attribute>' from MBean '<MBean>': the attribute does not exist, is transient or cannot be read. The module is not created.
  • Database targets not defined: Instances target strings is empty or contains only comments. The task generates no agents.
  • Error while parsing configuration zones or instances: <error>: the jmx_mbeans value is not a valid JSON list (manual execution).
  • Failed to read custom attributes: <error> and Failed to parsing module names: <error>: the custom metrics or the module names could not be read.
  • No MBeans appear in the second step: check the JMX Url, the credentials and the network path from the Pandora FMS server to that endpoint.
  • Fewer modules than expected: review the regular expressions; a metric that does not match Allow regexp, or that matches Deny regexp, is not created.

docs.title: JMX Basic
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Instances target strings _targetstrings_ text area — One or several targets per line, separated by commas. Each target is a JMX service URL, optionally followed by \|<agent name>. Lines that start with # are ignored JMX Url _jmxUrl_ string — Reference endpoint used to list the MBeans in the next step Auth basic _authBasic_ checkbox off Shows User and Password User _user_ string — Optional. Shown when Auth basic is on Password _password_ password — Optional. Shown when Auth basic is on

Added to each module name Use prefix for agents _usePrefixAgents_ checkbox off Shows Prefix for agents created Prefix for agents created _prefixAgents_ string empty Optional. Accepted by the task, but this version does not pass it to the Tentacle client Regexp to filter modules _regexpFilter_ checkbox off Shows Allow regexp Allow regexp _allowRegexp_ string empty Optional. The regular expressions are searched anywhere in the text (they are not anchored). They are applied to the <MBean>/<attribute> name of each attribute of the selected MBeans and to each whole line of the custom metrics, thresholds included.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. It has a [CONF] section and an optional [MODULE_NAMES] section. Values are key = value pairs.

Key Default Description jmx_url empty Reference endpoint. Read for compatibility with the task; targets come from --target_instances user empty JMX user password empty JMX password jmx_mbeans [] JSON list of MBean names whose attributes are all collected, for example ["java.lang:type=Threading","java.lang:type=ClassLoading"] module_prefix empty Prefix for module names agent_prefix empty Prefix for agent aliases agents_group_name jmx Group of the generated agents interval 300 Agent interval, in seconds. A value that is not a number is read as 0 threads 4 Worker processes. A value that is not a number is read as 0 transfer_mode tentacle local writes the data files locally; any other value sends them with Tentacle tentacle_client tentacle_client Tentacle client executable tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle server port tentacle_opts empty Accepted, not passed to the Tentacle client in this version data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Accepted for compatibility with the other Discovery addons temporal /tmp Accepted for compatibility with the other Discovery addons allow_regexp empty Only metrics that match are created deny_regexp empty Metrics that match are not created

The [MODULE_NAMES] section holds one original name | new name per line.

Example:

[CONF]
user = <USERNAME>
password = <PASSWORD>
jmx_url = service:jmx:rmi:///jndi/rmi://<TARGET_HOST>:<JMX_PORT>/jmxrmi
module_prefix = app.
agent_prefix = app.
agents_group_name = jmx
interval = 300
threads = 2
transfer_mode = tentacle
tentacle_ip = <TENTACLE_SERVER_IP>
tentacle_port = 41121
allow_regexp =
deny_regexp =
jmx_mbeans = ["java.lang:type=Threading","java.lang:type=ClassLoading"]

[MODULE_NAMES]
java.lang:type=Threading/ThreadCount | Threads.count

docs.title: Kubernetes Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Kubernetes Discovery plugin connects to the Kubernetes API server of a cluster and discovers its workloads and infrastructure: nodes, pods, deployments, namespaces, services, component statuses and the API health endpoints. It generates one Pandora FMS agent per discovered resource and fills it with availability, capacity and performance modules read from the API.

The plugin generates agents for:

  • the cluster itself, through a global Kubernetes agent;
  • every node, when Scan Nodes is enabled;
  • every deployment with condition data, when Scan Deployments is enabled;
  • every pod already scheduled to a node, when Scan Pods is enabled.

The global agent also carries the cluster-wide API status, health endpoints, service count, namespace count and component statuses.

The plugin runs as a Discovery task: the console creates the task, the Discovery server runs the plugin, and the generated agents and modules are created automatically. The task delivers the generated agent data through Tentacle.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.3 (pandorafms.kubernetes) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity A Kubernetes cluster exposing the API server over HTTPS Required The plugin connects to https://<host>:<port> and reads the API resources. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement A Bearer token that can read the queried API resources Required The plugin authenticates with Authorization: Bearer <token> to list nodes, pods, deployments, services, namespaces and component statuses. Health and component endpoints may require elevated permissions. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement The Kubernetes Metrics API (metrics.k8s.io) for CPU and memory usage Required for CPU and memory modules Node and container CPU and memory modules are read from /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1. Without it, node and pod agents are still generated, but those modules are omitted A specific Kubernetes version Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete Kubernetes release Host operating system running the plugin Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and the console to define it.
  2. A Kubernetes API server reachable from the Discovery server, addressed by host and port. The plugin always uses HTTPS; enter the host without a scheme.
  3. A Bearer token for the API server. It is required to read the protected endpoints; grant it read access to the resources the task queries and no more. The Scan API health checks and Scan component statuses options may need elevated API permissions, as noted in the task tips.
  4. A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents. Both come from the Discovery task and are inherited by every generated agent.
  5. Network reachability to the Tentacle destination, because the task transfers the generated agent data through Tentacle.
  6. The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) that the Discovery server executes on the Pandora FMS server.

Direct API connections use HTTPS without certificate verification: the server identity is not authenticated, so self-signed certificates work. Restrict network access accordingly. Proxy mode uses the supplied proxy URL and omits the Bearer header. The token is entered in the task and written to its configuration; restrict access to both. For manual runs, keep the token in a protected configuration file, not in shell commands.

docs.title: Check target access
docs.text:
Before creating the task, verify the Metrics API and the node/pod metrics with an account authorized for the target cluster:

kubectl get --raw /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/
kubectl top node
kubectl top pod --all-namespaces

If the cluster does not expose the Metrics API, node and pod agents are still generated, but their CPU and memory modules are omitted. These diagnostic commands do not grant the plugin token any permissions.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text: Obtain the .disco package from the Kubernetes Marketplace entry and load it in Discovery from Management → Discovery → Extension manager. Once loaded, Kubernetes appears under the Applications category of the Discovery wizard. This page covers package 1.3.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text: Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → Kubernetes. The wizard walks through the generic task definition and two plugin steps: Kubernetes base and Kubernetes detailed. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

docs.title: Step 1 — Task definition
docs.text: The generic step asks for the task name, the agent group and server on which the task runs, and the interval. The group and the interval are passed to the plugin and inherited by every generated agent.

docs.title: Step 2 — Kubernetes base
docs.text:
Connection details and the Tentacle destination:

  • Kubernetes host is the address or hostname of the API server.
  • Kubernetes port is the API server port.
  • Kubernetes token is the Bearer token used to authenticate against the API.
  • Use prefix shows Prefix, the text prepended to generated agent identities. Clear Prefix when disabling this option: a populated prefix is still applied in this version.
  • Filter namespace restricts discovery to a set of namespaces, and Namespace is the list of namespaces to monitor.
  • Use proxy routes the API requests through a proxy; Proxy url is that proxy.
  • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port set the Tentacle destination for the generated data. Leave the defaults unless your environment needs another Tentacle target.

docs.title: Step 3 — Kubernetes detailed
docs.text:
What to scan:

  • Scan Deployments, Scan Nodes and Scan Pods enable or disable each resource category.
  • Scan API health checks generates the API health endpoint modules. Health endpoints may require elevated API permissions.
  • Scan component statuses generates the component count and the component condition modules. Component statuses may require elevated API permissions.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Run the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary shows the overall progress and a summary with the number of node agents, pod agents and deployment agents generated, and the total number of agents.
  2. The agents. Expect the global Kubernetes agent plus one agent per discovered node, deployment and scheduled pod. Node and pod agents are generated even when the Metrics API is unavailable; deployment agents require returned condition data.
  3. The modules. Every generated agent carries the modules of its resource; a reachable cluster with the Metrics API available populates the CPU and memory values. Do not treat the summary counters as proof of successful data ingestion.
  4. The execution information. A successful run reports no errors; any per-request failure is recorded there.

If the task fails before generating anything, the host, the port, the network reachability and the token are the first things to check.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per discovered resource. Agent names are built from the original resource name plus the optional prefix.

Agent Name Parent agent Global [Prefix]Kubernetes — Node [Prefix]<node> The global agent Deployment [Prefix]<deployment> Kubernetes (without the prefix) Pod [Prefix]<namespace>/<pod> The node agent that runs the pod

Node agents refer to the prefixed global agent; deployment agents refer to the unprefixed Kubernetes parent even when a prefix is set. Each pod agent refers to its prefixed node and uses the pod IP as its address. The global agent is described as Kubernetes global agent, node agents as Kubernetes node, deployment agents as Kubernetes deployment and pod agents as Kubernetes pod.

Node and pod agents do not depend on the Metrics API: when it is unavailable, they are still generated without CPU and memory modules. Only pods already scheduled to a node are discovered: a pod without an assigned node is skipped, as are resources the API returns without a name. Pod identities include the namespace, so equal pod names in different namespaces do not collide; deployment identities do not include the namespace, so equal deployment names in different namespaces can collide. Use separate prefixes for different clusters; namespace filtering does not add a namespace to the deployment identity.

Changing Prefix later changes the identity of every generated agent. The Filter namespace option applies only to deployments and pods, because nodes are cluster-scoped. Namespace matching is exact and case-sensitive, and the list is entered as a JSON array, for example ["default","kube-system"]. When Filter namespace is enabled, list at least one namespace: an empty list matches no workload and no deployment or pod agent is generated.

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
Every agent receives the modules of its resource. The values are read from the API during every task run; the exact name, type and unit of each module are listed in Generated modules.

Agent Modules it carries Global API status, API health endpoints, service count, namespace count, component statuses, deployment count Node Pod usage against the node allocatable, node conditions and, when the Metrics API is available, CPU and memory usage Deployment Replica counts, readiness and availability of the deployment Pod Pod phase and conditions, container count and, when the Metrics API is available, per-container CPU and memory usage

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can also be run outside the Discovery wizard with a configuration file. This is useful for testing connectivity or for a one-off run. Write a configuration file with the key=value pairs listed in Configuration file keys, then run the plugin entry point with the file as argument:

pandora_kubernetes --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

For example, this direct-mode configuration enables every resource category and scan option. Replace every placeholder before use; the example has not been executed:

ip=<TARGET_HOST>
port=<API_PORT>
token=<API_TOKEN>
agents_group_name=<AGENT_GROUP>
interval=300
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<TENTACLE_HOST>
tentacle_port=41121
prefix=<CLUSTER_PREFIX>
use_prefix=1
use_namespace=1
filter_namespace=["default","kube-system"]
use_proxy=0
deployments=1
nodes=1
pods=1
health_checks=1
component_checks=1

Execution returns a Discovery JSON summary and generates XML for each agent. An illustrative summary is {"summary":{"Total agents":4,"Nodes agents":1,"Pods agents":1,"Deployments agents":1}}; these counters describe generation, not confirmed delivery.

The operational CLI input is --conf (-h/--help displays help). When the plugin runs as a Discovery task, the server builds that file from the task fields. Manual examples have not been executed against a live target.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check The execution reports a request error Confirm Kubernetes host and Kubernetes port, that the API server is reachable from the Discovery server, and that the host does not include a scheme. Requests fail with 401 or 403 The token is missing, invalid or lacks read access to the queried resources. Health checks and component statuses may need elevated permissions. Check access to the exact paths in the API reference; no validated role definition is provided here. No deployments or pods are generated but nodes are Review Scan Deployments and Scan Pods, and Filter namespace: when it is enabled, names must match exactly and in the same case, and an empty list matches nothing. Expected pods are missing Only pods already scheduled to a node are discovered. A pod in Pending without an assigned node is not generated. Node CPU and memory modules are missing The Kubernetes Metrics API is not available in the cluster. The node agent is still generated. Some global, health or component modules are missing Those endpoints returned 401, 403 or 404, or the corresponding scan option is disabled. The plugin skips an optional endpoint that is not accessible instead of failing the whole run. API status is 0 The /healthz endpoint did not return ok. Check the API server health itself. If /healthz is inaccessible, the module is omitted. A deployment has no agent Check Scan Deployments, namespace filtering and returned deployment conditions. Deployment Available looks healthy despite a failing condition It reflects the first condition's type, not its Boolean status. Check replica counts and cluster conditions directly. API requests time out Requests use a fixed 5-second timeout and it is not configurable. Confirm the latency between the Discovery server and the API server. Tentacle transfer fails Confirm the Discovery server can reach Tentacle IP on Tentacle port. The global agent uses proxy mode but is not authenticated When Use proxy is enabled the plugin sends requests to Proxy url and does not add the Bearer token.

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds this file from its own fields; a manual run supplies it with --conf. It is a plain text file of key=value lines.

Required manual inputs are ip, port and, for protected endpoints, token in direct mode; proxy_url in proxy mode; and transfer_mode=tentacle with tentacle_ip for delivery. Other keys are optional and use the defaults below. Protect the file because it contains the token.

Name Required Default Description ip Direct mode Empty API server host, without a scheme port Direct mode Empty API server port token Protected direct endpoints Empty Bearer token agents_group_name No Empty manually; task group Target agent group interval No 300 Agent interval in seconds; task interval in Discovery transfer_mode For delivery Empty manually; tentacle in task Use tentacle for the documented transfer path tentacle_ip For Tentacle Empty manually; 127.0.0.1 in task Transfer destination tentacle_port No 41121 Transfer port use_prefix No 0 Shows the task prefix field; does not suppress a populated prefix prefix No Empty Prefix applied to agent identities use_namespace No 0 1 enables workload namespace filtering filter_namespace When filtering [] JSON array; exact namespace matches use_proxy No 0 1 uses proxy_url without the Bearer header proxy_url Proxy mode Empty Base URL including scheme deployments No 1 1 collects deployments and generates deployment agents nodes No 1 1 collects nodes and generates node agents pods No 1 1 collects pods and generates pod agents health_checks No 1 1 generates the API health endpoint modules component_checks No 1 1 generates the component status modules data_dir No Empty Accepted but does not select an output directory

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Command Description pandora_kubernetes --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> Runs the plugin with a configuration file

docs.title: Global agent
docs.text:
Module name Type What it reports API status generic_proc 1 when /healthz returns ok, 0 otherwise; created only when /healthz responds One module per health endpoint generic_proc 1 when the response is ok, 0 otherwise; only when Scan API health checks is enabled and the endpoint responds Services generic_data Number of services; omitted if the request is not accessible Namespaces generic_data Number of namespaces; omitted if the request is not accessible Components generic_data Number of component statuses; only when Scan component statuses is enabled and the request is accessible <component>.<condition> generic_data 1 when the component condition status is TRUE, 0 otherwise Deployments generic_data Number of deployments; 0 when Scan Deployments is disabled

Health module names and their exact paths are listed in API requests. A module is created only for an endpoint that responds. Optional endpoint failures do not prevent the global agent from being transferred.

docs.title: Node agents
docs.text:
Module name Type Unit What it reports Pods generic_data — Pods counted during collection on the node Pods (%) generic_data % Collected pod count against the node's allocatable pod capacity; omitted when the capacity is missing CPU (cores) generic_data cores CPU used by the node. Requires the Metrics API CPU (%) generic_data % CPU used against the allocatable CPU. Requires the Metrics API Memory (bytes) generic_data bytes Memory used by the node. Requires the Metrics API Memory (%) generic_data % Memory used against the allocatable memory. Requires the Metrics API NetworkUnavailable, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure generic_proc — 1 when the corresponding condition is False, 0 otherwise Ready generic_proc — 1 when the condition is True, 0 otherwise

Node agents are generated even when the Metrics API is unavailable; the CPU and memory modules are then omitted. Pods counts pods processed from the returned data, not an independently validated count of every pod on the node.

docs.text:
Module name Type Unit What it reports Ready generic_proc — 1 when the ready replicas equal the desired replicas, 0 otherwise Age generic_data _timeticks_ Creation timestamp in centiseconds since 1970, not elapsed age Replicas generic_data — Desired replicas Updated replicas generic_data — Replicas updated to the desired template Ready replicas generic_data — Ready replicas Available replicas generic_data — Available replicas Unavailable replicas generic_data — Replicas still required for the deployment to reach full availability Available generic_data — 1 if the first condition type is Available or Progressing, otherwise 0; ignores the condition status. Warning threshold at 2, critical at 0

Deployment agents are generated only when the deployment returns at least one condition.

docs.text:

Requires the Metrics API Container <name> CPU (%) generic_data % CPU used by the container against the allocatable CPU of its node. A per-container CPU or memory module is created only when the container exposes that metric; the pod agent is still generated when a metric is missing. The percentages use the node's allocatable resources, not container requests or limits.

docs.text: Field Value App short name pandorafms.kubernetes Plugin version 1.3 Type Discovery application (.disco) Section Discovery → Applications

docs.title: KVM Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-19.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The KVM Discovery plugin connects to KVM hypervisors and reads their inventory and state through virsh and ps, either over SSH or locally on the machine that runs the task. It creates a two-level agent hierarchy in Pandora FMS:

  • one agent per KVM host, named KVM <host>;
  • one agent per virtual machine, named <vm> (<host>) and created as a child of its host agent.

Host agents carry the libvirtd status and, when Monitor KVM server performance is enabled, the RAM and CPU usage of the KVM server, including its RAM consumption in bytes. Virtual machine agents carry the VM power state and, for running VMs, the number of assigned vCPUs, the CPU usage per vCPU, the memory usage in percent and the memory consumption in bytes. CPU usage is a gauge: the plugin samples virsh domstats --vcpu twice around a one-second window and translates the vCPU time delta into a per-vCPU percentage. For running VMs, the plugin also resolves the VM IPv4 address with virsh domifaddr and uses it as the agent address when one is available. The plugin only generates Discovery data; the task re-executes on its configured interval to refresh the inventory and the module values.

The plugin runs as a Discovery task: the console creates the task, the Discovery server runs the plugin, and the generated agents and modules are created automatically.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.0 (pandorafms.kvm) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled Required The integration runs as a Discovery task created from the console. libvirt with virsh on every monitored host Required Every metric is read through virsh, and the libvirtd process check decides whether a host is up. SSH access to every remote target Required Remote targets are monitored over SSH on the configured port; only local targets run without it. A Linux distribution, KVM or libvirt version of the monitored hosts Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete distribution or libvirt release. Operating system of the server that runs the task Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and a console to define it.
  • On every monitored KVM host: libvirt installed with the virsh command available, and the libvirtd daemon running. A host without libvirtd is still generated, with KVM Server status = 0 and without performance or VM modules.
  • An SSH account on every remote host allowed to run ps and virsh. Reading libvirt usually requires membership in the libvirt group or root.
  • For SSH key authentication: a private key readable by the user that runs the discovery task, with its public key installed on every monitored host. Optionally, a known_hosts file with the host keys of those hosts to enable host key verification.
  • For Pandora credentials authentication: a custom credential in the Pandora credential manager that stores the SSH username and password.
  • A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents. Both come from the Discovery task and are inherited by every generated agent.
  • A local target runs ps and virsh on the machine that executes the task, so use it only when the task runs on the KVM host itself.
  • Network reachability from the Discovery server to every remote host on the SSH port. With Transfer mode set to tentacle, the configured Tentacle destination must also be reachable.
  • The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) that the Discovery server executes on the Pandora FMS server.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
From the Marketplace. Open Marketplace → Search in the console, find the KVM Discovery entry and click Install. Installation requires an administrator account. The package is installed directly and KVM appears under the Applications section of the Discovery wizard.

Manual installation. Load the .disco package from Management → Discovery → Manage disco packages: choose Select a file, pick the package, and click Upload DISCO. After loading, KVM appears in the package list and under the Applications section of the Discovery wizard.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text: Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → KVM. The wizard walks through the generic task definition and three plugin steps: KVM Connection, Authentication and KVM Monitoring Options. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

docs.title: Step 1 — Task definition
docs.text: The generic step asks for the task name, the agent group and server on which the task runs, and the interval. The group and the interval are passed to the plugin and inherited by every generated agent.

docs.title: Step 2 — KVM Connection
docs.text:
The target list and the connection settings:

  • KVM hosts is the target list, one entry per line; comma-separated values are also accepted inside a line. At least one entry is required. Each entry is user@host, host or local:
  • user@host connects to host over SSH as user, which overrides the configured authentication user;
  • host connects to host over SSH with the default SSH user (key mode) or the credential user (credentials mode);
  • local runs ps and virsh on the machine that executes the task and uses no authentication.
  • SSH port is the SSH port used to connect to the remote hosts. Default 22.
  • Command timeout is the SSH connection and command timeout in seconds. Default 10.
  • Authentication mode selects how the plugin authenticates: SSH key or Pandora credentials. The next step renders the fields of the selected mode.

docs.title: Step 3 — Authentication
docs.text:
The fields of this step depend on the Authentication mode selected in the previous step.

In SSH key mode:

  • SSH private key path is the path to the SSH private key on the Pandora server, readable by the user that runs the discovery task. Required in this mode.
  • Default SSH user is the user used for targets without an explicit user@ prefix. The user@ part of a target overrides it.
  • SSH known_hosts file: when set, the host key of every target is verified against this file and unknown hosts are rejected. When empty, unknown host keys are accepted.

In Pandora credentials mode:

  • Pandora credentials is the custom credential selected from the Pandora credential manager. Required in this mode.
  • SSH known_hosts file behaves as in key mode.

docs.title: Step 4 — KVM Monitoring Options
docs.text:
What the task monitors and how the data is delivered:

  • Monitor KVM server performance, when enabled, adds the KVM Server RAM usage (%), KVM Server RAM consumption (bytes) and KVM Server CPU usage (%) modules to the host agent. The KVM Server status module is always created.
  • Monitor virtual machines, when enabled, creates one agent per virtual machine and the Number of VMs module on the host agent.
  • Allow list is a regular expression applied to VM names: only matching VMs get an agent. Empty allows every VM.
  • Deny list is a regular expression applied to VM names after the allow list: matching VMs are excluded. Empty denies no VM.
  • Transfer mode selects how the generated data reaches Pandora FMS. native lets the Discovery server read the agent data directly; tentacle sends the generated agent files to Tentacle IP on Tentacle port with the Tentacle client.
  • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port are the Tentacle destination used in tentacle mode. Defaults 127.0.0.1 and 41121.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Run the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary shows the overall progress and a summary with Total Targets, Total Agents and Total Modules.
  2. The agents. Expect one host agent (KVM <host>) per reachable target, plus one agent per monitored virtual machine, created as a child of its host agent.
  3. The modules. A host with libvirtd running carries KVM Server status and, depending on the enabled options, the server performance modules and Number of VMs. Every VM agent carries Status of <vm>; a running VM also carries its vCPU and memory modules.
  4. The execution information. A successful run reports no errors; connection or command failures, and the reason why a module was omitted, are recorded there.

The example above reports one target, two agents and ten modules: the KVM host agent with five modules and one of its virtual machines with the other five. If the task fails before generating anything, the target list, the SSH connectivity and the selected credentials are the first things to check.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per KVM host and one agent per virtual machine, with the host agent as the parent of each of its VM agents. Every generated agent belongs to the task's agent group, inherits its interval and carries one of the following aliases. With Transfer mode native, generated agents also report KVM as their operating system.

Element Agent alias Parent agent KVM host KVM <host> — Virtual machine <vm> (<host>) The host agent

<host> is the host part of the target as written in KVM hosts. The host agent reports that host as its address (no address for local targets), and a running VM agent uses the VM IPv4 address when it can be resolved.

Generated data also carries stable extra_data markers that identify the origin of each element. Names are normalized to lowercase and characters other than letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores are replaced with underscores:

Element Marker Host agent kvm:host:<host> VM agent kvm:vm:<host>:<vm> Host module kvm:metric:<host>:<metric> VM module kvm:metric:<host>:<vm>:<metric>

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
The module values are read from each target during every task run; the exact name and creation condition of each module are listed in Generated modules.

Agent Modules it carries KVM host libvirtd status; with Monitor KVM server performance: RAM usage, RAM consumption and CPU usage of the KVM server; with Monitor virtual machines: the number of defined virtual machines Virtual machine VM power state; for running VMs: assigned vCPUs, CPU usage per vCPU, memory usage in percent and memory consumption in bytes

A host without libvirtd keeps its agent with KVM Server status = 0 and no other modules, and generates no VM agents.

The virtual memory usage of a running VM is measured on the host as the resident memory of the domain against its current memory allocation, so it reports what the VM consumes on the host rather than the memory assigned to it, and it can exceed 100%.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can also be run outside the Discovery wizard with a configuration file and a targets file. This is useful for testing connectivity, for a one-off run, or for a custom schedule.

Write a [CONF] configuration file with at least the authentication mode and its values, and a targets file with one entry per line in the same formats as KVM hosts. Then run pandora_kvm --conf <config_file> --targets_file <targets_file>. All parameters are documented in Configuration file.

[CONF]
auth_mode = key
ssh_key_path = <PATH_TO_SSH_KEY>
ssh_user = <USER>
ssh_port = 22
timeout = 10
transfer_mode = native
interval = 300
agents_group_id = <GROUP_ID>
monitor_host = 1
monitor_vms = 1

In credentials mode use auth_mode = credentials and credentials = <BASE64_CREDENTIAL> instead of ssh_key_path. The credential value is an encoded username and password, not an encrypted one, so protect the configuration file as a secret.

docs.title: Execution behavior
docs.text:
• Targets are processed sequentially, in the order they are listed. A connection or command error on one target is recorded in the execution information and the remaining targets are still processed.
  • VM CPU usage is sampled per host, not per VM: when at least one VM is running, the plugin reads virsh domstats --vcpu twice, one second apart, and uses the measured window for the percentage. A run takes about one extra second per host with running VMs, and the sampling window is not configurable.
  • When the default virsh list --all returns no virtual machines, the plugin retries the listing with /usr/bin/virsh -r -c qemu:///system and uses that connection for the VM metrics of the host.
  • When the console leaves an unresolved macro placeholder in the generated configuration, for example credentials in SSH key mode, the plugin treats the value as empty.
  • A non-running virtual machine still gets its agent with its status module; its performance modules are not created.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check The task reports Error connecting to <host> Confirm SSH reachability and the port. In key mode check SSH private key path and Default SSH user; in credentials mode check the selected credential. The task reports SSH key authentication requires a key path The task runs in SSH key mode but SSH private key path is empty. Set the path or switch to Pandora credentials. The task reports Invalid Pandora credentials The credential is missing, is not a valid custom credential or has an empty password. Select a custom credential in the Authentication step. The connection is rejected and SSH known_hosts file is set The host key of the target is missing or has changed. Update the file (ssh-keyscan -p <port> <host>) or clear the field. The task reports No agents were created for any target Every target failed. Review the per-target errors in the execution information, starting with connectivity and credentials. The task reports Error listing VMs on <host> Run virsh list --all on the host with the same user and confirm the libvirt permissions. The host agent has KVM Server status = 0 libvirtd is not running on that host, or the SSH user cannot see its processes. No VM agents although the host is up Confirm Monitor virtual machines is enabled and review the Allow list and Deny list expressions. An invalid regex is ignored: it neither allows nor denies anything. The Number of VMs module is not created Monitor virtual machines is disabled. Assigned vCPUs of <vm> or Virtual CPU usage of <vm> (%) is missing A virsh domstats --vcpu sample was missing in either read, the vCPU time delta was negative (the VM restarted between samples) or the command failed. The reason is recorded in the execution information. Virtual memory consumption of <vm> (bytes) is missing virsh dommemstat failed and the virsh dominfo fallback could not read the used memory. Virtual memory usage of <vm> (%) is still created and reports 0. The reason is recorded in the execution information. The KVM Server RAM or KVM Server CPU modules are not created Monitor KVM server performance is disabled, libvirtd is not running, or virsh nodememstats / virsh nodecpustats --percent failed. Both RAM modules are omitted together. A VM agent has no address virsh domifaddr returned no usable IPv4 address (no NIC, no DHCP lease yet or IPv6 only). This is best effort and not an error.

docs.title: Task parameters
docs.text: The console presents these fields after the generic task definition. The macro column is the identifier used in the generated task configuration.

docs.title: KVM Connection
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes KVM hosts _pluginTargets_ textarea — Targets, one per line: user@host, host or local. Comma-separated values are also accepted. Required SSH port _sshPort_ number 22 SSH port used to connect to the KVM hosts Command timeout _timeout_ number 10 SSH connection and command timeout in seconds Authentication mode _authMode_ select SSH key SSH key or Pandora credentials. Required

docs.text:
Field Macro Type Default Notes SSH private key path _sshKeyPath_ string — Key mode only. Path to the SSH private key on the Pandora server. Required in key mode Default SSH user _sshUser_ string — Key mode only. Used for targets without an explicit user@ prefix Pandora credentials _credentials_ select — Credentials mode only. Custom credential from the Pandora credential manager. Required in credentials mode SSH known_hosts file _knownHosts_ string — Both modes. When set, host keys are verified against this file and unknown hosts are rejected

The step renders the fields of the selected Authentication mode only.

docs.title: KVM Monitoring Options
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Monitor KVM server performance _monitorHost_ checkbox on Adds the KVM server RAM and CPU modules to the host agent Monitor virtual machines _monitorVms_ checkbox on Creates one agent per virtual machine and the Number of VMs module on the host agent Allow list _allowList_ string — Regex for VM names. Empty allows all Deny list _denyList_ string — Regex for VM names, applied after the allow list. Empty denies none Transfer mode _transferMode_ select native native or tentacle Tentacle IP _tentacleIp_ string 127.0.0.1 Tentacle destination used in tentacle mode Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number 41121 Tentacle destination port used in tentacle mode

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds a configuration file for the plugin, and a manual execution uses the same format. It is a plain text file with a [CONF] section of key = value lines.

Parameter Default Description auth_mode key key or credentials. An empty value falls back to credentials when credentials has a value, and to key otherwise ssh_key_path — Path to the SSH private key. Required in key mode ssh_user — Default SSH user for targets without an explicit user@ prefix known_hosts — SSH known_hosts file. When set, host keys are verified and unknown hosts are rejected credentials — Credential produced by the Pandora credential manager: a base64 JSON value with user and password ssh_port 22 SSH port used to connect to the KVM hosts timeout 10 SSH connection and command timeout in seconds transfer_mode native native or tentacle tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle destination tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle destination port interval Task interval (300 from the command line) Interval assigned to the generated agents agents_group Task group Agent group name used in tentacle mode agents_group_id Task group ID Numeric agent group used in native mode allow_list — Regex allow list for VM names deny_list — Regex deny list for VM names monitor_host 1 Set to 0 to disable the KVM server performance modules monitor_vms 1 Set to 0 to disable virtual machine discovery prefix — Prefix added to the generated agent aliases and module names. The Discovery task never sets it

Command-line values act as defaults for this file; a parameter present in the configuration file overrides its command-line counterpart.

In credentials mode the selected credential is stored as the base64 JSON value in the task configuration, or in credentials in a manual configuration file. This is an encoding, not encryption: protect the Pandora FMS console, the configuration file and the file permissions of anything that stores it. The SSH private key stays on the server and is referenced by path.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text: The plugin generates the following modules per agent. Created when is the condition under which the module appears.

docs.title: KVM host agent
docs.text: Module Type Unit Created when KVM Server status generic_proc — Always. 1 when at least one libvirtd process runs on the host, 0 otherwise KVM Server RAM usage (%) generic_data % Monitor KVM server performance enabled and libvirtd running KVM Server RAM consumption (bytes) generic_data bytes Same condition as the RAM usage module KVM Server CPU usage (%) generic_data % Monitor KVM server performance enabled and libvirtd running Number of VMs generic_data — Monitor virtual machines enabled and libvirtd running. Counts the entries returned by virsh list --all

docs.title: Virtual machine agent
docs.text:
Module Type Unit Created when Status of <vm> generic_proc — Always. 1 when the VM is running, 0 otherwise Assigned vCPUs of <vm> generic_data — Running VM with a complete CPU sample Virtual CPU usage of <vm> (%) generic_data % Running VM with a complete CPU sample Virtual memory usage of <vm> (%) generic_data % Running VM Virtual memory consumption of <vm> (bytes) generic_data bytes Running VM whose used memory can be determined

A module that depends on a measurement that could not be read is omitted and the reason is recorded in the task execution information; the rest of the agent modules are still created. Virtual memory usage of <vm> (%) is always created for a running VM and reports 0 when its measurement fails.

docs.title: Commands run on the target
docs.text:
Metric Command libvirtd status ps aux \| grep libvirtd \| grep -v grep \| wc -l VM list virsh list --all (fallback: /usr/bin/virsh -r -c qemu:///system list --all) KVM server RAM virsh nodememstats KVM server CPU virsh nodecpustats --percent VM vCPUs and CPU usage virsh domstats --vcpu, twice around a one-second window VM memory virsh dommemstat <vm> (fallback: virsh dominfo <vm>) VM IP address virsh domifaddr <vm> (running VMs, best effort)

The virsh binary is resolved with whereis virsh | cut -f2 -d' ' and falls back to /usr/bin/virsh.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Command Description pandora_kvm --conf <config_file> --targets_file <targets_file> Runs the plugin with a configuration file and a targets file pandora_kvm --conf <config_file> --targets_file <targets_file> --as_server_plugin true Server plugin mode: returns 1 when at least one agent was created and 0 otherwise

Every configuration parameter has an equivalent command-line flag with the same meaning (--auth_mode, --ssh_key_path, --monitor_vms, and so on), except agents_group, agents_group_id and prefix, which are configuration-file only. --as_server_plugin is command-line only.

docs.title: Meraki Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Meraki Discovery addon monitors Cisco Meraki network devices through the Meraki Dashboard REST API. For one Meraki network it reads the status of the devices of three product types, appliance, switch and wireless, and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: device status, appliance uplink status and performance score, switch port status and traffic, wireless throughput and connected clients, and optionally the aggregated appliance traffic of the network.

A Discovery task generates these agents:

  • One agent per appliance with its status and uplink status.
  • One agent per switch with its status and the status and traffic of each port.
  • One agent per wireless device with its status, throughput and client count.
  • One network traffic agent (optional) with the aggregated traffic of the appliances of the network.

The task authenticates with a Bearer token and sends the generated agent data to Pandora FMS with Tentacle.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.meraki, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the Meraki Dashboard API Required Every request goes to the API URL configured in the task Meraki API Bearer token with access to the organization Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Specific Meraki hardware models and firmware Not validated No model or firmware matrix has been recorded

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the Meraki Dashboard API (the task form suggests https://api.meraki.com/api/v1 as the URL).
  2. A Meraki API Bearer token that can read the organization, its networks and their devices. The addon only issues read (GET) requests.
  3. The organization ID and, for the network to monitor, its name (or part of it) and its network ID. See Configure the Discovery task for how each value is used.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it. The generated data is sent with Tentacle, so the Tentacle server address and port must be reachable from the Discovery server.

The addon ships its own executable, bin/pandora_meraki, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.meraki

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Meraki is available among the applications when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Application → Meraki. The console presents the fields in two steps, Meraki base and Meraki Detailed; every field is documented in Task parameters.

One task monitors one network. To monitor several networks, create one task per network.

  1. Meraki base — connection and target:

    • ID: text that identifies the network by name. The addon looks for the first network of the organization whose name contains this text (a plain substring match, not a regular expression) and monitors the devices that belong to it.
    • Token: the Meraki API Bearer token.
    • Url: the API base URL, for example https://api.meraki.com/api/v1.
    • Organization: the organization ID.
    • Network: the ID of the network. It is used as-is in the network-level requests (aggregated appliance traffic and wireless usage), so enter the ID of the same network selected with ID.
    • Use location and Location: secondary groups added to the generated agents.
    • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent.

  2. Meraki Detailed — naming and scope:

    • Use prefix, Agent Prefix and Module Prefix: prefixes added to agent and module names.
    • Interval monitoring: time window of the switch port statistics, in seconds.
    • Use API and the Api fields: reserved fields that this version does not use. See Task parameters.
    • Name Agent Hostname: name the agents after the device name instead of its serial number.
    • Scan appliances, Scan switches, Scan wireless and Scan Appliance Traffic Network: which device types and data to collect.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated.
    • Total appliance agents, Total switches agents and Total wireless agents: agents per device type.
    • Total network appliance traffic agents: 1 when the network traffic agent was generated.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. Their aliases start with the agent prefix (if any) followed by Appliance_, Switch_ or Wireless_ and the device name or serial number.

  3. The modules. Every device agent has a status module. See Understand the results for the rest.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Address Secondary groups Appliance <agent prefix>Appliance_<name or serial> Public IP address of the device Location, plus Router Switch <agent prefix>Switch_<name or serial> Public IP address of the device Location, plus Switch Wireless <agent prefix>Wireless_<name or serial> Public IP address of the device Location, plus Access Points Network traffic <agent prefix> Traffic Appliance_<Network> None Location
  • With Name Agent Hostname enabled, switch and wireless agents use the device name, falling back to the serial number when the device has no name; when disabled, the serial number is used. Appliance agents also read the flag, but they take the name from the switch data, which the appliance path does not have: with Name Agent Hostname enabled the run stops with an error when it reaches an appliance. Disable it to create appliance agents named after the serial number.
  • The agent identity is derived from the agent prefix and the name or serial used. Changing the prefix or the Name Agent Hostname setting, or renaming a device, produces a new agent instead of updating the previous one.
  • Only devices that belong to the monitored network and whose type is enabled (Scan appliances, Scan switches, Scan wireless) produce agents.
  • Agents report with the task group and interval.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Module names are shown without the module prefix.

Appliance agent

Module Type Condition Description status generic_proc Always 1 when the device status is online, 0 otherwise. The description carries the status reported by Meraki perfScore generic_data When Meraki returns a performance score for the device Performance score, in % Uplink <interface>_ifOperStatus generic_proc One per uplink reported for the device 1 when the uplink status is active, 0 otherwise. The description carries the uplink status

Switch agent

Module Type Condition Description status generic_proc Always 1 when the device status is online, 0 otherwise Port <portId>_ifOperStatus generic_proc One per port 1 when the port status is Connected, 0 otherwise Port <portId>_ifOutOctets generic_data One per port Traffic sent by the port, in Kbps Port <portId>_ifInOctets generic_data One per port Traffic received by the port, in Kbps

Wireless agent

Module Type Condition Description status generic_proc Always 1 when the device status is online, 0 otherwise totalKbps generic_data When Meraki returns usage data Total throughput, in Kbps sentKbps generic_data When Meraki returns usage data Throughput sent, in Kbps receivedKbps generic_data When Meraki returns usage data Throughput received, in Kbps clientCount generic_data When Meraki returns the client count Clients connected

Network traffic agent (when Scan Appliance Traffic Network is enabled)

Module Type Description Traffic appliance <Network> total_sent generic_data Sum of the data sent over all the applications reported by Meraki for the appliances of the network Traffic appliance <Network> total_recv generic_data Sum of the data received over the same applications Traffic appliance <Network> total_clients generic_data Sum of the number of clients over the same applications

docs.title: How the values are obtained
docs.text:
• Device status, appliance uplink status and the device list are read for the whole organization and then filtered by the monitored network.
  • The switch port statistics cover the last Interval monitoring seconds.
  • The wireless throughput and client count, and the network appliance traffic, are read for the last 86400 seconds (24 hours) and are not configurable.
  • For wireless devices, the module values are the first data point that Meraki returns for the device.
  • The network traffic agent is generated whenever Scan Appliance Traffic Network is enabled, even when Scan appliances is disabled.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_meraki --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON execution result with the summary and any error messages, and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode. In tentacle mode (the default) the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

The configuration file contains the Bearer token. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the information of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • error: id its required, error: base url its required, error: bearer token its required, error: organization its required, error: network its required: the named setting is empty. All five are mandatory.
  • Meraki nets could not be obtained.: the request to list the networks of the organization did not return data. Check the Url, the Organization ID, the validity of the Token and the connectivity to the API.
  • Request Error: <detail>: the connection to the API failed. The detail carries the error of the HTTP client.
  • Error: 204 : Data could not be obtained. and Error: 204 : PerfScore data could not be obtained.: Meraki answered without content for a request. The corresponding modules are not created.
  • No agents are generated: the text in ID does not match the name of any network of the organization, the monitored network has no devices of the enabled types, or the device types are disabled.
  • No perfScore or Uplink modules on an appliance: Meraki did not return performance or uplink data for that device.
  • No wireless modules besides status: the network-level wireless requests returned no data for the device in the last 24 hours.
  • Error getting switch data: <detail>, Error getting wireless data: <detail> or Error getting appliance data: <detail>: the data of a device could not be processed. The detail carries the cause.
  • Data does not reach Pandora FMS: check Tentacle IP and Tentacle port, and the connectivity to the Tentacle server.

First network that matches is used Token _token_ password Yes — Meraki API Bearer token Url _baseUrl_ string Yes — API base URL. The form suggests https://api.meraki.com/api/v1 Organization _organization_ string Yes — Organization ID Network _network_ string Yes — Network ID used in the network-level requests Use location _useLocation_ checkbox No off Enables Location Location _location_ string No — Secondary groups added to the agents. Shown when Use location is on Tentacle IP _tentacleIP_ string No 127.0.0.1 Server that receives the agent data Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number No 41121 Tentacle port

Shown when Use prefix is on Module Prefix _modulePrefix_ string No — Added to the module names. Off: named after the serial number Scan appliances _scanAppliance_ checkbox No on Generate appliance agents Scan switches _scanSwitch_ checkbox No on Generate switch agents Scan wireless _scanWireless_ checkbox No on Generate wireless agents Scan Appliance Traffic Network _scanApplianceTrafficNetwork_ checkbox No on Generate the network traffic agent

There is no option to monitor Meraki cellular gateway devices in this version.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. One key = value per line, without sections. Numeric options accept 1 to enable and 0 to disable; a value that is not a number is read as 0.

Key Required Default Description id Yes — Text contained in the name of the network to monitor base_url Yes — API base URL bearer_token Yes — Bearer token organization Yes — Organization ID network Yes — Network ID used in the network-level requests location No empty Secondary groups of the agents agents_group_name No empty Group of the generated agents interval No 300 Agent interval, in seconds agent_prefix No empty Prefix of the agents module_prefix No empty Prefix of the modules interval_monitoring No 3600 Time window of the switch port statistics, in seconds agentname_hostname No 1 1 names agents after the device name, 0 after the serial number scan_appliance No 1 Appliance agents scan_switch No 1 Switch agents scan_wireless No 1 Wireless agents scan_traffic_appliance_network No 1 Network traffic agent transfer_mode No tentacle tentacle sends the data files with Tentacle; local moves them to the default Pandora FMS data directory (/var/spool/pandora/data_in/) tentacle_address No 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port tentacle_client No tentacle_client Tentacle client executable tentacle_opts No empty Extra Tentacle client options. This version reads the value but does not pass it to the transfer, which always runs without extra options temporal No /tmp Directory where the data files are written before sending. This version reads the value but does not pass it to the transfer, which always uses /tmp data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Destination of the data files in local mode. This version reads the value but does not pass it to the transfer, which always uses /var/spool/pandora/data_in/

The keys api_url, api_user, api_pass and api_user_pass are accepted but not used by this version.

Example:

base_url = https://api.meraki.com/api/v1
bearer_token = <API_TOKEN>
organization = <ORGANIZATION_ID>
id = <NETWORK_NAME_TEXT>
network = <NETWORK_ID>
location = <SECONDARY_GROUP>

agents_group_name = MerakiAgents
agent_prefix = Meraki
module_prefix = Meraki_
interval = 300
interval_monitoring = 3600
agentname_hostname = 1

scan_appliance = 1
scan_switch = 1
scan_wireless = 1
scan_traffic_appliance_network = 1

tentacle_address = <TENTACLE_SERVER_IP>
tentacle_port = 41121

docs.title: Meraki API requests
docs.text:
All requests are GET requests with the Bearer token, sent to the configured Url.

Data Request Networks of the organization /organizations/<organization>/networks Device status /organizations/<organization>/devices/statuses Appliance uplink status /organizations/<organization>/uplinks/statuses Appliance performance /devices/<serial>/appliance/performance Network appliance traffic /networks/<network>/traffic Switch port status and traffic /devices/<serial>/switch/ports/statuses Wireless usage /networks/<network>/wireless/usageHistory Wireless clients /networks/<network>/wireless/clientCountHistory
