docs.text: Field Value App short name pandorafms.nginx Plugin version 1.0 Type Discovery application (.disco) Section Discovery → Applications Console extension nginx_view (ships with the console, not with the package)

docs.title: Office 365 Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Office 365 Discovery addon monitors the health and the licensing of a Microsoft 365 tenant. It queries the Microsoft Graph API and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: the status of every Microsoft 365 service, the unresolved incidents of each service, the service announcements as log entries, and the usage of every subscribed license.

A Discovery task generates up to two agents:

  • A service health agent with, for each Microsoft 365 service, a status module and a module listing its unresolved incidents. The service announcements (maintenance and incident messages) are sent to the Pandora FMS log collector associated with this agent.
  • A licensing agent (optional) with, for each license subscribed by the tenant, modules for its status and for the units enabled, consumed and available.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.office365, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com Required The addon authenticates and queries data through these hosts Microsoft Entra ID application with the permissions listed in Microsoft Graph permissions Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace shows a general notice for all its integrations; no version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the Microsoft endpoints above.
  2. A Microsoft Entra ID application registered in the tenant to monitor, with a client secret and the application permissions described below.
  3. The tenant ID, the client ID and the client secret of that application.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

The addon ships its own executable, bin/pandora_o365, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Register the application in Microsoft Entra ID
docs.text:
The addon authenticates with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow, with no signed-in user. Prepare the application in the Azure portal:

  1. Open Microsoft Entra ID and register a new application in App registrations. Register it in the tenant you want to monitor.
  2. In Certificates & secrets, create a client secret and copy its value immediately: Azure shows it only once.
  3. From the application overview, copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
  4. In API permissions, add the Microsoft Graph application permissions listed below and grant administrator consent.

docs.title: Microsoft Graph permissions
docs.text:
The addon requests an application token with the https://graph.microsoft.com/.default scope, so it receives the application permissions granted to the registered application. Each data set it reads is covered by the following Microsoft Graph application permissions, according to the Microsoft Graph documentation of each endpoint:

Microsoft Graph request Used for Application permission /admin/serviceAnnouncement/healthOverviews Service status and unresolved incidents ServiceHealth.Read.All /admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages Service announcements sent as logs ServiceMessage.Read.All /subscribedSkus Licensing agent LicenseAssignment.Read.All (the least privileged option listed by Microsoft; Organization.Read.All and Directory.Read.All also work)

Grant only the permissions of the features you enable: omit ServiceMessage.Read.All when Logs is disabled and LicenseAssignment.Read.All when licensing monitoring is disabled. Do not grant the ReadWrite variants.

The client secret is a credential: store it only in the task and revoke it in Microsoft Entra ID when it is no longer needed.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.office365

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Office 365 is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create a Discovery task and choose Office 365. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Office365 base — access to the tenant and data destination:

    • Client ID, Tenant ID and Secret: the values of the Microsoft Entra ID application. The console treats the three of them as password fields.
    • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent. The defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 41121; they rarely need changing.

  2. Office365 Detailed — agents and data to collect:

    • Agent Name: name of the service health agent.
    • Use prefix and Prefix: prefix added to the agent name and to its modules. Prefix is shown only when Use prefix is enabled.
    • Logs: send the service announcements to the Pandora FMS log collector.
    • utf8: encode the value of the incident modules as UTF-8 text.
    • Not data: do not create the status and incident modules.
    • Activate licensing monitoring, Licensing agent name and Prefix for licensing data: create the licensing agent. The last two are shown only when licensing monitoring is enabled.
    • Max threads: shown for compatibility; this version of the addon does not use it.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports Total agents and Total modules. Total agents is 2 with licensing monitoring enabled and 1 otherwise. Total modules adds the status, incident, log and licensing modules generated.

  2. The agents. The service health agent, named after Agent Name (default Pandora_O365), and, when licensing monitoring is enabled, the licensing agent (default Pandora_O365_licensing).

  3. The modules. The service health agent has a <service>_status and a <service>_active_issues module for every Microsoft 365 service; the licensing agent has the license modules described in Understand the results. Log entries appear in the log collector under the service name.

When a step fails, the task records the error in its execution information instead; see Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Name and alias Group Created when Service health agent <Prefix><Agent Name> Task group Always Licensing agent <Prefix for licensing data><Licensing agent name> Task group Activate licensing monitoring is enabled

Both agents are refreshed at the task interval and report the description Agent generated by pandora_o365 plugin. The two prefixes are independent: Prefix does not apply to the licensing agent.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Service health agent

Module Type Condition Description <Prefix><service id>_status generic_data_string Not data disabled Status of the Microsoft 365 service as reported by Microsoft Graph. The module is warning when the status matches investigating, restoringService or extendedRecovery, and critical when it matches serviceDegradation or serviceInterruption <Prefix><service id>_active_issues generic_data_string Not data disabled Identifier and title of each unresolved incident of the service, concatenated without a separator, so consecutive incidents run together; None when the service has no unresolved incident. Description: <service> Issues Ids Log entries Log collector Logs enabled One entry per service announcement read from offset 100, with the source <Prefix>_<service>. The content is the announcement, converted to plain text. The collection is not paged, so the first 100 announcements are never collected and a tenant with fewer than 100 announcements produces no entries

<service id> is the service identifier returned by Microsoft Graph, for example the identifier of Exchange Online or Microsoft Teams.

Licensing agent

For every license (SKU) subscribed by the tenant, the agent has the following modules. <name> is the license part number returned by Microsoft Graph and each module description is the identifier of the license.

Module Type Description <Prefix><name> generic_data_string Capability status of the license <Prefix><name> consumedUnits generic_data Units consumed <Prefix><name> Units enabled generic_data Units enabled <Prefix><name> Units lockedOut generic_data Units locked out <Prefix><name> Units suspended generic_data Units suspended <Prefix><name> Units warning generic_data Units in warning state <Prefix><name> Consumed Units % generic_data Percentage of enabled units consumed, rounded to two decimals, in %. It is 0 when no unit is enabled <Prefix><name> Units Available generic_data Enabled units minus consumed units

Here <Prefix> is Prefix for licensing data.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_o365 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode and prints a JSON summary with the Total agents and Total modules counts. When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages.

The configuration file contains the client secret. Protect it with restrictive permissions and do not keep it after the test.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the information recorded in the execution result of the task.

  • HTTP error: ... on https://login.microsoftonline.com/...: Microsoft Entra ID rejected the authentication. Check the tenant ID, the client ID and the client secret, and that the secret has not expired.
  • Request error: ...: the Discovery server cannot reach login.microsoftonline.com. Check outbound connectivity, DNS and any proxy or firewall.
  • Error requesting url: ... (<status>) on https://graph.microsoft.com/...: Microsoft Graph rejected a data request. A 403 status can indicate that the application lacks the permission of that endpoint or that administrator consent was not granted; see Microsoft Graph permissions. The message names the endpoint.
  • error with status data: ..., error logs data: ... or error with licensing data: ...: reading or processing that data set failed. The error text is appended to the message.
  • error with accounts data: ...: the configuration file cannot be read. It appears only in manual execution.
  • No _status or _active_issues modules: Not data is enabled.
  • No licensing agent: Activate licensing monitoring is disabled.
  • No log entries: Logs is disabled, Microsoft Graph returned no announcements after the first 100, or the tenant has fewer than 100 announcements.
  • Incident values show a byte string: utf8 is disabled. Enable it unless the environment requires raw bytes.

docs.title: Office365 base
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Client ID _clientid_ password empty Mandatory. Application (client) ID Tenant ID _tenantid_ password empty Mandatory. Directory (tenant) ID Secret _secret_ password empty Mandatory. Client secret value Tentacle IP _tentacleIP_ string 127.0.0.1 Server that receives the agent data Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number 41121 Tentacle port

docs.title: Office365 Detailed
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Max threads _threads_ number 1 Optional. Not used by this version of the addon Agent Name _agentname_ string Pandora_O365 Name and alias of the service health agent Use prefix _usePrefix_ checkbox off Shows Prefix Prefix _prefix_ string empty Optional. Shown when Use prefix is on. Prepended to the agent name, the module names and the log source Logs _logs_ checkbox on Send service announcements to the log collector utf8 _utf_ checkbox on Encode the incident value as UTF-8 text; when off, the value is written as raw bytes Not data _activemonitoring_ checkbox off When on, the status and incident modules are not created Activate licensing monitoring _licensing_ checkbox on Create the licensing agent Licensing agent name _agentnameLicensing_ string Pandora_O365_licensing Optional. Shown when licensing monitoring is on Prefix for licensing data _prefixLicensing_ string empty Optional. Shown when licensing monitoring is on

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. One key = value per line; keys that are not present take the default listed here. A numeric option that is not a number is read as 0; 1 enables and 0 disables.

Key Default Description agents_group_name empty Group of the generated agents interval 300 Agent interval, in seconds transfer_mode tentacle Data transfer mode. The Discovery task always uses tentacle tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle server port client_id empty Application (client) ID tenant_id empty Directory (tenant) ID secret empty Client secret value agent_name Pandora_O365_ Name and alias of the service health agent prefix empty Prefix for the agent name, module names and log source logs 1 Create the log entries utf8 1 Encode the incident value as UTF-8 text no_data 1 When 1, the status and incident modules are not created. Set it to 0 to create them licensing 1 Create the licensing agent agent_name_licensing Pandora_O365_licensing Name and alias of the licensing agent prefix_licensing empty Prefix for the licensing agent name and its modules

The default of agent_name and no_data differs between the Discovery task and manual execution: the task defaults to Pandora_O365 and no_data = 0, while a configuration file without the keys uses the values above.

Example:

agents_group_name    = <GROUP_NAME>
interval             = 300
transfer_mode        = tentacle
tentacle_ip          = <TENTACLE_SERVER_IP>
tentacle_port        = 41121
client_id            = <CLIENT_ID>
tenant_id            = <TENANT_ID>
secret               = <CLIENT_SECRET>
agent_name           = Pandora_O365
prefix               =
logs                 = 1
utf8                 = 1
no_data              = 0
licensing            = 1
agent_name_licensing = Pandora_O365_licensing
prefix_licensing     =

docs.title: OpenSearch Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The OpenSearch Discovery addon monitors an OpenSearch cluster through its REST API. It reads the cluster health, the statistics of every node and the aggregated index statistics of the cluster, and turns them into Pandora FMS agents and modules.

A Discovery task generates agents by functional role instead of a single agent per cluster:

  • One cluster agent with the health of the cluster: status, nodes and shard allocation.
  • One agent per node with the operating system, process, JVM, thread pool, transport, circuit breaker, cache and disk statistics of that node.
  • One primary metrics agent with the aggregated index statistics (documents, indexing, search, merges, segments, translog and more) of the primary shards and of all shards.

Each group of agents is optional: you choose which of the three metric groups the task collects, and you can exclude individual modules from each group.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.opensearch, version 1.2 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the OpenSearch REST endpoint Required The addon connects to the IP address and port configured in the task Access to the Nodes stats, Cluster health and Indices stats APIs Required The addon calls these three APIs; each one is needed only for its metric group OpenSearch versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the OpenSearch HTTP(S) port, usually 9200.
  2. Access to the cluster APIs. When the cluster requires authentication, a user and password that can read the cluster health, the node statistics and the index statistics. Credentials are optional: the addon authenticates only when both the user and the password are set.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task, the console to define it and a Tentacle server that receives the generated agent data.

The addon is distributed ready to run, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.opensearch

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, OpenSearch is available in the applications section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery applications and choose OpenSearch. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. OpenSearch Basic — connection and data transfer:

    • OpenSearch IP and OpenSearch Port: address and port of the OpenSearch REST endpoint. Both are mandatory.
    • User and Password: credentials, both optional.
    • Verify SSL: connect over HTTPS. See Connection security.
    • Verify Certs: validate the server certificate.
    • transfer mode, tentacle ip and tentacle port: how and where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. OpenSearch Detailed — naming and metric groups:

    • agent prefix, Agent group, Custom module prefix and Module group: naming and grouping of the generated agents and modules.
    • Primary metrics, Nodes Metrics and Cluster Metrics: the metric groups to collect. Enabled by default.
    • Exclude primary metrics, Exclude nodes metrics and Exclude cluster metrics: modules to leave out of each group. Each one is shown only when its metric group is enabled.

The execution interval comes from the generic task-definition step and is applied as the interval of the generated agents.

docs.title: Connection security
docs.text:
• Verify SSL controls the protocol: enabled, the addon connects over HTTPS; disabled, it connects over plain HTTP. It is enabled by default.
  • Verify Certs controls the certificate: enabled, the addon validates the server certificate; disabled (default), it accepts any certificate. Certificate hostname verification is always disabled, even when Verify Certs is enabled.
  • With Verify SSL enabled and Verify Certs disabled the traffic is encrypted but the server is not authenticated. Use a network you trust or enable Verify Certs.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes reports:

    • Total Agents: agents generated.
    • Total Modules: modules generated across all agents.

    Errors found while collecting a metric group are recorded in the task's execution information.

  2. The agents. One cluster agent, one primary metrics agent and one agent per node, according to the metric groups you enabled.

  3. The modules. The cluster agent has cluster_status, number_of_nodes and unassigned_shards, among others; see Modules per agent.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Created when Cardinality Primary metrics <agent prefix>_primary_metrics Primary metrics enabled and the statistics could be read One per task Node <agent prefix>_node_metrics_<node name> Nodes Metrics enabled and the statistics could be read One per node of the cluster Cluster <agent prefix>_cluster_metrics Cluster Metrics enabled and the statistics could be read One per task

Agent identity is derived from the alias, which includes the agent prefix. Changing the prefix of a task creates new agents instead of updating the existing ones, and the history of the previous agents is not carried over. Use a different prefix for each cluster, so two tasks never write to the same agents.

The agents are placed in the Agent group when one is set, and have no address, operating system or parent.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Module names are the metric name, preceded by <Custom module prefix>_ when a prefix is set.

Agent Modules Cluster Cluster name and status (green, yellow or red), number of nodes and data nodes, active, relocating, initializing, unassigned and delayed unassigned shards, active primary shards, pending tasks, unfinished fetches and the percentage of active shards Node Operating system CPU, load average and memory and swap usage; process CPU, file descriptors and virtual memory; JVM heap, non-heap, memory pools, threads and garbage collection; thread pool statistics; transport and HTTP connections and traffic; circuit breakers; indexing pressure; request cache; disk space; and the index statistics of the node Primary metrics Index statistics, prefixed primaries_ for primary shards and total_ for all shards: documents, store size, indexing, get, search, merges, refresh, flush, warmer, query cache, fielddata, completion, segments, translog, request cache and recovery

The full list is in Module reference.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The package contains the pandora_opensearch executable, which takes the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_opensearch --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It sends one data file per agent with the configured transfer mode and prints a summary with the total agents and modules created. Errors are listed in the same output.

With --as_server_plugin 1 the addon is run as a server plugin: it prints no summary, and prints 1 when it created at least one agent without errors and 0 otherwise, including when the configuration file does not exist.

./pandora_opensearch --as_server_plugin 1 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The configuration file contains the OpenSearch password in plain text. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the task's execution information, or the output of the manual execution.

  • Error: Could not connect to OpenSearch cluster with <host>:<port>: also reported as node or primary instead of cluster, depending on the metric group that failed. The endpoint is unreachable, the protocol does not match (see Verify SSL) or the credentials are rejected. Check the address, the port and the protocol from the Discovery server.
  • Error: when attempting to obtain cluster statistics and Error: when attempting to obtain node data: the request reached the cluster but failed. The message includes the error returned by OpenSearch, for example a missing permission.
  • Unable to obtain OpenSearch metrics.: no metric group produced data. Either the three metric groups are disabled or all of them failed; check the other messages.
  • Error create agent <name>: <error>: the agent could not be created or sent.
  • A group of agents is missing: the metric group is disabled, or its request failed and the cause is in the execution information. The other groups are still generated.
  • A node agent fails after adding an exclusion: an exclusion that matches the text node_name removes the node name the addon needs to create the agent. Use more specific exclusion text.
  • More modules disappeared than expected: exclusions are case-insensitive regular expressions applied to the metric name without the module prefix, so a short text can match several modules. See Excluding modules.
  • Error reading the configuration file (Error file: <path> does not exist, Error while reading configuration file): in manual execution, the path passed to --conf is wrong or the file is not readable or well-formed.

docs.title: OpenSearch Basic
docs.text: Field Macro Type Required Default Description OpenSearch IP _opensearchIp_ string Yes — Address of the OpenSearch endpoint OpenSearch Port _opensearchPort_ number Yes — Port of the endpoint, for example 9200. Must be a number User _opensearchUser_ string No empty Authentication is used only when both User and Password are set Password _opensearchPassword_ password No empty Password of the user Verify SSL _verifySSL_ checkbox No on Connect over HTTPS when on, over plain HTTP when off Verify Certs _verifyCerts_ checkbox No off Validate the server certificate. Hostname verification stays disabled transfer mode _transferMode_ string No tentacle How the agent data is delivered. docs.title: Excluding modules
docs.text: Each exclusion box accepts a list of entries separated by commas. An entry removes every module of that group whose metric name matches it. Matching is case-insensitive and finds the entry anywhere in the name; entries are interpreted as regular expressions, so an invalid expression makes the metric group fail. For example, unassigned, active in Exclude cluster metrics removes every cluster module whose name contains unassigned or active, including unassigned_shards, active_shards and active_primary_shards.

docs.title: OpenShift Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-23.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
OpenShift Discovery reads the cluster API and produces a global agent plus agents for nodes, pods and deployments. The Discovery task generates agent XML and sends it through Tentacle. The global agent summarizes services, namespaces, component statuses, replication controllers and API services; resource agents report capacity, conditions and container CPU/memory.

This page covers the Discovery application, not the older OpenShift CLI/server plugin. Do not reuse that plugin's cli, user, password, project, agent_* or as_server_plugin settings here.

docs.title: Compatibility and requirements
docs.text:
Scope State Requirement or limitation pandorafms.openshift, package 1.0 Documented target Discovery application (.disco) Pandora FMS Discovery server and console Required Define and execute the application task OpenShift API reachable from Discovery Required Direct connections use https://<TARGET_HOST>:<API_PORT> Bearer token Required for protected direct endpoints Read access to the exact resources and health paths in API requests; no validated least-privilege role is supplied Metrics API (metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1) Required for node/pod discovery Discovery starts from metrics, not just from resource lists Tentacle destination Required for delivery Reachable from the Discovery server Specific OpenShift, Pandora FMS or host OS releases Not validated No release-specific compatibility or live test result is established here

Obtain the .disco package from the OpenShift Marketplace entry and load it as a Discovery application. Select the application named Openshift in its package definition. No oc executable, CLI login or project parameter is used by this task.

Ask the cluster administrator to provide API access and confirm node/pod metrics are available. The administrator must authorize the queried surface; the older CLI guide's role and local cluster setup are not a validated access policy for this application.

docs.title: Connection safety
docs.text:
Direct API requests use HTTPS without certificate verification, so they do not authenticate the server identity. Restrict network access. The task stores the token in its generated configuration file; protect task configuration and file access. Manual runs should use a protected configuration file, not a token in command arguments.

With Use proxy enabled, requests use Proxy url and omit the Bearer header. The proxy URL must include its scheme. No request timeout is configured by this package; network delays can hold up collection.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Define the task name, execution server, agent group and interval in Discovery. All generated agents inherit the task group and interval. The package defines two configuration steps, Openshift base and Openshift detailed. The exhaustive field reference is below.

  1. In Openshift base, provide Openshift host without a scheme, Openshift port, and Openshift token for direct API access. For proxy access, enable Use proxy and supply Proxy url instead.
  2. Set Tentacle IP and Tentacle port to the destination that receives the generated XML; defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 41121.
  3. In Openshift detailed, choose Scan Deployments, Scan Nodes and Scan Pods. All default to enabled.
  4. Run the task and inspect its execution information and generated agents.

There are no wizard controls for namespace filtering, prefixes, health checks, components, operators or imagestreams. The three scan switches control resource-agent generation; metrics, deployment and global requests still run when those switches are disabled.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
1. Inspect the Discovery summary: Total agents, Nodes agents, Pods agents, and Deployments agents count generated agents. They do not confirm successful Tentacle delivery.
  2. Check the global Openshift agent and the resource categories enabled in the task. Node/pod agents require complete metric, allocation, node and IP data. Deployment agents require a condition of type Available or Progressing with status True.
  3. Compare representative replica counts and CPU/memory values with the target cluster. Percentages use the node's allocatable resources, not container requests or limits.
  4. Inspect execution errors before treating missing agents or modules as absence of resources. A partial run can produce some agents and still report failures.

Do not use API status = 1 as proof of connectivity: this package always assigns that value. Check the health endpoint modules and request errors. Likewise, deployment Available is always 0 for generated deployments in this package; verify actual availability from replicas and cluster conditions.

No live cluster execution or package installation was performed for this documentation. The manual example below is unexecuted.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
Agent Alias Parent Global Openshift None Node <NODE_NAME> Openshift Deployment <DEPLOYMENT_NAME> Openshift Pod <POD_NAME> Its node

The task does not expose a prefix. Manual configuration accepts prefix, prepending it to aliases and identities. Nodes then use the prefixed global parent and pods the prefixed node; deployments still refer to unprefixed Openshift. Pod agents use the pod IP as their address.

Pod and deployment identities omit the namespace. Equal names in different namespaces can collide; unprefixed identities can also collide across clusters. There is no namespace filter in this application. Changing a manual prefix changes generated identities; the deployment-parent limitation still applies.

docs.title: Functional summary
docs.text:
Agent Results Global Health checks, service/namespace counts and lists, components, replication-controller and API-service counts/status lists, deployment count Node Collected pod count and capacity percentage, CPU/memory and node conditions Deployment Desired, updated, ready, available and unavailable replicas; Available and Progressing modules with the limitations below Pod Phase, one condition module, container count and per-container CPU/memory

Node agents originate from node metrics; pod agents originate from pod metrics. Incomplete data can interrupt an entire processing stage and leave partial output. The node Pods count reflects processed pods with metrics, not a separately validated count of every scheduled pod.

Node conditions are not normalized to healthy = 1: every returned condition is 1 for status True, otherwise 0, including pressure conditions. Pod output contains only the last returned condition, not a module for every condition. Check the module name before interpreting its value.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
Use the distributed executable with a protected file of key=value lines:

pandora_openshift --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

Replace all placeholders in this unexecuted direct-mode example:

ip=<TARGET_HOST>
port=<API_PORT>
token=<API_TOKEN>
agents_group_name=<AGENT_GROUP>
interval=300
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<TENTACLE_HOST>
tentacle_port=41121
use_proxy=0
deployments=1
nodes=1
pods=1

Execution produces Discovery JSON with generation counters and creates/transfers agent XML. An illustrative summary is {"summary":{"Total agents":4,"Nodes agents":1,"Pods agents":1,"Deployments agents":1}}. Do not apply the older server plugin's numeric success/error codes to this executable. -h/--help displays argument help.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Signal Check Error en la solicitud a <endpoint>: <status> Inspect host, port, endpoint reachability and HTTP status. For 401/403, check the token and authorization for that exact path. Direct host values must not contain a scheme. Can't get metrics, Error: Nodes or Error: Pods Check Metrics API responses, allocatable CPU/memory/pods, assigned nodes, pod IPs and condition data. Missing fields can interrupt collection or generation. Missing deployments or Error: Deployments Check the scan switch, returned deployment data and a True Available/Progressing condition. Available is 0 although the deployment is available A package limitation makes this value unreliable; use replica counts and cluster conditions. Progressing is 0 although that condition is True The selected status is the first matching True Available/Progressing condition. A preceding Available condition takes precedence. API status remains 1 during API failures It is a constant, not a connectivity test. Inspect health modules and execution errors. Failed health requests omit their modules. Missing global modules or Error: global_agent Inspect each request and the deployment data. Failed optional global requests can omit individual module groups; other incomplete data can prevent global-agent transfer. Only one pod condition appears This version emits only the final condition returned for the pod. Collection stalls There is no configured HTTP request timeout; inspect network connectivity and task execution. Proxy access fails Check the complete proxy base URL and its authentication arrangement; the task does not send the Bearer header in proxy mode. Agents counted but not received Check connectivity to the configured Tentacle destination; summary counters precede transfer.

docs.title: Oracle Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-20.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Oracle Discovery plugin monitors Oracle Database instances by running SQL queries against them and turning the results into Pandora FMS monitoring modules. It collects availability, session and connection usage, query counts, restart detection, tablespace usage and status, fragmentation, cache hit ratios, and any custom SQL query the operator defines.

The plugin creates one agent per target database. When a target is an Oracle multitenant container database (CDB), it can additionally discover its pluggable databases (PDBs) and monitor them either inside the container agent or as one agent per PDB.

A target can be written as a simple HOST:PORT/SERVICE string or as a full Oracle DSN descriptor. DSN descriptors keep multi-address failover and are also used to reach PDBs, whose name is substituted as the service name.

The plugin is designed for use through the Pandora FMS Discovery system. It does not generate XML agent files: it returns the discovered agents and modules in the JSON output of the execution, and the Discovery task creates them.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.12 (pandorafms.oracle) Documented target The version this page describes, identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity Oracle multitenant CDB/PDB whose PDB services are registered in the listener under a db_domain name Tested Ticket #24889 verification run: the task completed with Targets up and generated the PDB agent and its modules. See Multitenant PDB connection and service resolution Network reachability from the Discovery server to every target database listener Required The plugin opens a remote Oracle connection per target A database user able to connect and with SELECT on the views used by the enabled modules Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Grant the required privileges Oracle Instant Client on the Discovery server, when Thick mode is enabled Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prerequisites Oracle Database 11 or earlier Not validated The official quick guide states thick mode is needed for Oracle 11 and earlier A specific Pandora FMS version Not validated No published test record establishes console or server version compatibility A specific host operating system for the machine that runs the plugin Not validated No host operating system has been recorded Oracle Database server versions Not validated Compatibility was established against the SQL queries and the connection contract, not a version matrix

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Network connectivity between the Discovery server and every target database listener.
  2. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task, and the console to define it.
  3. A database user with permission to connect, and with SELECT privileges on the views used by the modules you enable.
  4. Oracle Instant Client installed on the Discovery server, only when Thick mode is used.

The plugin is distributed as a self-contained Discovery application: the .disco package ships its own executable, so no additional runtime has to be installed for a normal run.

docs.title: Grant the required privileges
docs.text:
The connection user needs at least the CREATE SESSION privilege:

GRANT CREATE SESSION TO pandora;

Each module reads specific Oracle views. Grant only what the enabled modules need.

Module group Oracle views Grant Connections (checkConnections) V$SESSION, V$PARAMETER GRANT SELECT ON V_$SESSION TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$PARAMETER TO pandora; Uptime (checkUptime) V$SESSION GRANT SELECT ON V_$SESSION TO pandora; Query statistics (queryStats) V$SQLSTATS GRANT SELECT ON V_$SQLSTATS TO pandora; Tablespaces (checkTablespaces) DBA_TABLESPACE_USAGE_METRICS, DBA_TABLESPACES, and DBA_DATA_FILES / DBA_FREE_SPACE for the Oracle 10 and earlier fallback GRANT SELECT ON DBA_TABLESPACE_USAGE_METRICS TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON DBA_TABLESPACES TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON DBA_DATA_FILES TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON DBA_FREE_SPACE TO pandora; Fragmentation (checkFragmentation) DBA_TABLES GRANT SELECT ON DBA_TABLES TO pandora; Cache (checkCache) V$LIBRARYCACHE, V$ROWCACHE, V$SYSSTAT GRANT SELECT ON V_$LIBRARYCACHE TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$ROWCACHE TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$SYSSTAT TO pandora; Multitenant PDB discovery (multitenant) V$PDBS and V$ACTIVE_SERVICES GRANT SELECT ON V_$PDBS TO pandora;GRANT SELECT ON V_$ACTIVE_SERVICES TO pandora; Database version PRODUCT_COMPONENT_VERSION GRANT SELECT ON PRODUCT_COMPONENT_VERSION TO pandora; Custom queries Depends on the query Grant SELECT on any table or view the custom queries reference

Version 1.12 reads V$ACTIVE_SERVICES to resolve the listener service name of each PDB. Without this grant the multitenant PDB discovery query fails and no PDB is monitored.

For convenience, SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE covers most V$ and DBA_ views:

CREATE USER pandora IDENTIFIED BY <PASSWORD>;
GRANT CREATE SESSION TO pandora;
GRANT SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE TO pandora;

When multitenant monitoring is used, the user must also be able to connect to each PDB and hold the module grants inside it:

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER = <PDB_NAME>;
GRANT CREATE SESSION TO pandora;
-- Repeat the module grants inside the PDB.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Load the .disco package for pandorafms.oracle from the Pandora FMS Marketplace:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.oracle

Once loaded, the Oracle application is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → Oracle. The console presents the fields in two steps: Oracle Base and Oracle Detailed. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Oracle Base — the targets and how to reach them:

    • Oracle target strings: one or more Oracle targets, separated by commas or one per line. Each line creates one agent. See Target strings.
    • User and Password: credentials used for every target in the task.
    • Thick mode and Client path: use the Oracle Instant Client; the client path is required when thick mode is enabled.
    • Multitenant: Discover and monitor PDBs within a CDB: enables PDB discovery on multitenant architectures.
    • Create agent per PDB: creates a separate agent for each discovered PDB instead of adding its modules to the container agent.
    • Enable entities file re-scan interval and Re-scan entities file interval: keep and periodically refresh the list of discovered PDBs.

    In the example above, the target string oracle-domain-mock:1521/FREE|PKI monitors the container database FREE and restricts multitenant monitoring to the PDB PKI.

  2. Oracle Detailed — monitoring scope and optional shaping:

    • Max threads: number of concurrent connections used to monitor the targets.
    • Target agent: names to assign to the generated agents, positionally matched with the target strings. Empty means the target string is used as the agent name.
    • Custom module prefix: prepended to every generated module name.
    • Check engine uptime, Retrieve query statistics, Analyze connections, Calculate fragmentation ratio, Monitor tablespaces, Retrieve cache statistics: select the module groups to create.
    • Execute custom queries and Custom queries: run operator-defined SQL and create one module per query.
    • Define tresholds: regular-expression thresholds applied to generated modules (except custom-query modules). See Thresholds.

The task's own group and interval, set in the generic task-definition step, become the agent group and the module interval.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A completed Oracle task reports:

    • Total agents: the number of agents generated by the task.
    • Targets up: targets the plugin connected to.
    • Targets down: targets it could not connect to.

    With Create agent per PDB enabled, Total agents includes the container agent plus one agent per monitored PDB.

  2. The agents. One per target string, plus one per PDB when Create agent per PDB is enabled. Every PDB agent is named <container agent> - PDB <pdb name>.

  3. The modules on each agent. A reachable target produces the availability module and one module per enabled group and discovered resource. The module list of the PDB agent shows the PDB PKI prefix on every PDB metric.

If the task reports Targets down for a target, work back through Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Agents and cardinality
docs.text:
• One agent per target string. The agent name is the target string, unless a Target agent name is given for that position. For a plain target, the filter appended after | is not part of the agent name. For a DSN target, the name is a readable label derived from the descriptor (Oracle <HOST>:<PORT>/<SERVICE>), with a short hash appended when the descriptor contains several addresses or services. The agent's OS is reported as Oracle and its OS version as the connected database version (or Discovery when it cannot be read).
  • One agent per PDB, optionally. When Create agent per PDB is enabled, each discovered PDB gets its own agent named <container agent> - PDB <pdb name>. Its address is HOST:PORT/<pdb name>, or the same generated name when the target is a DSN descriptor. When the option is disabled, each PDB's modules are added to the container agent with a PDB <pdb name> prefix.

docs.title: Module groups
docs.text:
A reachable target always produces the availability module <prefix>Oracle connection, with value 1 when the connection succeeded and 0 when it did not.

Group Modules Type Notes Availability <prefix>Oracle connection generic_proc 1 connected, 0 not connected Uptime <prefix>restart detection generic_proc 0 when the engine restarted within the last two intervals, 1 otherwise Query statistics <prefix>queries: select, <prefix>queries: insert, <prefix>queries: delete, <prefix>queries: update generic_data Number of statements of each kind active during the last interval Tablespaces <prefix>tablespace <name> free and <prefix>tablespace <name> status generic_data (%) and generic_proc Free percentage and 1 when the tablespace is ONLINE Connections <prefix>session usage generic_data (%) Current sessions against the configured maximum Fragmentation <prefix>fragmentation ratio generic_data (%) Average fragmentation ratio Cache <prefix>cache hit ratio (dictionary), <prefix>cache hit ratio (library), <prefix>cache hit ratio (buffer) generic_data (%) With default warning/critical thresholds Custom queries <prefix><query name> Per query One module per custom query

The exhaustive inventory, including PDB prefixes and default thresholds, is in Generated modules.

docs.title: Multitenant PDB connection and service resolution
docs.text:
In Oracle multitenant, a PDB is reached through its service name, but the PDB name is not necessarily the service the listener exposes. A PDB can exist while its listener service is only registered under a qualified name, for example when the database has a db_domain configured. Connecting to the PDB name alone then fails with DPY-6001: Service "..." is not registered with the listener (equivalent to ORA-12514).

The plugin resolves the service name of each PDB and tries these candidates in order:

  1. The listener service names registered for that PDB, including the service names read from the entities file.
  2. The same service names qualified with the database domain (db_domain) when the listener exposes them as fully qualified names.
  3. The PDB name itself, as a last resort.

How each candidate is applied depends on the target format:

  • Plain target (HOST:PORT/SERVICE): the plugin connects to the PDB as HOST:PORT/<service name>.
  • DSN target: the plugin rewrites the descriptor, replacing the value of SERVICE_NAME with the candidate while keeping the addresses, ports and failover settings. If the descriptor identifies the connection with a SID instead, the plugin replaces that SID clause with SERVICE_NAME=<service name>.
  • If the descriptor contains neither SERVICE_NAME nor SID, the PDB connection cannot be built and the PDB is reported in the execution information and skipped.
  • A PDB or service name that contains characters outside letters, digits and _ $ # . - is rejected as invalid.

Only when every candidate fails is a warning reported, and (with Create agent per PDB) the PDB agent is created with its connection module at value 0.

Only PDBs in READ WRITE open mode are monitored during discovery; the others are named in the execution information and skipped. PDBs restored from the entities file are monitored as cached.

The Oracle target strings field can restrict which PDBs are monitored by appending |<pdb> or |<pdb1>;<pdb2>;... to a target, as shown in Configure the Discovery task.

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text: Each custom query generates one module on every agent the query applies to. A query can be limited to the container scope (cdb), to PDBs (pdb), or both (all), and can be scheduled with a five-field crontab expression. The target_databases key selects the agents the query applies to: matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace, and accepts the full target string, the SID, or the PDB name. all or an empty value applies the query everywhere. Scheduled queries keep their last successful execution, so an occurrence that was missed while the plugin was not running is executed on the next task run. See Custom queries reference.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The plugin reports its diagnostics in the JSON execution summary printed to standard output: connection warnings, Oracle error codes, and skipped queries are added there.

  • A DSN target cannot connect — the plugin does not fall back from a DSN descriptor to a HOST:PORT/SID connection. Check the descriptor syntax and that it is reachable.
  • A PDB is skipped with DSN contains no SERVICE_NAME or SID to replace — the DSN target used to reach the container does not contain a SERVICE_NAME or SID to substitute with the PDB name. Use a descriptor that identifies the connection with one of them.
  • A PDB is skipped as invalid — the PDB or service name contains characters outside letters, digits and _ $ # . -.
  • DPY-6001: Service "..." is not registered with the listener (or ORA-12514) — the PDB service is not reachable under the name that was tried. The plugin resolves the registered service names and the db_domain qualification automatically; if it still fails, verify that the user has SELECT on V$ACTIVE_SERVICES and that the PDB service is actually registered with the listener.
  • Targets down for a target — the container connection failed. Check network access from the Discovery server, the target string format, and the credentials.
  • No PDBs discovered — the discovery query failed (often a missing grant on V$PDBS or V$ACTIVE_SERVICES), or no PDB matches the |PDB filter in the target string.
  • A PDB is skipped — only PDBs in READ WRITE open mode are monitored; skipped PDBs are named in the execution summary.
  • ORA-00942: table or view does not exist — the monitoring user lacks SELECT on a required view. Grant the privilege for the enabled module group and re-run.
  • agent_per_pdb has no effect — it only applies when Multitenant is enabled.
  • A custom query is missing from an agent — its target_databases value does not match that agent's target string, SID or PDB name. The execution summary names the skipped query and the identifiers it was compared with.
  • An invalid crontab expression is ignored — a custom query crontab must have five fields. An invalid expression produces a warning and the query is skipped.
  • Thick mode fails to start — Client path must point to the Oracle Instant Client libraries installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Target strings
docs.text:
The Oracle target strings field accepts one target per line or comma separated. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. Each target can use any of these formats:

HOST
HOST/SID
HOST:PORT
HOST:PORT/SID
HOST:PORT/SERVICE_NAME
dsn=(DESCRIPTION=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST=<HOST>)(PORT=1521))(CONNECT_DATA=(SID=<SID>)))

When the port is omitted, 1521 is used. A DSN descriptor can be written with or without the leading dsn= (the comparison is case-insensitive), and can describe a failover configuration with several addresses:

dsn=(DESCRIPTION=(FAILOVER=ON)(ADDRESS_LIST=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST=<HOST_1>)(PORT=1521))(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST=<HOST_2>)(PORT=1521)))(CONNECT_DATA=(SID=<SID>)))

For a DSN target the agent name is not the raw descriptor: the plugin builds a readable label from the first host, port and service (Oracle <HOST>:<PORT>/<SERVICE>), and appends a short hash when the descriptor contains several addresses or services.

When the target is a multitenant container and Multitenant is enabled, a PDB filter can be appended with |:

HOST:PORT/SERVICE_NAME|PDB1
HOST:PORT/SERVICE_NAME|PDB1;PDB2

Without a filter, every eligible PDB is monitored.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
A Discovery task builds this file from its own fields. A manual run supplies it with --conf.

Key Default Description agents_group_id 10 Group id assigned to the generated agents interval 300 Agent and module interval in seconds user Empty Connection user. Required password Empty Connection password. Required thick_mode 0 1 enables thick mode client_path Empty Path to the Oracle Instant Client libraries; used with thick mode threads 1 Number of concurrent monitoring threads modules_prefix Empty Prefix for generated module names multitenant 0 1 discovers and monitors PDBs agent_per_pdb 0 1 creates one agent per PDB; requires multitenant=1 execute_custom_queries 1 1 runs custom queries analyze_connections 1 1 creates the session usage module engine_uptime 1 1 creates the restart detection module query_stats 1 1 creates the query statistics modules cache_stats 1 1 creates the cache hit ratio modules fragmentation_ratio 1 1 creates the fragmentation ratio module check_tablescpaces 1 1 creates the tablespace modules (the key keeps this spelling) entities_list Task temporary file Path of the file where discovered PDBs are stored enable_entities_interval 0 1 enables the PDB list re-scan entities_interval 86400 Re-scan interval in seconds cron_state_dir Task temporary file Directory where the last successful execution of scheduled custom queries is stored

Example:

[CONF]
agents_group_id=10
interval=300
user=<USERNAME>
password=<PASSWORD>
thick_mode=0
multitenant=1
agent_per_pdb=1
execute_custom_queries=1
analyze_connections=1
engine_uptime=1
query_stats=0
cache_stats=1
fragmentation_ratio=1
check_tablescpaces=1

The configuration file and the target lists hold the database password in plain text. Restrict them to the account that runs the plugin and keep them out of shared directories, logs and version control.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
The plugin can be executed by hand, which is the fastest way to confirm a target and its credentials before wiring it into a task.

./pandora_oracle \
    --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> \
    --target_databases <PATH_TO_TARGETS> \
    [ --target_agents <PATH_TO_AGENT_NAMES> ] \
    [ --custom_queries <PATH_TO_CUSTOM_QUERIES> ]
Parameter Description --conf Path to the configuration file --target_databases Path to the file containing the target databases --target_agents Path to the file containing the agent names, positionally matched with the targets --custom_queries Path to the file containing the custom queries

The run returns a JSON summary of the execution. The collected data is exposed in the summary's monitoring_data field for the Discovery server to consume.

docs.title: Custom queries reference
docs.text:
Each custom query is a block delimited by check_begin and check_end. Only SELECT statements are allowed.

Key Description name Module name. Mandatory description Module description target SQL query to execute. Mandatory. Only SELECT statements are accepted target_databases Comma-separated target strings, SIDs or PDB names the query applies to. Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace. all or empty applies it everywhere target_scope cdb, pdb or all. Empty or all applies it to both scopes. pdb requires multitenant monitoring operation value returns a single value; full returns all rows as a string. Empty behaves as full datatype generic_data, generic_data_string or generic_proc. A full operation is forced to generic_data_string min_warning, max_warning Warning thresholds min_critical, max_critical Critical thresholds warning_inverse, critical_inverse Set to 1 to invert the corresponding threshold interval str_warning, str_critical String thresholds module_interval Module interval as a multiplier of the agent interval crontab Five-field cron expression. When present, the query only runs when an occurrence is due

Example:

check_begin
name Invalid objects count
description Number of invalid objects
operation value
datatype generic_data
min_warning 5
target SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ALL_OBJECTS WHERE STATUS != 'VALID'
target_scope all
check_end

The console ships a commented guide with the field and a set of example queries as the default content of the Custom queries textarea.

docs.title: Thresholds
docs.text:
The Define tresholds field applies thresholds to the generated modules by module name, except custom-query modules. One definition per line, with a regular expression matching the module name and the thresholds separated by |:

<REGEX> = <threshold>|<threshold>|...

Example:

^tablespace = min_warning 10|max_warning 20|min_critical 0|max_critical 10

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text: All module names carry the Custom module prefix when one is set. Modules created for a PDB keep the container prefix and add a PDB <pdb name> segment.

Module Type Group Enabled by <prefix>Oracle connection generic_proc Availability Always <prefix>restart detection generic_proc Uptime Check engine uptime <prefix>queries: select generic_data Query statistics Retrieve query statistics <prefix>queries: insert generic_data Query statistics Retrieve query statistics <prefix>queries: delete generic_data Query statistics Retrieve query statistics <prefix>queries: update generic_data Query statistics Retrieve query statistics <prefix>tablespace <name> free generic_data Tablespaces Monitor tablespaces <prefix>tablespace <name> status generic_proc Tablespaces Monitor tablespaces <prefix>session usage generic_data Connections Analyze connections <prefix>fragmentation ratio generic_data Fragmentation Calculate fragmentation ratio <prefix>cache hit ratio (dictionary) generic_data Cache Retrieve cache statistics <prefix>cache hit ratio (library) generic_data Cache Retrieve cache statistics <prefix>cache hit ratio (buffer) generic_data Cache Retrieve cache statistics <prefix><query name> Per query Custom queries Execute custom queries

The cache hit ratio modules carry default thresholds:

Module max_warning max_critical cache hit ratio (dictionary) 98 40 cache hit ratio (library) 98 40 cache hit ratio (buffer) 89 40

docs.title: PDB modules (Create agent per PDB disabled)
docs.text: The same modules as the container agent, with PDB <pdb name> inserted after the custom prefix, for example <prefix>PDB <pdb name> tablespace <name> free.

docs.title: PDB agent (Create agent per PDB enabled)
docs.text:
Each PDB agent is named <container agent> - PDB <pdb name>. It contains:

  • <prefix>Oracle PDB <pdb name> connection (availability)
  • Every enabled module group, prefixed with PDB <pdb name>
  • The custom queries whose scope applies to PDBs

docs.title: OVH Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The OVH Discovery addon monitors OVHcloud environments through the OVHcloud API. It turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: the state of Public Cloud instances, optional per-instance CPU, memory and network statistics, Public Cloud volumes, dedicated servers and, optionally, the monthly and overall costs.

A Discovery task generates four kinds of agents:

  • A global agent named OVH, with the number of instances found and, optionally, the cost modules. It is created on every run, except in January when Get monthly and overall costs is enabled: the cost calculation for the previous month fails in that month and the global agent is not generated.
  • One agent per virtual machine (Public Cloud instance), with its state and, optionally, its performance statistics.
  • One agent per volume (Public Cloud volume), with its status, size and attachment.
  • One agent per dedicated server, with its status and hardware and location attributes.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.ovh, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the Discovery server to the OVHcloud API Required The addon queries the OVHcloud API of the ovh-eu endpoint OVHcloud API credentials (application key, application secret and consumer key) Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon

The addon always connects to the ovh-eu OVHcloud API endpoint. Accounts that belong to a different OVHcloud API region are not covered by this version.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the OVHcloud API.
  2. An OVHcloud application key, application secret and consumer key. The process is described in the OVHcloud guide on getting started with its API: OVHcloud API getting started.
  3. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

docs.title: OVHcloud API access
docs.text:
The addon only issues read requests (GET). The consumer key must be authorized for the paths that correspond to the options you enable:

Path Used for /cloud/project and /cloud/project/{project} Listing Public Cloud projects (always) /cloud/project/{project}/instance Listing virtual machines (always) /cloud/project/{project}/instance/{instance}/monitoring CPU, memory and network statistics (when Advanced statistics is enabled) /cloud/project/{project}/volume Volumes (when Scan Volumes is enabled) /dedicated/server and /dedicated/server/{server} Dedicated servers (when Scan Servers is enabled) /me/bill and /me/bill/{bill} Costs (when Get monthly and overall costs is enabled)

The application secret and consumer key are credentials: do not share them and do not paste them in tickets or screenshots.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.ovh

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, OVH is available in the Cloud section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management > Discovery > Cloud and choose OVH. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. OVH base — credentials and where the generated agent data is sent:

    • OVH application key, OVH application secret and OVH consumer key: the OVHcloud API credentials.
    • Tentacle IP and Tentacle port: where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. OVH detailed — the resources to monitor:

    • Scan Volumes, Scan Servers and Monitor virtual machines: which resource types get agents.
    • Get monthly and overall costs: adds the cost modules to the global agent.
    • Advanced statistics: shown only when Monitor virtual machines is enabled; adds the performance modules to the virtual machine agents.
    • Autodisabled agents: creates the agents in disabled mode.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

Enabling Advanced statistics and Get monthly and overall costs can lengthen the task execution, because each requires additional OVHcloud API requests.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: all agents generated, including the global agent.
    • VMs agents: virtual machine agents.
    • Storage agents: volume agents.
    • Server agents: dedicated server agents.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. The global agent plus one agent per virtual machine, volume and dedicated server found, according to the options enabled.

  3. The modules. The global agent has OVH VMs count; every virtual machine agent has <VM name>.status. See Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Address Notes Global agent OVH None Created on every run, except in January when Get monthly and overall costs is enabled Virtual machine agent The instance name The instance IPv4 address; empty when it has none One per instance name of every Public Cloud project: instances with the same name in different projects share one agent. Created only when Monitor virtual machines is enabled. The description includes the instance region Volume agent The volume name None Created only when Scan Volumes is enabled Dedicated server agent The server name The server IP address Created only when Scan Servers is enabled

All agents are created in the task group. When Autodisabled agents is enabled they are created in disabled mode.

docs.title: How agent identity works
docs.text: Each agent is identified by a hash of its prefix and name; volume and dedicated server agents also include the OVHcloud identifier of the resource. Agents with the same identity keep reporting to the same Pandora FMS agent between runs, so renaming a virtual machine in OVHcloud produces a new agent.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_ovh --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON summary and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode:

{"summary": {"Total agents": 13, "VMs agents": 8, "Storage agents": 1, "Server agents": 3}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1. In tentacle mode the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

A configuration file contains the OVHcloud credentials. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • Error: Connector Cannot create client to OVH API: the OVHcloud API client could not be created with the credentials provided.
  • Error getting instances: Unexpected error: the Public Cloud projects or instances could not be listed. Check connectivity, the three credentials and that the consumer key is authorized for /cloud/project.
  • Error: Getting volumes, Error: Getting servers or Error: Getting costs: the corresponding request failed; the message includes the error returned by OVHcloud. Check the matching path in OVHcloud API access.
  • Error: Getting metrics ... for instance: <id>: statistics could not be obtained for that instance. Its other modules are still generated.
  • Error while reading configuration file: the configuration file given to --conf cannot be read (manual execution).
  • No virtual machine agents: Monitor virtual machines is disabled. The global agent still reports the number of instances found.
  • No statistics modules: Advanced statistics is disabled, or Monitor virtual machines is.
  • Fewer agents than expected: only the resource types enabled in the task are created, and only the Public Cloud projects, volumes and dedicated servers visible to the credentials are scanned.

docs.title: Playwright
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-09-01.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Playwright Discovery plugin provides synthetic web monitoring with Playwright: you supply a single Playwright .ts test, the plugin runs it inside a preconfigured Docker container (locally or on a remote host over SSH) and turns the result into Pandora FMS monitoring modules that plug into the console's WUX transactional view — global status and time, per-phase status and time, error screenshot and custom metrics.

The execution model is built around Playwright's native behavior:

  1. The Discovery task (or a manual CLI run) launches a Docker container from the Playwright image (pandorafms/pandora_playwright:noble).
  2. The .ts test is copied into the container and executed with npx playwright test --reporter=json.
  3. The plugin reads the JSON reporter and builds one agent per Playwright test(...), with modules for the overall status and time, each test.step as a phase, an error screenshot on failure, and any custom metrics.
  4. Results are returned as Discovery monitoring data, or (with -x) sent as agent XML via Tentacle.

It is the Playwright counterpart of pandorafms.selenium.4, but there is no custom library to import and no DSL to learn: you write standard Playwright code and the plugin harvests everything from Playwright's JSON reporter. Execution is always in Docker; with worker_mode = remote the container runs on a remote host reached over SSH.
