docs.title: Prometheus Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Prometheus Discovery addon turns the results of your own PromQL queries into Pandora FMS modules. A Discovery task connects to the HTTP API of a Prometheus server, runs every query you define and creates agents and modules with the values returned. You decide which metrics are collected, which thresholds the modules carry and which agent each metric belongs to.

A Discovery task generates:

  • A main agent, named Agent name (Prometheus by default), which receives every metric that is not assigned to another agent.
  • Additional agents (optional), one for each distinct agent name you assign to a query.

The addon collects only what your queries return. It defines no queries of its own, so a task without queries generates no modules and reports an error.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.prometheus, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. The Marketplace entry offers the package pandorafms.prometheus.1.0.disco Network access from the Discovery server to the Prometheus HTTP API Required The addon calls <URL>/api/v1/query Prometheus server versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace states only a general compatibility with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions for its entries; no matrix has been recorded for this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Discovery server to the Prometheus server, for example http://<PROMETHEUS_HOST>:9090.
  2. Valid TLS certificate when the URL uses https. The addon always verifies the certificate of the Prometheus server and has no option to disable the verification.
  3. Credentials only when the Prometheus server is protected with HTTP basic authentication.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

Nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.prometheus

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, Prometheus is available in the application section of the Discovery task wizard.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create a Discovery task and choose Prometheus. The console presents the fields in three steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. prometheus base — connection:

    • Url: address of the Prometheus server, for example http://<PROMETHEUS_HOST>:9090. Mandatory. Do not end it with a slash.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. prometheus detailed — agent and authentication options:

    • Agent name: name of the main agent.
    • Use prefix and Prefix: text prepended to the name of every agent created.
    • Auth basic, Username and Password: HTTP basic authentication.

  3. prometheus custom — the queries, three free-text boxes with one definition per line:

    • Custom queries: <METRIC_NAME> = <PROMQL_QUERY>.
    • Define tresholds: <METRIC_NAME> = <THRESHOLD> <VALUE>|<THRESHOLD> <VALUE>.
    • Define agents: <METRIC_NAME> = <AGENT_NAME>.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Define queries, thresholds and agents
docs.text:
The name before the = is the key of the metric. It prefixes the name of the modules the query generates and links the query to its threshold and agent lines. Keys are case-insensitive (they are converted to lowercase) and cannot contain = or :.

node_cpu_avg = avg_over_time(node_cpu_seconds_total[15m])
up_status = up
cpu_idle_avg = node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle",cpu="0"}
disk_free_last = node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/"}
node_cpu_seconds = node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle",cpu="0"}[15m]

Thresholds, one line per key, with several thresholds separated by |:

cpu_idle_avg = min_critical 75|min_warning 60

Agents, one line per key. Keys without a line go to the main agent:

node_cpu_seconds = Prometheus cpu

Rules:

  • Lines that start with # are comments.
  • A threshold or agent line is applied only when a query with the same key exists; otherwise it is ignored.
  • Each threshold is a name and a value separated by a space. Items that do not have exactly two words are ignored. The name is passed to the module as is; the addon does not validate it.
  • The percent sign (%) cannot be used in the three text boxes. It makes the task fail with Error while reading specification configuration file.

The query examples above are written for a Prometheus server that exports the node_exporter metrics. Adapt the metric names to your own server.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Total agents: agents generated.
    • Total modules: modules generated.

    When the task generates no modules, the execution information shows Error: The task has not generated modules. Please check your access to the environment, permissions, or queries.

  2. The agents. The main agent and one agent for each name assigned in Define agents.

  3. The modules. One or more modules per query; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Alias Notes Main agent Prefix + Agent name Contains every metric without an agent assignment Additional agent Prefix + the name given in Define agents One per distinct name. Several keys can share it

An agent is created only when it receives at least one module. All agents belong to the task's group and report at the task's interval.

Agent identity is derived from the alias, that is, Prefix + agent name, and not from the task or the Prometheus URL. Two tasks that use the same prefix and agent name report to the same agent, even if they point to different Prometheus servers. Use a different Prefix per Prometheus server to keep their agents apart.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
Each series returned by a query becomes one module. Its name is the query key followed by the labels of the series, in the form <KEY> {'label': 'value', ...}, for example up_status {'__name__': 'up', 'instance': '<HOST>:9100', 'job': 'node'}. A query that returns several series therefore creates several modules with the same key.

Query result Module type Value Instant query, one value per series generic_data The value returned, as a number Range selector, such as metric[15m] generic_data_string The list of values returned, each one with its timestamp

Queries with no results are skipped. The thresholds defined for a key are applied to every module of that key.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes a single parameter, the path to the configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_prometheus --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

It prints a JSON execution result and sends one data file per agent using the configured transfer mode. The Discovery task uses the same executable with a temporary configuration file built from the task fields.

When a configuration file contains password, protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Queries must return instant or range vectors. A query that returns a scalar, such as scalar(up), makes the task fail.
  • The addon always verifies TLS certificates.
  • Basic authentication is applied only when both Username and Password are set.
  • Every query is an instant query evaluated by Prometheus at the time of the run.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug mode. Its diagnostic channel is the information field of the execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information.

  • HTTP Error querying Prometheus: <CODE> ...: the server answered with an HTTP status other than 200. The message includes the response body and the failing query. A 401 means the basic authentication is missing or wrong; a 404 usually means an incorrect Url. The remaining queries still run.
  • Prometheus query error: ...: Prometheus rejected the query, for example because of a syntax error. The message includes the failing query. The remaining queries still run.
  • [Error] Please, check and change your configuration ...: the task could not complete, followed by the error text. Typical causes are a server that cannot be reached, a TLS certificate that cannot be verified, or a query that returns a scalar.
  • Error while reading specification configuration file: one of the three text boxes is not valid. Check for % characters and for lines without =.
  • Error: The task has not generated modules ...: no query returned data. Run the same query in the Prometheus expression browser and check Url, credentials and query keys.
  • Fewer modules than expected: queries that return no series produce no modules, and two series that give the same module name are collapsed into one module.
  • Thresholds or agent assignment not applied: the key in the threshold or agent line does not match a query key. Keys are case-insensitive.
  • Tentacle extra options have no effect: the addon does not read this value, so it cannot change how the data is sent.

Prepended to every agent name Auth basic _authBasic_ checkbox No off Shows Username and Password Username _userName_ string No — Shown when Auth basic is on Password _password_ string No — Shown when Auth basic is on

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The configuration file passed with --conf is an INI file. Sections [QUERIES], [THRESHOLDS] and [AGENTS] take the same lines as the text boxes of the third wizard step. Keys of the [CONF] section that are not listed below are ignored.

Key Required Default Description url Yes http://localhost:9090 Prometheus URL agents_group No 0 Numeric group ID for the agents interval No 300 Agent interval, in seconds prefix No empty Prefix for the agent names. Write it without quotes: quotes become part of the prefix agent_name No Prometheus Name of the main agent username No empty Username for basic authentication password No empty Password for basic authentication transfer_mode No tentacle How the data files are delivered tentacle_ip No 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle port 
[CONF]
agents_group = <GROUP_ID>
interval = 300
prefix = <PREFIX>
agent_name = Prometheus
url = http://<PROMETHEUS_HOST>:9090
username = <USERNAME>
password = <PASSWORD>
tentacle_ip = <TENTACLE_IP>
tentacle_port = 41121

[QUERIES]
up_status = up
cpu_idle_avg = node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle",cpu="0"}
node_cpu_seconds = node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle",cpu="0"}[15m]

[THRESHOLDS]
cpu_idle_avg = min_critical 75|min_warning 60

[AGENTS]
node_cpu_seconds = Prometheus cpu

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Parameter Required Default Description -c, --conf Yes — Path to the configuration file. If the file does not exist, the execution ends with Configuration file not found: <PATH>

docs.title: Proxmox Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Proxmox Discovery plugin connects to a Proxmox VE cluster through the Proxmox VE API and discovers its resources. It generates one Pandora FMS agent per discovered resource and fills it with availability, capacity, configuration and performance modules read from the Proxmox API.

The plugin generates agents for:

  • every Proxmox node;
  • every QEMU virtual machine;
  • every LXC container;
  • every storage defined on a node;
  • one cluster agent for scheduled backups;
  • one data center agent with the cluster summary.

The resource categories are selectable in the task, and a per-task entities list lets you fine-tune which resources are monitored and rename the resulting agents.

The plugin runs as a Discovery task: the console creates the task, the Discovery server runs the plugin, and the generated agents and modules are created automatically. The task delivers the generated agent data through Tentacle.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.6 (pandorafms.proxmox) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. Proxmox VE cluster with the API reachable on the configured port (default 8006) Required The plugin authenticates and reads every resource through the Proxmox VE API. An account or API token with read access to nodes, guests, storage, backups and cluster status Required The plugin lists nodes, QEMU and LXC guests, storage and cluster backups; it never changes the Proxmox configuration. A specific Proxmox VE version Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete Proxmox VE release. Host operating system running the plugin Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and a console to define it.
  • A Proxmox VE endpoint reachable from the Discovery server, with the API exposed on the configured port. The default Proxmox VE API port is 8006.
  • One of the following credentials:
    • a Proxmox user in the user@realm format, for example root@pam, with its password;
    • a Proxmox API token, provided as its token name and token secret.
  • A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents. Both come from the Discovery task and are inherited by every generated agent.
  • Network reachability to the Tentacle destination, because the task transfers the generated agent data through Tentacle.
  • A writable path for the entities list file. The default is a file specific to the Discovery task under Pandora's temporary directory.
  • The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) that the Discovery server executes on the Pandora FMS server.

Grant the Proxmox account or API token only the read access your monitoring needs. The plugin only queries the API; it never modifies nodes, guests, storage or backups.

The plugin connects to the Proxmox VE API without verifying its TLS certificate. Run the task only over a network you trust, or protect the traffic through a tunnel. There is no option to enable certificate verification for this plugin.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text: Load the .disco package from Management → Discovery → Manage disco packages: choose Select a file, pick the package, and click Upload DISCO. After loading, Proxmox appears in the package list and under the Applications section of the Discovery wizard.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text: Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → Proxmox. The wizard walks through the generic task definition and two plugin steps: Proxmox base and Proxmox detailed. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

docs.title: Step 1 — Task definition
docs.text: The generic step asks for the task name, the agent group and server on which the task runs, and the interval. The group and the interval are passed to the plugin and inherited by every generated agent.

docs.title: Step 2 — Proxmox base
docs.text:
Connection details, authentication and the Tentacle destination:

  • Proxmox host is the address or hostname of the Proxmox VE endpoint.
  • Port is the API port. The default is 8006.
  • Proxmox user is the account in user@realm format, for example root@pam.
  • Password Authentication controls the visibility of Password. Enter the password of the Proxmox user.
  • Token API Authentication controls the visibility of Token Name and Token Password. Enter the name and secret of a Proxmox API token.
  • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port, Tentacle client path and Tentacle extra options set how the generated data is sent. Leave the defaults unless your environment needs another Tentacle target.
  • Agent name prefix is prepended to the generated agent names. The default is Proxmox..
  • Agent autodisable mode creates the generated agents in autodisabled mode.

The two authentication checkboxes only control which fields the wizard shows. The plugin authenticates with the API token when both Token Name and Token Password are set, and with the Proxmox user and password otherwise. Do not fill only one of the token fields: in that case the plugin falls back to password authentication.

docs.title: Step 3 — Proxmox detailed
docs.text:
Resource categories, the entities list and the re-scan behaviour:

  • Scan VMs, Scan LXC, Scan backups, Scan nodes, Scan data center and Scan storage enable or disable each resource category. All of them are enabled by default.
  • Enable entities list re-scan interval rebuilds the resource sections of the entities list after the configured interval. See Entities list file for the consequences.
  • Re-scan entities list interval is how often the list is rebuilt. It is only shown when Enable entities list re-scan interval is on.

The wizard does not expose the path of the entities list. The plugin keeps it in a file specific to the task under Pandora's temporary directory and reads it on every run. Edit that file to choose which individual resources are monitored and to rename their agents. See Entities list file.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Run the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary reports the total number of generated agents and how many belong to each resource group.
  2. The agents. Expect one agent per enabled and reachable resource, plus the cluster backups agent and the data center agent when their categories are enabled.
  3. The modules. Every generated agent carries the modules of its resource type; a reachable environment populates availability, capacity and performance values.
  4. The execution information. A successful run reports no errors; any per-resource failure is recorded there.

If the task fails before generating anything, the Proxmox host, the port and the credentials are the first things to check.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per discovered resource. Every generated agent belongs to the task's agent group and inherits its interval. Node, virtual machine and LXC agents also carry a custom field, proxmox_device, whose value is Node, VM or LXC.

Each agent has a stable internal name and a readable alias. The internal name is a hash scoped to the Discovery task, the Proxmox host and port, the resource type and the resource ID. The alias is built from the configured prefix and the resource identity, and can be rewritten with a rename rule.

Resource Alias template (default) Scope Node <prefix>.<node>.<node id> One agent per node Virtual machine <prefix>.<vm name>.<vmid>.<node> One agent per QEMU guest LXC container <prefix>.<container name>.<vmid>.<node> One agent per LXC guest Storage <prefix>_<storage>_<node> One agent per node storage Backups <prefix>_Backups One agent for the whole cluster Data center <prefix>_Data_Center One agent for the whole cluster

Because the internal name includes the Discovery task ID and the Proxmox endpoint, two tasks monitoring different Proxmox environments cannot update the same agent even if their resource names coincide. The entities list filename is also specific to the task.

Rename rules change the visible alias only. The internal name is not affected, and guest agents are identified by VMID, so renaming a guest keeps updating the same agent.

docs.title: The entities list file
docs.text:
On its first run, the plugin creates the entities list file with a section heading per resource type and the resources it discovered:

Node
pve1
VM
pve1/100
LXC
pve1/200
Storage
pve1/local
Backups
Backups
Datacenter
Data_Center
Rename
web-prod TO Production web

Remove a resource line to exclude it from monitoring. Changes take effect on the next task execution. The list is how this plugin selects individual resources and renames their agents; see Entities list file in the reference for the exact semantics, including what happens when a resource is deleted in Proxmox VE, and the re-scan behaviour.

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
Each agent receives the modules of its resource type. The module values are read from the Proxmox API during every task run; the exact name and unit of each module are listed in Generated modules.

Agent Modules it carries Node Host status and state, CPU, memory, disk, storage capacity, kernel and manager version, SSL fingerprint and network traffic Virtual machine Power status and state, CPU, memory, disk and network usage LXC container Power status and state, CPU, memory, disk and network usage, plus usage percentages relative to the container and to the host Storage Used-space percentage, enabled and active state, total and used capacity, type, path and content types Backups One pair of modules per scheduled backup job: its state and the time remaining until the next run Data center Node, VM and LXC counters and the general CPU, memory and storage usage percentages

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can also be run outside the Discovery wizard with a configuration file. This is useful for testing connectivity, for a one-off run, or for a custom schedule. The configuration file is a plain list of key=value lines:

pandora_proxmox --conf <path to configuration file>

A minimal configuration file for a manual run looks like this:

host=<PROXMOX_HOST>
port=8006
user=<PROXMOX_USER>
password=<PROXMOX_PASSWORD>
prefix=Proxmox.
interval=300
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<TENTACLE_IP>
tentacle_port=41121
entities_list=/tmp/proxmox_entities_list.txt

All keys are documented in Configuration file. When no task_id is provided, manual executions fall back to the endpoint identity for the internal agent names.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The plugin does not verify the Proxmox VE TLS certificate.
  • The task writes the connection credentials to its configuration file on the Pandora FMS server. There is no password encryption option for this plugin, so protect access to the server and its temporary files.
  • Backups are read at cluster level. Only scheduled cluster backup jobs are reported; per-guest backup retention is not exposed by this plugin.
  • Storage discovery pairs the storage list of a node with the cluster storage list. If a node reports a different number of storages than the cluster list, that node's storage is skipped.
  • The entities list only excludes or renames resources. Removing a resource from Proxmox does not delete its agent automatically.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check The task reports an error logging into the Proxmox environment Confirm Proxmox host and Port, that the API is reachable from the Discovery server, and that the credentials are valid. Authentication fails with a password account The Proxmox user must use the user@realm format, for example root@pam. Token authentication is not used Fill both Token Name and Token Password. With only one of them set, the plugin falls back to the user and password. No agents are generated at all Confirm the credentials, that the Proxmox cluster has the resources you expect, and that the relevant Scan options are enabled. Expected resources are missing Review the entities list file: a removed line excludes the resource, and a disabled category is not written when the list is first built. An agent is reported as critical after a resource is deleted in Proxmox VE The resource line is still in the entities list. Delete the line, or enable Enable entities list re-scan interval so the next rebuild drops resources that no longer exist. A manually excluded resource is monitored again after a re-scan A rebuild restores lines for resources that still exist in Proxmox VE. To keep manual exclusions, leave the re-scan interval off or remove the line again after the rebuild. A renamed agent is not updated Use the original alias, the resource name or the resource identifier in the rename rule, and confirm the rule is under the Rename section. Storage agents are missing for a node The plugin skips a node whose node storage list does not match the cluster storage list. Confirm the node reports its storages correctly. New agents appeared after upgrading the plugin This version changed the internal agent identity: earlier versions built it from the display name. The first run of this version creates new agents instead of updating the ones created by earlier versions. Review alerts and dashboards that refer to the old agents before removing them. Tentacle transfer fails Confirm the Discovery server can reach Tentacle IP on Tentacle port and that the Tentacle client is available, or set Tentacle client path.

docs.title: Task parameters
docs.text: The console presents these fields after the generic task definition. The macro column is the identifier used in the generated task configuration.

docs.title: Proxmox base
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Proxmox host _proxmoxHost_ string — Address or hostname of the Proxmox VE endpoint. docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds a configuration file for the plugin. The same format is used for a manual execution. It is a plain text file of key=value lines. This is the configuration surface for every parameter.

Key Default Description host — Proxmox VE address or hostname. Required port 8006 Proxmox VE API port user — Proxmox account in user@realm format password — Proxmox user password proxmox_token_name — Proxmox API token name proxmox_token_pass — Proxmox API token secret prefix Proxmox. Prefix for the generated agent aliases agents_group_name — Agent group for the generated agents interval 300 Agent interval for the generated agents task_id — Discovery task identifier. Used to scope the internal agent names agent_autodisable False Set to true to create the generated agents in autodisabled mode scan_nodes 1 Generate an agent per node scan_backups 1 Generate the cluster backups agent scan_vms 1 Generate an agent per QEMU virtual machine scan_lxc 1 Generate an agent per LXC container scan_data_center 1 Generate the data center agent scan_storage 1 Generate an agent per node storage discard_nodes [] JSON list of node names to discard from node, guest and storage monitoring entities_list /tmp/proxmox_entities_list.txt Path of the entities list file. A Discovery task always sets a task-specific path under Pandora's temporary directory enable_entities_interval False Set to true to rebuild the entities list on an interval entities_interval 86400 Rebuild interval in seconds transfer_mode tentacle tentacle sends the data through Tentacle; local writes it to local_folder tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 Tentacle destination address tentacle_port 41121 Tentacle destination port tentacle_path — Optional path to the Tentacle client tentacle_opts — Extra options passed to the Tentacle client temporal /tmp/ Working folder for temporary files local_folder /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Destination folder when transfer_mode is local pandora_url — Console API URL api_user — Console API user api_pass — Console API password apiuser_pass — Console API user password

The console API parameters are used to create the proxmox_device custom field in Pandora FMS when it does not exist yet.

docs.title: Entities list file
docs.text:
The entities list is a plain text file that selects and renames resources. The plugin creates it on the first run and reads it on every run. In a Discovery task the path is fixed to a task-specific file under Pandora's temporary directory and is not configurable from the wizard; only a manual execution can set it with the entities_list key.

In this plugin, the entities list is the mechanism that decides which discovered resources are monitored and how their agents are named. Use it to:

  • exclude an individual resource, such as one virtual machine, from monitoring without disabling its whole scan category;
  • keep a selection of monitored resources between task runs, because the file is read on every run;
  • rename the visible agent aliases with Rename rules.

If a resource is removed from Proxmox VE but its line remains in the file, the plugin stops collecting it on the next run and its agent can be reported as critical. The line is removed only when the list is rebuilt after the re-scan interval, which must be enabled for this to happen; you can also delete the line manually. A rebuild also restores lines you removed for resources that still exist in Proxmox VE, so review the file after a re-scan.

Section Entry format Example Node Node name pve1 VM <node>/<vmid> pve1/100 LXC <node>/<vmid> pve1/200 Storage <node>/<storage> pve1/local Backups The fixed entry Backups Backups Datacenter The fixed entry Data_Center Data_Center Rename ORIGINAL TO NEW web-prod TO Production web

Rules:

  • Remove a resource line to exclude it from monitoring. Changes take effect on the next task execution.
  • The entry all inside a section permits every current resource of that type.
  • Disabled scan categories are not written when the list is first built. Enable an interval or add entries manually if you enable a category later.
  • Enable entities list re-scan interval rebuilds the resource sections after the configured interval. It is off by default so manual exclusions persist. A rebuild discovers new resources and retains the Rename rules, but it restores the resource lines you removed.
  • The file must be writable by the account that runs the Discovery task.

docs.title: Rename rules
docs.text:
Add mappings under the Rename section using ORIGINAL TO NEW.

  • ORIGINAL may be the original agent alias including the prefix, or the source resource name, for example web-prod.
  • The target becomes the visible agent alias.
  • A rename does not change the internal hashed agent name. Guest agents are identified by VMID.
  • For equal resource names on different nodes, use the full original alias to target one agent.

docs.title: RabbitMQ Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The RabbitMQ Discovery plugin connects to one or more RabbitMQ brokers through their Management API and turns the state and performance of the cluster into Pandora FMS agents and modules. It reads a list of targets given as Management API URLs, authenticates with HTTP Basic credentials, and collects cluster, node, exchange, connection, queue, channel and virtual host data through the read endpoints of the API.

A Discovery task creates one agent per target. Every metric group is optional and controlled from the task, so the same plugin can collect only the cluster overview or the full inventory of queues, channels and virtual hosts.

A companion console extension, RabbitMQ Dashboard, presents the generated agents and modules in a single monitoring view.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Plugin version 1.0 (pandorafms.rabbitmq.discovery) Documented target The version this page describes, as identified by the package definition. See Plugin identity. A reachable RabbitMQ Management API endpoint Required The plugin establishes remote connections to each target and queries its /api endpoints. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. The RabbitMQ management plugin enabled on each broker Required The collected data is served by the Management API. Without it the endpoints are not available. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. A RabbitMQ user able to read the Management API Required The plugin authenticates with HTTP Basic credentials on every request. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prepare RabbitMQ access. A specific RabbitMQ version Not validated No published test record establishes compatibility with a concrete RabbitMQ release. A specific Pandora FMS version Not validated No published test record establishes console or server version compatibility. A specific host operating system Not validated No published test record establishes operating-system compatibility for the machine that runs the plugin.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS server with Discovery enabled to run the task, and a console to define it.
  2. The RabbitMQ management plugin enabled on every broker to monitor, so the Management API is served.
  3. Connectivity between the Pandora FMS server and each broker's Management API (default port 15672 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS).
  4. A RabbitMQ user with read access to the Management API. See Prepare RabbitMQ access.
  5. A target agent group and a monitoring interval for the generated agents, taken from the Discovery task.

The plugin is distributed as a Pandora FMS Discovery application (.disco package) with its Python dependencies bundled, so no extra Python libraries have to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Prepare RabbitMQ access
docs.text:
The plugin authenticates against the Management API with HTTP Basic and only issues read (GET) requests, so the account only needs access to the endpoints the task queries.

  • Enable the management plugin on each broker and confirm the Management API responds, for example https://<TARGET_HOST>:15672/api/overview.
  • Create a dedicated user and grant it the least privileges that allow reading the Management API of the virtual hosts being monitored. No management write access is required.
  • Prefer HTTPS. Over plain HTTP the Basic credentials travel unencrypted. To use HTTPS with a private certificate authority, set CA file to the PEM bundle on the Pandora server.

The plugin never publishes, consumes or changes RabbitMQ resources; it only reads the API.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Load the .disco package from Management → Discovery → Extension manager (the Manage disco packages view). Once loaded, RabbitMQ appears under the Applications category of the Discovery wizard.

The companion RabbitMQ Dashboard is a console extension. Install it as a console extension package; once installed it adds the RabbitMQ Dashboard entry to the Monitoring menu. It requires the agents generated by this plugin to exist.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → RabbitMQ. The generic first step defines the task; the package adds Connection, Agents and filters and Metrics and module filters. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

Step 1 — Task definition. Name, agent group, server and interval. The group ID and the interval are passed to the plugin and applied to every generated agent.

Step 2 — Connection. The targets to connect to and how the API is reached:

  • Targets is the list of Management API URLs, one per line or comma-separated. Each entry is a plain URL, for example http://172.17.0.2:15672, or a JSON object with url, user, password and alias. Lines starting with # are comments. See Targets file.
  • Default user and Default password apply to targets that do not carry their own credentials inline, and to plain URL targets.
  • Request timeout seconds and HTTP retries tune how the API is called.
  • Verify TLS certificates validates HTTPS certificates and hostnames, and CA file points to an optional PEM bundle on the Pandora server.

Step 3 — Agents and filters. Agent naming and the resource filters:

  • Agent alias prefix is prepended to the agent display alias. The agent identity is not affected.
  • Module prefix is prepended to every generated module name.
  • Agent autodisable mode creates the generated agents in Pandora FMS mode 2, which disables an agent when all its modules become unknown.
  • Queue name regexp and Vhost name regexp restrict which queues, exchanges and virtual hosts are collected. Empty matches all.

Step 4 — Metrics and module filters. Which metric groups are collected and which modules are kept:

  • The twelve toggles enable the cluster overview, the global message rates, the node metrics and resources, the node IO counters, the queue metrics and rates, the exchanges, the connection summary and per-connection detail, the channels and the virtual hosts.
  • Modules allow regexp and Modules deny regexp filter the final module names. The deny list takes priority over the allow list.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary reports resources_discovered, resources_vanished, modules and errors. resources_discovered is the number of targets in the task, whether they are reachable or not; errors counts the API endpoints that failed during the run. The example below shows a single target discovered with 141 modules and no errors.

  2. The agent. One agent appears per target, named rabbitmq-<identifier> with the alias taken from the target URL or its alias. An unreachable target still produces an agent whose Availability module reports 0, and the connection or timeout error is reported in the execution information.

  3. The modules. The agent carries the Availability module plus the metric groups enabled in step 4, according to what the broker reports.

The agent detail lists the generated modules with their current value, state and description.

docs.title: Agents and identity
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per target. The agent name is rabbitmq- followed by a 32-character identifier derived from the task and the normalized target URL, so the name is stable across runs for the same task and target. The alias is the target alias when provided, or the target URL, with the Agent alias prefix prepended.

Each generated agent reports Other as its operating system, belongs to the task's group (by ID) with the task interval, and carries the base address of the target. It is marked with the agent-level extra_data value rabbitmq:agent:<identifier>, which lets the console and the companion dashboard identify it as a RabbitMQ discovery agent. With Agent autodisable mode enabled the agents are created in Pandora FMS mode 2.

Targets are grouped by their normalized URL; duplicate normalized URLs are rejected. Targets that do not carry inline credentials use the task's Default user and Default password.

docs.title: Modules by agent
docs.text:
Every module is created on the target agent; the resource name is appended to the module name so a single agent can hold every node, queue, channel or virtual host. Resource suffixes are <label> - <node> for nodes, <label> - channel <name> for channels, <label> - vhost <name> for virtual hosts, <label> - connection <name> for connections, and <label> - ["<vhost>","<name>"] for queues and exchanges.

Toggle Modules it adds Overview modules Cluster name, RabbitMQ version, message totals and object totals Global message rates Global publish, deliver, get, ack, confirm and related rates Node modules Node status, memory and Erlang process metrics per node Node resource modules Limits, alarms, descriptors, sockets, uptime and run queue per node Node IO counters Read/write operation, byte and garbage-collection counters per node Queue modules Per-queue messages, consumers, memory, state and type Queue message rates Per-queue publish, deliver, ack and redeliver rates Exchange modules Aggregate exchange rates and per-exchange publish in/out rates Connection summary Connection totals and aggregate network rates Per connection modules Per-connection channels, network rates and state Channel modules Per-channel consumers, counters and rates Vhost modules Per-virtual-host message totals and rates

Module names are <Module prefix> plus the module name. The exhaustive inventory and the exact API field behind each module are in Generated modules and agents.

docs.title: RabbitMQ Dashboard
docs.text:
RabbitMQ Dashboard is a companion console extension that reads the agents marked with rabbitmq:agent: (and, as a fallback, agents named rabbitmq-) and their enabled modules, and presents them in one view. It appears in the Monitoring menu and requires the standard agent read permission.

The dashboard has three filters: Target (one agent or all), Section (one section or all) and Chart period for the history graph. The available sections are Overview, Message rates, Nodes, Exchanges, Connections, Queues, Channels, Vhosts and History.

  • Overview shows the cluster KPIs, the message backlog (ready versus unacknowledged) and the object totals. Message rates charts the global rates reported by the overview endpoint.

  • Nodes lists every node with its status, memory, process, disk, descriptor, socket, uptime, run queue and alarms. Exchanges lists the publish in/out rates and the busiest exchanges.

  • Connections shows the connection summary, the state breakdown and the per-connection detail. Queues lists every queue with its state, backlog, consumers, memory and type.

  • Channels and Vhosts list the per-resource consumers and message rates. History plots the key counters over the selected period.

When no RabbitMQ agent is found, the dashboard shows the message No RabbitMQ data found with the instruction to run the discovery task and verify that the agents and modules were created.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The plugin can run outside Discovery, from a Pandora FMS agent or directly from the command line, with a configuration file, a targets file and the optional module filter files:

./pandora_rabbitmq --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --targets-file <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --module-allow-list-file <PATH_TO_ALLOW> --module-deny-list-file <PATH_TO_DENY>

Only --conf and --targets-file are required. The plugin reads each target, collects the enabled metric groups and prints the Discovery JSON output with the agents and modules on standard output. See Configuration file and Command-line execution.

The targets file may embed a username and a password. Restrict it to the account that runs the plugin and keep it out of shared directories, logs and version control. When the credentials travel in command arguments, shell history and the process list may expose them; prefer the configuration file.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Check The agent is created but its Availability module reports 0 and the execution information logs a connection or timeout error Confirm the broker is reachable from the Pandora FMS server on its Management API port (default 15672 for HTTP), that the management plugin is enabled and that the target URL is correct. The execution information logs HTTP 401 The user or password is wrong, or the user cannot read the Management API. Review Default user and Default password, and the inline credentials of the target. The execution information logs HTTP 404 The URL does not point to the Management API of the broker. Check the host and port, and remove any /api suffix, which the plugin strips automatically. TLS certificate errors Set CA file to the PEM bundle that signs the broker certificate, or disable Verify TLS certificates only for trusted test environments. The queue or virtual host inventory is empty while the cluster overview works Enable Queue modules, Queue message rates, Channel modules or Vhost modules, and review Queue name regexp and Vhost name regexp: an empty value matches everything, a non-matching expression keeps nothing. Expected modules are missing Review the Metrics and module filters toggles and the Modules allow regexp / Modules deny regexp filters. The deny list is applied after the allow list. The dashboard shows No RabbitMQ data found Run the discovery task and confirm the plugin created agents marked rabbitmq:agent: (or named rabbitmq-), and that the console account can read them.

docs.text: The console presents the task fields in three steps after the generic task definition. The macro column is the identifier used in the generated task configuration.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The Discovery task builds a temporary --conf file from its own fields. A manual run supplies it directly. The file has a [CONF] section; a file without a section header is read as if it had one.

Key Default Description user Empty Default user for targets without their own credentials pass Empty Default password for targets without their own credentials timeout 10 Timeout of every HTTP request, in seconds retries 2 Retries for transient HTTP errors, between 0 and 5 verify_tls 1 Validates HTTPS certificates and hostnames ca_file Empty PEM CA bundle used for HTTPS targets task_id — Task identifier; used to derive the stable agent name. Required group_id 0 ID of the group where the agents are created. Must be positive interval 300 Monitoring interval in seconds, inherited by the agents agent_prefix Empty Prefix for the agent display alias module_prefix Empty Prefix for all module names agent_autodisable 0 Creates the agents in Pandora FMS mode 2 when enabled queue_filter Empty Queue name regular expression vhost_filter Empty Vhost regular expression for queues, exchanges and vhosts overview_enabled 1 Enables the overview modules message_rates_enabled 1 Enables the global message rates nodes_enabled 1 Enables the node modules node_resources_enabled 1 Enables the node resource modules node_io_enabled 0 Enables the node IO counters queues_enabled 0 Enables the queue modules queue_rates_enabled 0 Enables the queue message rates exchanges_enabled 1 Enables the exchange modules connections_enabled 1 Enables the connection summary connection_details_enabled 0 Enables the per-connection modules channels_enabled 0 Enables the channel modules vhosts_enabled 0 Enables the vhost modules module_allow_list Empty Inline allow regular expressions, one per line module_deny_list Empty Inline deny regular expressions, one per line

docs.title: Targets file
docs.text:
The --targets-file file holds the targets. It accepts a JSON array of target objects:

[
  {"url": "http://172.17.0.2:15672", "user": "monitor", "password": "<PASSWORD>", "alias": "RabbitMQ lab"},
  {"url": "https://rabbitmq-prod.internal.company.com", "user": "monitor", "password": "<PASSWORD>"}
]

or a plain list separated by commas or newlines, with lines starting by # ignored:

# Production cluster
http://172.17.0.2:15672
https://rabbitmq-prod.internal.company.com

Each URL is normalized before use: http:// is assumed when the scheme is missing, the port defaults to 443 for HTTPS and 15672 for HTTP, a trailing /api is removed, and embedded credentials, query strings and fragments are rejected. Duplicate normalized URLs are rejected, and every target requires a user, either inline or from the default.

docs.title: Module filter files
docs.text: --module-allow-list-file and --module-deny-list-file hold one regular expression per line, matched against the final module names (after the module prefix). A module is kept when it matches the allow list (or the allow list is empty) and does not match the deny list. The same expressions can be supplied inline through the module_allow_list and module_deny_list configuration keys instead.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
./pandora_rabbitmq --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --targets-file <PATH_TO_TARGETS> --module-allow-list-file <PATH_TO_ALLOW> --module-deny-list-file <PATH_TO_DENY>
Option Description --conf Path to the configuration file. Required in Discovery --targets-file Path to the file with the targets --module-allow-list-file Path to the file with the allow regular expressions --module-deny-list-file Path to the file with the deny regular expressions --host Single target URL, used when no targets file is given --user, --pass Default credentials --group-id, --interval Group ID and interval for the generated agents --task-id Task identifier used to derive the agent name --timeout, --retries, --ca-file HTTP and TLS options --agent-prefix, --module-prefix Alias and module prefixes --version Prints the plugin version

Example configuration file:

[CONF]
user=monitor
pass=<PASSWORD>
timeout=10
retries=2
verify_tls=1
task_id=manual
group_id=10
interval=300
overview_enabled=1
message_rates_enabled=1
nodes_enabled=1
node_resources_enabled=1
exchanges_enabled=1
connections_enabled=1

docs.title: Generated modules and agents
docs.text:
Module names are <Module prefix><module name>. Resource modules append - <resource> as described in Modules by agent.

Target agent (one per target)

Always created:

  • Availability: generic_proc, 1 when the cluster overview was read, 0 otherwise.

Created when the matching toggle is enabled:

  • Overview modules: Cluster name and RabbitMQ version (generic_data_string), Total queue messages, Messages ready, Messages unacknowledged, Overview connections, Total queues, Total exchanges, Total channels and Total consumers (generic_data).
  • Global message rates (per rate): Queue publish rate, Queue deliver get rate, Queue get rate, Queue deliver rate, Queue deliver no ack rate, Queue ack rate, Queue redeliver rate, Queue confirm rate, Queue return unroutable rate and Queue drop unroutable rate (generic_data).
  • Node modules (per node): Node status (generic_proc), Memory used, Memory rate, Proc used and Proc details (generic_data).
  • Node resource modules (per node): Memory limit, Disk free, Disk free limit, File descriptors used, File descriptors total, Sockets used, Sockets total, Proc total, Uptime ms and Run queue (generic_data), and Memory alarm and Disk alarm (generic_proc).
  • Node IO counters (per node): Io read count, Io write count, Io read bytes, Io write bytes, Gc num and Gc bytes reclaimed (generic_data_inc).
  • Queue modules (per queue): Messages, Messages ready, Messages unacknowledged, Consumers, Consumer capacity, Memory, Message bytes and Messages ram (generic_data), and State and Type (generic_data_string).
  • Queue message rates (per queue): Queue publish rate, Queue deliver get rate, Queue ack rate and Queue redeliver rate (generic_data).
  • Exchange modules: Exchanges in rate and Exchanges out rate (generic_data), plus Exchange publish in rate and Exchange publish out rate (generic_data) per exchange. The aggregate rates are created only when every exchange reports the underlying rate.
  • Connection summary: Total connections, Connections running, Connections blocked, Connections other, Total received octets rate and Total sent octets rate (generic_data).
  • Per connection modules (per connection): Channels, Received octets rate and Sent octets rate (generic_data), and State (generic_data_string).
  • Channel modules (per channel): Consumers, Messages unacknowledged, Messages unconfirmed and Prefetch count (generic_data), plus Channel publish rate, Channel deliver get rate, Channel ack rate and Channel redeliver rate (generic_data).
  • Vhost modules (per vhost): Messages, Messages ready and Messages unacknowledged (generic_data), plus Vhost publish rate, Vhost deliver get rate, Vhost ack rate and Vhost redeliver rate (generic_data).

docs.title: Redis Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The Redis Discovery addon monitors Redis instances. It connects to each instance you declare, reads its statistics and turns them into Pandora FMS modules: memory usage, connected clients, executed commands, persistence, replication, CPU, latency, keyspace and more. It can also run your own search queries against a Redis search index and publish each result as a module.

The addon creates one agent per Redis instance, so a single Discovery task can cover as many instances as you list in its connection strings.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon version 1.0 (pandorafms.redis) Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace carries a general banner for all its integrations, not a statement specific to this addon Network reachability from the Discovery server to every Redis instance Required The addon opens one connection per instance Redis search capability (FT.SEARCH) on the instance Required for custom queries only Prerequisite of the Custom queries feature, not a compatibility statement Any specific Redis release, edition or deployment mode Not validated No test record is available for a version matrix Host operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No host operating system has been recorded

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Network access from the Discovery server to each Redis host and port.
  2. A Redis account that can connect and read server information. When the instance uses ACLs, the user must be allowed to run at least PING and INFO. Custom queries additionally need permission to run the search command they use (FT.SEARCH).
  3. A Redis search index, only when you define custom queries. The index must already exist on the instance.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it.

Example of an ACL user that can run the base collection:

ACL SETUSER <USERNAME> on ><PASSWORD> ~* +info +ping

Typing a password in a command exposes it in the shell history. Prefer setting it from a protected configuration file or an interactive client session.

docs.title: Availability and license
docs.text: The Marketplace entry states that the download of this addon is limited to licensed users. The Marketplace lists version 1.0, last updated on 2026-01-12.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Load the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/

Once loaded, the Redis application is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Applications → Redis. The console presents the fields in three steps. Every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. Redis base — which instances to read and where to send the data:

    • Connection strings: one Redis connection per line. See Connection strings.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where the generated agent data is sent. They normally keep their default values.

  2. redis detailed — shape the result:

    • Max threads, module and agent prefixes, and the allow and deny regular expressions.
    • One switch per group of Redis statistics. All of them are enabled by default.

  3. redis custom — optional thresholds for the created modules and custom queries.

The task's own group and interval come from the generic task-definition step. They become the group and the interval of the created agents.

docs.title: Connection strings
docs.text:
Write one connection per line, as comma-separated key=value pairs. Add | followed by a name to choose the agent name:

host='<REDIS_HOST_1>', port=6379|<AGENT_NAME>
host='<REDIS_HOST_2>', port=6379
  • Quotes around text values are optional and removed. true and false are read as booleans and whole numbers as numbers.
  • The pairs are passed to the connection as they are and are not validated by the addon. The shipped examples use host and port only.
  • Do not use a comma inside a value, because the comma separates the pairs.
  • Agent name: when the line has no | <name> suffix, the agent is named redis_<host>, where <host> is the value of host (or unknown when the line has no host). Two instances on the same host without an explicit name would produce the same agent. Always give an explicit name when several instances share a host, and keep every name unique.
  • Lines that are empty or start with # or ; are ignored.

Connection strings may contain credentials. They are stored in the task definition; restrict who can edit Discovery tasks accordingly.

docs.title: Thresholds
docs.text:
Each line defines the thresholds of one module, or of every module whose name matches a regular expression:

<MODULE_NAME_OR_REGEXP> [<TYPE>] = <TAG> <VALUE>|<TAG> <VALUE>
  • <TYPE> is name (exact module name) or regexp (regular expression searched in the module name). Without a type, name is assumed.
  • Each <TAG> <VALUE> pair is two words separated by a space; pairs are separated by |. The shipped examples use min_warning and min_critical.
  • The match is made against the final module name, including the module prefix. With the prefix pre-, the line must read pre-used_memory [name] = ....
  • Only the first matching line applies to a module.
  • Lines starting with # or ; are comments. Every other line must contain =, otherwise the whole task fails with Error while reading configuration file.
pre-used_memory [name] = min_warning 75|min_critical 85
pre-used_cpu [regexp] = min_warning 50|min_critical 80

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text:
Each line defines one module whose value comes from a Redis search query:

<MODULE_NAME>|<MODULE_TYPE>|<INDEX>|<QUERY>|<FIELD>
Part Required Description <MODULE_NAME> Yes Name of the module. The module prefix is prepended <MODULE_TYPE> Yes Pandora FMS module type, for example generic_data_string. With generic_data, a value that is not a whole number falls back to generic_data_string <INDEX> Yes Name of an existing search index <QUERY> Yes Search query for that index <FIELD> No Key to extract from the result document. Applied only when the query returns exactly one document 
custom_module 1|generic_data_string|idx:users|Paul @age:[30 40]|name
custom_module 2|generic_data_string|idx:users|@city:{Tel Aviv}
  • A line with fewer than four parts is skipped silently, and a line cannot contain | inside the query.
  • When the query returns several documents, the value is the documents as text, one per line, and <FIELD> is ignored. When it returns none, the value is empty.
  • Custom queries create one module per query in every agent of the task, and are not affected by the allow and deny expressions.
  • A failing query is reported in the execution information as [ERROR] Query '<MODULE_NAME>' failed.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A completed task reports Total agents, the number of agents it created.

  2. The execution information. Failed connections and failed queries are listed here, for example [<AGENT_NAME>] Connection failed. A connection failure does not stop the other instances.

  3. The agents. One per connection string, named as described in Connection strings.
  4. The modules. Check for uptime_in_seconds (server), connected_clients (clients) and used_memory (memory), according to the enabled switches.

docs.title: Agents and modules generated
docs.text:
• Agent: one per connection string. The alias is the agent prefix plus the agent name; the internal agent name is derived from that alias, so changing the prefix or the name creates a new agent.
  • Modules: one per statistic returned by Redis, named <module prefix><statistic>, plus one per custom query. A numeric statistic becomes a generic_data module and any other becomes generic_data_string.
  • Not created: a statistic whose value is 0, empty, or a list does not produce a module. A counter that is 0 at the first run appears when it first has a value.
  • Filters: the allow and deny expressions are applied to the statistic name without the module prefix. The allow expression is evaluated first, then the deny expression.
  • A group of statistics is only read when its Scan switch is on, and the set of statistics inside a group depends on the Redis version and on the modules loaded in it.

docs.title: Statistics groups
docs.text:
Switch What it reads Scan server stats Server identity, process and uptime Scan clients stats Connected, blocked and tracking clients and client limits Scan memory stats Memory use, peaks, fragmentation, allocator and eviction policy Scan persistance stats Snapshot and append-only file state Scan threads stats Thread information Scan stats Connections, commands, network traffic, expirations, evictions and hit/miss counters Scan replication stats Role, replicas and replication backlog Scan CPU stats CPU time used by the server and its children Scan command stats Calls and time for each executed command (cmdstat_<command>) Scan latency stats Latency percentiles for each executed command Scan sentinel stats Sentinel information Scan cluster stats Whether cluster mode is enabled Scan modules stats Loaded modules and, with the search module, index statistics (search_*) Scan keyspace stats One entry per database (db0, db1, ...) Scan error stats Error counters (errorstat_<error>)

The Marketplace entry lists the statistic names produced by each group in a reference run. A group may hold fewer or more statistics on your Redis version. Command, latency, keyspace and error statistics carry the command, database or error name in the module name, and their value is a composite of several figures.

docs.title: Operate
docs.text:
The addon can be run by hand with the configuration file the Discovery task builds. This is the fastest way to test connections, queries and thresholds without a Discovery task.

./pandora_redis --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

--conf is the only parameter and is required. The run prints the Discovery summary (including Total agents) and sends the agent data with Tentacle.

[CONF]
threads = 1
prefix = pre-
prefix_agents =
agents_group = <GROUP_ID>
interval = 300
tentacle_ip = <TENTACLE_SERVER_IP>
tentacle_port = 41121
allow_regexp =
deny_regexp =
scan_server = 1
scan_clients = 1
scan_memory = 1

[CONNECTION_STRINGS]
host='<REDIS_HOST_1>', port=6379
host='<REDIS_HOST_2>', port=6379|<AGENT_NAME>

[THRESHOLDS]
pre-used_memory [name] = min_warning 75|min_critical 85

[QUERIES]
custom_module 1|generic_data_string|idx:users|Paul @age:[30 40]|name
  • The section is [THRESHOLDS]. A section named [UMBRALS] is ignored.
  • A scan_* key that is omitted is enabled. Set it to 0 to disable it.
  • Credentials in a configuration file need the same protection as the task definition. Restrict the file permissions.

Parallelism: Max threads limits how many Redis instances are processed at the same time. A higher value shortens the run and increases CPU use on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the execution information of the task.

Symptom or message Cause and action [<AGENT_NAME>] Connection failed. The instance did not answer PING. Check host, port, network path and credentials from the Discovery server. A failed instance creates no agent [ERROR] Can't create client / [ERROR] Can't obtain data The connection string could not be used or the information could not be read. Check the syntax and that the user may run INFO Error while reading configuration file A thresholds line lacks =, or another line of the generated file is malformed. Correct the thresholds [WARNING] The defined thresholds could not be parsed. Please check your syntax. The thresholds block was ignored. Review the format [WARNING] The defined queries could not be parsed. Please check your syntax. The queries block was ignored. Review the format [ERROR] Query '<MODULE_NAME>' failed: ... The index does not exist, the query is invalid, or the user cannot run the search command A query line produces no module It has fewer than four parts, or it is commented out Can't aplicate defined thresholds in modules. Check syntax Thresholds could not be applied. Review the syntax Thresholds are not applied The line does not match the final module name, which includes the module prefix Two instances produce one agent They share a name. Give each connection string a unique | <name> An expected module is missing Its statistic is 0 or empty, its group is disabled, or an allow/deny expression removed it Tokens_dict must be a non-empty dictionary Every Scan switch is disabled. Enable at least one

docs.title: SAP HANA Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The SAP HANA Discovery plugin connects to one or more SAP HANA databases, runs a set of SQL queries against the system views, and turns the results into Pandora FMS monitoring modules. Out of the box it covers availability, version, memory, connections, transactions, backup size estimation, I/O, CPU, license, row store fragmentation, volumes and per-service statistics. Each group is switched on or off from the task. You can add your own SQL-based modules on top.

The plugin creates one agent per SAP HANA target, with an availability module plus one module per enabled metric. A single Discovery task can list several targets, so one task covers a whole set of databases.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Add-on version 1.0 (pandorafms.sap.hana) Documented target Version published in the Marketplace entry, last updated 2026-06-11. See Plugin identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported Statement shown on the Marketplace for all its integrations SAP HANA SQL port reachable from the Discovery server Required The plugin opens one database connection per target A database user able to read the SYS monitoring views Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement. See Prerequisites Any specific SAP HANA release Not validated No release or edition matrix has been recorded

The add-on download is limited to licensed users, according to its Marketplace entry. This page does not describe any further license terms.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Network access from the machine that runs the Discovery task to the SQL port of every SAP HANA target.
  2. A database user and password for SAP HANA. The plugin runs only SELECT statements in its built-in checks, against these system views: SYS.M_DATABASE, SYS.M_HOST_RESOURCE_UTILIZATION, SYS.M_SERVICE_STATISTICS, SYS.M_CONNECTIONS, SYS.M_BLOCKED_TRANSACTIONS, SYS.M_TRANSACTIONS, SYS.M_VOLUMES, SYS.M_VOLUME_IO_TOTAL_STATISTICS, SYS.M_RS_MEMORY, SYS.M_CONVERTER_STATISTICS and SYS.M_LICENSE. It also reads the catalog views SYS.OBJECTS, SYS.VIEWS, SYS.TABLES, SYS.VIEW_COLUMNS and SYS.TABLE_COLUMNS to check which views and columns exist, and queries DUMMY for the timestamp and connection probes. The user must be able to read the views behind the groups you enable; no narrower privilege set is documented. A view the user cannot read produces a module with an empty value rather than a failure of the whole task.
  3. A Pandora FMS credential of type Custom in the credential store, holding that user and password. Both are required.
  4. Pandora FMS: a Discovery server to execute the task, and the console to define it.

The plugin is distributed as a self-contained package, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Load the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.sap.hana

Once loaded, the SAP HANA application is available when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Create the credential
docs.text:
1. In the Pandora FMS console, open the credential store and create a new credential of type Custom.
  2. Enter the SAP HANA user and password.
  3. Give it an identifier you will recognize when choosing it in the task.

The credential is stored in the console and referenced by the task, so the password is not written in the task fields.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from Management → Discovery → Application → SAP HANA. The console presents the fields in two steps, and every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. SAP HANA Base — the targets and how to authenticate:

    • SAP HANA target strings: one target per line, or several separated by commas, in the form HOST:PORT\DATABASE. Lines starting with # are comments. Each valid target generates one agent.
    • HANA Credentials: the Custom credential created above.

  2. SAP HANA Detailed — optional shaping of the result:

    • Max threads and Target agent.
    • Regexp to filter modules with Allow regexp, and Regexp to discard modules with Deny regexp.
    • One checkbox per built-in metric group. The defaults are listed in Task parameters.
    • Execute custom queries and Custom queries.
    • Custom module prefix.
    • Custom modules (legacy).

The task's own agent group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents and modules the plugin creates.

docs.title: Target string format
docs.text:
A target is written as HOST:PORT\DATABASE, for example:

<HANA_HOST_1>:<SQL_PORT>\<DATABASE_NAME>
<HANA_HOST_2>:<SQL_PORT>\<DATABASE_NAME>
# <HANA_HOST_3>:<SQL_PORT>\<DATABASE_NAME>
  • HOST may be a name or an IP address. A name must resolve from the Discovery server.
  • PORT is the numeric SQL port of the instance or database. It is required.
  • DATABASE is passed to SAP HANA as the database name to connect to.
  • A : is also accepted in place of \ before the database name.

A line that does not match this format is not monitored and is counted in Targets down. See Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Map targets to agent names
docs.text: By default each agent is named HOST - DATABASE. To choose the names yourself, fill Target agent with one agent name per line, in the same order as the target strings. Empty lines and lines starting with # are discarded from both lists, so names are assigned by position among the valid targets: a blank line does not leave that target with its default name, it shifts every name after it to the previous target. The name is used both as agent name and alias.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from Management → Discovery → Task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. The execution reports:

    • Total agents: agents generated by the task.
    • Targets up: targets the plugin connected to.
    • Targets down: targets that could not be monitored.

    Expect one agent per valid, reachable target. Each failed target adds a line to the execution information with its host, port, database and the reason.

  2. The agents. One per target, with the address set to the target host and the operating system field set to SAP HANA.

  3. The modules on each agent. With the default options a reachable target produces:

    Module Expected value hana_availability 1 — the plugin connected to the database version SAP HANA version string backups_estimated_size_bytes Estimated size in bytes connections_total, connections_running, connections_idle Connection counts memory_used_bytes, memory_allocation_limit_bytes Memory in bytes blocked_transactions, open_transactions Transaction counts

    Module names carry the Custom module prefix when one was set, and the regular expression filters can remove any module except hana_availability.

If the task reports no agents, check Targets down and the execution information, and work through Troubleshoot.

docs.title: Agents and modules generated
docs.text:
The plugin creates one agent per target string. The agent name and alias are HOST - DATABASE, or the name you supplied in Target agent. Two targets that resolve to the same name report to the same agent.

hana_availability is a generic_proc module with value 1 whenever the plugin connected to the target. It is always created for a reachable target and is not affected by the allow or deny expressions. A target that cannot be reached creates no agent and no 0 value: it is reported only in the execution information and in Targets down.

When a query fails or the view does not exist in that SAP HANA environment, the module is still created with an empty value. Metric modules otherwise are generic_data (numbers) or generic_data_string (text).

docs.title: Module groups
docs.text:
The groups below are switched by the task checkboxes. The exact modules of each group are listed in Agents and modules.

Group (checkbox) Default What it provides Enable Backups Size On Estimated backup size in bytes Enable Timestamp Off Current UTC timestamp of the database Enable Hana Version On SAP HANA version Enable Data Disk Information Off Number of volumes and of volume I/O entries Enable Hana Service Statistics Off Status, memory, CPU, requests and threads of each service Enable Hana CPU Time Off Aggregated CPU time of the services Enable Hana RS Fragmentation Off Row store fragmentation percentage Enable Hana License Off License records, expiration date and usage Enable Hana IO Stats Off Accumulated bytes read and written, and I/O time Enable Hana Get Stated Connections On Total, running and idle connections Enable Hana Memory On Memory used and allocation limit Enable Hana Transactions On Blocked and open transactions

docs.title: Custom queries
docs.text:
With Execute custom queries enabled, you can define extra modules as SQL queries in Custom queries. The task is delivered with a commented template of the format. Each module is a check_begin / check_end block, with one key value pair per line:

check_begin
name custom_running_connections
description Connections in RUNNING state
operation value
target SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SYS.M_CONNECTIONS WHERE CONNECTION_STATUS = 'RUNNING'
datatype generic_data
unit conns
check_end

check_begin
name custom_service_status
description Status of every service
operation full
target SELECT HOST, SERVICE_NAME, ACTIVE_STATUS FROM SYS.M_SERVICE_STATISTICS
datatype generic_data_string
check_end

These examples were checked against the plugin's parser; they were not executed against a live SAP HANA system.

Rules:

  • name, target and datatype are required in every block. A block without them is ignored.
  • target must be on a single line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped.
  • operation value (default) takes the first column of the first row. If the query returns no rows or a null, the value is 0. operation full returns every row, columns joined by ; and rows by line breaks, as text: a datatype of generic_data is converted to generic_data_string.
  • $__self_dbname in the query is replaced by the database name of the target being queried.
  • By default a block runs on every target. Limit it with target_instances (comma-separated HOST:PORT values, written exactly as in the target string), target_databases, and ignore_databases. target_scope selects which of these filters apply: instances applies only the instance filter, databases applies only the database filters, and all (default) applies both.
  • A failed query still creates the module, with an empty value.
  • Custom modules are subject to Custom module prefix and to the allow and deny expressions.

The template also lists the keys min_warning, max_warning, min_critical, max_critical, inverse_warning, inverse_critical, str_warning, str_critical, interval and parent. The current version reads them but does not apply them to the created modules, so configure thresholds and intervals on the modules afterwards from the console.

docs.title: Legacy custom modules
docs.text:
Custom modules (legacy) accepts one module per line in the format:

module_name:SQL_query:datatype:description

datatype must be generic_data, generic_data_string or generic_proc; description is optional. The query may itself contain : characters. These modules are created even when Execute custom queries is disabled. Use custom queries for new definitions.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The Max threads value is accepted by the task but does not change how the targets are processed in this version: targets are queried one after another.
  • The connection uses the database user and password from the credential. The plugin has no field to select encryption options.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The plugin has no debug option in the task. Its diagnostic channel is the execution summary and the execution information of the Discovery task.

  • Missing required parameters — the credential has no user or no password, or the target list is empty after removing comments. The summary shows which of them is missing.
  • No agents generated — no target could be monitored. Read the Target down lines in the execution information.
  • Target down HOST:PORT\DATABASE - Cannot resolve hostname — the Discovery server cannot resolve the name. Use an IP address or fix the DNS resolution.
  • Target down ... - SAP HANA connection failed: ... — the database refused the connection or the credentials. Check the port, the database name, the user and the password, and that the Discovery server reaches the SQL port.
  • Targets down is greater than the failures listed — a line that does not follow HOST:PORT\DATABASE is counted as down without a message. Check the format of every target string.
  • A module exists with an empty value — the query behind it failed or the view is not available in that SAP HANA environment, for example because the user cannot read it. Run the same SELECT with that user to see the database error.
  • Expected modules are missing — a Allow regexp or Deny regexp removed them. The expressions are matched anywhere in the module name (including the prefix), and an invalid expression is ignored silently.
  • Metrics from another group do not appear — only the groups with their checkbox enabled create modules. See Module groups.

docs.title: SAP HANA Base
