docs.title: XenServer Discovery
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it monitors
docs.text:
The XenServer Discovery addon monitors the hosts, storage repositories and virtual machines of a XenServer environment. A Discovery task connects to one XenServer, reads its inventory and performance data through the XenAPI and the server RRD data, and creates Pandora FMS agents and modules from the result.

A Discovery task generates three kinds of agents:

  • One agent per host, with the number of running and installed virtual machines, memory usage and average CPU load.
  • One agent per virtual machine, with its power state, memory usage, per-CPU load, guest tools status and per-disk size and throughput. The virtual machine agent is a child of the agent of the host that runs it.
  • One agent per storage repository (SR), with its physical size, used space, free space and used percentage.

The task decides which of the three kinds are scanned, and hosts, virtual machines and storage repositories can be excluded or renamed by name.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.xenserver, version 1.3 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity XenServer 6.2 or later Required Prerequisite stated by the Marketplace entry; no test record is available for this version Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Stated by the Marketplace General notice shown on the Marketplace for all entries, not specific to this addon Operating system of the Discovery server Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Specific XenServer releases Not validated No test matrix has been recorded for this version

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. A XenServer host reachable from the Discovery server, with TCP port 80 open for the RRD queries and the connection to the XenAPI. The Marketplace entry also lists TCP port 443 for the XenAPI queries.
  2. XenServer credentials (user and password) able to query the XenAPI. No narrower set of roles or permissions is documented for this addon.
  3. Pandora FMS: the Discovery server to run the task and the console to define it. Generated agents are sent with Tentacle.
  4. Guest tools installed on the virtual machines. Without them the guest information is limited: the virtual machine agent does not get the IP address of the guest and the XenServer tools module reports 0.

Warning

The addon connects to the XenServer with HTTP URLs and sends the user and password in the HTTP basic authentication of the RRD requests. Run it only from a network you trust and use credentials dedicated to monitoring.

The addon ships its own executable, bin/pandora_xenserver, so nothing else has to be installed on the Discovery server to run a task.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .disco package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.xenserver

Load it into Pandora FMS. Once loaded, XenServer is available in the Applications section when creating Discovery tasks.

docs.title: Configure the Discovery task
docs.text:
Create the task from the Discovery applications and choose XenServer. The console presents the fields in two steps; every field is documented in Task parameters.

  1. XenServer base — connection and data delivery:

    • XenServer IP, XenServer user and Password: address and credentials of the XenServer to monitor.
    • ID as Name: use the SR identifier (UUID) as the name of the storage repository agents. The alias remains the SR name.
    • Tentacle IP, Tentacle port and Tentacle extra options: where and how the generated agent data is sent. They rarely need changing.

  2. XenServer detailed — scope and tuning:

    • Autodisabled agents: create the agents in autodisabled mode.
    • Time adjustment: seconds subtracted from the current time to set the start of the RRD query window.
    • Scan VM IP, Scan all Hosts, Scan all VM and Scan all SR: which data the task collects.
    • Extra settings: optional block added as is to the end of the plugin configuration. Use it for the REJECT and RENAME sections described in Exclude and rename elements.

The task's group and interval come from the generic task-definition step and are applied to the agents the task creates.

docs.title: Verify the first run
docs.text:
Force the task from the Discovery task list and check the result in this order.

  1. The task summary. A task that completes successfully reports:

    • Hosts: hosts monitored.
    • Storage: storage repositories monitored.
    • VMs: virtual machines monitored, excluding templates, snapshots and control domains. A control domain is the special virtual machine that manages each host.
    • Hosts VMs running: running virtual machines on the monitored hosts, excluding control domains. It is counted while scanning hosts, so it is 0 when Scan all Hosts is disabled.

    A task that does not complete successfully records the errors in its execution information instead.

  2. The agents. One per host, one per virtual machine and one per storage repository, according to the enabled scan options.

  3. The modules. Every virtual machine agent has Status, Memory used and XenServer tools. CPU and disk throughput modules appear only on running virtual machines; see Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Agent Name and alias Parent Notes Host The host name None Address is the host address. Operating system Xen Server, version is the product brand and version reported by the host Virtual machine The virtual machine name The host that runs it, empty when the machine is not resident on a host Address is the list of guest IP addresses, comma separated, when Scan VM IP is enabled and the guest reports them Storage repository Name: the SR UUID when ID as Name is enabled, otherwise the SR name. Alias: always the SR name None The description lists the hosts and the device or location of the repository

In host and virtual machine agent names the character / is replaced with _; storage repository agent names are left unchanged. Templates, snapshots and control domains are never monitored as virtual machines. Storage repositories whose name contains XenServer Tools or whose physical size is 0 produce no agent.

docs.title: Modules per agent
docs.text:
Host agent

Module Type Unit Description VMs running generic_data Running virtual machines, excluding the control domain VMs installed generic_data Virtual machines resident on the host, including the control domain Memory used generic_data % Percentage of RAM in use Load CPU avg generic_data % Average CPU load

Virtual machine agent

Module Type Unit Condition Description Status generic_proc Always 1 when the machine is Running, 0 otherwise. The description carries the power state Memory used generic_data % Always Percentage of RAM in use; 0.0 when the machine is not running cpu<N> generic_data % Running Load of each virtual CPU XenServer tools generic_proc Always 1 when the guest reports installed tools, 0 otherwise VDI_<disk name>_size generic_data GB One per attached disk Size of the disk as presented to the guest VDI_<disk name>_used generic_data % One per attached disk Percentage of the disk size that the image occupies in the storage repository, capped at 100. Thick-provisioned disks always report 100 vbd_<device>_write, vbd_<device>_read generic_data bytes/sec Running Disk write and read rate of each virtual block device

Storage repository agent

Module Type Unit Description physical_size generic_data GB Physical size of the repository physical_utilisation generic_data GB Physical space in use free space generic_data GB Free space, as a whole number of GB used percent generic_data % Percentage of the repository in use

docs.title: How the values are obtained
docs.text:
• Inventory data comes from the XenAPI. Memory, CPU and disk throughput come from the RRD data of the XenServer, queried from the moment set by Time adjustment (default 10 seconds before the execution).
  • Each execution creates the data of every selected element again; newly added hosts, virtual machines and storage repositories are included on the next run without changing the task.

docs.title: Exclude and rename elements
docs.text:
Put these sections in Extra settings (or in the configuration file for manual execution). Names are the host, virtual machine or storage repository names; a name that contains / is written with _ instead.

[REJECT]
<ELEMENT_NAME> = 1
regexp_host = <REGEX>
regexp_vm = <REGEX>
regexp_sr = <REGEX>

[RENAME]
<ELEMENT_NAME> = <NEW_NAME>
  • <ELEMENT_NAME> = 1 excludes that host, virtual machine or storage repository. For a storage repository the name is its SR name, not its UUID.
  • regexp_host, regexp_vm and regexp_sr exclude every element whose name matches the regular expression from the start of the name. For storage repositories the expression is matched against the agent name, so against the UUID when ID as Name is enabled.
  • RENAME changes the agent name. For hosts and virtual machines it changes the alias too; storage repositories keep their SR name as alias.

docs.title: Manual execution
docs.text:
The addon can run outside a Discovery task. The executable takes the path to a configuration file described in Configuration file:

./pandora_xenserver --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

Add --as_discovery_plugin 1 to print the execution summary as JSON instead of a status module:

./pandora_xenserver --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --as_discovery_plugin 1

{"summary": {"Hosts": 1, "Storage": 7, "VMs": 23, "Hosts VMs running": 10}}

When errors occur, the JSON also contains an info key with the messages and the exit code is 1. Without --as_discovery_plugin 1, a successful run prints a status module:

<module>
<name><![CDATA[XenServer Plugin]]></name>
<type><![CDATA[async_string]]></type>
<description><![CDATA[Result of XenServer Plugin execution]]></description>
<data><![CDATA[OK]]></data>
</module>

In local transfer mode the data files are moved to data_dir. In tentacle mode the tentacle_client executable must be available in the PATH of the user running the addon.

The interval of the configuration file is the interval of the generated agents. It must match the execution interval of the plugin; otherwise the modules turn unknown when an agent expects data before the next execution.

The configuration file contains the XenServer password in plain text. Protect it with restrictive permissions.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
The addon has no verbose or debug flag. Its diagnostic channel is the info field of the JSON execution result, which is shown in the task's execution information, and the log file set by logfile in manual execution.

  • CRITICAL: Cant get XenServer session or CRITICAL: Cant login to XenServer: the connection or the login failed. The message includes the error returned. Check XenServer IP, the credentials and that port 80 is reachable from the Discovery server.
  • ERROR - Could not write file: the directory for the temporary data files is not writable.
  • Tentacle error: the data file could not be sent. The message includes the error of the Tentacle client; check Tentacle IP and Tentacle port.
  • A virtual machine agent has no IP address: Scan VM IP is disabled, or the guest does not report addresses because the guest tools are not installed.
  • No cpu<N> or vbd_ modules on a virtual machine: the machine is not running.
  • A storage repository has no agent: its physical size is 0, its name contains XenServer Tools, Scan all SR is disabled or it matches a REJECT rule.
  • Fewer agents than expected: check which of Scan all Hosts, Scan all VM and Scan all SR are enabled, and the REJECT rules.

docs.title: XenServer base
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes XenServer IP _serverIP_ string — Address of the XenServer XenServer user _user_ string — User of the XenServer Password _password_ password — Password of the user ID as Name _idAsName_ checkbox on SR UUID as the storage repository agent name Tentacle IP _tentacleIP_ string 127.0.0.1 Server that receives the agent data Tentacle port _tentaclePort_ number 41121 Tentacle port Tentacle extra options _tentacleExtraOpt_ string — Optional. Extra Tentacle client options

docs.title: XenServer detailed
docs.text: Field Macro Type Default Notes Autodisabled agents _autodisabledAgents_ checkbox off Creates the agents in autodisabled mode Time adjustment _timeAdjustment_ number 10 Optional. Seconds subtracted from the current time to set the start of the RRD query window Scan VM IP _scanVMIP_ checkbox on Read the IP addresses of the virtual machines Scan all Hosts _scanAllHosts_ checkbox on Create host agents Scan all VM _scanAllVM_ checkbox on Create virtual machine agents Scan all SR _scanAllSR_ checkbox on Create storage repository agents Extra settings _extraSettings_ text area — Optional. Raw block added to the end of the plugin configuration

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Used by manual execution. The Discovery task generates the same file from its fields, with transfer_mode = tentacle, the task group and interval, and data_dir set by the Discovery server. All keys of CONF and PANDORA except id_as_name and autodisabled_agents are required; the keys of TUNNING and REJECT are optional. Numeric options accept 1 to enable and 0 to disable.

Section Key Default Description CONF xen_server_ip — Address of the XenServer CONF user — XenServer user CONF password — XenServer password CONF temporal — Directory for temporary files PANDORA group — Group of the generated agents PANDORA logfile — Log file. It is overwritten on every execution PANDORA interval — Agent interval, in seconds. Must match the execution interval PANDORA transfer_mode — local moves the data files to data_dir; any other value sends them with Tentacle PANDORA tentacle_client — Tentacle client executable. This version reads the value but does not use it: the command always runs tentacle_client from the PATH of the Discovery server PANDORA tentacle_ip — Tentacle server address PANDORA tentacle_port — Tentacle server port PANDORA tentacle_opts — Extra Tentacle client options; may be empty PANDORA data_dir — Destination of the data files in local mode PANDORA id_as_name 1 SR UUID as storage repository agent name PANDORA autodisabled_agents 0 Autodisabled mode TUNNING time_adjustment 10 Seconds subtracted from the current time to set the start of the RRD query window TUNNING scan_vm_ip 1 Read virtual machine IP addresses TUNNING scan_all_host 1 Create host agents TUNNING scan_all_vm 1 Create virtual machine agents TUNNING scan_all_sr 1 Create storage repository agents REJECT, RENAME See Exclude and rename elements

Example:

[CONF]
xen_server_ip = <XENSERVER_IP>
user = <USERNAME>
password = <PASSWORD>
temporal = /tmp

[PANDORA]
group = Unknown
logfile = /tmp/pandora_xenserver.log
interval = 300
transfer_mode = tentacle
tentacle_client = tentacle_client
tentacle_ip = <TENTACLE_SERVER_IP>
tentacle_port = 41121
tentacle_opts =
data_dir = /tmp/data_in
id_as_name = 1

[TUNNING]
time_adjustment = 10
scan_vm_ip = 1
scan_all_vm = 1
scan_all_sr = 1
scan_all_host = 1

[REJECT]
<VM_NAME> = 1

[RENAME]
<VM_NAME_2> = <NEW_NAME>

docs.title: How to document
docs.text: Reference for anyone writing or migrating documentation into this site: where new content goes, what each page type must cover, and the mechanics of adding pages, sections, and images.

docs.title: How to contribute
docs.text:
All the documentation lives in the plugin-docs repository. To contribute:

  1. Make your changes in a branch (or fork) and open a pull request (PR) against the repository. The PR form is pre-filled from the repository's PR template (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md): type of change, affected section, language coverage, and local build verification.
  2. An administrator verifies the PR and, once everything checks out, approves and merges it.

The official documentation is published at https://pandorafms.com/docs/integrations/ and is synchronized periodically with the main branch of the repository, so merged changes reach the live site automatically.

docs.title: Where does new content go?
docs.text:
Section What belongs here Example Discovery Plugins that integrate with Pandora's Discovery task wizard: the console creates a task, runs the plugin, and auto-generates agents/modules from its output. NGINX, Playwright Integrations Connectors to external communication/collaboration tools, used mainly for alerting (the "send a Pandora alert to X" pattern: configure the external service, then create a Pandora alert command/action). Telegram, Google Chat, Microsoft Teams Plugins Standalone/manual plugins that are not driven by the Discovery wizard — run manually or wired as a regular server plugin, without auto-generated Discovery tasks. Oculix, Logparser (Advanced Log Parser) Extras Meta content about the site itself: this page, contributor notes, anything that isn't product documentation. This page

If a plugin could arguably fit two sections (e.g. it has both a Discovery task and a manual CLI mode), classify it by its primary, documented usage path — don't duplicate the same content in two sections.

docs.title: Required sections per content type
docs.text: Every page starts with a single # Title (this becomes both the sidebar label and the page <title>), followed by the article's last-updated line and the sections below.

docs.title: The reading order is a contract
docs.text:
Whatever the content type, a page walks the reader through the same journey:

Overview → Prepare → Configure → Verify → Understand → Troubleshoot → Reference

The point is progressive disclosure: the reader has to be able to install, configure and confirm the integration before meeting exhaustive detail. The exhaustive parameter reference goes at the end — it is what a reader comes back to, not what they read first.

Three rules follow from that:

  • Never reorder the stages to fit the content you already have. When you update or migrate an existing page, realign it to this order; do not inherit the order of the older page.
  • Omit a stage that does not apply instead of emitting an empty heading. What is flexible is which stages appear and what you call them — never the order of the ones that do.
  • English and Spanish must use the same section order. If the existing pair diverges, align both in the same change.

If a section fits none of the stages, or you cannot tell where it goes, ask before publishing. Do not invent a position, do not drop the section, and do not leave it where the old page happened to have it.

docs.title: Discovery plugins
docs.text:
1. Overview / What it monitors — the target, what is collected, what the plugin produces, and the Discovery task model.
  2. Prepare — validated environment and compatibility, prerequisites, permissions, target-side setup, and installation.
  3. Configure the Discovery task — the wizard fields and task behaviour, with screenshots where they remove real ambiguity.
  4. Verify — a successful run, the task summary, the expected agents and representative modules.
  5. Understand the results — agent identity and cardinality, plus a functional summary of the module groups.
  6. Troubleshoot — evidenced failure signals and diagnostics.
  7. Reference — exhaustive parameters, grouped by input surface (console, configuration file, CLI, environment), and the full module inventory.

Add an Operate stage before Troubleshoot when the plugin has a real day-to-day surface — manual execution, timeouts, debug modes, custom runtimes. The Playwright page is the worked example.

Put a short functional summary before any long inventory, and group a large reference by resource, generated agent, or condition.

docs.title: Plugins (agent, server or standalone)
docs.text:
Same journey, with the integration path as the variable:

  1. Overview / What it does — purpose, execution model, input, output.
  2. Prepare — prerequisites, installation, dependencies, permissions, compatibility.
  3. Configure — the agent configuration, the server plugin registration and module setup, or the standalone configuration, whichever the plugin actually supports.
  4. Verify — expected output, a successful execution, and ingestion into Pandora FMS where applicable.
  5. Understand the results — functional summary first, detailed output later.
  6. Operate and troubleshoot — manual execution, verbose mode, limitations, diagnostics.
  7. Reference — parameters by surface and exhaustive outputs.

Do not write a separate template per plugin subtype, and do not let a documented manual run imply agent- or server-plugin support.

docs.title: Integrations (notifications and external services)
docs.text:
1. Overview / What it does — the destination, what is sent, and the outcome for the operator.
  2. Prepare the external service — the steps performed in the external tool (create a bot, a webhook, a channel...), with screenshots. Usually the bulk of the page. Omit it for built-in workflows that need nothing there.
  3. Configure Pandora FMS — the built-in integration, or the alert command and the alert action that uses it, with console screenshots.
  4. Verify — a safe test procedure and the expected result at both ends.
  5. Understand the integration — verified flow, payload behaviour or delivery constraints, when they help.
  6. Troubleshoot — evidenced errors, logs and recovery checks.
  7. Reference — parameters by surface and any relevant limits.

docs.title: Adding a page to an existing section
docs.text:
1. Create a markdown file under docs/en/<section>/<page>.md (and its docs/es/<section>/<page>.md translation, if ready).
  2. Start the file with a # Title — that's what shows up in the sidebar, not the filename.
  3. Commit and push. The sidebar picks it up automatically, no mkdocs.yml edit needed.

docs.title: Adding a new section or page
docs.text:
The top-level sections are Plugins, Integrations, Discovery, and Extras (docs/en/plugins/, docs/en/integrations/, docs/en/discovery/, docs/en/extras/ — mirrored under docs/es/). The sidebar is generated from this folder structure by mkdocs-awesome-pages-plugin — there's no nav: list to maintain by hand for individual pages.

Top-level section order, however, needs a bit more than a .pages file: mkdocs-static-i18n always alpha-sorts the top-level nav when it builds each language's tree, which would silently undo any custom order set via .pages. hooks.py (registered in mkdocs.yml's hooks: key) runs after that sort and pins specific section titles to the end — currently just Extras. Any other top-level section is left in whatever order mkdocs-static-i18n alphabetized it into; if you need a different fixed position for a new section, add its title to PINNED_LAST in hooks.py (order in that list is the order they'll appear in, all pinned after the alphabetized ones).

To add a new top-level section (e.g. "Dashboards"):

  1. Create docs/en/dashboards/ (and docs/es/dashboards/).
  2. Add a .pages file inside it to set the section title: 
    title: Dashboards
  3. Add at least one .md page inside the new folder.
  4. It will appear in the sidebar automatically, alphabetized among the other non-pinned sections. No .pages or hooks.py edit required unless you specifically need it pinned to a fixed position (see above).

To add a subcategory inside an existing section (e.g. group plugins by "Monitoring" / "Network"), just nest another folder with its own .pages:

docs/en/plugins/
  example.md
  monitoring/
    .pages           # title: Monitoring
    cpu.md
    memory.md

No depth limit — folders inside folders become nested sidebar sections.

docs.title: Menu translations
docs.text: Nothing needs to be translated besides the content: the title shown in the menu is each page's # H1, so it's enough for docs/es/<section>/<page>.md to have its own Spanish title. Section .pages files (title:) are translated the same way, by duplicating the file under docs/es/ with the corresponding text.

docs.title: Adding an image
docs.text:
Images live under docs/<lang>/assets/images/<section>/<plugin-slug>/, one subfolder per plugin/integration — never loose in assets/images/ directly. This keeps screenshots from different plugins from colliding on filenames (BookStack exports things like image.png or nU2image.png, which are not unique across plugins) and makes it obvious what a folder belongs to.

Example, following the pattern already used by the Telegram integration:

docs/en/assets/images/integrations/telegram/
  nU2image.png
  Qe2image.png
  ...
docs/es/assets/images/integrations/telegram/
  Milimage.png        # ES-only image (see fallback note below)
  1. Create docs/<lang>/assets/images/<section>/<plugin-slug>/ (matching the page's section — plugins, integrations, or discovery) and drop the file there (git add or the GitLab/GitHub Web IDE drag & drop).
  2. Reference it from markdown with a path relative to the current page. From a page inside a section folder (the common case, e.g. integrations/telegram.md), that's ../assets/images/<section>/<plugin-slug>/my-file.png. From a root-level page like index.md (no section folder), drop the leading ../.
  3. Per-language images: if a screenshot only differs from the other language's version (e.g. because it shows localized UI text), add it under docs/es/assets/images/<section>/<plugin-slug>/ with the same filename to override it — fallback_to_default: true means any file not overridden there is served automatically from the en folder, so you only need to add the images that actually differ.
  4. Images are centered and open in a lightbox on click automatically (mkdocs-glightbox + the centering rule in stylesheets/extra.css) — no extra markup needed, a plain ![alt](path) is enough.

docs.title: Local preview
docs.text:
Python:

python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve

Docker (no local Python needed):

UID=$(id -u) GID=$(id -g) docker compose up

Both open http://localhost:8000 with live reload — edits to any .md or image refresh the browser automatically.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Run the automated checks before opening a pull request:

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_validate_docs.py'
python3 scripts/validate_docs.py --fail-on blocking
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict

Blocking gates cover language path parity, one real H1 per page, existing local images with Spanish-to-English fallback, and high-confidence secret signatures. The validator also reports local link and anchor problems, cross-language links, legacy URLs, pending markers, rendered PandoraFMS usage, and known content contamination signatures. Report-only findings remain visible but do not fail the default command. Use --fail-on all to treat every finding as a local failure.

A browser preview is useful for visual review, but it does not replace these checks.

docs.title: Discord integration
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
This integration posts Pandora FMS alerts to a Discord text channel through a channel webhook. Each alert becomes one Discord message: an embed with a title, a description, one field for every key=value pair you pass, and optionally a thumbnail, a footer and an attached module graph.

The connector is distributed with Pandora FMS; there is no Marketplace entry and no console component of its own. It is an external command launched by a standard Pandora FMS alert command, so the Pandora FMS side of the integration is the alert command plus the alert action that stores the webhook URL. A run creates no agent, generates no module and keeps no state: it posts once and exits.

The destination is a webhook, not a bot. The connector writes to one channel and reads nothing back from Discord.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Discord connector distributed with Pandora FMS Documented target Connector this page describes. It has no Marketplace entry and declares no version. See Connector identity A Discord text channel with a channel webhook Required Every run posts to one webhook URL HTTPS access from the host that runs the connector to discord.com (TCP 443) Required The alert is delivered as an HTTPS POST to the webhook URL A python3 interpreter and the libraries declared in the connector's requirements.txt Required The bundled command definition invokes python3 pandora_discord_cli.py, and the connector loads those libraries at start-up Pandora FMS release Not validated No release-specific validation record exists for this connector Discord API version Not validated No version of the Discord webhook API has been recorded for this connector Operating system of the Pandora FMS server Not validated No operating system is recorded for this connector

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Discord account that can manage webhooks in the target channel: the Manage Webhooks permission on that channel.
  2. A text channel to receive the alerts. A dedicated channel keeps alert traffic apart and lets you restrict who reads it.
  3. Network access from the host that runs the connector to discord.com on TCP 443.
  4. The connector directory on the Pandora FMS server, with its libraries installed, readable and executable by the user the Pandora FMS server runs as.
  5. The webhook URL, kept as a secret (see Create the webhook).

docs.title: Create the webhook
docs.text:
Create one webhook for the channel that will receive the alerts:

  1. Open the target text channel and its settings.
  2. Open Integrations and create a webhook for that channel.
  3. Give it a name and, optionally, an avatar. This is the identity channel members see as the sender of every alert.
  4. Copy the webhook URL and save the webhook.

The URL has the shape https://discord.com/api/webhooks/<WEBHOOK_ID>/<WEBHOOK_TOKEN> and is the only credential the connector uses: posting needs no other authentication. Anyone who holds that URL can post to the channel, so treat it as a secret and create a new webhook if it leaks. Deleting the webhook in Discord invalidates the URL immediately.

A webhook is not a bot: it can post into its own channel and nothing else. It cannot read messages, list channels or react.

docs.title: Install the connector
docs.text:
Unzip the connector package on the Pandora FMS server. The command definition shipped with the package expects it under /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora-discord, and the examples in this page use that path; any other directory works as long as the Pandora FMS server can read and execute it. Install its libraries from that directory:

cd /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora-discord
pip3 install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Create the alert command
docs.text:
Go to Alerts → Commands → Create. The command is a free-text shell command, and the console replaces _field1_ … _field20_ with the alert values before running it. Paste the definition included in the connector's test-exec.txt file:

python3 /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora-discord/pandora_discord_cli.py -u "_field1_" -d "_field2_" -D "_field3_" --tittle_color _field4_ --thumb _field5_ --api_conf "_field6_" --module_graph "_field7_" -A "Pandora FMS Alert system" --footer "PandoraFMS" --author_icon_url "https://pandorafms.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/software-de-monitorizacion-pandorafms-logo.png" --author_url https://pandorafms.com/ --tmp_dir /tmp

The command uses seven fields. Describe each one in the command: the description is the label the alert action shows next to the field.

Field Value at run time Hide _field1_ Discord webhook URL Yes _field2_ Alert data as comma-separated key=value pairs No _field3_ Embed description (-D) No _field4_ Embed title colour: six hexadecimal digits (-T) No _field5_ Thumbnail URL (--thumb) No _field6_ Console API settings used to build the module graph (--api_conf) Yes _field7_ Module graph settings (--module_graph) No

Tick Hide on Field 1 so the webhook URL is masked when the action is edited, and on Field 6 as well if you put console credentials there. The hidden flag only masks the value on screen; it does not encrypt anything.

The form shows as many field rows as the console setting max_macro_fields allows (10 by default, 20 at most). This command needs seven. The form also has a Field N values column: those values are ignored for this command, because what the connector receives comes from the alert action.

The remaining options of the line (author, footer, author icon and link, temporary directory) are constants of the command. Edit the command line if you need other values.

Save the command with a name and a group.

docs.title: Create the alert action
docs.text:
Go to Alerts → Actions → Create and select the command you just created. The form shows one pair of values per field the command declares. Fill the triggering values:

Field Example Field 1 <DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL> Field 2 Agent=_agent_,Module=_module_,Status=_alert_text_severity_,Data=_data_,Timestamp=_timestamp_ Field 3 Alert on _agent_ Field 4 ed2512 Field 5 Do not fill it if you do not want a thumbnail Field 6 user=<USERNAME>,pass=<PASSWORD>,api_pass=<API_TOKEN>,api_url=<PANDORA_FMS_URL>/pandora_console/include/api.php Field 7 module_id=_id_module_,interval=3600

Field 2 is the payload of the alert: every pair becomes one field of the embed. The console expands alert macros inside every field value, so _agent_, _module_, _data_, _alert_text_severity_ and _timestamp_ are replaced with the values of the alert that fired.

Field 4 has no usable default through this command: the command passes its value even when the field is empty, and an empty value stops the run with an error before anything is sent. Use six hexadecimal digits without #; the three-digit shorthand is read as a different colour.

Leave Field 5 empty unless you want a thumbnail. Leave Fields 6 and 7 empty if you do not want the module graph.

Set a recovery value for Field 2 if you want a different payload for recovery events. When a recovery field is left empty, the console prefixes [RECOVER] to the value of fields 2 to 20, so the first pair of the data string arrives as [RECOVER]Agent.

docs.title: Apply the action
docs.text: Give the action a name and a group, then save it with Create. To make it fire, attach it through an alert template to the modules or the policy you want to monitor, or add it to the alerts of a module.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
1. Run the connector by hand from the Pandora FMS server, without the graph:
python3 /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora-discord/pandora_discord_cli.py \
  -u "<DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL>" \
  -d "Agent=<AGENT_NAME>,Module=<MODULE_NAME>,Status=CRITICAL,Data=22"

Expected output:

To get graph data api conf shoul be provided please set an api config
Error status code: 204

The first line is printed on every run that does not pass --api_conf. The second line reports the HTTP status Discord answered: Message sent. status code: 200 when it answered 200, and Error status code: <code> for any other status. Discord accepts a webhook post with 204 No Content, so an accepted message normally prints the Error status code: 204 form. Confirm the message in the channel.

  1. Open the Discord channel. The message comes from the webhook identity, with an embed titled Pandora FMS alert fired, the description alert, the four fields of the data string and a timestamp with the run time.
  1. Trigger the alert from Pandora FMS: force the module into the state the action watches, or use the alert template where you attached the action, and confirm that the same message reaches the channel.

docs.title: How an alert reaches Discord
docs.text:
1. The alert fires and the console builds the command, replacing each _fieldN_ with the value of the same field in the alert action, after expanding the alert macros inside it.
  2. The Pandora FMS server runs the resulting command with the user it runs as.
  3. The connector builds one webhook message and posts it once to the URL.
  4. Discord publishes the message in the channel with the identity of the webhook.
  5. The connector prints the status line and exits.

docs.title: Where each option lands
docs.text:
Part of the message Set by Sender name and avatar The webhook configuration in Discord. --avatar_url overrides the avatar for that message Plain text above the embed -m, --message. Empty by default Embed title -t, --alert_tittle. Default PandoraFMS alert fired Embed description -D, --alert_desc. Default alert Embed colour bar -T, --tittle_color. Default 53e514 Embed author line -A, --author, with --author_url and --author_icon_url Thumbnail --thumb. Omitted when empty Footer -F, --footer. Omitted when empty Timestamp Always the moment of the run. There is no option Fields One per key=value pair of -d, in the order you write them Image The module graph, when --api_conf and --module_graph are both set

The embed author is not the sender. The sender is the webhook identity in Discord; -A only fills the author line inside the embed.

docs.title: How data is parsed
docs.text:
-d is split on commas, and each piece on the equals sign, with spaces trimmed around the key and the value.

  • A piece without an equals sign stops the parse: the run prints Warning, error parsing keypairs values: …, keeps the pairs read so far and drops the rest. A value that itself contains an equals sign, such as Data=a=b, and a substituted value with a comma, such as an agent name, both trigger it.
  • An empty value produces an empty embed field, and Discord refuses the whole message with 400.
  • Fields are sent as they arrive: the connector does not truncate, escape or reorder them.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text:
Status When 0 The POST was answered with any HTTP status, including 4xx and 429. Also when the run is interrupted with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM 1 An uncaught error before or during the POST: a colour that is not hexadecimal, an empty or malformed webhook URL, or a DNS, TCP or TLS failure 2 Usage error: -d or -u missing, or an unknown option

The exit status does not report delivery. Read the printed status line and confirm the message in the channel.

docs.title: Operate
docs.text:
• Manual execution. Run the same command the alert command runs, from the Pandora FMS server or from any host that reaches discord.com. It is also the quickest way to test a webhook before creating the action.
  • One attempt per run. The connector posts once and does not retry. A 429 or a 5xx loses that alert.
  • Rate limit. Discord limits how often a webhook can post. A burst of alerts can be refused; nothing is queued locally.
  • Graph download. The request the connector makes to the console API to build the module graph has no timeout. If that API stops answering, the run stays open until the alert system's global timeout ends it.
  • Temporary file. The graph is written to --tmp_dir (default /tmp) as graph_<MODULE_ID>.<EPOCH>.png and deleted at the end of the run. Two runs for the same module in the same second share the file name.
  • Server log. At verbosity 8 or higher, pandora_server.log records the full command line of the action, including the webhook URL and the console credentials of Field 6. Keep that in mind before raising the verbosity for a support case.
  • Graph credentials. The console API request carries the user, the password and the API pass in its query string, and the default API URL is plain http://127.0.0.1. Pointing api_url at a remote console sends those credentials across the network in the URL and leaves them in the access log of that web server.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Symptom Cause and fix To get graph data api conf shoul be provided please set an api config on every run Normal when no --api_conf is given. The graph is skipped and the alert is still sent Error status code: 204 The message was accepted: Discord answers 204 No Content. Confirm it in the channel before treating it as a failure Error status code: 400 The payload was refused: an empty field value, an empty pair, more than 25 fields, or a text above the Discord length limits. Fix the data string Error status code: 401, 403 or 404 The webhook URL is wrong, truncated or revoked. Copy it again from the channel settings, or recreate the webhook Error status code: 429 Discord is rate-limiting the webhook. The alert is lost: the connector does not retry A traceback ending in invalid literal for int() with base 16 Field 4 is empty or contains something other than hexadecimal digits. Use six digits without # A traceback ending in MissingSchema or a connection error The webhook URL is empty or malformed, or discord.com cannot be reached: DNS, proxy, TCP 443 or TLS usage: … error: the following arguments are required: -d/--data, -u/--url The command line lost one of its options, usually because the command was edited or a field was removed. Restore the definition from test-exec.txt Warning, error parsing keypairs values: … A pair has no equals sign, or a substituted value contains a comma or an equals sign. Set a recovery payload if you do not want the prefix

Option Required Default Description -u, --url Yes — Discord webhook URL, the destination channel -d, --data Yes — Comma-separated key=value pairs, one embed field each -t, --alert_tittle No PandoraFMS alert fired Embed title. Limit Value Fields per embed 25 Field name length 256 characters Field value length 1024 characters Embed title length 256 characters Embed description length 4096 characters Footer length 2048 characters Author name length 256 characters Total characters of all embeds in the message 6000 Plain text content length 2000 characters Messages per run 1 Channels per run 1, the one of the webhook URL Retries None Attachments The module graph image, when enabled

The connector does not truncate: an alert above these limits is refused by Discord with 400.

docs.title: GLPI
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The GLPI addon connects Pandora FMS alerts to the GLPI service desk. It is not a monitoring plugin: it creates no agents and no monitoring modules. A Pandora FMS alert command runs it once per alert event, and that run creates, comments or replaces a GLPI ticket through the GLPI REST API.

Each run works on one GLPI group and does one of three things:

  • Create a ticket when the Pandora FMS module has no ticket registered for that group.
  • Add a followup comment to the registered ticket while it is open.
  • Replace the ticket when the registered one is solved or closed, so the next incident starts a new ticket instead of reviving a finished one.

The addon keeps the link between a module and its tickets in the module's custom ID field, with one entry per GLPI group, and reads and writes that field through the Pandora FMS console API. It stores nothing on disk: the log file is the only local artifact.

Two command modes drive the ticket lifecycle:

  • --recovery 0 (trigger) creates tickets and refreshes their content.
  • --recovery 1 (recovery) comments on the open ticket and removes the association when the ticket is already closed.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions A GLPI instance whose REST API answers at /apirest.php, reachable from the host that runs the alert command Required Every operation uses that endpoint; the addon appends /apirest.php/... to --url A Pandora FMS node console whose API can read and write the module custom ID, with the host listed in the console's IP list with API access Required The association is read and written through include/api.php before and after the GLPI calls GLPI releases Not validated No GLPI version matrix is recorded for this addon Operating system of the host that runs the alert command Not validated No operating system is recorded for version 1.0 GLPI installed plugins or custom ticket fields Not validated The addon only uses core item types

The GLPI version, the GLPI account and the node console are operational prerequisites, not compatibility statements.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity from the Pandora FMS server that executes the alert command to the GLPI instance, over HTTPS whenever possible.
  2. A GLPI account and an API application token. Every request carries the account credentials as HTTP basic authentication and the token in the App-Token header. The account must be able to read GLPI computers, search and read tickets, create tickets, add ticket followups and link a computer to a ticket.
  3. A Pandora FMS node console that stores the module the alert belongs to, with the console API enabled. The host that runs the command must appear in the console's IP list with API access, and the API user must be able to read the module's agent and hold write permission on it: setting the module custom ID is checked against the write ACL. The custom ID functions are not served in metaconsole mode, so --api_url must address the node console.
  4. Numeric GLPI identifiers for the ticket category and the group, plus the priority and request type you want. The addon sends them as numbers; it does not resolve names.
  5. A GLPI computer whose name matches the Pandora FMS agent alias when the ticket has to be linked to that computer. The comparison is case-insensitive. Without a match the ticket is still created, but it is not linked to a computer and it is placed in entity 0.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
The Marketplace entry distributes the addon as pandorafms.glpi.1.0.zip, with a free download. Extract the pandora_glpi executable and copy it to the Pandora FMS server that executes the alert command — for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_glpi — then make it executable.

The addon has no configuration file: every setting is a command-line argument, and the alert command is the place where they are stored.

docs.title: Prepare the log file
docs.text: The default log is /tmp/glpi_logfile.txt. To keep the record across reboots, create the directory of another path first, for example /var/log/pandora, and give write permission to the user that runs the Pandora FMS server process. The addon creates the file when it is missing, but not its directory; an unwritable path only prints an error and the run continues.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: Pandora FMS runs the addon from an alert command, and each alert action holds the field values for the triggering and for the recovery event. One command plus two sets of field values covers both --recovery modes.

docs.title: Create the alert command
docs.text:
1. Open Alerts → Commands → Create.
  2. Fill Name, Group and Description with something the operators of the alert will recognise, for example GLPI ticket.
  3. Paste the command, keeping one line per argument group:
/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_glpi \
  -u _field1_ -x _field2_ -i _field3_ -a _field4_ \
  -n _agent_ -m _id_module_ \
  -t "_alert_name_ - _module_" \
  -d "_timestamp_ | _module_ | _data_" \
  -p _field5_ -c _field6_ -g _field7_ -k _field8_ \
  -l /var/log/pandora/glpi.log -r _field9_
  1. Give every field a description. The command uses these fields:
Field Description to enter Suggested values _field1_ GLPI user The account that creates the tickets _field2_ GLPI password — mark Hide — _field3_ GLPI base URL, without a trailing slash https://<GLPI_URL> _field4_ GLPI application token — mark Hide <APP_TOKEN> _field5_ GLPI ticket priority 1 to 6, see Ticket priority _field6_ GLPI category ID <CATEGORY_ID> _field7_ GLPI group ID <GROUP_ID> _field8_ Ticket title used when the GLPI computer is not found Unknown computer _field9_ Mode: 0 trigger, 1 recovery 0 or 1
  1. In Field 9 values, enter 0,Trigger;1,Recovery so the field becomes a selection list instead of a free text box.

_agent_, _id_module_, _alert_name_, _module_, _data_ and _timestamp_ are Pandora FMS alert macros, expanded before the addon starts. _agent_ gives the agent alias, which is exactly the value the addon compares with the GLPI computer name. Keep -m as _id_module_ unless the command serves a single fixed module: the module ID decides which module stores the ticket association.

docs.title: Create the alert action
docs.text:
1. Open Alerts → Actions → Create.
  2. In Command, choose the command created above and fill its fields under Triggering with _field9_ = 0.
  3. Fill the same fields under Recovery with _field9_ = 1.
  4. Set Threshold to a value that prevents a flapping module from running the command repeatedly in a short interval.
  5. Save the action and apply it through an alert template or directly on the module.

Both field sets are stored in the action, so the same command serves every module. The values that change per module are the ones Pandora FMS expands as macros; the ones that change per alert are the field values.

docs.title: Ticket priority
docs.text:
--ticket_priority is the numeric GLPI priority. GLPI defines the scale:

Value Priority 1 Very low 2 Low 3 Medium 4 High 5 Very high 6 Major

--ticket_request_type is also a numeric identifier — 8 by default — and must be a request type that exists in your GLPI instance.

docs.title: Ticket content and the %ticketID% macro
docs.text:
--ticket_name and --ticket_description become the ticket title and content. Both accept the macro %ticketID%, which the addon replaces with the ID of the ticket it has just created. GLPI stores the content as sent, so you can include its markup in --ticket_description when you want a formatted ticket body.

The macro is resolved by updating the ticket right after creating it, so the ticket exists for a moment with the literal %ticketID% text. If that update is refused, the ticket keeps the literal text.

--ticket_name_error is the title used when no GLPI computer matches the agent alias, but the addon renames the new ticket to the resolved --ticket_name immediately afterwards: in practice both titles end up being the same. See Limitations.

docs.title: The module custom ID
docs.text:
The addon stores its state in the custom ID field of the module identified by --id_module, as a map of GLPI group → ticket ID. It reads that map before creating or commenting a ticket and writes it after creating or closing one.

  • Treat that field as addon-owned. If you overwrite it with free text, the addon cannot parse it, takes the map as empty and creates a new ticket the next time the alert fires.
  • --ticket_group is both the GLPI group assigned to the ticket and the key of the map. Changing the group in a command starts a new association, so the next trigger creates a new ticket instead of commenting the existing one.
  • One module can hold one open ticket per group. Use different groups — in separate commands or actions — when a single module has to open tickets in different GLPI queues.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the addon by hand before trusting an alert with it. Use a test module and a test agent, because a successful run creates a real ticket.

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_glpi \
  -u '<USERNAME>' -x '<PASSWORD>' -i 'https://<GLPI_URL>' -a '<APP_TOKEN>' \
  -n 'test-agent' -m <MODULE_ID> \
  -t 'Pandora FMS test - %ticketID%' \
  -d 'Manual verification run' \
  -p 3 -c <CATEGORY_ID> -g <GROUP_ID> -k 'Unknown computer' \
  -l /var/log/pandora/glpi.log -r 0

A run that creates a ticket ends with lines like these on standard output:

Succesful: Added custom id ' <GROUP_ID> : <TICKET_ID> ' in module with id <MODULE_ID>
Succesful: Ticket created successfully.

Check all four results:

  1. Standard output shows the two lines above.
  2. The log file contains the same messages with a timestamp prefix.
  3. GLPI has the new ticket, with the title and content from the command.
  4. The module in Pandora FMS shows the association in its custom ID field.

Then repeat the run with -r 1 and the same arguments. This time the addon adds a followup comment to the existing ticket instead of creating one:

Succesful: Added tracking in the ticket : <TICKET_ID>

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The addon decides what to do from two facts: the association stored in the module and the current status of the associated ticket.

Association for the group --recovery 0 (trigger) --recovery 1 (recovery) None Creates a ticket, links the computer when it exists, stores the ticket ID Creates nothing; logs Error: There is no ticket open for the module with id <MODULE_ID> and group <GROUP_ID> Ticket open — any status other than 5 or 6 Adds a followup comment with the resolved --ticket_description; no new ticket Adds the same followup comment Ticket solved (5) or closed (6) Creates a new ticket, replaces the stored ID with the new one, links the computer Removes the stored entry and adds the followup comment to the closed ticket

A created ticket carries these values:

Ticket field Value Title --ticket_name, %ticketID% resolved Content --ticket_description, %ticketID% resolved Priority --ticket_priority Category --ticket_category Assigned group --ticket_group Request type --ticket_request_type Entity The entity of the matching GLPI computer; 0 when no computer matches. When a closed ticket is replaced, the entity of the previous ticket Linked computer The GLPI computer whose name matches --alias_agent, case-insensitive

Consequences worth knowing:

  • A solved ticket counts as closed. GLPI status 5 (Solved) is enough for the next trigger to open a new ticket, even if the ticket has not been closed yet.
  • The ticket is never closed, solved or deleted by the addon. A recovery only comments; closing the ticket is a manual or GLPI-side workflow.
  • Repeated triggers do not duplicate tickets while the ticket stays open: every trigger after the first one appends a comment.
  • The comment uses the current command values. A followup added on recovery carries the description resolved for that run, so the ticket history keeps the sequence of events the alert reported.

docs.title: Scheduling and concurrency
docs.text:
• Every run is one-shot: it authenticates, works on one group, closes the GLPI session and exits. There is no daemon, no state on disk and no background execution, so a manual run at any time is safe.
  • The addon relies on the alert direction. It does not read the module status to decide between trigger and recovery; that is why --recovery must be driven by the action field values.
  • Avoid overlapping runs for the same module and group. The association is read at the start and written after the ticket is created, so two runs that start together can both create a ticket. A non-zero action Threshold keeps the window small.
  • Every run that has to create a ticket walks the whole GLPI computer inventory page by page to find the agent alias. On a large inventory this is slow: raise --pagination_results from its default 1 when the run takes too long.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The GLPI password, the application token and the console credentials are command-line arguments. They are visible in the process list while the addon runs, and they are stored in the alert command and in the alert action inside the console. Mark the secret fields with Hide, restrict who can read alert commands, and protect the server's process list.
  • The console API password and the console user password travel in the query string of the include/api.php URL, so they can be recorded in the web server access log of the console. Use a dedicated API user with the narrowest rights that still allow reading the module and setting its custom ID.
  • HTTPS certificates are verified against the trust store of the host. The addon has no option to disable verification or to supply a CA bundle: a GLPI instance with a certificate from a private CA needs that CA installed on the host.
  • With plain HTTP the GLPI credentials travel unencrypted in the Authorization header. Restrict GLPI to a trusted network or place it behind TLS.

docs.title: Exit status and the log
docs.text:
Every handled error is printed on standard output and appended to the log file with a YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS - prefix. The exit status is not a reliable success signal:

Status Meaning 0 The run finished. Most handled failures — rejected credentials, a refused ticket creation, a refused comment — also end with 0 after printing the error 2 The command line was rejected before any request: a missing required argument or a value of the wrong type, for example a category name instead of its numeric ID

Read the log file, or check the ticket in GLPI, to decide whether a run worked. The log is append-only and shared by every run, so rotate it.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text: Symptom Cause and check Unauthorized: Check your credentials. GLPI rejected the login. Check --user, --password and --app_token, and that the GLPI account is active Error logging in: <status> - <body> The GLPI API answered with an error other than an authentication failure. The body is the GLPI message Bad Request: <body> while reading or writing the custom ID The console API rejected the request. Check --api_pass, --api_user, --api_user_pass, the host entry in the IP list with API access, and that --api_url points to a node console Error getting custom id: <status> - <body> / Error setting custom id: ... The console API answered with an error other than a bad request. The body identifies it Bad Request: <body> after a trigger GLPI refused the ticket. The body names the offending field: usually a category, group or request type that does not exist in that instance Error: There is no ticket open for the module with id <MODULE_ID> and group <GROUP_ID> A recovery ran with no association. Confirm the recovery uses the same --id_module and --ticket_group as the trigger Two tickets for the same incident Two overlapping triggers, or --ticket_group changed between runs Every trigger creates a new ticket and the module custom ID stays empty --api_url points at a metaconsole, where the custom ID functions are not served. Use the node console that stores the module The run stops with an unexpected error after login The GLPI session expired or the ticket could not be read. The log records what the addon had done until that point Nothing is written to the log The log path is not writable. The addon prints the write error and keeps going

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One GLPI instance per run. Tickets in two instances require two commands.
  • One ticket per module and group at a time.
  • --ticket_name_error does not survive the run: the addon renames the ticket to the resolved --ticket_name right after creating it, so the title for an unknown computer is replaced. Use %ticketID% and the description to flag the missing computer instead.
  • No request timeout is set. If GLPI accepts the connection and stops answering, the alert command waits; wrap the call in the system timeout command if that risk matters in your installation.
  • The addon closes the GLPI session only at the end of a completed run. A run that exits early leaves its session open until GLPI expires it.
  • The log file is the only audit trail the addon keeps; the ticket history in GLPI is the record of what the alerts reported.

docs.title: Command-line arguments
docs.text:
Argument Required Default Description -u, --user Yes — GLPI account used to authenticate -x, --password Yes — Password of the GLPI account -i, --url Yes — GLPI base URL; the addon appends /apirest.php/... to it -a, --app_token Yes — GLPI application token, sent in the App-Token header -n, --alias_agent Yes — Agent alias, compared case-insensitively with the GLPI computer names -m, --id_module Yes — Numeric ID of the Pandora FMS module that stores the ticket association -t, --ticket_name Yes — Ticket title. Accepts %ticketID% -d, --ticket_description Yes — Ticket content and followup comment. Accepts %ticketID% -p, --ticket_priority Yes — Numeric GLPI priority, 1 to 6 -c, --ticket_category Yes — Numeric ID of the GLPI category -g, --ticket_group Yes — Numeric ID of the GLPI group assigned to the ticket, and key of the stored association -k, --ticket_name_error Yes — Title used when no GLPI computer matches the agent alias. It is replaced by --ticket_name right after creation -j, --ticket_request_type No 8 Numeric ID of the GLPI request type -l, --log_file No /tmp/glpi_logfile.txt Log file, appended with timestamped lines -r, --recovery No 0 0 for a trigger, 1 for a recovery --api_url No http://localhost Base URL of the Pandora FMS node console; the addon appends /pandora_console/include/api.php --api_user No admin Console API user --api_pass No 1234 Console API password, sent as apipass --api_user_pass No pandora Password of the console API user --pagination_results No 1 Page step used while walking the GLPI computer inventory -h, --help No — Prints the usage summary and exits

The usage summary of the addon documents a --ticket_message argument. No such argument exists: the ticket content is --ticket_description.

docs.title: Execution and output
docs.text: Condition Behavior The command line is missing a required argument The addon prints the usage summary, names the missing arguments and exits with status 2 A numeric argument receives text, for example a category name The addon prints the rejected value and exits with status 2 GLPI rejects the login Prints Unauthorized: Check your credentials., appends it to the log and exits The module custom ID cannot be read Prints the console API answer and stops without touching GLPI No association and --recovery 0 Creates the ticket, stores the ID and prints two confirmation lines No association and --recovery 1 Prints Error: There is no ticket open for the module with id ... and group ... Association to an open ticket Adds a followup comment and prints Succesful: Added tracking in the ticket : <TICKET_ID> Association to a solved or closed ticket, --recovery 0 Creates a new ticket and replaces the stored ID Association to a solved or closed ticket, --recovery 1 Removes the stored entry and adds the followup comment to the closed ticket The run completes Closes the GLPI session and exits
