docs.title: Pandora Azure SQL plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use Azure SQL Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora Azure SQL plugin turns the Azure Monitor metrics of one Azure SQL database into Pandora FMS modules. Each run authenticates in Microsoft Entra with a service principal, reads 23 metrics of the database over the last hour at five-minute resolution, and publishes them as a new agent with 23 modules.

The database is identified by its full Azure resource ID, which you write in a local configuration file together with the credentials. The plugin never opens a SQL connection: it reads the metrics Azure Monitor already stores for the resource, so nothing is installed on the database server and no port has to be reachable on it.

One run covers one database and produces one agent. Monitoring several databases means one execution per database, each with its own configuration file and its own agent name.

The addon supports the two execution models of a Pandora FMS plugin:

  • Server plugin mode (default): each run builds the agent document and either copies it into the Pandora FMS data directory or sends it with Tentacle.
  • Agent plugin mode (--as_agent_plugin 1): each run prints the module XML on standard output, for the Pandora FMS agent to ingest.

This page documents two different command lines. The Marketplace record and the package's registration file describe only the metric collector, pandora_azuresql, which is the subject of this page. A second executable, pandora_azuresqlquery, runs SQL sentences against the same database over ODBC, with its own options, its own configuration format and its own output. The Marketplace record does not describe it and does not state whether your package contains it. It is documented separately in The query runner so that the two are never confused.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Marketplace addon pandorafms.azuresql, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. A general public statement that covers every entry, not a test record for this addon An Azure SQL database, identified by its full resource ID Required The configuration file carries one database_id and every metric query is made against it. Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement A Microsoft Entra service principal allowed to read that database resource and its metrics Required The plugin authenticates with a tenant, an application identifier and a client secret, and reads Azure Monitor metrics for the resource. No official source names a narrower role for this addon HTTPS access to the public Azure endpoints Required The plugin has no endpoint option, so it authenticates and queries the public cloud only. Sovereign or custom clouds are Not validated tentacle_client on the host that runs the plugin Required when --tentacle_address is used Tentacle delivery Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server on the host that runs the plugin Required when using the query runner The query runner requests that driver by name and has no option to change it. See The query runner Azure SQL service tier and edition Not validated Some metrics apply only to vCore-based or serverless databases, and others not at all to data warehouses. The plugin requests all 23 regardless of the tier Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated The legacy guide names CentOS 7, Fedora and Rocky Linux as tested and "any Linux" as expected. No test record supports either claim

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. An Azure SQL database and its full resource ID.
  2. A Microsoft Entra service principal: tenant identifier, application (client) identifier and a client secret.
  3. Read access for that service principal to the database resource and to its Azure Monitor metrics. Grant read access on the smallest scope that covers the database.
  4. Outbound HTTPS from the host that runs the plugin to the public Azure endpoints.
  5. Pandora FMS to receive the output: the Pandora FMS server in server plugin mode, or the Pandora FMS agent of the monitored host in agent plugin mode.
  6. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) available in PATH, only when you deliver with --tentacle_address.

The metrics are read from Azure Monitor and never from the database itself, so the account that reads them is an Azure identity, not a database user.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the pandorafms.azuresql.1.0.pspz2 package from the Marketplace entry:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.azuresql

Register the package from the Pandora FMS console plugin manager. The package carries a registration file that declares the plugin command and its three module fields, documented in Register the plugin in the console.

The executable can also be deployed on its own and run from a terminal or from a scheduler; see Command-line execution.

docs.title: Prepare Azure access
docs.text:
1. Create or select an application registration in Microsoft Entra ID and generate a client secret for it.
  2. Record three values: the tenant (directory) identifier, the application (client) identifier, and the secret value. Copy the value, not the secret identifier: the plugin sends it verbatim to the authentication endpoint.
  3. Grant the service principal read access to the database resource and to its metrics.
  4. Copy the database's full resource ID. It has this form:
/subscriptions/<SUBSCRIPTION_ID>/resourceGroups/<RESOURCE_GROUP>/providers/Microsoft.Sql/servers/<SQL_SERVER>/databases/<DATABASE>

The plugin sends that string as the resource URI of every metric query, so it must be the database resource, not the server.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The plugin takes its credentials and its target from one configuration file, and everything else from the command line. There is no precedence between the two: no delivery setting can be written in the file, and no credential can be passed as a flag.

docs.title: The configuration file
docs.text:
The file is mandatory and is passed with -c/--conf. It holds one key:value pair per line:

# Azure credentials
tenant_id:<TENANT_ID>
client_id:<CLIENT_ID>
secret:<CLIENT_SECRET>
# Target database
database_id:/subscriptions/<SUBSCRIPTION_ID>/resourceGroups/<RESOURCE_GROUP>/providers/Microsoft.Sql/servers/<SQL_SERVER>/databases/<DATABASE>

The parser applies these rules:

  • The separator is a colon, not an equals sign.
  • Blank lines are skipped.
  • A line that contains # anywhere is skipped, not only a line that starts with it. Do not append a comment to a value line.
  • A value ends at the next colon: a client secret that itself contains : is truncated, and authentication fails.
  • A repeated key keeps its last value.
  • The four keys are matched by name. If one is missing, the run stops with a NameError traceback instead of a message naming the missing key.

The file holds the client secret in plain text. Restrict it to the account that runs the plugin (for example with chmod 600) and keep it out of shared directories and version control.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
The minimum server-mode run, which writes the agent document into the Pandora FMS data directory:

./pandora_azuresql -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The same run delivered with Tentacle, with an explicit agent name and group:

./pandora_azuresql -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG> \
    --agent_name <AGENT_NAME> -g <GROUP> \
    --tentacle_address <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER> --tentacle_port 41121

Agent plugin mode, which prints the module XML instead of building an agent:

./pandora_azuresql -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --as_agent_plugin 1

The command line selects one of three output branches. --tentacle_address takes precedence over the mode option:

Command line What the run does --tentacle_address is set, with or without --as_agent_plugin Builds the agent document, sends it with tentacle_client and prints 1 No --tentacle_address, and --as_agent_plugin is absent or not 1 Builds the agent document, writes it into --data_dir and prints 1 --as_agent_plugin 1 and no --tentacle_address Prints the module XML on standard output and writes no file

Key points:

  • --as_agent_plugin 1 selects agent plugin mode; the default is server plugin mode. The option name is the inverse of the default, so confirm the mode before reading any output.
  • --data_dir, --agent_name and -g have no effect in agent plugin mode. No file and no agent document are built, so the agent name and the group never reach Pandora FMS.
  • --prefix_module is accepted and ignored. No module name receives a prefix in this collector; see Generated modules.
  • The group is written by name into the agent document, so it must be a group that exists in the console. The registration file suggests azuresql; the built-in default is Azure.
  • The agent document always declares agent mode 1 and an empty interval, so the interval is applied by the console, not by the plugin.
  • The plugin keeps no state between runs, so any execution can be repeated manually.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
1. Open Servers → Plugins and register the pandorafms.azuresql.1.0.pspz2 package, or add the plugin manually with the path of the pandora_azuresql executable as its command.
  2. The parameters already declared by the package are:
-c " _field1_ " --agent_name " _field2_ " -g " _field3_ "
  1. The package defines three fields:
Field Description in the package Value to supply _field1_ Conf path (obligatory) Absolute path of the configuration file on the Pandora FMS server _field2_ Agent name (optional) Name of the agent that will hold the 23 modules _field3_ No definition in the package Name of an existing Pandora FMS group

The packaged parameters break the configuration path

Each macro is quoted with a space inside the quotes: -c " _field1_ ". After the console substitutes the field value, the argument keeps a leading and a trailing space, and the plugin opens that path without trimming it, so the run fails with FileNotFoundError. Remove the spaces when you register the plugin, for example -c "_field1_" --agent_name "_field2_" -g "_field3_".

The registration file declares total_macros_provided = 3 but defines [macro_1], [macro_2] and [macro_4]. There is no [macro_3], so the third field, which the command line uses as _field3_, is the one the package leaves without a description, and the group definition is the one that is not used.

  1. Give each field a value per module. The plugin module is only the trigger: in server plugin mode its own value is 1, and the 23 metric modules land on the agent named by --agent_name, not on the agent that holds the trigger module.
  2. Each plugin module executes on the Pandora FMS server selected for it, including a remote server, so several databases can be monitored from the server closest to each one without installing anything on the database host.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually in agent plugin mode to see the output without publishing anything:

./pandora_azuresql -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --as_agent_plugin 1

A successful run prints 23 <module> blocks on standard output. Every block is a generic_data_string module whose value is a <datalist> with one entry per data point of the last hour:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[cpu_percent]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <datalist>
    <data>
        <value><![CDATA[The cpu_percent at 2026-10-27 09:05:00+00:00 is 2.4]]></value>
    </data>
    <data>
        <value><![CDATA[The cpu_percent at 2026-10-27 09:10:00+00:00 is 3.1]]></value>
    </data>
    </datalist>
    <description><![CDATA[CPU percentage]]></description>
</module>

This excerpt shows the document structure the plugin produces; it was not captured from a live database.

Then run the plugin without --as_agent_plugin to deliver the agent:

./pandora_azuresql -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --agent_name <AGENT_NAME>

A successful server-mode run prints 1 and writes <AGENT_NAME>.<epoch>.data into the data directory, or sends it with Tentacle. Once the data server processes the file, the agent named <AGENT_NAME> appears in Pandora FMS with its 23 modules.

The plugin prints its usage summary with ./pandora_azuresql -h.

docs.title: What each run publishes
docs.text:
One agent with 23 modules, always the same set, grouped by the part of the service they describe:

Family Modules Compute cpu_percent, cpu_limit, cpu_used, sqlserver_process_core_percent, app_cpu_percent, app_cpu_billed Storage storage, storage_percent, allocated_data_storage I/O and log physical_data_read_percent, log_write_percent Connections and sessions connection_successful, connection_failed, blocked_by_firewall, sessions_percent, workers_percent, sqlserver_process_memory_percent, app_memory_percent TempDB and in-memory OLTP tempdb_data_size, tempdb_log_size, tempdb_log_used_percent, xtp_storage_percent Contention deadlock

docs.title: Why every module is a list of text
docs.text:
Each module is a generic_data_string whose value is a <datalist>, and each entry reads The <metric> at <timestamp> is <value>. This has consequences worth knowing before you build anything on top of the data:

  • The value is text, not a number. Pandora FMS cannot plot the module as a numeric series or apply numeric thresholds to it, and the plugin sets no unit, interval or threshold on any module.
  • Every run republishes the whole last hour. With a five-minute execution interval, each data point appears in the module value of 12 consecutive runs.
  • A point without a value is published as None. Azure Monitor does not fill every point of every metric, and the plugin writes what it receives.
  • All 23 modules are created on every run, including metrics the database does not report. Such a module appears with an empty <datalist>. An empty module is not proof of a failure.
  • The counters are averaged like the gauges. connection_successful, connection_failed, blocked_by_firewall and deadlock are requested with the Average aggregation over the five-minute granularity, so the published numbers are per-interval averages, not totals.
  • There is no availability module. Nothing in the output states whether the run could reach Azure. A failed run publishes nothing at all, and the missing data is the only signal.

docs.title: One agent per database
docs.text: The agent name and the target database are both per-execution settings, so monitoring several databases means one configuration file per database (a different database_id) and one execution per database (a different --agent_name). Reusing the same agent name for two databases merges both sets of modules into one agent, and the second run overwrites the first.

docs.title: Compared with Azure SQL Discovery
docs.text:
Azure SQL Discovery addresses the same service through a Discovery task. The differences that matter when choosing:

This plugin Azure SQL Discovery Databases monitored One, named by its resource ID in the configuration file Every database of the subscription or Resource Group, or those matching the name filters Agents One agent per run, named with --agent_name One agent per database, or a single target agent Modules 23 string datalists covering the last hour Numeric modules, one per enabled metric family Credentials A plain-text file on the host that runs the plugin The Pandora FMS credential store, referenced by the task Configuration Command-line flags A Discovery task Recommended for new installations No Yes

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
• 23 sequential requests per run. The package declares a plugin timeout of 20 seconds. On a slow connection, or when the client retries a request, the run can be cut before it finishes; force the module and check the timestamp of the agent data.
  • A successful server-mode run prints 1. That 1 is the value of the trigger module, not a summary of the delivery. With Tentacle, a failed transfer still prints 1: the plugin ignores the result of the send and prints 1 unconditionally, and it leaves the .data file in --data_dir because it deletes the file only after a successful transfer. Check the agent data in the console, not the 1.
  • The data file is opened in exclusive mode. Two executions of the same agent name within the same second stop with ERROR - Could not write file: ... please check directory permissions, which is also the message for a real permission problem.
  • There is no debug mode. Errors reach standard error as a traceback, and the messages below are the ones to look for.
Symptom Cause and action The run ends with status 2 and a usage error on standard error -c is missing. It is a required argument. Traceback ending in NameError naming tenant_id, client_id, secret or database_id The configuration file has no line for that key, or the line was skipped because it contains #. The plugin has no message for a missing key. FileNotFoundError on the configuration path The path is wrong, or it arrived with surrounding spaces from the packaged parameter template. See the warning in Register the plugin in the console. ERROR - Could not write file --data_dir is not writable by the plugin user, or another run of the same agent wrote in the same second. 1 is printed but no agent appears in the console With --tentacle_address, the transfer failed. Check the address, the port and the Tentacle server log. Without Tentacle, check that the data server is running and reading --data_dir. Traceback from the authentication step The tenant, the client identifier or the secret is wrong, the secret has expired, or the service principal has no read access to the resource. Traceback naming a metric or an Azure response error Azure rejected one of the 23 requests. The run has no error handling, so the execution stops and publishes nothing. Check the database tier and the resource ID. A module shows only None values Azure Monitor has no datapoints for that metric and that database. --prefix_module is set but the module names are unchanged The option has no effect in this collector.

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Option Required Default Description -c, --conf Yes — Path of the configuration file with the credentials and the database resource ID --agent_name No Azure_SQL Name of the agent created in Pandora FMS. Has no effect in agent plugin mode -g, --group No Azure Name of the Pandora FMS group assigned to the agent. Has no effect in agent plugin mode --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Directory where the agent document is written. Has no effect in agent plugin mode --tentacle_address No — Address of the Tentacle server. When set, the agent document is sent and the other two delivery modes are ignored --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port --as_agent_plugin No 0 1 prints the module XML on standard output. Any other value builds the agent document --prefix_module No — Accepted and ignored -h, --help No — Prints the usage summary and exits

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
Key Required Description tenant_id Yes Microsoft Entra tenant (directory) identifier client_id Yes Application (client) identifier of the service principal secret Yes Client secret value database_id Yes Full resource ID of the Azure SQL database

The file uses key:value lines. See The configuration file for the parsing rules, including the lines that are skipped.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
Every module is generic_data_string with a <datalist> of the datapoints of the last hour, sampled every five minutes. The plugin sets no unit and no threshold; the description is the text it writes into the module.

Module name Family Description written by the plugin cpu_percent Compute CPU percentage cpu_limit Compute CPU limit. Applies to vCore-based databases cpu_used Compute CPU used. Applies to vCore-based databases sqlserver_process_core_percent Compute CPU usage as a percentage of the SQL DB process. Not applicable to data warehouses app_cpu_percent Compute App CPU percentage. Applies to serverless databases app_cpu_billed Compute App CPU billed. Applies to serverless databases storage Storage Data space used. Not applicable to data warehouses storage_percent Storage Data space used percent. Not applicable to data warehouses or hyperscale databases allocated_data_storage Storage Allocated data storage. Not applicable to data warehouses physical_data_read_percent I/O and log Data IO percentage log_write_percent I/O and log Log IO percentage. Not applicable to data warehouses connection_successful Connections Successful connections connection_failed Connections Failed connections blocked_by_firewall Connections Blocked by firewall sessions_percent Connections Sessions percentage. Not applicable to data warehouses workers_percent Connections Workers percentage. Not applicable to data warehouses sqlserver_process_memory_percent Connections Memory usage as a percentage of the SQL DB process. Not applicable to data warehouses app_memory_percent Connections App memory percentage. Applies to serverless databases tempdb_data_size TempDB and XTP Space used in tempdb data files, in kilobytes. Not applicable to data warehouses tempdb_log_size TempDB and XTP Space used in the tempdb transaction log file, in kilobytes. Not applicable to data warehouses tempdb_log_used_percent TempDB and XTP Space used percentage in the tempdb transaction log file. Not applicable to data warehouses xtp_storage_percent TempDB and XTP In-Memory OLTP storage percent. Not applicable to data warehouses deadlock Contention Not applicable to data warehouses

docs.title: The query runner
docs.text:
A second executable, pandora_azuresqlquery, is a different tool: it runs SQL sentences against the database over ODBC and turns their rows into modules. It shares neither the options nor the configuration format of the metric collector described above. The Marketplace record does not describe it and does not state whether your package contains it; confirm that the file is present before relying on it.

./pandora_azuresqlquery -s <TARGET_HOST> -d <DATABASE> -u <USERNAME> -p <PASSWORD> \
    --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --agent_name <AGENT_NAME>
Option Required Default Description -s, --servidor Yes — Server name, passed to the driver as tcp:<TARGET_HOST> -d, --database Yes — Database name -u, --user Yes — Database user -p, --password Yes — Password for that user --conf Yes — Path of the file with the queries --agent_name No AzureSQL Name of the agent created in Pandora FMS -g, --group No Azure Pandora FMS group name --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Directory where the agent document is written --tentacle_address No — Tentacle server address; takes precedence over --as_agent_plugin --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port --as_agent_plugin No 0 1 prints the module XML on standard output --prefix_module No — Prefix prepended to every module name, followed by _

The query file holds one query per line, in this form:

<module name>:<SQL sentence>:<module type>:<description>

The third field is written verbatim as the module type, without validation, and the fourth is optional. An example from the configuration shipped with the tool:

User_connections:SELECT count(*) FROM sys.dm_exec_connections:generic_data_string:shows user connections.

The parser applies the rules of the metric collector with the same consequences: a line containing # anywhere is skipped, and a value ends at the next colon, so a SQL sentence that contains a colon is truncated. A line with fewer than three fields stops the run and drops every query after it. A query that fails prints its error on standard error, is skipped, and the run continues with the next one.

Each module value is a <datalist> in which every row is one ;-joined string of the returned columns, so these modules are text as well. The token _database_ in a query is replaced by the database name, quoted.

Two behaviours are worth knowing before using it in production:

  • A connection failure is reported as a successful run. The tool prints Error while creating PostgreSQL table and the driver error, then a second Error: line on standard error, then 0, and it exits with status 0. The messages name PostgreSQL, not Azure SQL: the agent description it writes is literally PostgreSQL agent.
  • The database password is a command-line argument. It is visible in the process list and in the shell history of the account that runs the tool.

docs.title: Pandora Azure Storage monitoring plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use Azure Storage Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora Azure Storage plugin reads the Azure Monitor metrics of one Azure storage account, and of the account services you enable — Blob, File, Queue, Table and Data Lake Storage — and publishes them as Pandora FMS modules, grouped in one agent per service.

Every run works on the resource IDs written in a configuration file: the storage account itself and each service you want to read. The plugin asks Azure Monitor for the last hour of every metric and builds the modules from the answer. There is no discovery step and no Azure resource enumeration: the account and the services are the ones you write in that file.

The plugin has three execution paths:

  • No delivery option (default). It prints one <module> XML block per module on standard output, for a Pandora FMS agent to collect.
  • --as_agent_plugin 1. It builds one agent_data XML document per enabled service, writes each one into data_dir and prints 1. Despite its name, this option produces the server-side run.
  • --tentacle_address. It builds the same agent_data documents, delivers each one with the Tentacle client and prints 1.

This page documents the pandorafms.azure_storage plugin, distributed as a .pspz2 package. Azure Storage Discovery is a different addon: it runs from a Discovery task, enumerates the storage accounts of a subscription or of one resource group, creates one agent per discovered account and needs no configuration file. See Azure Storage Discovery. The Discovery application also uses pandorafms.azure_storage as its short name, so check the package type before installing: .pspz2 is this plugin, .disco is Discovery.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.azure_storage, version 1.0 Documented target Version of the Marketplace entry and of the distributed package. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. It is a catalogue-wide statement covering this addon, not a test record for it CentOS 7, Fedora and Rocky Linux as the host system Known compatible The previous edition of this guide records these systems as the ones where the plugin was tested; not re-validated for version 1.0 Other host systems Not validated No other system is recorded for this addon A Microsoft Entra app registration that can read the Azure Monitor metrics of the account Required Every collection call authenticates with its tenant ID, client ID and secret The Azure resource ID of the storage account and of each service you enable Required Each value is queried directly as the metrics resource of that service tentacle_client in PATH Required when --tentacle_address is used Delivery runs the Tentacle client A writable data_dir Required when the agent document is written The XML document is created in that folder Azure sovereign or custom clouds Not validated The addon exposes no endpoint option, so the Microsoft endpoints cannot be redirected

The Marketplace entry does not state any maintenance or lifecycle status for this addon.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Pandora FMS installation with the plugin server enabled, to run the plugin, and the data server to ingest the agent_data documents when the run writes them.
  2. An Azure subscription with at least one storage account to monitor.
  3. A Microsoft Entra app registration for the plugin: its tenant ID, its client ID and a client secret.
  4. The Azure resource IDs of the storage account and of each service you want to read, written in the configuration file.
  5. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) available in PATH, only when the run delivers through Tentacle.

docs.title: Prepare Azure access
docs.text:
Create an app registration in Microsoft Entra ID and note its tenant ID, its client ID and a client secret value. These three values go to the configuration file.

The plugin does not name the Azure role to assign. It only calls the Azure Monitor metrics API for the resource IDs in the configuration, so the registration needs permission to read the metrics of those resources. Assign the narrowest role that grants that read on the storage account or on its resource group.

Two further groups of values are needed:

  • The resource ID of the storage account, the account scope the plugin queries for its account-level metrics. Its form is /subscriptions/<SUBSCRIPTION_ID>/resourceGroups/<RESOURCE_GROUP>/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/<ACCOUNT>.
  • The resource ID of each service you enable — Blob, File, Queue, Table and Data Lake Storage. The previous edition of this guide obtains all of them from the account's own pages in the Azure portal.

The plugin sends each value exactly as written. A malformed identifier, or one that the app registration cannot read, fails the run with the Azure exception; a valid identifier that has no data for a metric only produces no module for that metric. Copy the identifiers from Azure instead of typing them.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Upload the .pspz2 package from the console plugin registration page. The package registers the plugin with the definition described in Register the plugin in the console, including the three macros of the registration form.

The plugin reads a configuration file that you provide. The shipped value of the first macro is /var/www/html/pandora_console/attachment/plugin/pandora_azure.conf, so either write the file there or change the macro to the path you use. The Configuration file section describes the content.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The file is plain text and uses key:value lines. Every value is trimmed. Three rules decide what the plugin reads:

  • A line that contains # anywhere is skipped, so comments start anywhere and a value that contains # is lost with its line.
  • A line is split on :, and only the second fragment is kept: a value that contains : is truncated at the first colon.
  • Keys are matched by substring, not as an exact key name: a line that contains a known key name is read as that key, a line that contains none is ignored, and a repeated key keeps the last value read.

This is the complete file shipped with the addon, with placeholders:

#credentials
tenant_id:<TENANT_ID>
client_id:<CLIENT_ID>
secret:<CLIENT_SECRET>
#id resources
account_id:<ACCOUNT_RESOURCE_ID>
blobservice_id:<BLOB_SERVICE_RESOURCE_ID>
fileservice_id:<FILE_SERVICE_RESOURCE_ID>
queueservice_id:<QUEUE_SERVICE_RESOURCE_ID>
tableservice_id:<TABLE_SERVICE_RESOURCE_ID>
datalakestorage_id:<DATA_LAKE_SERVICE_RESOURCE_ID>
#active agents
account_agent:1
blobservice_agent:1
fileservice_agent:1
queueservice_agent:1
tableservice_agent:1
datalakestorage_agent:1

The three credential keys and the six <service>_agent switches are mandatory: the plugin reads all of them before collecting anything, and a missing one stops the run with a NameError traceback. Each <service>_id is only needed when its switch is 1. A switch holds 1 to enable the service and 0 to leave it out; any other value stops the run with a ValueError.

To monitor only the account and Blob service, for example:

#credentials
tenant_id:<TENANT_ID>
client_id:<CLIENT_ID>
secret:<CLIENT_SECRET>
#id resources
account_id:<ACCOUNT_RESOURCE_ID>
blobservice_id:<BLOB_SERVICE_RESOURCE_ID>
#active agents
account_agent:1
blobservice_agent:1
fileservice_agent:0
queueservice_agent:0
tableservice_agent:0
datalakestorage_agent:0

An empty value is read as empty and fails at authentication time, not at parse time. Keep the file readable only by the user that runs the plugin: it holds the client secret in clear text.

docs.title: Execution modes and delivery
docs.text:
The plugin processes the enabled services in a fixed order, starting a new list of modules for each one: account first, then Blob, Queue, File, Table and Data Lake Storage. Each service delivers its own agent, so a run with all six switches enabled delivers six agents.

Delivery is chosen per service, by these rules:

Command line What the run does --tentacle_address <TARGET_HOST> Writes the agent_data document of the service and sends it with tentacle_client -v -a <TARGET_HOST> -p <port> <file>. Prints 1 after each service --as_agent_plugin 1 without --tentacle_address Writes the agent_data document of the service into data_dir and prints 1 Neither option Prints the modules of the service as <module> XML blocks on standard output, and writes no file

The Tentacle path deletes the local document after a successful send, so the data_dir folder holds nothing when the run succeeds. The plugin passes only the address and the port to the Tentacle client; it has no option for a Tentacle password.

--tentacle_address takes precedence over --as_agent_plugin, so a run can write the document, deliver it and print 1 with both options present.

The Data Lake Storage service does not follow the same rule: with --as_agent_plugin 1 and no Tentacle address it prints its modules on standard output instead of writing a document, and it only writes the document when --as_agent_plugin is absent or different from 1. See Limitations.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The client secret is stored in the configuration file in clear text. Restrict the file permissions to the user that runs the plugin and keep the file out of shared directories and version control.
  • The secret is not a command-line option, so it does not appear in the shell history or in the process list. It does appear in the configuration file that the console plugin command references.
  • The addon exposes no endpoint option: authentication and metric queries go to the default Microsoft identity and management endpoints. There is no setting for a sovereign cloud, a custom endpoint or a proxy.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
The plugin can be registered in the Pandora FMS console as a server plugin, so Pandora FMS executes it from the server that runs the modules instead of from a command line. The registration definition of the .pspz2 package sets these values:

Field Value Plugin name Pandora Azure Storage Description Take data from azure storage Plugin type Standard (plugin_type = 0) Maximum timeout 20 seconds Plugin command The pandora_azure file of the package Plugin parameters -c " _field1_ " --agent_name " _field2_ " -g " _field3_ " Modules provided 0 (total_modules_provided = 0)

The definition declares three macros. The format has no per-macro type, and all three have hide = 0, so the console shows the three fields in clear text:

Macro Required Default Hide Description and help _field1_ Yes, according to its description /var/www/html/pandora_console/attachment/plugin/pandora_azure.conf No Conf path (obligatory). Help: Path conf _field2_ No _agentname_ No Agent name (optional). Help: Name of the agent. The default is the console macro replaced with the name of the agent that holds the module _field3_ No azure No group (optional). Help: Pandora FMS Target Group

The registered parameters do not include --tentacle_address or --as_agent_plugin, so a module run started from this definition prints the module XML on standard output. To make each run deliver its agents itself, add the delivery option to Plugin parameters, for example:

-c " _field1_ " --agent_name " _field2_ " -g " _field3_ " --tentacle_address 127.0.0.1

Each plugin field is a configuration value, not a service selection: the services are enabled in the configuration file, so one registered plugin serves every account whose file you reference. The maximum timeout of 20 seconds is low for a run that queries every service; raise it if the run reaches the timeout. See Scheduling and runtime.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from a terminal, passing the configuration file after -c. In the default mode it prints the modules of every enabled service:

./pandora_azure -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The run executes once and exits. A successful run prints <module> blocks and nothing on standard error. The sample below shows the shape of the output for the account service, with one data point per module:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[UsedCapacity]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1099511627776.0]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[2026-10-26 09:00:00+00:00 The amount of storage used by the storage account.]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[bytes]]></unit>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Transactions]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <datalist>
    <data>
        <value><![CDATA[The Transactions at 2026-10-26 09:05:00+00:00 is 142.0]]></value>
    </data>
    <description><![CDATA[The number of requests made to a storage service or the specified API operation.]]></description>
</module>

The sample is built from the module definitions of the addon; it is not a captured run, because the values depend on the account.

To check the server-side path, run it with --as_agent_plugin 1 and a throwaway data folder, then inspect the file:

mkdir -p /tmp/azure-storage-check
./pandora_azure -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --as_agent_plugin 1 --data_dir /tmp/azure-storage-check
ls /tmp/azure-storage-check

A successful run prints 1 once per enabled service, and the folder contains one <agent name>.<epoch seconds>.data document per enabled service. The Data Lake Storage service is the exception described in Limitations. The file name uses the --agent_name value followed by the service suffix, so the default names are Azure_Monitor.Azure_Storage_Account_Metrics.<epoch>.data and Azure_Monitor.Blob_Service_Metrics.<epoch>.data.

In Pandora FMS, after the first delivered run, the agents appear with their modules. The account agent carries UsedCapacity and the six string modules; each service agent carries its capacity modules and its own six string modules. See Understand the results.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
A run creates one agent per enabled service, and the service suffix is appended to the --agent_name value without a separator:

Service switch Agent name suffix Default agent name account_agent Azure_Storage_Account_Metrics Azure_Monitor.Azure_Storage_Account_Metrics blobservice_agent Blob_Service_Metrics Azure_Monitor.Blob_Service_Metrics queueservice_agent Queue_Service_Metrics Azure_Monitor.Queue_Service_Metrics fileservice_agent File_Service_Metrics Azure_Monitor.File_Service_Metrics tableservice_agent Tables_Service_Metrics Azure_Monitor.Tables_Service_Metrics datalakestorage_agent Datalake_Storage_Service_Metrics Azure_Monitor.Datalake_Storage_Service_Metrics

The agent_data header sets agent_mode to 1 and takes the group from -g (Azure when the option is absent), and the alias from the same value as the name. The plugin does not set an agent interval: interval travels empty in the header.

The File service agent carries the description Blob Service Metrics, the same text as the Blob agent. See Limitations.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Every service publishes two kinds of module:

  • Capacity and count modules are generic_data. They carry the value returned for one metric, with the unit bytes when the metric is a size. They only appear when Azure returns data for that metric.
  • Rate and latency modules are generic_data_string with a datalist. Each entry is the text The <metric> at <timestamp> is <value>, one per data point of the last hour, so a run normally writes about twelve entries. These modules are created even when Azure returns no data, in which case the datalist arrives empty.

The account-level set is UsedCapacity, Transactions, Ingress, Egress, SucessServerLatency, SuccessE2ELatency and Availity. Each service repeats the six rate, latency and availability modules with its own suffix, for example Transactions_blobs or Availity_tables. The exhaustive list is in Agents and modules.

The module names are the ones the addon publishes, including the spellings SucessServerLatency and Availity. Alerts, reports and dashboards must use those exact names.

A capacity module is created once per data point returned, and every entry has the same name. A capacity query over one hour with a sixty-minute granularity normally returns one or two points, so the same module name can appear twice in one document. See Limitations.

docs.title: Scheduling and runtime
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state between runs: every execution queries Azure at that moment. The run can be repeated manually at any time.
  • A run with all six services enabled makes 57 Azure Monitor requests, one per metric, one after another: 7 for the account, 10 for Blob, 9 for Queue, 12 for File, 9 for Table and 10 for Data Lake Storage. The registration definition declares a maximum timeout of 20 seconds, which a full run can exceed; raise the timeout in the console or enable only the services you need.
  • In server mode, schedule the plugin from Pandora FMS or from cron. The plugin does not set the agent interval itself: interval travels empty in the agent_data header.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No endpoint option. Authentication and metric queries go to the default Microsoft endpoints, so a sovereign or custom cloud cannot be configured.
  • No proxy option, and the plugin does not retry. A failed request ends the run with the exception that produced it; repeating the collection is up to the next scheduled run.
  • Data Lake delivery is inverted. With --as_agent_plugin 1 and no Tentacle address, the Data Lake Storage service prints its modules on standard output instead of writing its document, while the other five services write theirs. Use --tentacle_address to deliver all six on the server side.
  • The delivery option is named after the opposite mode. --as_agent_plugin 1 produces the server-side document; the default mode is the agent plugin one.
  • --prefix_module has no effect. The option is accepted and ignored: it does not prefix module names, and the modules keep the names of Agents and modules.
  • One account per configuration file. The file holds one set of resource IDs, so monitoring several accounts needs one file and one plugin run per account.
  • No secret protection. The client secret is stored in clear text in the configuration file.
  • Capacity entries can repeat. A metric that returns more than one data point produces several modules with the same name in the same document.
  • The File agent carries the Blob description. Both agents report Blob Service Metrics.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The run prints a traceback and exits with status 1 — an Azure call failed. The usual causes are a wrong or expired client secret, a wrong tenant or client ID, and a resource ID the identity cannot read. The traceback names the failing call.
  • The run stops with NameError — a mandatory key is missing from the configuration file: one of tenant_id, client_id, secret, or one of the six <service>_agent switches. A line containing # is skipped as a comment, so a secret with # in it produces this error.
  • The run stops with ValueError — a <service>_agent value is not an integer. Use 1 or 0.
  • The run stops with IndexError — a line contains a known key name but no : separator, so the plugin finds no value to read. Use key:value.
  • Authentication fails although the secret looks correct — the value is truncated at the first : because the parser keeps only the second fragment of the line. A secret that contains : cannot be used from this file.
  • A service produces no capacity modules — Azure returned no data for those metrics. Traffic, latency and availability modules still appear, with an empty datalist.
  • Could not write file: ... — the data_dir folder does not exist or is not writable by the user that runs the plugin. The document is created with an exclusive name <agent name>.<epoch seconds>.data; a second run of the same service within the same second fails with this message.
  • Tentacle error on standard error with 1 on standard output — the Tentacle delivery failed, and the run still prints 1 and exits with status
  • Check that tentacle_client is in PATH and that the address and port reach the Tentacle server. The document stays in data_dir when the send fails.
  • No output at all — every <service>_agent switch is 0.

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text:
./pandora_azure -c <PATH_TO_CONFIG> [--agent_name <AGENT_NAME>] [-g <GROUP>]
    [--data_dir <PATH>] [--as_agent_plugin <0|1>]
    [--tentacle_address <TARGET_HOST>] [--tentacle_port <PORT>]
    [--prefix_module <PREFIX>]
Option Required Default Description -c, --conf Yes — Path to the configuration file. Without it the run stops with the usage message and exit status 2 --agent_name No Azure_Monitor. Prefix of the agent names. The service suffix is appended without a separator -g, --group No Azure Pandora FMS group assigned to the created agents --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Folder where the agent_data documents are written --as_agent_plugin No 0 1 writes the documents into data_dir and prints 1; any other value prints the modules on standard output. The Data Lake Storage service reverses this rule; see Limitations --tentacle_address No — Tentacle server address. When set, each document is delivered with the Tentacle client --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port, passed to the client as -p --prefix_module No — Accepted and ignored. It does not prefix module names -h, --help No — Prints the option summary and exits

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
Key Required Default Description tenant_id Yes — Microsoft Entra tenant ID of the app registration client_id Yes — Client ID of the app registration secret Yes — Client secret value. docs.title: Cisco Inventory configuration
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Cisco Inventory configuration addon reads the running configuration of a Cisco network device and stores it in the Pandora FMS inventory of an agent. Each execution connects to the device over SSH, enters privileged (enable) mode, disables terminal pagination, runs show running-config, and writes the returned configuration to standard output. Pandora FMS stores that text as the value of the inventory module that runs the addon.

The addon is an inventory collector, not a monitoring plugin: it does not create agents or monitoring modules. It produces one text result per execution, and the inventory module decides which agent receives it. For an addon that runs an arbitrary command instead of the fixed show running-config, see Inventory SSH plugin.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions A Cisco device whose CLI accepts enable, terminal length 0 and show running-config Required These are the commands the addon issues on every run SSH access to the device on the default SSH port (22) Required The addon connects to the SSH service without a port option A device user allowed to enter privileged mode and run show running-config Required The addon enters enable mode before reading the configuration Cisco device models and IOS, IOS XE, IOS XR or NX-OS versions Not validated No model or firmware matrix has been recorded Host operating system that runs the inventory module Not validated No operating system matrix has been recorded

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the inventory module to the device, over SSH on the default port.
  2. Credentials: a device user and its SSH password, plus the enable password when the device requests one.
  3. The get-config executable on the host that runs the inventory module, with execute permission.
  4. Pandora FMS with an inventory module assigned to the agent that will store the configuration.

No component is installed on the Cisco device.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the addon from its Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.cisco_inventory_configuration

Extract the package and copy the get-config executable to a path readable and executable by the user that runs the inventory module, for example /usr/local/bin/get-config. Keep its execute permission:

chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/get-config

docs.title: Arguments and order
docs.text:
Pandora FMS runs the executable with positional arguments. Configure the inventory module so the values arrive in this order:

Position Argument Required Description 1 address Yes IP address or host name of the device 2 username Yes Device user 3 sshpassword Yes SSH password of that user 4 enablepassword Yes Enable password; use an empty value when the device does not request one 5 sleep No Seconds to wait after each command; default 5

The argument names are the names used by the executable's help. The inventory module passes values by position, so the order matters more than any label the console shows. If the inventory module always sends the fifth value, enter a number: an empty value is rejected because the argument is parsed as an integer. Omit the argument entirely to use the default.

docs.title: Enable mode
docs.text:
Every run sends enable and the enable password before reading the configuration. If the device does not ask for an enable password, pass an empty value in the fourth position:

./get-config <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> <PASSWORD> ""

If the device asks for one, put it in the same position:

./get-config <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> <PASSWORD> "<ENABLE_PASSWORD>"

The addon does not detect whether the enable step succeeded. A wrong enable password, or a user without privilege, is not reported as an enable failure: the module stores whatever the device returns, which can be an error message or an incomplete configuration.

docs.title: Register the inventory module
docs.text:
Create an inventory module in the Pandora FMS console and point it at the executable on its host. Add the module to the agent that will store the configuration, and enter the five values in the order above. Mark the SSH password and the enable password as hidden values where the console offers that option. If the console offers an inline-code mode, leave it disabled: the addon runs as an executable.

The module runs on the host of the agent to which it is assigned, so that host must reach the device. The addon does not copy anything to the device.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The SSH password and enable password are passed as command-line arguments. On a manual run they appear in the shell history and in the process list while the addon runs. In the console, they are stored in the inventory module configuration. Restrict access to the console and to the agent configuration.
  • The SSH session encrypts the credentials in transit. The addon accepts any SSH host key and does not verify it, so a man-in-the-middle on the network path can impersonate the device. Run the addon only from a trusted management network, or enforce device identity at the network layer.
  • The running configuration is stored as inventory data and can contain enable secret, user password hashes, SNMP communities, crypto keys and other sensitive values. Anyone who can read the agent inventory can read those values. Restrict inventory access accordingly.

The addon has no credential-file option, no port option, and no host-key verification option.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the executable manually from the host that will run the inventory module:

./get-config <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> <PASSWORD> ""

A successful run exits with status 0, prints the running configuration on standard output, and prints progress messages on standard error:

Connected. Enabling...
Now dumping running-config...

The last line of the response is removed; in a normal run it is the device prompt. The remaining text is the configuration that the inventory module stores.

With the default sleep of 5 seconds, the addon waits about 25 seconds per run before it finishes: it waits once after opening the shell, once after each of the enable, password and pagination steps, and once after show running-config. Allow a module timeout longer than that.

Then check the agent inventory. The module value is the configuration text returned by the device.

If the run prints an error or no configuration, see Operate and troubleshoot.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The addon stores the raw text of the running configuration. It does not parse the configuration into interfaces, routes, users or other objects, and it does not create one module per section: the complete text is the value of the inventory module.

  • The inventory value can be large. The addon reads a single response of up to about 1 MB; a configuration larger than that, or a device that returns its output in several slower blocks, can be truncated.
  • The addon always removes the last line of the response, assuming it is the device prompt. When the response does not end with a prompt, the last configuration line is lost.
  • The addon does not filter the configuration. Every line the device returns, except the last line it removes, is stored, including credentials and keys.
  • The addon does not validate that the text is a configuration. If the device returns an error message, the message is stored as the module value.
  • Each execution produces the configuration at that moment. The addon itself does not compare runs or report changes.

docs.title: Scheduling and timing
docs.text: Run the inventory module on the interval you need. Each execution opens a new SSH session and closes it at the end. The sleep value controls how long the addon waits after each command; increase it for slow devices or large configurations. Lower values make the run faster but can capture an incomplete response.

docs.title: Exit status and diagnostics
docs.text: Condition Status Output Successful capture 0 Configuration on standard output; progress messages on standard error SSH connection failure 1 Connection error: <reason> on standard error Missing or invalid positional argument 2 Usage summary on standard error

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• Connection error: ... — the device is unreachable, the SSH service is not on the default port, the user or password is wrong, or the device rejects the connection. Check the address, the SSH service and the credentials from the same host.
  • The output is a device error or an incomplete configuration — the enable step failed, the user lacks privilege, or the device does not accept terminal length 0. Check the enable password, the user privilege and the device CLI.
  • The output is empty — show running-config returned nothing, the session did not reach privileged mode, or the wait was too short. Increase sleep and run the command manually on the device.
  • The output is truncated — the configuration exceeded the single read of about 1 MB or the device needed more time. This version has no option to read further; retrieve the configuration with a narrower command outside the addon if you need the complete text.
  • The run never returns — the addon has no configurable connection or read timeout. A device that stops responding can leave the execution waiting. Use the inventory module timeout where the console provides one, and check the device.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No SSH port option: the addon uses the SSH default port.
  • No connection or read timeout option.
  • One response read of up to about 1 MB per run.
  • No credential file: credentials are positional arguments.
  • No host-key verification: any SSH host key is accepted.
  • No output filtering or redaction: the full configuration is stored.

docs.title: Command-line arguments
docs.text:
Argument Position Required Default Description address 1 Yes — IP address or host name of the Cisco device username 2 Yes — Device user sshpassword 3 Yes — SSH password enablepassword 4 Yes — Enable password; pass "" when the device does not request one sleep 5 No 5 Seconds to wait after each command

-h or --help prints the usage summary and exits.

docs.title: Execution and output
docs.text:
./get-config <TARGET_HOST> <USERNAME> <PASSWORD> <ENABLE_PASSWORD> [SLEEP]
Stream Content Standard output Running configuration, with CRLF normalized to LF and the last line removed Standard error Connected. Enabling..., Now dumping running-config..., or a connection error Exit status 0 on success, 1 on a connection error, 2 on an argument error

The addon uses the SSH default port and has no option to change it. It reads a single response of up to 999999 bytes; it does not loop to collect more.

docs.title: Citrix monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Citrix monitoring plugin collects the state of a Citrix server through the Pandora FMS Windows agent and prints it as Pandora FMS modules. Each run reads four groups of data from the server it runs on:

  • Performance counters. Every counter path listed in the counters file, sampled with Get-Counter.
  • Service state. For every Windows service display name listed in the services file, 1 while the service runs and 0 otherwise, queried through WMI.
  • Sessions. The number of active sessions the server currently reports.
  • Connected users. The number of logged-on user sessions the server currently reports.

The plugin runs as an agent plugin: the Pandora FMS Windows agent executes it at every agent interval and ingests the <module> blocks it writes to standard output. It has no server plugin mode, sends nothing over the network and delivers nothing through Tentacle: everything it reports comes from the server where the agent runs. The usual arrangement is therefore one agent per Citrix server, with the plugin installed next to that agent.

All of its configuration is a command line plus two plain-text lists. The plugin reads no other configuration file, keeps no state between runs and creates no agents of its own.

Citrix NetScaler is a different addon and is not covered by this page.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.citrix_monitoring_plugin, version 1.0 Documented target The Marketplace package version this page describes. See Addon identity Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions Windows Server 2008 with Citrix XenApp 6 Known compatible The vendor guide for this addon records that combination as the system where it was tested A Windows server with the Citrix components whose counters and services you monitor Required The shipped counter list names Citrix Presentation Server, Citrix Licensing and XenApp counter sets, and the shipped service list names Citrix XenApp services Windows PowerShell and the WMI service on the monitored server Required Prerequisite for the plugin; it is not a compatibility statement grep, gawk and wc in the PATH of the account that runs the plugin Required The service and session groups are computed with those tools; they are not part of Windows A PowerShell execution policy that allows the script to run Required Prerequisite for the agent to execute it Windows Server versions other than 2008 and Citrix versions other than XenApp 6 Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Pandora FMS agent versions Not validated The agent version is not recorded for this addon

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Windows Server host with the Citrix role or components you want to monitor. The counters and services in the shipped lists belong to Citrix Presentation Server / XenApp 6 and to Windows itself. A host without those components simply has no such counters: the plugin reports the Windows counters and the services whose display names match.
  2. Windows PowerShell and WMI enabled. The plugin is a PowerShell script and reads service state through WMI.
  3. grep, gawk and wc available in the PATH of the account that runs the plugin, on the monitored server. The shipped implementation uses them to extract the service state and to count sessions, and it has no fallback when they are missing.
  4. The Pandora FMS Windows agent, installed on the same Citrix server and configured to run agent plugins.
  5. A PowerShell execution policy that allows the script, as described in Permissions and execution policy.

No database, no API endpoint and no remote credential is involved: the plugin reads the local server.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the package from the Marketplace entry, whose download is limited to licensed users, and copy its files to the Citrix server:

  • The plugin script, Pandora_Plugin_Citrix.ps1.
  • The counter list, counters.txt.
  • The service list, services.txt.

Place them in any folder the agent account can read, normally the util folder of the agent installation, and keep the two lists together with the script: throughout this page <PATH_TO_CONFIG> is that folder.

The lists are ordinary text files that you edit. They are not generated by the plugin and the plugin never writes to them.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The plugin has no console screen and no configuration file of its own. To put it to work you add one module_plugin line to the agent configuration and write the two lists.

docs.title: Run the plugin from the agent
docs.text:
Add the plugin to the pandora_agent.conf of the agent installed on the Citrix server. One line is enough:

module_plugin "C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\Pandora_Plugin_Citrix.ps1 -perf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\counters.txt -serv <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\services.txt 2> <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\plugin_error.log
  • -File must be followed by the absolute path of the plugin script.
  • -perf receives the path of the counter list; -serv receives the path of the service list.
  • -ExecutionPolicy Bypass allows this process to run the script whatever the machine policy is. Remove it when the machine policy already allows the script; it has no effect when a Group Policy sets the execution policy.
  • 2> <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\plugin_error.log writes the diagnostics of the run to a file, because the agent only reads standard output. Without it, PowerShell's error output is lost.

Restart or reload the agent after editing the file. The agent executes the plugin at every agent interval and ingests its output as the modules of the agent itself.

The options of the plugin are independent, so the same line covers the supported combinations:

Command line Modules generated No parameters, or -perf perfcounters The usage summary only; no modules -perf <PATH> Counters as generic_data, services, sessions and users -perf <PATH> -inc <any value except incremental> Counters as generic_data_inc and generic_data, services, sessions and users -perf none Services, sessions and users; no counter modules -serv none Counters, sessions and users; no service modules -perf none -serv none Sessions and users only

-perf defaults to perfcounters, which is the value that prints the usage summary. That default is why the pure default invocation produces no modules: always pass the counter list, or none, explicitly.

docs.title: Write the counter list
docs.text:
The counter list is one performance counter path per line, in the \Object(Instance)\Counter syntax that Get-Counter accepts. A line that names a multi-instance object without an instance, or an object that the host does not have, cannot be sampled: check every line on the target server.

The shipped list monitors processor, memory, paging file and disk throughput, plus Citrix Presentation Server, Citrix Licensing and the IMA service. See Counter list for its exact content.

Two properties of the file matter in practice:

  • Trailing spaces. The shipped file ends most lines with a space. The path is passed as it is read, so remove the trailing space when a counter is not collected.
  • Localized counter names. Counter names follow the operating system language. On a non-English Windows the shipped paths do not resolve; list the local names instead.

To obtain the counters a server actually provides:

Get-Counter -ListSet * | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Paths > counters.txt

That file is a starting point: delete the counters you do not need and keep one per line.

docs.title: Write the service list
docs.text:
The service list is one Windows service display name per line, as shown in the Name column of the services console — not the short service name. The plugin builds a WMI query with the line verbatim, so the value must match exactly, with no trailing space and with the capitalization of the display name.

A line that matches no service still produces a module, with value 0, so a typo looks like a stopped service. See Service list for the shipped entries and their known quirks.

docs.title: Permissions and execution policy
docs.text:
• The agent account must be able to read the plugin script and the two list files, and to execute powershell.exe.
  • The PowerShell execution policy of the account must allow the script. This is normally solved by signing the script, by setting a policy that allows local scripts, or by passing -ExecutionPolicy Bypass in the invocation shown above.
  • No official source for this addon documents a required role or a narrower permission set. Grant the agent account only what the plugin uses: read the script and the two lists, execute powershell.exe, and read the local performance counters and the local WMI service data.
  • The plugin produces diagnostics on standard error, and those messages can include the path of the script and of the lists: keep the error log readable only by the agent account.

counters.txt and services.txt are plain text and can be deployed like any other agent file, for example with a file collection or a policy, so the same lists reach every Citrix server without editing them one by one there.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually on the Citrix server, from a PowerShell window, before you rely on the agent:

powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\Pandora_Plugin_Citrix.ps1 -perf <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\counters.txt -serv <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\services.txt

A successful run prints one <module> block per generated module on standard output and ends. The excerpt below shows the last two blocks, the pair the plugin always generates:

<module>
<name><![CDATA[Citrix Sessions]]></name>
<type><![CDATA[generic_data]]></type>
<description><![CDATA[Opened active sessions on server]]></description>
<data><![CDATA[3]]></data>
</module>
<module>
<name><![CDATA[Users_Connected]]></name>
<type><![CDATA[generic_data]]></type>
<description><![CDATA[Users connected to this server]]></description>
<data><![CDATA[3]]></data>
</module>

Citrix Sessions and Users_Connected are generated by every run that generates modules, so if they do not appear nothing else was generated either.

To read the usage summary, run the script with no parameters at all:

powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <PATH_TO_CONFIG>\Pandora_Plugin_Citrix.ps1

The plugin has no help option: -h is not a parameter of the script and only produces a PowerShell parameter error. The summary is the default behaviour of the script, because -perf starts at perfcounters.

In Pandora FMS, open the agent that runs the plugin and confirm that the module list of its last contact contains Citrix Sessions, Users_Connected, the Status of service ... modules and the PerfCounter ... modules.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The plugin generates the same module catalog on every run. The four groups answer different questions and fail independently:

  • Counters. One generic_data module per counter sample, named PerfCounter <counter path>. The path is the one the host returns, so the module name contains the object, the instance and — for many counters — the server name. Two servers never share these module names.
  • Services. One generic_proc module per line of the service list, named Status of service <display name>, with 1 when the extracted state is exactly Running and 0 in every other case, including a service that does not exist.
  • Sessions. Citrix Sessions, a generic_data module with the number of lines of query session that contain Active.
  • Users. Users_Connected, a generic_data module with the number of lines of quser that contain Active.

Neither count deduplicates accounts: both count active session lines, from two different Windows commands, so a user with two open sessions counts twice. When one command is unavailable, the corresponding module is the only indication.

The counter group and the service group are independent, and so are they from the session pair: a counter file that cannot be read leaves the counter group empty, a service file that cannot be read leaves the service group empty, and the session modules are still generated.

When a counter list is supplied, generic_data is the default module type. The generic_data_inc type is added only when -inc receives a value other than incremental, and it is added in addition to the absolute modules, not instead of them: both sets are named PerfCounter <counter path> and read the same file.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
• Every run is independent: the plugin samples the server, prints the modules and exits. There is no cache, no state and no service to restart.
  • The plugin has no interval of its own. The agent interval of the module_plugin line decides how often it runs.
  • There is no verbose or debug flag. The diagnostic channel is standard error, which the example invocation redirects to plugin_error.log.
  • The plugin resizes the console buffer at start-up, so it expects a console host. If a run started by the agent produces nothing while the same command works in an interactive PowerShell window, that difference is the first thing to check.
Symptom Cause and fix The output is the usage summary instead of modules -perf was left at its default perfcounters, or -perf perfcounters was passed. Pass the counter list path, or none. A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'h' The plugin has no -h. Run it with no parameters to print the summary. No PerfCounter module at all The counters file could not be read, or Get-Counter rejected every path. Check the path of the file and then the counter paths of Counter list on that server. Some counters are missing Those paths do not exist on that host, name a localized counter, or need an instance such as (_Total). Compare with the output of Get-Counter -ListSet *. A counter is not collected and its line ends with a space The path is passed exactly as written. Remove the trailing space. Every service reports 0 The display names do not match, or grep/gawk are not in the PATH. Compare a line of the list with the display name shown by the services console and check that both tools resolve. Get-Content : Cannot find path ...\services -serv was not passed, so the default value services was read as a file name. Pass the service list, or -serv none to skip that group. You cannot call a method on a null-valued expression and the run stops wc is missing, so the session counter has no value to trim. Add wc to the PATH. grep or gawk is not recognized The tool is not available to the agent account. Install it or add its folder to the PATH of that account. The agent creates no modules although the manual run prints them Check the -File path, the execution policy of the agent account, and the error log written by 2>. ... cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system The execution policy blocks the script. See Permissions and execution policy. Module names are not the ones in the list Counter modules are named after the path the host returns, which includes the object, the instance and the server name. That is expected.

The plugin does not set an exit status of its own and does not stop on the errors it produces: a run that cannot read a list file reports the error on standard error and finishes, so the agent does not detect the failure. Read plugin_error.log when a module stops updating.

docs.title: Addon identity
docs.text:
Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.citrix_monitoring_plugin Name Citrix monitoring plugin Version 1.0 Marketplace last update 2025-07-29 Category Miscelaneus License One; the download is limited to licensed users Package pandorafms.citrix_monitoring_plugin.1.0.zip Marketplace entry pandorafms.citrix_monitoring_plugin

The script prints its own revision banner, v1.1, 02 Aug 2014, when it shows the usage summary. That string is internal to the script and is not the version of the addon package, which is 1.0.

docs.title: Invocation parameters
docs.text:
Option Required Default Description -perf No perfcounters Path of the counter list. Any value other than perfcounters and none is read as a file. none skips the counter group. The default value perfcounters only prints the usage summary. -serv No services Path of the service list. Any value other than none is read as a file. none skips the service group. The default value services is a bare word, not a path, so pass the file explicitly. -inc No incremental Mode selector, not a path. With the default value incremental the counter modules are generic_data. With any other value the plugin also emits one generic_data_inc module per counter, read from the -perf file, while the generic_data modules are still emitted.

The options are PowerShell parameters: they are case-insensitive, each one takes exactly one value, and a name the script does not define is rejected before the run starts. The script defines no -h, -help or -verbose.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Command line Counter modules Service modules Citrix Sessions and Users_Connected No parameters None (usage summary only) None None -perf perfcounters None (usage summary only) None None -perf <PATH> generic_data From -serv Yes -perf <PATH> -inc <value other than incremental> generic_data_inc and generic_data From -serv Yes -perf none None From -serv Yes -perf <PATH> -serv none generic_data None Yes -perf none -serv none None None Yes

Citrix Sessions and Users_Connected are generated by every run that gets past the usage summary, whatever the counter and service options are.

Points to check against the target server:

  • \Processor(*) produces one module per processor instance.
  • \Paging File\% Usage names a multi-instance object without an instance; the host exposes it as \Paging File(_Total)\% Usage.
  • \Memory\Pages /sec contains a space in the counter name; the Windows counter is \Memory\Pages/sec.
  • \PhysicalDisk(_Total)\% Free Space names a counter of logical disks; physical disks do not expose % Free Space.
  • The six Avg. Disk Sec/... lines contain a space between the backslash and the counter name. Remove it when the counter is not collected.
  • Every line of the shipped file ends with a space. The path is passed as read, so trim the line when the counter is not collected.
  • The Citrix MetaFrame Presentation Server and Citrix Licensing sets exist only where that Citrix component is installed.
  • Every path uses English counter names.
