Points to check against the target server:

  • The entries are display names. ImaSrv, for example, is the short name of Citrix Independent Management Architecture.
  • Several lines of the shipped file end with a space, and the value is used verbatim: trim the line when the service reports 0 although it runs.
  • The sixth entry ends with Estados Servicios, which is not a Windows display name pattern. It is used verbatim, so replace it with the exact display name of that service on your server.
  • Server, Workstation, Netlogon, Print Spooler and Remote Procedure Call (RPC) are operating system services. They are monitored with the same mechanism as the Citrix ones.
  • The list is a default, not a limit: any display name you add becomes a module.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
Module name Type Value PerfCounter <counter path> generic_data, or generic_data_inc for the incremental set The sampled value of that counter Status of service <display name> generic_proc 1 when the extracted state is Running, 0 otherwise Citrix Sessions generic_data Number of query session lines that contain Active Users_Connected generic_data Number of quser lines that contain Active

Each module is written as a <module> block with name, type, description and data elements, and no <agent> element: the modules belong to the agent that executes the plugin.

docs.title: Output and exit status
docs.text:
Condition Behavior Normal run <module> blocks on standard output; the process ends with status 0 Usage summary path The banner, the parameter list and the usage example on standard output; no modules Counter list unreadable or counters refused PowerShell error on standard error, no counter modules, the rest of the run continues Service list unreadable PowerShell error on standard error, no service modules, the rest of the run continues grep or gawk missing Each service reports 0; the error appears on standard error wc missing The run stops at the session count with You cannot call a method on a null-valued expression Undefined parameter The run ends before generating modules, with the PowerShell parameter error on standard error

The script never calls exit. A run that only produces errors on standard error still finishes successfully, which is why the invocation redirects standard error to a file.

docs.title: Citrix NetScaler monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The plugin monitors a Citrix NetScaler (ADC) appliance from Pandora FMS through the NITRO REST stat API. Each run asks the appliance which statistic objects it exposes, reads the ones listed in the configuration file and creates Pandora FMS agents from the result: one agent per object returned for each configured service, plus a status module on the main agent.

The plugin is a standalone executable run once per invocation and then exits. It takes a single configuration file, keeps no state between runs, and starts no service. It is not a Discovery plugin: Pandora FMS does not drive it from a task.

The agents are never printed for an agent to collect. Every run builds Pandora FMS agent XML documents and delivers them, either through Tentacle or by copying them into a local data folder. The only Pandora FMS modules the plugin produces on standard output are the ones of a failed run (see Verify).

Nothing is installed on the appliance. The plugin reads statistics with HTTP GET requests authenticated by NITRO headers, so the account only needs read access.

The module catalogue is not fixed. The modules of an object are the statistic fields the appliance returns for it, filtered by the list in the configuration file, so the same plugin adapts to the fields a device or firmware exposes.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its entries are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions; it is a catalogue-wide statement covering this addon, not a test record A Citrix NetScaler appliance exposing the NITRO stat API at ns_url Required The catalogue request targets <ns_url>, and each service read appends /<service> A NetScaler account allowed to read the stat API Required The credentials travel in the X-NITRO-USER and X-NITRO-PASS headers of every request A Perl runtime providing LWP::UserAgent and JSON Required The plugin does not start without them Network access from the plugin host to the appliance Required Statistics are read over HTTP or HTTPS from that host A writable temporary directory Required Each agent document is written to temp before it is delivered A delivery destination: the Pandora FMS Tentacle service, or a writable local data folder Required mode selects one of the two NetScaler models and firmware versions Not validated No model or firmware matrix has been recorded for this addon. The legacy guide names NSMPX-10500 as the platform it was tested on; no current record confirms it Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A Citrix NetScaler appliance whose NITRO stat API answers on the configured URL, reachable from the host that runs the plugin.
  2. An account on the appliance allowed to read the statistics of the services you want to monitor. Use a dedicated read-only account.
  3. A host to run the plugin with the Perl runtime and the two modules listed in Compatibility.
  4. A destination for the generated agents: the Pandora FMS Tentacle service, with the Tentacle client available, or a local data folder that the Pandora FMS server reads.
  5. Write access to the temp directory and, in local mode, to local_folder.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the addon from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.citrix_netscaler

The addon consists of the citrix_netscaler.pl executable and its configuration file citrix_netscaler.conf. Copy both to the host that will run the plugin and make the executable runnable. The configuration file can live anywhere, because every execution passes its path as the only argument.

The sample file ships with example hosts, an example account and example Tentacle and API addresses. Replace them before running the plugin (see Configure), and restrict the file permissions: it holds the appliance password in plain text.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin takes one argument, the path of its configuration file, and no command-line options:

./citrix_netscaler.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

The equivalent explicit form, useful when the executable bit is not set or the interpreter must be selected by hand:

perl citrix_netscaler.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

There is no -h or --help option: a run without any argument prints the usage summary and exits with status 1.

docs.title: Configuration file format
docs.text:
The file is plain text with one key = value per line:

  • A blank line is ignored.
  • A line whose first character is # is a comment. A # anywhere else is part of the value, so trailing comments are not supported.
  • The key and the value are trimmed of leading and trailing blanks.
  • A key repeated with a scalar value keeps the last occurrence.
  • ns_services is the exception: every occurrence adds one service.
  • The parser accepts any key. A key the plugin does not read has no effect (see Accepted but not applied).
  • A line without = is stored with an empty value instead of being reported.

This is a complete configuration for a first run that delivers with Tentacle:

ns_url = https://<NETSCALER_HOST>/nitro/v1/stat/
ns_user = <USERNAME>
ns_pass = <PASSWORD>

ns_services = system;0
ns_services = lbvserver;1

modules_list = state,status,cpuusage,memusagepcnt

agent_name = netscaler-main
agent_interval = 300

mode = tentacle
tentacle_ip = <PANDORA_FMS_URL>
tentacle_port = 41121

The same collection copied into a local data folder instead:

ns_url = https://<NETSCALER_HOST>/nitro/v1/stat/
ns_user = <USERNAME>
ns_pass = <PASSWORD>

ns_services = system;0
ns_services = lbvserver;1

agent_name = netscaler-main

mode = local
local_folder = /var/spool/pandora/data_in

docs.title: Connection and credentials
docs.text:
• ns_url is the base URL of the stat API, for example https://<NETSCALER_HOST>/nitro/v1/stat/. The plugin requests that URL once to obtain the catalogue of statistic objects, then appends / and the service name for each read, so the value must include the API path and not only the host.
  • Both http:// and https:// URLs are accepted. Use HTTPS: over plain HTTP the headers carrying the credentials and the collected statistics travel unencrypted.
  • The credentials are sent as the X-NITRO-USER and X-NITRO-PASS headers on every request.
  • The plugin exposes no certificate option. An HTTPS device certificate must be trusted by the host that runs the plugin, including any private certification authority in its trust store.
  • lwp_timeout sets the HTTP request timeout in seconds. It is absent from the sample file, and with no value the plugin applies no explicit timeout, so a silent appliance can hold the run for as long as the HTTP client waits.
  • The HTTP client honours the http_proxy, https_proxy and no_proxy environment variables.
  • ns_pass is stored in plain text. Restrict the file to the user that runs the plugin, for example with chmod 600, and do not keep it in a shared directory.

docs.title: Services and modules to collect
docs.text:
ns_services selects what to read. Each line has the form ns_services=<service>;<value>:

  • <service> is the name of a NITRO statistic object, such as system or lbvserver. It is compared with the catalogue the appliance returns, and a service the appliance does not list is skipped without an error.
  • <value> is 1 or 0 and only controls the parent of the generated agents: with 1 they declare the configured agent_name as their parent, with 0 (or with no value) they are generated without a parent.

There is no default service. A configuration file without any ns_services line reads the catalogue and nothing else, so the run only reports the status module on the main agent.

modules_list filters the statistic fields of each object. It is a comma-separated list of exact, case-sensitive field names, without blanks:

modules_list = state,status,cpuusage,memusagepcnt

Each name in the list becomes a module only when the object returns that field. The sample file suggests state,status,vbshealth,primaryaddress,cpuusage,disk1avail,memusagepcnt,powersupply2status; adjust the list to the fields your appliance and firmware actually return. When modules_list is absent or empty, the filter is disabled and every field of the object becomes a module, including its name field.

The filter applies to the stat fields of the object itself. The stat-bindings modules described in Understand the results are not filtered: they are generated for every service the appliance answers with a list of objects, whatever its value.

ns_service_prefix prepends a fixed text to the name of the agents generated for the objects of a multi-instance service, which helps when several appliances deliver to the same Pandora FMS installation. A single-instance service is named after the value the appliance returns.

docs.title: Agents and delivery
docs.text:
agent_name names the main agent and is also the parent declared by the object agents of a service configured with value 1. It defaults to NetScaler, so set it explicitly for every monitored appliance.

mode selects how the documents leave the host:

  • mode = tentacle (the default) writes the document to temp and sends it with the Tentacle client: tentacle_client -v -a tentacle_ip -p tentacle_port tentacle_opts <file>. The document is deleted after a successful transfer. tentacle_client defaults to tentacle_client, resolved through PATH; set it to a full path when the client is not in the search path. tentacle_opts is inserted verbatim into that command line, so treat its value as trusted operator input. tentacle_ip takes the address of the Pandora FMS server, without scheme or path.
  • Any other value of mode, including local, copies the document into local_folder and deletes the temporary copy on success. local_folder has no default; without it the copy fails and the plugin reports the error on standard error.

temp is the directory used to write the document before delivery. It defaults to /tmp and must exist and be writable by the user that runs the plugin.

A failed Tentacle transfer is retried once, after one second. If the second attempt also fails, the document is discarded and the plugin prints [<file>] discarted on standard error; the exit status of the run is not affected.

docs.title: Schedule the run
docs.text:
The plugin does not schedule itself. Run it from cron with the period you want to monitor at, for example every five minutes. This entry assumes the executable is installed in the Pandora FMS server plugin directory:

*/5 * * * * root /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/citrix_netscaler.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

agent_interval only declares the agent interval to Pandora FMS; it does not change when the plugin runs. Keep the cron period and agent_interval aligned so the declared interval matches the real data rate.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin once from a terminal:

cd /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin
./citrix_netscaler.pl <PATH_TO_CONFIG>
echo $?

A successful run is quiet: the plugin prints nothing on standard output and exits with status 0. On success:

  • With mode = tentacle, the document is written to temp, transferred and deleted. Nothing remains in temp for the finished agent.
  • With mode = local, a file named <agent>_<epoch>.data appears in local_folder, and the copy in temp is removed.
  • In Pandora FMS, the configured main agent appears with the Plugin message module, followed by the object agents of the services you configured.

When the first request to ns_url fails, the run takes the opposite path: it prints the agent document on standard output, still delivers it, and exits with status 1. That document holds a single module:

<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<agent_data description='' version='' os_version='NetScaler Plugin' os_name='NetScaler Plugin' timestamp='2026/10/26 09:00:00' interval='300' parent_agent_name='' agent_name='netscaler-main'>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Plugin message]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[0]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[No response from https://netscaler.example.com/nitro/v1/stat/]]></description>
    <module_interval><![CDATA[1]]></module_interval>
</module>
</agent_data>

The same document shape is delivered with Plugin message set to 1 and the description Execution OK on a successful run, without being printed. Attribute order inside <agent_data> is not significant and can change between runs.

docs.title: Agents generated
docs.text:
Every generated agent declares NetScaler Plugin as both operating system and operating system version, an empty version, the timestamp of the run, the configured agent_interval and the configured agent_desc as description.

Agent Agent name Parent Main agent agent_name, NetScaler when it is empty None Object of a multi-instance service, value 1 ns_service_prefix + the name field of the object The main agent Object of a multi-instance service, value 0 ns_service_prefix + the name field of the object None Single-instance service, such as system The name field returned for the service; ns_service_prefix + agent_name when it is empty Per the service value

Because a single-instance service names its agent after the appliance, the agent called agent_name usually holds only the Plugin message module, and the device statistics live in the agent named after the appliance. That is the documented behaviour, not a missing module: the status module is always delivered on the configured main agent.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
Module Type Condition Meaning Plugin message generic_proc Always, on the main agent 1 when the run completed and the catalogue was read; 0 when the request to ns_url failed, with the failing URL in the description <field> generic_data when the value is numeric, generic_data_string otherwise The object returns the field and modules_list allows it, or the filter is disabled The statistic value exactly as the appliance returns it <object> statbindings generic_data_string Multi-instance service OK when the stat-bindings request returned valid JSON, UNREACHABLE when it did not, with the cause in the description <object> <binding> generic_data when the state is numeric, generic_data_string otherwise Multi-instance service and a valid stat-bindings response The state of each server bound to the object; the description carries its Primary IP Address

Statistic field names are the identifiers the appliance returns, so the module names depend on the device and firmware. A module name is not prefixed with the service name: it is the field name alone.

Every module carries <module_interval> with module_interval (1 in the sample file) and <module_group> with module_group (NetScaler by default, empty in the sample file). The keys module_tags and agent_group are accepted but have no effect, so the generated documents carry no tags and no group.

docs.title: Run behaviour
docs.text:
• The plugin runs once, reads the appliance and exits. It keeps no state, so two consecutive runs return the values the appliance reports at their own time.
  • Standard output is empty on success. Diagnostics, copy errors and discarded transfers go to standard error. There is no log file and no debug or verbose option.
  • A delivery failure does not change the exit status: cron reports success even when the document was discarded. Use the freshness of the agents and of Plugin message in Pandora FMS, not the exit status alone, to confirm delivery.
  • Set lwp_timeout on networks where the appliance can be slow to answer; without it the run waits for the HTTP client default.
  • Store the configuration file with restrictive permissions: it contains the appliance password.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The usage summary is printed and the status is 1 — the plugin received no argument. Pass the configuration file path.
  • Nothing is reported about a wrong configuration path — the plugin does not diagnose an unreadable configuration file: it continues with empty values and fails later, typically on the first request. Check the path in the cron entry.
  • Plugin message reports 0 with No response from ... — the request to ns_url did not return a successful JSON response. Check the URL and its API path, that the appliance is reachable from the plugin host, that the account can authenticate, and that the device certificate is trusted.
  • The run stops with an error and delivers nothing — the appliance answered with a body that is not the expected JSON, and decoding it ends the run before any agent is built. Confirm that ns_url points to the stat API and not to a login page or another endpoint.
  • A service in ns_services produces no agent — its name is not in the catalogue the appliance returns, or it was written with different case or blanks. Compare the name with the objects the device exposes.
  • The run stops after some agents were delivered — a service listed in the catalogue answered with an error, and this version does not recover from it: the remaining services are not processed. Correct the credentials or the service permissions and run the plugin again.
  • <object> statbindings reports UNREACHABLE — the stat-bindings request failed or returned invalid JSON; the rest of the object modules are still generated.
  • <object> statbindings reports OK and no per-server module appears — the response contains no bound server for that object.
  • An object agent holds only a few modules — modules_list does not include the fields the object returns, or the appliance does not return them. Remove the filter to see every field in a test run.
  • No document reaches Pandora FMS — check that temp exists and is writable, and then the destination: tentacle_client, tentacle_ip and tentacle_port for Tentacle, or an existing writable local_folder for local mode. The cause is printed on standard error.
  • There was a problem copying local file to ... — mode is not tentacle and the copy into local_folder failed. Check that the directory exists and is writable.
  • [...] discarted — both Tentacle attempts failed and the document was removed. Check the Tentacle service and the client path.
  • The values look stale — the plugin always reports what the appliance returns at run time. Check that cron still runs it and that agent_interval matches the cron period.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description ns_url Yes Empty Base URL of the NITRO stat API, with scheme and API path. The plugin requests it to read the catalogue and appends /<service> for each service read ns_user Yes Empty Account used to read the stat API, sent in the X-NITRO-USER header ns_pass Yes Empty Password of that account, sent in the X-NITRO-PASS header. Stored in plain text ns_services Yes, at least one None Repeatable. ns_services=<service>;<value>, where <value> is 1 to declare agent_name as parent, 0 or empty for no parent modules_list No Empty, filter disabled Comma-separated allowlist of statistic field names, exact and case-sensitive, without blanks ns_service_prefix No Empty Text prepended to the names of the agents generated for the objects of a multi-instance service agent_name No NetScaler Name of the main agent and parent reference of the object agents agent_desc No Empty Description written into every generated agent agent_interval No 300 Agent interval declared to Pandora FMS, in seconds module_interval No 1 Value written as module_interval in every module module_group No NetScaler Value written as module_group in every module mode No tentacle tentacle delivers with the Tentacle client; any other value copies the document into local_folder local_folder Yes when mode is not tentacle Empty Destination folder for the copied agent documents tentacle_ip Yes when mode = tentacle Empty Address of the Pandora FMS Tentacle server tentacle_port No 41121 Port of the Pandora FMS Tentacle server tentacle_client No tentacle_client Tentacle client to execute, resolved through PATH when it is a bare name tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options inserted verbatim into the Tentacle command line temp No /tmp Directory where the agent document is written before delivery. Must exist and be writable lwp_timeout No Not set HTTP request timeout, in seconds. With no value the plugin applies no explicit timeout

Keys and values are trimmed; a repeated scalar key keeps its last value, and ns_services accumulates.

docs.title: Accepted but not applied
docs.text:
These keys are read without error but have no effect on the generated documents in this version:

Name Effect module_tags No tags are written into the modules agent_group The agent document carries no group log No log file is written api_url, api_user, api_user_pass, api_pass The Pandora FMS API is never called; no group or tag is created in the console

The sample configuration file still lists them, so removing or keeping them changes nothing.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text: Condition Behaviour No argument Prints the usage summary and exits with status 1 One argument Runs with that file as configuration More than one argument Only the first is read; the rest are ignored Any option, such as -h or --help Treated as the configuration file path; there is no option parsing The argument names an unreadable file The run continues with empty configuration values and fails later, without a diagnostic about the file

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Variable Effect http_proxy, https_proxy, no_proxy Used by the HTTP client for the requests to the appliance

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text: Module Type Emitted on Description Plugin message generic_proc agent_name 1 with Execution OK, or 0 with No response from <ns_url> Statistic field names returned by the object generic_data or generic_data_string Agent of the object One module per allowed field and returned value <object> statbindings generic_data_string Agent of the object, multi-instance service OK or UNREACHABLE <object> <binding> generic_data or generic_data_string Agent of the object, multi-instance service and valid response State of a bound server, with its primary IP address in the description

docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.citrix_netscaler Name Citrix NetScaler monitoring Version 1.0 Package pandorafms.citrix_netscaler.1.0.zip License One; the download is limited to licensed users Marketplace last update 2025-07-09 Downloads 1 Author Pandora FMS

docs.title: DB2 Remote plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use DB2 Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path. The Marketplace entry states that this addon is no longer actively maintained.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The DB2 Remote addon monitors IBM Db2 databases from Pandora FMS over TCP/IP. Nothing is installed on the database server: each execution opens one connection from the host that runs the addon, runs the statements you keep in a query file and publishes the result as Pandora FMS modules.

A run produces two kinds of output:

  • Query modules. One module per statement in the query file, with one data-list entry per row the statement returns.
  • Default performance modules. A fixed set of buffer pool and transaction log metrics, read from Db2 administrative views. They are enabled unless you disable them.

Every execution is one-shot: it connects, collects, delivers and exits. The addon keeps no state between runs, so an execution at any moment reports the values the database has at that moment.

The modules reach Pandora FMS either as module XML on standard output, for a Pandora FMS agent to ingest, or as agent data documents written into a Pandora FMS data folder (see Configure).

DB2 Discovery (pandorafms.db2) is a different addon: it runs from the Discovery task wizard and generates one agent per database automatically. The DB2 Remote plugin is configured per execution and publishes the modules produced by the statements you write. See DB2 Discovery.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.db2_remote, version 1.0 Documented target Version of the Marketplace entry, also printed by the addon's usage summary. See Addon identity TCP access from the host that runs the addon to the Db2 listener (default port 50000) Required The addon connects with --hostname, --port and --protocol A Db2 user allowed to read every object your statements read Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement A python3 interpreter with the ibm-db driver 3.1.4 Required The package's requirements.txt pins ibm-db==3.1.4 Db2 server versions and platforms Not validated No version matrix is recorded for this addon Operating system of the host that runs the addon Not validated No operating system is recorded for version 1.0 Pandora FMS release Not validated No release-specific validation record exists. The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later

The Marketplace entry states that this addon is no longer actively maintained or updated, and points to the alternatives published in its library.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the addon to the Db2 listener, by default on TCP port 50000.
  2. A Db2 user and its password, allowed to read every object your statements read and, when default metrics are enabled, the administrative views listed in Database access.
  3. A host to run the addon: the Pandora FMS server for a console server plugin, a host with a Pandora FMS agent for agent plugin mode, or any host whose data folder the Pandora FMS data server reads.
  4. A python3 interpreter with the ibm-db driver installed, in the version pinned by the package's requirements.txt.
  5. A Pandora FMS installation that receives the output: the plugin server that runs the registered plugin, the agent that runs it, or the data server that reads the data folder.
  6. Write permission on the data folder for the user that runs the addon, when documents are delivered there.
  7. A query file. The addon reads it on every execution, including runs that only need the default metrics (see Known limitations).

docs.title: Database access
docs.text:
The addon reads only what your statements and the default metrics ask for:

Read When The objects your own statements read Every execution SYSCAT.BUFFERPOOLS, SYSIBMADM.BP_HITRATIO, SYSIBMADM.LOG_UTILIZATION Default metrics enabled, which is the default

Db2 defines which authority each administrative view requires. No official source for this addon documents a narrower grant, so give the user the minimum Db2 accepts for the reads you enable.

The addon executes the statement text exactly as written and does not restrict it to SELECT. Use a dedicated user with read-only access and keep only read statements in the query file.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.db2_remote

Copy the addon script pandora_db2.py and its example query file db2.conf to the host that will run it. For a console server plugin the recommended folder is /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/.

Install the driver pinned by the package's requirements.txt (ibm-db==3.1.4) for the interpreter that will run the addon.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text: The addon has no configuration file of its own: everything is a command-line option, and the queries live in the separate file named by --conf.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
A run needs the host, the database, a user and a password:

python3 pandora_db2.py --hostname <TARGET_HOST> --port 50000 --database <DB_NAME> \
    --uid <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --as_agent_plugin 1

--port defaults to 50000 and --protocol to TCPIP, so both can be omitted. The addon builds a complete connection string from these options, so no local Db2 client, catalog entry or DSN is needed on the host that runs it.

--password on the command line is kept in the shell history and is visible in the process list while the run lasts. The addon has no credentials-file option in this version; in the console, mark the field that holds the password as hidden (see Register the plugin in the console).

docs.title: Choose the delivery mode
docs.text:
Mode Option Behavior Data folder (default) none Writes one <agent_name>.<timestamp>.data document into --data_dir (default /var/spool/pandora/data_in/) for every document it produces, and prints 1 per document Agent plugin --as_agent_plugin 1 Prints one <module> block per module on standard output and writes no files Tentacle --tentacle_address <ADDRESS> Configured with --tentacle_address and --tentacle_port; it does not deliver in version 1.0 (see Known limitations)

--tentacle_address takes precedence over --as_agent_plugin; any --as_agent_plugin value other than 1 selects the data folder.

Use agent plugin mode when a Pandora FMS agent runs the addon: the agent ingests the printed modules. Use the data folder when the plugin server runs it in the console and the local data server collects the documents.

--default_metrics is 1 by default; any other value publishes only the query modules.

docs.title: Define the queries
docs.text:
The query file has one statement per line, split into colon-separated fields:

name:statement:module_type[:description]

This is the example shipped with the package:

query_test:select * from department:generic_data:testing query
  • name becomes the module name, module_type the module type and the optional fourth field the module description. The first three fields are mandatory.
  • The statement cannot contain a colon. The line is split on every colon, so a : inside the statement shifts the type and the description and produces a different module without warning.
  • A line that contains # anywhere is skipped as a comment, not only a line that starts with #.
  • Blank lines are ignored.
  • _database_ is replaced by the connected database name in single quotes, so it can be used where a string literal is expected. With --database <DB_NAME>, the line select * from syscat.tables where tabschema = _database_ reaches the database as select * from syscat.tables where tabschema = '<DB_NAME>'.
  • Each statement produces one module. Every returned row becomes one entry of the module data list, holding the row as a column/value mapping.
  • Every statement in the file is executed on every run.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
A console server plugin runs the addon from the Pandora FMS server. The plugin server executes it, the addon writes its documents into the data folder and the data server ingests them, so the agents and their modules appear in the console.

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set the name, the plugin type Standard, an optional maximum timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the path to pandora_db2.py on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/pandora_db2.py.
  4. In Plugin parameters, pass the connection through the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... and keep the query file at a fixed path on the server:
--hostname _field1_ --port 50000 --database _field2_ --uid _field3_ --password _field4_ --conf /etc/pandora/plugins/db2.queries --agent_name db2-remote
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Db2 host name or IP address <TARGET_HOST> _field2_ Database name <DB_NAME> _field3_ Db2 user that runs the statements <USERNAME> _field4_ Password for that user; mark Hide value —

--agent_name names the agent that receives the query modules; without it the addon uses DB2, and the metrics agent is <agent_name>_metrics.

In this mode the module value is the text the addon prints, normally 1 per delivered document. An execution that has to deliver several documents is subject to the data folder limitation described in Known limitations.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the addon manually with --as_agent_plugin 1, so it prints the modules instead of writing files:

python3 pandora_db2.py --hostname <TARGET_HOST> --database <DB_NAME> \
    --uid <USERNAME> --password <PASSWORD> --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --as_agent_plugin 1

A successful run prints one <module> block per module and exits with status 0. The values below are illustrative; yours come from your database. This is the module produced by the example query:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[query_test]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <datalist>
    <data>
        <value><![CDATA[{'DEPTNO': 'A00', 'DEPTNAME': 'SPIFFY COMPUTER SERVICE DIV.'}]]></value>
    </data>
    </datalist>
    <description><![CDATA[testing query]]></description>
</module>

When the default metrics are enabled they are printed after the query modules, one block per metric:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[no_of_bufferpools_<DB_NAME>]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[3]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[count]]></unit>
</module>

With the default data folder delivery the same run prints 1 once per document and writes files named <agent_name>.<timestamp>.data in --data_dir:

/var/spool/pandora/data_in/db2-remote.<timestamp>.data

After the first scheduled execution, check the console:

  1. The agent named by --agent_name (default DB2) with one module per statement in the query file.
  2. The agent <agent_name>_metrics with the default performance modules.
  3. The value of the plugin module that triggered the execution.

The addon prints its usage summary, with a manual execution example, when it runs with -h.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
A run creates at most two agents. Both are assigned the group passed with --group, and both carry the description Agent generated by pandora_db2.

Agent Name Alias Content Condition Query agent --agent_name (default DB2) Same as the name One module per statement in the query file The query file has at least one statement Metrics agent <agent_name>_metrics <agent_name> The default performance modules --default_metrics 1

The metrics agent repeats the alias of the query agent, so the console shows the same alias for both agents.

docs.title: Query modules
docs.text: Each module is named after the first field of its line and typed with the third field. Its value is a data list with one entry per row, and each entry keeps the column names of the row visible in the module data. The module description is the fourth field, and it is empty when that field is absent.

docs.title: Default performance modules
docs.text: The metrics cover three groups: the number of buffer pools, the buffer pool read counters and the transaction log utilization. Every module name ends with the database name. The full list is in Generated modules.

docs.title: Run-time behavior
docs.text:
• One execution connects once, runs every statement of the query file in order, then the default metrics, delivers and exits.
  • The query modules are delivered before the metrics, so a metrics failure does not undo what the statements already published.
  • The addon has no verbose or debug option. Its output is the module XML with --as_agent_plugin 1, one 1 per document in the data folder mode, or an error message.
  • The addon keeps no state between executions. The query file is re-read on every run.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These are behaviors of version 1.0, documented as they are.

  • The query file is effectively mandatory. Every run reads --conf before anything else. Without it the run prints Error al conectarse ... and 0, exits with status 0 and publishes nothing, default metrics included. To collect only the default metrics, pass an empty query file.
  • Tentacle delivery does not work. With --tentacle_address the run writes the document into --data_dir and then stops with an unhandled error before sending anything, so no document reaches the Tentacle server. Use the data folder or the agent plugin mode.
  • Data folder documents can collide. Document names use one-second resolution (<agent_name>.<timestamp>.data) and are created exclusively. When a run produces several documents for the same agent within the same second and Pandora FMS has not collected the previous file yet, the write fails with ERROR - Could not write file: ... please check directory permissions and the remaining documents of the run are lost. A default-metrics run produces, with every metric available, seventeen documents for the metrics agent, ten of them with a module, so this is likely in that mode. Keep one document per run (--default_metrics 0 and a single statement) or run the addon in agent plugin mode, which writes no files.
  • Four collected metrics are not published. total_hit_ratio_percent, data_hit_ratio_percent, index_hit_ratio_percent and xda_hit_ratio_percent are read from the database, but no module is created for them.
  • A statement cannot contain a colon. The line format uses the colon as separator, so a statement with a colon is silently misread.
  • A malformed query line stops the run with status 0. A line with fewer than three fields prints It is mandatory to specify name, query and type! and ends the execution, including the statements that had not run yet.
  • A failed default-metrics query stops the metrics stage. If the user cannot read one of the three views, the stage ends with an unhandled error after the query modules were already delivered. Disable the metrics with --default_metrics 0 or grant the reads.
  • The usage summary shows a command that does not run as shipped. -h prints the manual execution as ./pandora_db2, but the distributed script is not executable on its own: invoke it through python3 pandora_db2.py.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: Symptom Cause and action no connection: followed by the driver error, status 1 The connection failed. Check the host, the port, the database name, the user and the password, and the network path to the Db2 listener Error al conectarse ... and then 0, status 0 The query file could not be opened. Check --conf, its path and its read permissions It is mandatory to specify name, query and type! A line of the query file has fewer than three colon-separated fields error with the query:<statement>.<error> on standard error The database rejected that statement. The following lines are still processed ERROR - Could not write file: ... The data folder is not writable, or a document with the same name already exists (see Known limitations) Nothing is printed and no file is written --as_agent_plugin 1 prints the modules and writes nothing; without it the addon writes into --data_dir and prints 1 per document A performance module is missing The database returned no value for that metric, or the metrics stage failed (see Known limitations)

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Option Required Default Description --hostname Yes — Db2 host name or IP address --port No 50000 Db2 listener port --protocol No TCPIP Protocol used in the connection string --database Yes — Database name on the Db2 server --uid Yes — User that runs the statements --password Yes — Password for that user --conf Yes — Query file. The addon reads it on every run, before the default metrics --default_metrics No 1 1 publishes the default performance modules; any other value disables them --agent_name No DB2 Name of the query agent; the metrics agent is <agent_name>_metrics -g, --group No db2 Group written in the agent data of both agents --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Folder for the agent data documents in the data folder mode --as_agent_plugin No 0 1 prints the modules on standard output; any other value writes documents into --data_dir --tentacle_address No — Tentacle server address. It takes precedence over --as_agent_plugin, and delivery does not work in version 1.0 --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port -h, --help No — Prints the usage summary and exits

docs.title: Query file
docs.text:
Field Required Description name Yes Module name statement Yes Statement executed against the connected database. It cannot contain a colon module_type Yes Pandora FMS module type, written verbatim into the module description No Module description

The field _database_ in a statement is replaced by the connected database name in single quotes.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text: Agent Module Type Unit Source Query As defined in the query file As defined in the query file — One module per statement Metrics no_of_bufferpools_<DB_NAME> generic_data count Number of buffer pools defined in the database Metrics total_logical_reads_<DB_NAME> generic_data count Sum of the total logical reads reported by the buffer pools Metrics total_physical_reads_<DB_NAME> generic_data count Sum of the total physical reads reported by the buffer pools Metrics data_logical_reads_<DB_NAME> generic_data count Sum of the data logical reads Metrics data_physical_reads_<DB_NAME> generic_data count Sum of the data physical reads Metrics index_logical_reads_<DB_NAME> generic_data count Sum of the index logical reads Metrics xda_logical_reads_<DB_NAME> generic_data count Sum of the XDA logical reads Metrics log_utilization_percent_<DB_NAME> generic_data % Average transaction log utilization Metrics total_log_used_kb_<DB_NAME> generic_data KB Total transaction log space in use Metrics total_log_available_kb_<DB_NAME> generic_data KB Total transaction log space available

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status Meaning 0 Successful run. Also used when the query file cannot be opened or a line of it is malformed 1 The connection failed, a default-metrics query failed, or a document could not be written 2 An option received a value of the wrong type, for example a non-integer --as_agent_plugin
