docs.title: Oracle VM monitoring plugin
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Oracle VM monitoring plugin monitors an Oracle VM environment from Pandora FMS through the REST API of its Oracle VM Manager. Each run reads the manager and what it manages, and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules: the manager state and its job counters, server pool capacity, the OVM Servers with their network ports, the virtual machines with their memory and disks, and the file servers with their file systems. Nothing is installed on the Oracle VM hosts: the plugin runs from a host that can reach the OVM Manager API.

Every execution is one-shot: it authenticates against the API, collects the whole environment and delivers one agent data document per element. Delivery is either through Tentacle or by copying the documents into a Pandora FMS data folder. The plugin has no agent plugin mode and does not print module XML on standard output.

Oracle VM monitoring is a different addon from Oracle Discovery (pandorafms.oracle), which monitors Oracle Database instances and is documented in Oracle Discovery. This page covers the Oracle VM virtualization manager only.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Oracle VM Manager 3.4.5 Known compatible The addon guide linked from the Marketplace entry states the plugin was developed against Oracle VM Manager 3.4.5 Oracle VM Manager versions other than 3.4.5 Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Reachability from the host that runs the plugin to the OVM Manager REST API Required Every run queries the API An OVM Manager user allowed to read the API resources Required Each request is authenticated with HTTP Basic credentials The Pandora FMS plugin library (PandoraFMS::PluginTools) Required The addon guide lists it as a prerequisite A Tentacle server reachable at tentacle_ip and tentacle_port Required when transfer_mode=tentacle Every generated document is sent to that address and port A writable data folder Required when transfer_mode is not tentacle Every generated document is copied into local_folder Oracle VM guest additions on the monitored virtual machines Required for VM IP addresses The addon guide states that IP collection needs guest additions A specific Pandora FMS release Not validated No version matrix is recorded for this addon. The Marketplace states that its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later A specific host operating system Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

The addon is distributed through the Pandora FMS Marketplace and its download is limited to licensed users.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the OVM Manager REST API. The example configuration uses HTTPS on port 7002.
  2. An OVM Manager user and its password. The plugin only reads: it requests the manager, the job list, the server pools, the servers, the virtual machines, the virtual NICs, the disks, the file servers and the file systems. Use an account with read access to those resources.
  3. A host to run the plugin with the Pandora FMS plugin library (PandoraFMS::PluginTools), which is part of a Pandora FMS installation. The Pandora FMS server that runs the plugin is the usual choice.
  4. A delivery target that Pandora FMS can read: a Tentacle server, or a data folder read by the Pandora FMS data server.
  5. Oracle VM guest additions inside the monitored virtual machines, only when you want their IP addresses in the agent data.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
The addon guide documents the plugin as the ovm-plugin.64 executable plus the ovm-plugin.conf configuration file. Copy both to the host that will run the plugin; for a console server plugin the recommended folder is /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/.

Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.oracle_vm_monitoring

The shipped configuration file contains sample values. Replace the API URL, the user and the password before the first run, and restrict the file permissions to the user that runs the plugin. If your package names the executable differently, use that name in place of ovm-plugin.64 in the examples.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The plugin takes its settings from three sources, in increasing precedence:

defaults < configuration file < command-line options

The configuration file is a plain-text file of key=value lines. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and a repeated key keeps its last value. To use a file, pass its path as the first and only positional argument. Any option can also be passed on the command line as a -key value pair, and the command-line value replaces the file value:

./ovm-plugin.64 -interval 600 -debug 1 <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

There is no help option. A run without a readable configuration and without the required options fails with the error that names the missing settings, followed by a usage line that shows the configuration file as the only argument.

This is the minimum configuration for a Tentacle delivery:

ovmm_api_url=https://<OVM_MANAGER_URL>:7002/ovm/core/wsapi/rest/
user=<USERNAME>
password=<PASSWORD>
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<PANDORA_FMS_URL>
tentacle_port=41121

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text:
ovmm_api_url is the base URL of the OVM Manager REST API, up to and including the REST root. The plugin appends the resource names (Manager, Job, ServerPool, Server, FileServer) and follows the resource URIs the API returns. A trailing slash is optional: the plugin adds one when it is missing.

The user and the password are sent with HTTP Basic authentication on every request. Requests ask for application/xml, and the plugin reads the XML responses.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• Use an https URL. With http the credentials and the collected data travel unencrypted; restrict the API to a trusted network if you cannot use HTTPS.
  • The plugin does not verify the OVM Manager certificate. It accepts any certificate, including a self-signed one, so HTTPS protects the credentials in transit but does not authenticate the server. Keep the API on a management network you control.
  • The password is stored in plain text in the configuration file. Keep the file owned by the plugin user and readable by nobody else, for example with chmod 600.
  • Avoid -password on the command line: the command is kept in the shell history and is visible in the process list while the plugin runs. The plugin has no separate credentials-file option, so prefer the configuration file and pass only non-secret overrides as options.
  • The include key reads another key file at that point in the configuration, so a shared file can hold the connection settings while the main file holds the rest. Keys read after the include line override the included ones.

docs.title: Agent names and renaming
docs.text:
Every generated agent has a default name taken from the OVM API:

Resource Default agent name OVM Manager The manager UUID Server pool The pool ID OVM Server The MD5 hash of the server ID, because the MAC-style server ID is not a valid agent name Virtual machine The VM ID File server The file server ID

The alias is the element name reported by the API (the manager name, the pool name, the server name, the VM name or the file server name). Set alias_as_name=1 to leave the alias empty so Pandora FMS uses the agent name as the alias instead.

The IDs come from the OVM Manager interface: open the element and read its ID field.

To rename an agent, add a configuration key whose name is exactly the default agent name. Any number of renaming keys can be added:

# A virtual machine, renamed by its VM ID.
0004fb0000060000ed21e30c8dbbbb65a=app-vm-01
# An OVM Server, renamed by the MD5 hash of its ID.
a62454d287e230c773f56d618b78500f=ovm-server-01

The renaming keys are ordinary configuration keys, so they follow the same precedence as the rest: a -key value option overrides the file. For a server, the key must be the MD5 hash, not the MAC-style ID, because the hash is the default agent name. The commented default_agent_name1 sample in the shipped file does not rename anything: the key is the ID value, not a field name. Renaming the manager, a pool or a server leaves its children pointing to the default name; see Known limitations.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text:
transfer_mode Behavior tentacle The plugin writes each document to tmp and sends it with the Tentacle client to tentacle_ip:tentacle_port Any other value, including empty The plugin writes each document to tmp and copies it into local_folder

Tentacle delivery requires tentacle_ip. A delivery mode other than tentacle requires local_folder. The plugin validates both conditions before contacting the OVM Manager, and stops with an error when the required value is missing.

The generated document is removed from tmp after a successful delivery and kept there when the delivery fails. Delivery errors are reported on standard error only when debug=1; by default a failed delivery is silent and the run continues with the next agent.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
The plugin can be registered in the Pandora FMS console as a server plugin, so the Pandora FMS server runs it periodically instead of a manual or cron execution. Every execution collects the whole environment and delivers all its agents.

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set the name, the plugin type Standard, a maximum timeout and a description. Raise the maximum timeout when a run over a large environment takes longer than the default.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the path to the ovm-plugin.64 executable on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/ovm-plugin.64.
  4. In Plugin parameters, pass the path to the configuration file as the only argument:
/etc/pandora/plugins/ovm-plugin.conf
  1. Keep the API user and password in that file rather than in console fields.

The same registration can pass individual settings with the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... instead of a file, for example -ovmm_api_url _field1_ -user _field2_ -password _field3_ -transfer_mode tentacle -tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1. In that case mark the password field as hidden.

The value printed by the execution is not the monitoring data: the plugin delivers the agents itself, and the data appears in the generated agents. All the agents of the environment are created or updated by the same execution.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually with the configuration file as its only argument:

./ovm-plugin.64 <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

A successful run ends with the line Complete! and exits with status 0. It prints nothing else unless debug=1 is set. With debug=1 the run also prints its progress, for example:

> Connecting to OVM Manager REST API...
 >> Collecting OVM Manager information...
 >> Creating XML structure for OVM Manager agent...
 >> Transferring OVM Manager agent XML...
> Scanning OVM servers pools...

Then check the console after the first execution:

  1. The OVM Manager agent, named after the manager UUID.
  2. One agent per server pool, one per OVM Server, one per virtual machine and one per file server, under the parent described in Generated agents.
  3. The modules of each agent, listed in Generated modules.

If the manager cannot be reached, the run prints ERROR: Unable to connect to '<URL>' with user '<USER>'. and exits with status 1 without creating or updating any agent. The message repeats the configured URL and user, so avoid running it in a shared terminal.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
A run produces up to five agent groups. Each group answers a different question:

  • Manager. Whether the OVM Manager is running, and how many of its jobs ended in SUCCESS or in FAILURE.
  • Server pools. How many virtual machines the pool holds, how many of its servers are running, and what share of the pool memory is still usable.
  • OVM Servers. Whether each server is running, its usable memory share, the state of each network port, and how many of its virtual machines are running.
  • Virtual machines. Whether each VM is running, the share of the server memory it uses and how much of each virtual disk is occupied.
  • File servers. The free space share of each file system, with its path.

The state modules are binary: 1 when the resource is in its healthy state (RUNNING for the manager, the servers and the VMs; PORT_UP for a port) and 0 otherwise. The description of each state module repeats the raw state reported by the API, so a stopped resource shows why in the module description.

The percentage modules are computed from the capacities the API reports:

  • Usable memory (%) is the memory still available for virtual machines, not the memory in use. It is usableMemory divided by memory, for a server or summed over the servers of a pool.
  • Used memory on server (%) is the current memory of the VM as a share of the server total memory, not of the memory assigned to the VM. The module description states the current, the server total and the assigned memory.
  • <disk name> on disk size (%) is the space the virtual disk occupies on storage as a share of its nominal size, which shows thin provisioning.
  • <file system> free size (%) is the free space as a share of the file system size.

A zero denominator produces 0 instead of an error. The plugin sets no warning or critical thresholds on the generated modules; add thresholds on the modules you want to alert on.

The agent aliases make the console readable: the alias is the element name, while the agent name is the API identifier. For OVM Servers the agent name is the MD5 hash of the server ID, so the server name only appears as the alias and in the description.

docs.title: Run-time behavior
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state between runs. Every execution collects the whole environment, so it can be run manually at any time.
  • Resources are collected in a fixed order: manager, job list, server pools, servers, the VMs of each server, and file servers. Each resource costs at least one API request, and the requests are sequential, so a large environment takes proportionally longer.
  • Every API request uses a three-second timeout. The configuration file has no key to change it; a manager that answers more slowly produces missing agents or missing modules.
  • debug=1 prints the progress of the run and the delivery errors. debug=0, the default, hides both.
  • The run ends with Complete! and status 0 even when one or more deliveries failed. Check the console, or run with debug=1, to confirm that every agent arrived.
  • The plugin collects the whole environment on every run: there is no option to limit it to one pool, server, VM or file server.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
These are behaviors of version 1.0, documented as they are.

  • A manager with fewer than two jobs stops the run. The job counter expects a list of jobs. With zero jobs or exactly one job the run stops with an unhandled error right after the Manager agent has been delivered, so no pool, server, VM or file server agent is produced. This affects a new or quiet OVM Manager.
  • scan_vm_ip=0 does not disable VM IP collection. The setting is enabled unless its value is something other than 0 or 1. To stop collecting addresses, set scan_vm_ip=2 or another value outside that pair.
  • A VM address is collected only from a virtual NIC with more than one IP address. A VM whose NIC reports a single address gets an empty agent address, even with guest additions installed.
  • The shipped rename sample does not work. The commented default_agent_name1=new_agent_name1 lines do not rename anything; the key must be the default agent name, as described in Agent names and renaming.
  • Renaming a parent agent breaks the hierarchy. Every parent reference is written with the default name of the parent (the manager UUID, the pool ID or the MD5 hash of the server), not with the renamed name. If you rename the manager, a pool or a server, its children (pools, file servers, servers and VMs) keep pointing to the old name. Rename only leaf agents, or keep the default names of the agents that have children.
  • Delivery failures are hidden by default. A failed Tentacle transfer or a failed copy leaves the document in tmp, is reported only with debug=1, and does not change the exit status.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: Symptom Cause and action ERROR: No OVM API URL, user or password provided. and a usage line, status 1 ovmm_api_url, user or password is missing, or the configuration file path does not exist and was therefore not read ERROR: transfer_mode set to tentacle, but no tentacle_ip provided., status 1 Tentacle delivery is selected without a Tentacle server address ERROR: transfer_mode set to local, but no local_folder provided., status 1 transfer_mode is not tentacle and local_folder is empty ERROR: Unable to connect to '<URL>' with user '<USER>'., status 1 The manager URL, the credentials or the network path is wrong. Check that the URL is the REST base and that the user can read the API. The certificate is not verified, so TLS is not the cause Only the Manager agent appears The job list broke the run (see Known limitations), or a later request failed. Run with debug=1 to see where the run stops The Manager agent and the pool agents appear, but no server agent The server list request failed, or the servers were not returned by the API. Run with debug=1 A VM agent has no address Guest additions are missing, or the NIC reports a single IP address (see Known limitations) No delivery error and no new data in the console Delivery failed silently, or the destination is not read by Pandora FMS. Run with debug=1 and check tentacle_ip/tentacle_port or local_folder The agents appear in a group other than group The Pandora FMS server is configured with autocreate_group_force 1, which gives the server autocreate group precedence over the group in the agent data The console shows an unexpected agent name The agent is named after the API ID by default; rename it with a key equal to that name, or check the MD5 hash for OVM Servers

docs.title: Configuration file parameters
docs.text:
The file uses key=value lines. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped.

Name Required Default Description ovmm_api_url Yes — Base URL of the OVM Manager REST API, up to the REST root, for example https://<OVM_MANAGER_URL>:7002/ovm/core/wsapi/rest/. The trailing slash is optional user Yes — OVM Manager user, sent with HTTP Basic authentication password Yes — Password for user, stored in plain text group No Servers Group name written in the agent data of the generated agents interval No 300 Agent interval, in seconds, written in the agent data tmp No /tmp Folder where the agent documents are written before delivery transfer_mode No Empty tentacle delivers through the Tentacle client. Any other value, including empty, copies the documents into local_folder local_folder Required when transfer_mode is not tentacle — Folder for the copied documents, for example /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ tentacle_ip Required when transfer_mode=tentacle — Tentacle server address tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port tentacle_client No tentacle_client Name or path of the Tentacle client executable tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options passed to the Tentacle client, separated by whitespace alias_as_name No 0 1 leaves the alias empty so the agent name is used as the alias; any other value uses the element name scan_vm_ip No Enabled Collects the VM IP addresses. Values other than 0 or 1 disable collection; 0 does not (see Known limitations) debug No 0 1 prints the progress of the run and the delivery errors on standard error; 0 hides them include No — Reads another key file at that point. Keys read after the include line override the included ones <default agent name> No — Any key whose name equals a default agent name replaces it. Applies to the manager UUID, pool IDs, VM IDs, file server IDs and the MD5 hash of a server ID

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
./ovm-plugin.64 <PATH_TO_CONFIG> [ -key value ... ]
Condition Behavior A positional argument that names an existing file The file is read and any further -key value pairs override its values No positional argument The plugin reads only the -key value pairs; the required connection keys must come from them A positional argument that does not name an existing file The file is not read and the path is not reported as an error; the run fails with the missing-settings error unless another source supplies them -key value Replaces the value of the same key from the file or the defaults. A trailing token without its pair is ignored An unknown key Accepted silently. Only a key equal to an agent name has an effect beyond configuration

docs.title: Generated agents
docs.text:
Agent One per Default name Alias Parent OVM Manager Run: always one Manager UUID Manager name None Server pool Server pool returned by the API Pool ID Pool name Manager agent OVM Server Server returned by the API MD5 hash of the server ID Server name Pool agent, or the Manager agent when the server has no pool Virtual machine VM listed by a server VM ID VM name Server agent File server File server returned by the API File server ID File server name Manager agent

Agent attributes:

Attribute Value Description OVM Manager <manager version> for the manager; the element description reported by the API when it is usable; otherwise OVM Server pool, OVM Server <version> (Hypervisor: <type> <version>), VM on <server name> or OVM File server (Type: <type>) Address The IPv4 address of ovmm_api_url for the manager (empty when the URL uses a host name); the server ipAddress for an OVM Server; the addresses collected from the virtual NICs for a VM; empty for pools and file servers OS version The VM osType for a VM agent; empty for the rest Group and interval The group and interval values of the configuration Timestamp The local time of the run

A VM is only monitored when the server that owns it lists it. A VM that no server reports does not get an agent.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text: The module names and descriptions below are the ones the plugin writes. The Successfull jobs spelling is the module name used by the plugin.

The two job modules are only generated when the job list request succeeds; a list with fewer than two entries stops the run (see Known limitations). The count covers every job the API returns, whatever its execution state.

docs.title: Pandora LDAP
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Pandora LDAP plugin monitors an OpenLDAP directory from Pandora FMS. Each run binds to the directory with a bind DN and a password, measures how long the bind takes, and reads the cn=Monitor subtree of the server's monitor backend. The result becomes Pandora FMS modules: the bind response time, the totals of initiated and completed operations, connection and statistic counters, and two per-second rates.

The plugin has three delivery paths:

  • Agent plugin mode (--as_agent_plugin 1): prints one <module> block per module on standard output.
  • Data file mode (default, --as_agent_plugin 0): writes an agent_data document for the agent into the Pandora FMS data directory and prints 1.
  • Tentacle delivery (--tentacle_address): writes the document, sends it with the Tentacle client and prints 1. This path takes precedence over --as_agent_plugin.

Every execution is independent: the plugin keeps no state between runs.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions. It is a general statement, not a test record for this plugin An OpenLDAP server that exposes the cn=Monitor subtree Required The plugin searches cn=Monitor and reads its monitor attributes on every run A directory account with read access to cn=Monitor Required Prerequisite, not a compatibility statement: the plugin binds with the credentials given in -b and -p Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the LDAP listener Required The plugin connects to the URL given in -s tentacle_client in PATH Required when --tentacle_address is used The plugin executes the Tentacle client to deliver the document Other directory servers, such as Active Directory Not validated The plugin reads the OpenLDAP monitor tree; no other directory server has been recorded OpenLDAP versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this plugin Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. An OpenLDAP directory reachable from the host that runs the plugin, with the monitor backend enabled and readable. See Prepare the LDAP server.
  2. A bind account with read access to cn=Monitor. The plugin needs no other permission, because it reads only the monitor subtree.
  3. Pandora FMS to receive the output: the plugin server for data file and Tentacle delivery, or a Pandora FMS agent for agent plugin mode.
  4. A writable data directory when the plugin writes the document itself. The default is /var/spool/pandora/data_in/.
  5. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) in PATH, only for Tentacle delivery.

docs.title: Prepare the LDAP server
docs.text:
The plugin reads the monitor backend of OpenLDAP. Check that the module is loaded; run this on the directory server as root:

ldapsearch -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// -b "cn=module{0},cn=config" -s base '(objectClass=*)' olcModuleLoad

If back_monitor appears among the olcModuleLoad values in the response, the monitor backend is enabled. Otherwise load it in cn=config; on a default installation the module entry is cn=module{0},cn=config. Use an LDIF file:

dn: cn=module{0},cn=config
changetype: modify
add: olcModuleLoad
olcModuleLoad: back_monitor

ldapmodify -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// -f <PATH_TO_CONFIG>

Then grant the bind account read access to the whole monitor subtree: in the cn=config ACL of the Monitor database, give read on dn.subtree="cn=Monitor" to the bind DN and deny it to everyone else. The database entry index (olcDatabase={n}Monitor) depends on the server, so list the databases of cn=config before editing the entry.

Verify the access with the account the plugin will use:

ldapsearch -x -LLL -H 'ldap://<TARGET_HOST>:389' -D '<BIND_DN>' -W -b 'cn=Monitor' -s sub '(objectClass=*)' monitorCounter

A correct account receives the entries of the monitor tree with their monitorCounter values. -W prompts for the password, so it is not stored in the shell history or exposed in the process list.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .pspz2 package from the Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.pandoraldap

Upload it in the Pandora FMS console with the plugin registration, described in Register the plugin in the console. The package contains the pandora_ldap executable and its plugin definition: the name Pandora LDAP, a 20-second maximum timeout, the parameter string and seven macros. The distributed package is self-contained: the host that runs it needs no Python installation.

Pandora FMS installs the executable in its plugin directory, typically /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/, and executes it from the server selected for the module.

docs.title: Execution models
docs.text:
The plugin selects the delivery path in this order:

  1. --tentacle_address is present. The plugin writes the agent_data document into --data_dir and sends it with tentacle_client to <tentacle_address>:<tentacle_port>. It prints 1 and removes the file after a successful transfer. --as_agent_plugin is ignored in this path.
  2. --as_agent_plugin 1. The plugin prints one <module> block per module on standard output, without an agent_data wrapper, and writes no file. This is the output a Pandora FMS agent plugin expects.
  3. Any other value, or the option omitted. The plugin writes the agent_data document into --data_dir and prints 1. The default value is 0, which selects this path.

--as_agent_plugin accepts only an integer: a value such as true is a usage error and the run stops with exit status 2.

docs.title: Run from the command line
docs.text:
A minimum agent plugin run needs the four mandatory options:

./pandora_ldap -s 'ldap://<TARGET_HOST>:389' -b 'cn=monitor,dc=example,dc=com' \
    -p '<PASSWORD>' -a ldap-lab --as_agent_plugin 1

A data file run, with the destination group and data directory made explicit:

./pandora_ldap -s 'ldap://<TARGET_HOST>:389' -b 'cn=monitor,dc=example,dc=com' \
    -p '<PASSWORD>' -a ldap-lab -g ldap --data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/

A Tentacle run:

./pandora_ldap -s 'ldap://<TARGET_HOST>:389' -b 'cn=monitor,dc=example,dc=com' \
    -p '<PASSWORD>' -a ldap-lab --tentacle_address <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER> --tentacle_port 41121
  • -s takes the LDAP URL, including the scheme and the port. Both ldap:// and ldaps:// are accepted; the plugin has no TLS options of its own, so the URL and the LDAP client configuration of the host govern the connection.
  • -a names the agent that the agent_data document creates or updates in the console. It is also the base of the output file name.
  • -g is the destination group of that agent. The default is ldap.
  • -m prefixes every module name, so the same directory can feed several agents with distinguishable modules. It has no default.
  • --data_dir must exist and be writable by the user that runs the plugin.
  • The Tentacle path uses tentacle_client from PATH, and there is no option for a Tentacle password.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
1. Open Servers → Plugins and upload the .pspz2 package with Register Plugin. The upload registers the plugin, its executable and its macros.
  2. Open the plugin in the list. The definition shows the name Pandora LDAP, a 20-second maximum timeout and this parameter string:
-s _field1_ -b _field2_ -p _field3_ -a _field4_ --as_agent_plugin _field5_ -g _field6_ --data_dir _field7_
  1. Fill each macro with the values of the directory. The macros are the registration surface of the addon:
Field Option Value to enter _field1_ -s LDAP URL with the port, for example ldap://<TARGET_HOST>:389 _field2_ -b Bind DN, for example cn=monitor,dc=example,dc=com _field3_ -p Password of the bind DN. Enable Hide value _field4_ -a Name of the agent that will hold the modules _field5_ --as_agent_plugin 1 to print the module XML, 0 to write the data file _field6_ -g Destination group of the agent, for example ldap _field7_ --data_dir Pandora FMS data directory, for example /var/spool/pandora/data_in/

Once registered, the plugin is available when creating plugin modules, and each module fills the macros individually.

The parameter string passes a value to every option, so it runs as it is only when every macro has a value. A macro left empty leaves its option followed by the next one, and the run stops with a usage error such as error: argument -g/--group: expected one argument. In practice _field6_ and _field7_ must be filled even though the package describes them as optional, or the parameter string must be edited to remove -g and --data_dir and let the defaults apply.

The package defines every macro with hide = 0, including the password. The console therefore shows the value of _field3_ in clear text in the macro editor: enable Hide value for it when you register the plugin, and treat access to the plugin definition as access to the credential.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The bind password is passed with -p, so the command is visible in the shell history and, while the plugin runs, in the process list of the host.
  • In the console the password lives in the module or plugin macro _field3_. With hide = 0 it is not masked; enable Hide value and restrict who can read the plugin configuration.
  • A plain ldap:// connection sends the bind password and the results unencrypted. Prefer ldaps:// when the directory supports it, or keep the traffic on a trusted network.
  • The generated agent_data document contains metrics only: no bind DN and no password are written into it.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from a terminal with the mandatory options and --as_agent_plugin 1:

./pandora_ldap -s 'ldap://<TARGET_HOST>:389' -b 'cn=monitor,dc=example,dc=com' \
    -p '<PASSWORD>' -a ldap-lab --as_agent_plugin 1

./pandora_ldap -h prints the option list and the usage header, which also reports the version of the executable.

In agent plugin mode a successful run prints one <module> block per module. The excerpt below shows the shape of the output; the values depend on the directory:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Response time]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[0.004]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[response time un sec]]></description>
    <unit><![CDATA[s]]></unit>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[active operations]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[3]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Number of active operations]]></description>
</module>

In data file mode the run prints 1 and writes <data_dir>/<agent_name>.<epoch>.data, where <epoch> is the number of seconds of the run. In Tentacle mode the run also prints 1, and the document is sent to the configured Tentacle server.

Before relying on this output, check the version limitation in Operate and troubleshoot. With the current package, a run against a directory that returns only the attributes the plugin requests ends with a KeyError before any module is delivered, in every delivery path.

docs.title: Agent generated
docs.text:
Data file and Tentacle delivery create one agent, named after -a:

Property Value Name and alias The -a value Description Ldap metrics Group The -g value, ldap by default Address Empty Operating system and version Empty Interval Empty: the plugin does not set one Timestamp Local time of the run, in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS form

Agent plugin mode creates no agent: the modules belong to the Pandora FMS agent that executes the plugin.

docs.title: Modules generated
docs.text:
The plugin always builds four fixed modules and adds the modules derived from the monitor subtree:

  • Response time. Seconds the bind took. The timer covers the bind only, not the search, so this module is not a measure of the whole run.
  • Total operation counters. active operations, operations/sec and authentications/sec come from the aggregate cn=Operations,cn=Monitor entry and from its Bind child: active operations is the difference between the initiated and the completed totals, while the two /sec modules receive the cumulative totals as incremental modules, so Pandora FMS derives the rate between samples.
  • Connection and statistic counters. One module per monitor entry that carries a monitorCounter value, renamed from the entry DN: connection counters, statistics and waiters.
  • Operation counters per type. For every operation entry, one <operation>initiated module and one <operation>completed module.

-m prefixes every module name of the run. Names are built by concatenating the prefix, the name and, for operation modules, the initiated or completed suffix without a space, so the names are Bind operationsinitiated and Bind operationscompleted, not Bind operations initiated.

The friendly counter names come from the entry DN, not from the attribute value: every entry whose DN contains Current is published as Current connections, including entries that describe something else. When two entries of the monitor tree collapse into the same name, the last one read wins and the other value is lost. An entry whose DN matches none of the keywords keeps its full DN as the module name.

The complete name list, including the DN keyword that produces each name, is in Generated modules.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
• Run the plugin periodically from the plugin server, or from a Pandora FMS agent in agent plugin mode. Each run queries the directory once; there is no cache and no state to reset.
  • In data file mode the file name includes the epoch second of the run. Two runs of the same agent within the same second collide: the second run reports ERROR - Could not write file: [Errno 17] File exists: ... please check directory permissions and exits with status 1. The message names permissions but the actual cause is the existing file.
  • In Tentacle mode the plugin prints 1 and exits with status 0 even when the client fails. The failure appears on standard error as Tentacle error, and the data file is kept instead of being removed, so it can be sent again.
  • KeyError: 'cn=Operations,cn=Monitor' and no output. This is the limitation of the current package. The plugin searches cn=Monitor requesting only the monitorCounter attribute, while the totals and the per-type operation modules are built from monitorOpInitiated and monitorOpCompleted. A directory returns only the attributes that were requested, so those values are empty and the run stops before building or delivering any module. The plugin has no option that changes the requested attributes, and the run exits with status 1.
  • Your username or password is incorrect. The bind was rejected. The plugin prints the message and exits with status 0, and delivers nothing, so a scheduler may report the run as successful. Check the bind DN, the password and the account state.
  • AttributeError: type object 'LDAPError' has no attribute 'message' in a traceback. The bind failed for a reason other than invalid credentials, for example an unreachable server or a refused connection, and the error handler itself fails. Exit status is 1. Check that the host resolves the URL of -s and that the LDAP listener is reachable.
  • error: argument -g/--group: expected one argument or the same message for --data_dir: the macro that feeds the option is empty in the console parameter string. Fill it, or edit the parameter string.
  • JSONDecodeError while reading the monitor tree. A monitorCounter or operation value is not numeric, and the plugin cannot parse it. Check the entry the traceback names.
  • A module is missing or reports the value of a different counter. Several monitor entries can share a DN keyword and therefore a module name. See Modules generated.

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text:
pandora_ldap -s <server> -b <binddn> -p <password> -a <agent> [options]
Option Default Required Description -s, --server — Yes LDAP URL with scheme and port, for example ldap://<TARGET_HOST>:389 or ldaps://<TARGET_HOST>:636 -b, --binddn — Yes DN of the account that binds to the directory -p, --password — Yes Password of the bind account -a, --agent — Yes Name of the agent created or updated by the document --as_agent_plugin 0 No 1 prints the module XML on standard output; any other integer writes the data file --tentacle_address none No Tentacle server address. When set, delivery uses Tentacle and overrides --as_agent_plugin --tentacle_port 41121 No Tentacle server port, used only with --tentacle_address -m, --module_prefix empty No Text prepended to every module name. Not exposed as a console macro -g, --group ldap No Destination group of the generated agent --data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ No Directory where the data file is written -h, --help — No Prints the usage and stops

docs.title: Console macros
docs.text:
The package registers seven macros. All of them are single-line text values.

Macro Option Type Default in package Required Hidden Description _field1_ -s text empty Yes No LDAP URL with the port _field2_ -b text empty Yes No Bind DN _field3_ -p text empty Yes No Bind password. The package sets hide = 0; enable Hide value _field4_ -a text empty Yes No Agent name _field5_ --as_agent_plugin text 0 No No 0 writes the data file; 1 prints the module XML _field6_ -g text empty No No Destination group. In practice it must be filled: see below _field7_ --data_dir text empty No No Data directory. In practice it must be filled: see below

The parameter string always passes -g _field6_ and --data_dir _field7_. An empty value for either macro leaves the option without a value, and the run stops with error: argument ...: expected one argument. Fill both macros, or remove the options from the parameter string and let the executable defaults (ldap and /var/spool/pandora/data_in/) apply.

-m, --tentacle_address and --tentacle_port have no macro in the package; they are available only when the plugin runs from the command line or when the parameter string is edited.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
<prefix> is the -m value. <DN> is a monitor entry DN that matches none of the keywords.

Module name Type Source <prefix>Response time generic_data, unit s Duration of the bind <prefix>active operations generic_data Aggregate cn=Operations,cn=Monitor: initiated minus completed <prefix>operations/sec generic_data_inc Aggregate cn=Operations,cn=Monitor: initiated total <prefix>authentications/sec generic_data_inc Bind entry: initiated total <prefix>Max Descriptor connections generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Max <prefix>Total connections generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Total <prefix>Current connections generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Current <prefix>Bytes statics generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Bytes <prefix>PDU statics generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains PDU <prefix>Entries statics generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Entries <prefix>Referrals statics generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Referrals <prefix>Read waiters generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Read <prefix>Write waiters generic_data Any monitorCounter entry whose DN contains Write <prefix><DN> generic_data A monitorCounter entry that matches none of the keywords <prefix><operation>initiated generic_data monitorOpInitiated of an operation entry <prefix><operation>completed generic_data monitorOpCompleted of an operation entry

The operation entries are renamed from their DN with these names, in this order of evaluation:

DN contains <operation> Bind Bind operations Unbind Unbind Operations Search Search operations Compare Compare operations Modify Modify operations Modrdn Modrdn Add Add operations Delete Delete operations Abandon Abandon operations Extended Extended operations none of them The full DN, for example cn=Operations,cn=Monitor

The suffix is appended without a space: Bind operationsinitiated, Bind operationscompleted, cn=Operations,cn=Monitorinitiated.

docs.title: Output file
docs.text:
In data file and Tentacle modes the plugin writes one file per run:

<data_dir>/<agent_name>.<epoch>.data

The file contains an agent_data document with the attributes of Agent generated and one <module> block per module. The plugin creates the file exclusively: a second run for the same agent within the same second fails instead of overwriting the first file. In Tentacle mode the file is removed after a successful transfer and kept when the transfer fails.

docs.title: Addon identity
docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.pandoraldap Name Pandora LDAP Version 1.1 Version reported by the plugin help 050821 License One Availability Download limited to licensed users Marketplace last update 2025-10-01 Author (Marketplace) Pandora FMS

docs.title: Pandora UX
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Deprecated

Pandora UX is deprecated. Web transaction monitoring is now covered by WUX, and Windows transaction monitoring by Oculix.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Pandora UX replays a recorded check, times it and reports the outcome to Pandora FMS, with a screenshot of the screen or the page at the moment of failure. The check is a web session driven through a Selenium server, a desktop session replayed on the machine that runs the plugin, or an automation script you already have.

Every run turns the result into Pandora FMS modules: a status module per check and phase, a latency module per check and phase, and an image module when a check fails. Desktop checks also keep a reference image of the correct result and compare every run against it.

The execution mode is chosen by the value of -exe, matched as a case-insensitive substring:

-exe value Mode What is replayed PWR Web checks A Selenium IDE suite, in the .side format or in the legacy .html format goliat Web checks with Pandora Webserver A Goliat task file. Linux only stats Web performance One or more URLs timed with curl Any other value Desktop or third-party automation A SikuliX project through pdr.cmd, or any executable with -args

Because the mode is a substring match, a utility whose path contains pwr, goliat or stats selects the internal mode instead of running your binary.

The plugin delivers its modules in two ways:

  • Agent plugin mode (default): it prints the module XML on standard output and the Pandora FMS agent of the host ingests it.
  • Server plugin mode (-agent <name>): it builds an agent_data document and delivers it through Tentacle or a local data folder.

The addon has no Discovery task: it runs from a terminal, from the Pandora FMS agent, or as a registered server plugin.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.pandora_ux, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity A Selenium server reachable from the host, for web checks Required Web checks open a session against -pwr_host:-pwr_port, localhost:4444 by default Selenium 3 server versions Not validated The client reports a Selenium 3 server older than 3.14 as incompatible when it cannot create a session; no version matrix has been recorded for this addon A Java runtime on the host, for PDR and for the PWR server Required pdr.cmd uses JAVA_HOME, then java from the path, then the standard Java runtime folders; the PWR readme asks for Java 8 curl in PATH, for stats mode Required The plugin probes for it when it builds its help and uses it to time every URL The Goliat component of Pandora FMS, for goliat mode Required Goliat mode loads its libraries and stops when they are missing An unlocked interactive desktop session, for desktop checks Required The check captures the desktop of the session that runs the plugin Operating systems Not validated The plugin help scopes PWR to Windows and Linux, PDR to Windows and Goliat to Linux; no test record exists for this version Third-party automation tools used with -exe Not validated Any executable is accepted; no tool has been recorded as validated Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace banner is general to all its integrations, not a statement for this addon

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Pandora FMS to receive the modules: the agent installed on the host in agent plugin mode, or a Pandora FMS server in server plugin mode.
  2. The addon package: the pandora_ux_x64.exe executable, plus the PWR server bundle and the PDR launcher when you use those modes.
  3. For web checks: a Selenium server that the host can reach, a Java runtime for that server, and a browser it can start.
  4. For desktop checks: a Windows host, a Java runtime and SikuliX. The PDR launcher in the package provides the SikuliX entry point.
  5. An interactive desktop session on the host that runs desktop checks.
  6. curl on the host when you use stats mode.
  7. Goliat, from Pandora FMS, when you use goliat mode.

The plugin holds no credentials of its own. In agent plugin mode it needs read access to the scripts and write access to the screenshot folder; in server plugin mode it writes the agent_data file to a temporary folder and then delivers it. Run it as the user whose desktop is checked, so the desktop session and the capture belong to the same user.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Pandora FMS Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.pandora_ux

Extract it on the host that will run the checks. The executable is pandora_ux_x64.exe. The package also provides the PWR server bundle and the PDR launcher; prepare them as described below when you use those modes.

docs.title: Prepare the PWR server
docs.text:
Web checks need a Selenium server, on the same host or on another host that the plugin can reach. The server does not have to share the machine with the plugin: -pwr_host and -pwr_port point at it. On Windows the package includes a PWR server bundle; the readme shipped with the addon documents this sequence:

  1. Install a Java 8 runtime.
  2. Prepare the Firefox profile that the server will use.
  3. Uncompress PWR_Server.zip into C:\PWR.
  4. Run C:\PWR\server\service_installer.bat as administrator.
  5. Start the service with net start PWRSRV.

The installer registers a Windows service named PWRSRV that runs the Selenium server with the Firefox profile in C:\PWR\profile. It uses the 64-bit service wrapper from the bundle and the java found in PATH, so it needs a 64-bit Windows and a Java runtime on the path of the account that runs it. The readme also documents starting the server in the foreground, on port 4444, instead of installing it as a service.

docs.title: Prepare a desktop host
docs.text:
Desktop checks replay a session that interacts with the real desktop, so they run on Windows, in an interactive session:

  1. Install a Java runtime. pdr.cmd uses JAVA_HOME when it is set and usable, then java from the path, and finally Program Files\Java\jre8, jre7 and jre6, including the 32-bit program folder. When it finds none it prints Java not found in standard places and stops.
  2. Copy the PDR folder of the package to C:\PDR. It contains pdr.cmd and the SikuliX entry point that the launcher runs.
  3. Point -exe at C:\PDR\pdr.cmd and pass -args -r, so the launcher replays the project given in -script.

The desktop session must stay unlocked and in the foreground: a locked session, a disconnected remote desktop session or a machine without a logged-in user has no desktop to capture, and the check fails.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Two decisions define a run: how the plugin delivers its modules, and which checks it executes.

Mode Selected by Modules on standard output Agent plugin No -agent value The module XML, ready for the Pandora FMS agent Server plugin -agent <name> One line with the global status, 1 or 0, after delivering the agent

The minimum command line for a web check is the mode, the Selenium server and the suite:

pandora_ux_x64.exe -exe PWR -script C:\pandora_ux\tests\std.side

Pass every argument as a -flag value pair. The parser reads the command line as consecutive pairs, so -flag=value is taken as a flag named flag=value, and a flag left without a value at the end is ignored.

docs.title: PWR scripts and phases
docs.text:
In web mode, -script takes one or more Selenium IDE suites separated by commas. Each suite runs in sequence and produces its own set of modules; a failure inside a suite stops the remaining commands of that suite but not the following suites.

Phases come from the suite itself. Add a comment to the Selenium IDE suite to open and close them:

phase_start:Login
... recorded commands ...
phase_end:Login

Every phase between the markers is timed and reported on its own. A suite without markers produces a single result for the whole suite.

Two more comments publish extra modules from the page:

getValue;Cart total;generic_data;([0-9.]+) items
getScreenshot;Cart page

getValue reads the page source and publishes the first capture of the regular expression as a module with the name and type you give. getScreenshot captures the whole page and publishes it as an image module. Both run only while the suite is still succeeding.

Two clients can talk to the Selenium server:

  • The default WebDriver client drives Selenium 2 and Selenium 3 servers and accepts both the .side and the legacy .html suite formats. Against a Selenium 2 server it supports Firefox only; Chrome, Internet Explorer and Edge need a Selenium 3 server. In this path the comment payload is split at : and ;, so keep those two characters out of a getValue expression.
  • -pwr_classic 1 uses the legacy Selenium 2 RC client. It needs a Selenium 2 server and the legacy .html suite format.

With Selenium 3, name the browser plainly (firefox, chrome): the leading * of the default value is removed for Firefox only. Chrome additionally accepts -user_data_dir and -profile_folder, and -accept_insecure_certs accepts any TLS certificate presented by the tested site.

docs.title: Desktop checks and reference images
docs.text:
In desktop mode -script takes one or more SikuliX projects or executables, separated by commas, and -folder is the folder where the plugin keeps its images. The folder must already exist and must end with the path separator, because the plugin appends the file name directly.

For every phase the plugin works with three files in that folder:

File Role screenshot_<phase>.png Result image of the run. If your automation tool writes it, the plugin uses it instead of capturing the screen ctrl_screenshot_<phase>.png Reference image of the correct result err_screenshot_<phase>.png Copy of the result image of a failed run

The first run of a phase, or any run with -checkpoint, rebuilds the reference image from the result image and publishes it as a UX_Control_Snapshot module. Later runs compare the result with the reference and fail when they differ by more than -max_differences, which is a percentage of differing characters of the encoded image (0.5 by default). Because the comparison works on the encoded image, a change of a single pixel normally changes every following character, so treat the default as a near-exact match and refresh the reference with -checkpoint when the expected result changes.

-ss_config selects what is captured: active captures the active window on Windows; any other value, including a coordinate list such as 0,0,100,100, falls back to the whole screen.

The external tool is executed as "<utility>" <args> <script>, so the utility path is quoted but -args and the script path are not: keep the script path free of spaces. If the tool already wrote screenshot_<phase>.png, that image is the result of the run.

-k is useful with batch and command files, which always report exit code 0: with -k 1 only the process exit code decides the result; without it, an exit code 0 with [error] in the tool output also counts as a failure.

docs.title: Macros
docs.text:
-s name=value substitutes every _name_ in the script before it runs:

pandora_ux_x64.exe -exe PWR -script C:\pandora_ux\tests\std.side -s today=now+1 -f "%Y%m%d"

now, now+<days> and now-<days> produce a date with the -f format, which defaults to %Y%m%d. The plugin copies the script to a temporary folder, applies the substitution there, executes the copy and deletes the folder afterwards. Your original script is never modified.

The command line holds one -s value per run: a second -s replaces the first, and so does a second -f. For a SikuliX project the substitution also needs the recursive-copy support of the runtime; when it is missing the plugin exits with status 1 before running the check, and the reason is printed only with -debug 1.

docs.title: Agent plugin mode
docs.text:
Add the plugin to the Pandora FMS agent configuration, or to the remote configuration of the agent in the console, as a module_plugin line:

module_plugin C:\pandora_ux\pandora_ux_x64.exe -exe C:\PDR\pdr.cmd -args -r -script C:\PDR\checkout.sikuli -folder C:\PDR\ -checkpoint

The agent executes the plugin on its own interval and ingests the modules it prints. Generated modules carry the group UX and no tags unless you set -g and -tag_list.

docs.title: Server plugin mode
docs.text:
-agent <name> switches the plugin to server plugin mode. It creates an agent with that name, holds the modules under it, and delivers the document according to -mode:

-mode Behavior local (default) Copies the agent_data file into -local_folder tentacle Sends it with the Tentacle client to -tentacle_ip:-tentacle_port

To run it from the console, register it as a server plugin:

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set a name, the plugin type Standard, an optional timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the path to pandora_ux_x64.exe on the Pandora FMS server.
  4. In Plugin parameters, use the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... for the values that change between modules:
-exe PWR -script _field1_ -pwr_host _field2_ -pwr_port _field3_ -agent _field4_ -mode local -local_folder /var/spool/pandora/data_in
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Path to the Selenium suite on the Pandora FMS server /opt/pandora_ux/tests/std.side _field2_ Host of the Selenium server <TARGET_HOST> _field3_ Port of the Selenium server 4444 _field4_ Name of the agent that will hold the modules Pandora UX checkout

Once registered, create a plugin server module on an agent, choose the Pandora UX plugin and fill its fields. Each module execution launches one run on the server selected for the module, so the Selenium server must be reachable from that Pandora FMS server.

Server plugin mode is meant for checks that can run without a desktop. Desktop checks need the interactive session of the monitored user, so they normally run as an agent plugin on the host itself.

docs.title: Email on failure
docs.text:
Setting -to makes the plugin send a message when a phase fails. -from, -subject and -content set the sender, the subject and the body; the subject defaults to Pandora UX test failed: followed by the phase name. -smtp_gw and -smtp_port point at an SMTP relay (127.0.0.1 and 25 by default).

The message has no authentication and no TLS options: use a relay that accepts the host. When the failing phase has an image file, the plugin attaches it; web checks report no file, so their message carries only the configured content.

docs.title: A manual run
docs.text:
Run the plugin from a terminal with the same arguments you will schedule. A web check with Selenium on the same host:

pandora_ux_x64.exe -exe PWR -script C:\pandora_ux\tests\std.side -debug 1

The run executes once and exits. The module XML goes to standard output; pass -debug 1 to see the progress messages on standard error, including which mode is running and the result of the post command. -v is accepted but does not change the output.

A successful single-phase web run prints the status and time modules. The descriptions below are the ones of the default WebDriver client, which writes <phase> OK; the legacy client writes Test OK instead.

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[UX_Status_std.side]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[std.side OK]]></description>
    <module_group>UX</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[UX_Time_std.side]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[16.317]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[std.side OK]]></description>
    <module_group>UX</module_group>
    <module_parent>UX_Status_std.side</module_parent>
</module>

A failing run reports 0 in the status module, the error text in the description, and adds an image module with the capture of the failure:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[UX_Snapshot_std.side]]></name>
    <type>async_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[data:image/png;base64, iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg...]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Image (last error)]]></description>
</module>

In server plugin mode the run prints nothing else: the last line is the global status, 1 or 0, and the agent appears in Pandora FMS with its modules.

docs.title: In the console
docs.text: With the agent plugin configured, the modules appear in the agent of the host at its next interval. Because names carry no host or instance prefix, one agent per machine keeps the module tree readable, and the UX_Status modules are the ones to alert on.

docs.title: Status, time and images
docs.text:
The three families mean the same in web and desktop checks:

  • UX_Status_* is generic_proc: 1 when the check or phase succeeded, 0 when it failed.
  • UX_Time_* is generic_data: the duration in seconds.
  • UX_Snapshot_* and UX_Control_Snapshot_* are async_string modules whose value is a data:image/png;base64, URI of the PNG.

The description of a status or time module carries the outcome: <phase> OK (Test OK with the legacy client), the error of the Selenium command, or the output of the automation tool.

docs.title: Transaction and phase names
docs.text:
When a transaction name exists, the plugin also reports the transaction as a whole and labels each phase with its position. A transaction name comes from -t, or is taken from the suite name when a web suite defines more than one phase. The label counts from 0 and reads Phase <n>:, so it becomes part of the module name:

Run Module names Web check, one suite, no phase markers, no -t UX_Status_<suite>, UX_Time_<suite> Web check with phase markers or -t UX_Status_Phase <n>: <transaction>.<phase>, UX_Time_Phase <n>: <transaction>.<phase>, plus UX_Global_Status_<transaction>, UX_Global_Time_<transaction> and, on failure, UX_Global_Snapshot_<transaction> Desktop check, no -t UX_Status_<phase>, UX_Time_<phase>, UX_Control_Snapshot_<phase> and, on failure, UX_Snapshot_<phase> Desktop check with -t UX_Status_Phase <n>: <phase>, UX_Time_Phase <n>: <phase>, the phase images, plus the UX_Global_* modules

<transaction> is the -t value or, in a web suite without -t, the suite name. <phase> is the phase marker of the suite in web checks, and the -name value for that position or the base name of the script in desktop checks.

Two details follow from the numbering: the global web summary is enumerated before the phases in the WebDriver path, so the first phase is reported as Phase 1:; the legacy client enumerates it last, so its numbering starts at 0. And the transaction prefix stays inside the phase name, which is why a web phase appears as Phase 1: std.side.Login when the suite is std.side and the marker is Login.

UX_Global_Status_<transaction> is 1 only when every phase succeeded, and its description is the list of the phase outcomes. UX_Global_Time_<transaction> is the total duration: the wall-clock time of the web run, or the sum of the phase durations in desktop mode. With -pwr_override_global_phase_time 1 a web run uses the sum of the phases as well, and -pwr_phases_time 1 adds a separate UX_Phases_Time_<transaction> module with that sum.

docs.title: stats and Goliat results
docs.text:
stats reports timings for a URL without a browser. For each URL the tag is the -name value for that position; without -name it is the last path segment of the URL, or the whole URL when that segment is empty. The modules are <tag>_Global_Status (generic_proc) and <tag>_UX_Stats_TT, _DNS, _TTCP, _TST and _TTC (generic_data, in milliseconds), plus _TSSL for an https URL. Global_Status is 1 only when curl returned exit code 0; the description names the curl error otherwise.

goliat reports one UX_Status_<task> and one UX_Time_<task> module per task_begin block of the task file, with the duration Goliat measured for it. It publishes no image modules.

docs.title: Retries and the post command
docs.text:
-retries sets how many times the whole transaction is attempted; the default is one attempt. A failed attempt is repeated in full, all phases included, not phase by phase, and the next attempt starts from the first script. Retries apply to web and desktop checks; stats and goliat runs execute once.

-post runs a command once, after the modules have been generated, whatever the result of the check. Use it to close what the check opened:

-post "taskkill /F /IM calc.exe"

It is not executed in stats mode, which ends before the report stage.

docs.title: Operating a desktop host
docs.text:
• Keep the agent running inside the interactive session of the monitored user, with the desktop unlocked. A machine at the logon screen has no desktop to capture.
  • Start the agent automatically at boot, so a machine restart does not leave the checks stopped until somebody logs in.
  • Reset a reference image by deleting ctrl_screenshot_<phase>.png, or by running the check once with -checkpoint when the expected result changes.
  • Keep -folder on a local disk: the plugin writes and re-reads the images there on every run.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• The plugin prints its parameter list and exits with status 1 — no argument, only -h, or a missing -exe or -script. The message mentions Missing <script> in arguments even when the missing value is -exe; check both.
  • A web run reports 0 in every status module with a connection error in the description — the Selenium server is not reachable or not ready. Check -pwr_host and -pwr_port, the service on the server (net start PWRSRV on Windows) and the firewall between the host and the server.
  • A web run publishes nothing at all and ends with status 0 — the run had -exit_on_fail 1 and could not reach the Selenium server. The option makes the plugin abandon the run instead of publishing a failed status, so use it only where an external scheduler watches the exit code.
  • A desktop run reports Control image not found, please check directory permissions — the folder in -folder does not exist, does not end with the path separator, or is not writable by the user that runs the plugin.
  • A desktop run fails with Error: Snapshot doesn't match the control one on a check that works — the reference image no longer matches the expected screen. Review the image in the UX_Snapshot module and refresh the reference with -checkpoint.
  • Java not found in standard places when a PDR run starts — there is no JAVA_HOME, no java in the path and no runtime in the standard Java folders. Install a Java runtime or set JAVA_HOME.
  • No progress message appears on standard error — the plugin writes its messages only with -debug 1. -v is accepted for compatibility and changes nothing.
  • The plugin stops with Goliat libraries not found or with a message about the Selenium 2 RC client — the optional component of that mode is not available on the host. Use the WebDriver path, or install the missing component.
  • No mail arrives on failure — -to is not set, the SMTP relay in -smtp_gw:-smtp_port refuses the host, or the failure happened before the report stage (a configuration error, for example).

docs.title: Execution parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -exe Yes — Automation utility, or the internal mode PDR, PWR, stats or goliat. The value is matched as a case-insensitive substring -args No Empty Arguments passed to the external utility before the script path -script Yes — Comma-separated list of suites, projects, executables or URLs, one per phase -name No Base name of the script Comma-separated names that match -script position by position, used in the module names and, in stats mode, as the module prefix -folder No %TEMP%\ on Windows, /tmp/ elsewhere Folder for the result, reference and error images of desktop checks. Must end with the path separator. Not used by web checks -retries No 1 Number of attempts of the whole transaction, in web and desktop modes -t No — Transaction name. Enables the UX_Global_* modules and the Phase <n>: label -k No 0 1 uses only the process exit code; by default an exit code 0 with [error] in the output also fails -post No — Command executed once after the modules are generated. Not executed in stats mode -debug No 0 1 prints progress messages and Selenium detail on standard error -v No 0 Accepted for compatibility. It does not change the output; use -debug 1

docs.title: PWR parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -pwr_host No localhost Host of the Selenium server -pwr_port No 4444 Port of the Selenium server -pwr_browser No *firefox Browser the Selenium server starts. With Selenium 3 use the plain name (firefox, chrome) -pwr_classic No 0 1 uses the legacy Selenium 2 RC client and the legacy .html suite format -pwr_phases_time No 0 1 adds UX_Phases_Time_<transaction>. Requires a transaction name -pwr_override_global_phase_time No Not set 1 sets the global time module to the sum of the phase times. Requires a transaction name -accept_insecure_certs No 0 1 accepts any TLS certificate. Selenium 3 only -pageLoadTimeout No 300000 Page load timeout in milliseconds -user_data_dir No — Chrome user data directory. Selenium 3 only -profile_folder No — Chrome profile folder inside -user_data_dir. Selenium 3 only -exit_on_fail No 0 1 abandons the run when the Selenium server cannot be reached, without publishing modules and with exit status 0 -phase_snapshot No 0 1 attaches the failure image to the failed phase in the legacy client

docs.title: Desktop and image parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -ss_config No Whole screen active captures the active window on Windows. Any other value falls back to the whole screen -checkpoint No 0 Rebuilds the reference image from the current result and publishes UX_Control_Snapshot_* -max_differences No 0.5 Maximum percentage of differing characters between the reference and the result image -classic_mode No 0 1 publishes the latency modules only when the check succeeded

docs.title: Macro parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -s name=value No — Substitutes _name_ in the script. now, now+<days> and now-<days> produce a date. One macro per run -f format No %Y%m%d Date format for the date macros. One format per run

docs.title: Email parameters
docs.text: Name Required Default Description -to No — Recipient of the failure notification. Without it, no mail is sent -from No pandora_ux@artica.es Sender of the message -subject No Pandora UX test failed: Subject prefix; the phase name is appended -content No Empty Body of the message -smtp_gw No 127.0.0.1 SMTP relay -smtp_port No 25 SMTP relay port

docs.title: Module, agent and delivery parameters
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description -agent No — Agent name. Switches the plugin to server plugin mode -agent_group No Empty Group of the agent created in server plugin mode -agent_interval No 300 Interval of the agent created in server plugin mode -interval No 1 Accepted and stored, but the generated modules are published without an interval -g No UX Group of the generated modules -tag_list No Empty Comma-separated tags added to the generated modules -mode No local local copies the agent document into -local_folder; tentacle sends it to -tentacle_ip:-tentacle_port -tentacle_ip No 127.0.0.1 Tentacle server address -tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port -tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options passed to the Tentacle client -local_folder No /var/spool/pandora/data_in Destination folder in local mode -temp No System temporary folder Folder used to write the agent document before delivery

When the first argument is the path of an existing file, the plugin reads it as key=value lines before processing the flags, and the flags override it. The plugin help does not list this form.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
Module Type Mode Meaning UX_Status_<phase> generic_proc Web, desktop and Goliat 1 when the phase succeeded, 0 when it failed UX_Time_<phase> generic_data Web, desktop and Goliat Duration of the phase, in seconds UX_Control_Snapshot_<phase> async_string Desktop Reference image rebuilt during this run UX_Snapshot_<phase> async_string Web and desktop Image at the moment of the failure UX_Global_Status_<transaction> generic_proc Web and desktop with a transaction name 1 when every phase succeeded UX_Global_Time_<transaction> generic_data Web and desktop with a transaction name Duration of the run, or the sum of the phases with -pwr_override_global_phase_time 1 UX_Global_Snapshot_<transaction> async_string Web and desktop with a transaction name Image of the failure, or No image available UX_Phases_Time_<transaction> generic_data Any mode with a transaction name and -pwr_phases_time 1 Sum of the phase times <tag>_Global_Status generic_proc stats 1 when curl completed with exit code 0 <tag>_UX_Stats_TT generic_data stats Total time of the request, in milliseconds <tag>_UX_Stats_DNS generic_data stats Name resolution time, in milliseconds <tag>_UX_Stats_TTCP generic_data stats TCP connection time, in milliseconds <tag>_UX_Stats_TSSL generic_data stats, https URLs TLS handshake time, in milliseconds <tag>_UX_Stats_TST generic_data stats Time to the first byte, in milliseconds <tag>_UX_Stats_TTC generic_data stats Transfer time, in milliseconds

Modules published by the getValue comment keep the name and type declared in the comment. The Phase <n>: transaction label and the <transaction>. prefix are part of the module name when a transaction name exists, as described in Transaction and phase names.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status Meaning 0 Normal end, including a run whose modules report failures. In server plugin mode the global status is printed instead: 1 or 0 1 The plugin printed its parameter list, or an optional component of the selected mode is missing Other An internal error stopped the process before it could report
