docs.title: Pandora Plugin Executor
docs.text: Article last updated: 2026-10-26.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
pandora-plugin_exec is a single standalone executable that monitors anything reachable with an HTTP request or a local command, and turns the result into Pandora FMS agents and modules. It replaces one plugin per technology with one program plus a catalog of YAML templates.

Each run reads one template and executes it once:

template.yml → run tasks → filter their output into variables → build agents and modules → deliver

A template declares four things:

  • Tasks — HTTP requests or local commands, executed sequentially. A later task can use values produced by an earlier one, so a login → token → authenticated request chain fits in a single run.
  • Filters — a jq expression or a regular expression that extracts values from a task's output into a variable.
  • Agents and modules — built from those variables with {{ }} expressions. One module per declared block, or one per element of an array.
  • Transfer — how the result reaches Pandora FMS: Tentacle, a local Pandora data directory, or the standard output of a software agent plugin.

The executor is one-shot: it runs the template once and exits. Scheduling stays where it already is — the Pandora FMS agent, cron, or the Pandora FMS server itself.

The addon ships ready-made templates, including replacements for the pandora_df_used_go, pandora_mem_used and pandora_netusage agent plugins. See Bundled templates.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon Pandora-Plugin-Executor, version 1.0 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity A host that can execute pandora-plugin_exec Required The addon is a standalone executable with no runtime dependencies; it is started by the agent, by cron or by hand /bin/sh and the commands your templates invoke Required local tasks are executed through /bin/sh -c; the binaries and files a template names (df, awk, /proc/meminfo, ...) must exist on that host Network access from that host to the URLs of the template Required when the template has request tasks The executor opens the connection itself The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) Required when transfer.mode: tentacle The document is sent by invoking the Tentacle client Write permission on transfer.local.directory Required when transfer.mode: local The agent document is written into that directory A Pandora FMS software agent able to run module_plugin commands Required when transfer.mode: agent_plugin The agent is what starts the executor and ingests the module fragments it prints Operating system, distribution and architecture Not validated No platform matrix has been recorded for this addon. The design record mentions end-to-end runs on a real host but does not identify the distribution, version or architecture, and the Marketplace tag linux is a tag, not a compatibility statement Windows Not validated This page describes no Windows installation path, and no Windows artefact is identified for this addon Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace banner ("All integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions") is general to every integration, not a statement about this addon

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A host to run the executable. It is delivered as a standalone file named pandora-plugin_exec; there is no installer, no service and no runtime to install.
  2. A shell and the tools your templates call. Every local task is a shell command, so the binaries and the files it references must exist on that host and be readable by the user that runs the executor.
  3. Pandora FMS to receive the result: the server in tentacle or local mode, or the Pandora FMS software agent of the monitored host in agent_plugin mode.
  4. The Tentacle client, only when the template delivers with transfer.mode: tentacle.

The executor runs with the privileges of the user that starts it. That user needs the Tentacle client in its PATH (or an absolute path in the template), or write access to the Pandora data directory, depending on the mode you choose.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the free Marketplace entry:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/Pandora-Plugin-Executor

The file identified for version 1.0 is Pandora-Plugin-Executor.1.0.zip. The artefact the addon distributes is the pandora-plugin_exec executable.

  1. Copy the executable to the host that will run it and make it executable, for example /usr/bin/pandora-plugin_exec.
  2. Copy the templates you are going to use to a directory that the user running the executor can read, for example /etc/pandora/templates/. The executor reads only the template named with -t; it never scans a directory.

Nothing is installed on the monitored system unless that system is also the host that runs the executor — which is the case only in agent_plugin mode.

docs.title: Choose a delivery mode
docs.text:
transfer.mode is mandatory and decides where the executor runs and what it prints.

Mode Runs on Produces Requirement agent_plugin The monitored host <module> fragments on standard output; the real Pandora FMS agent adds the agent header The Pandora FMS software agent starts it as a module_plugin tentacle Any host with network access to the Pandora FMS server One complete <agent_data> document per template agent, sent with the Tentacle client tentacle_client available, and transfer.tentacle.address local The Pandora FMS server, or any host that can write into a Pandora data directory One complete <agent_data> document per template agent, written as a .data file transfer.local.directory writable by the user that runs the executor

This is the shortest complete template, in agent_plugin mode: it reads root filesystem usage and publishes one module.

tasks:
  - name: disk_root
    type: local
    local:
      command: "df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -d ' %'"
    variable: disk_pct

modules:
  - name: "Root disk used"
    type: generic_data
    data: "{{ disk_pct }}"
    unit: "%"
    min_warning: 80
    min_critical: 90

transfer:
  mode: agent_plugin

The same template in tentacle mode, with an agent block instead of top-level modules, because a full agent document needs an agent name:

tasks:
  - name: api_stats
    type: request
    request:
      url: "https://<TARGET_HOST>/api/stats"
      headers:
        Authorization: "Bearer <API_TOKEN>"
      timeout: 10
    filter:
      type: jq
      expression: ".users.active"
    variable: active_users

agents:
  - name: "myapp"
    group: "Applications"
    interval: 300
    modules:
      - name: "Active users"
        type: generic_data
        data: "{{ active_users }}"

transfer:
  mode: tentacle
  tentacle:
    address: "<PANDORA_FMS_URL>"

For local mode, replace the last block:

transfer:
  mode: local
  local:
    directory: "/var/spool/pandora/data_in"

docs.title: Register the executor in Pandora FMS
docs.text:
The executor does not install itself anywhere and does not schedule anything. Choose the registration that matches the mode.

As a software agent plugin (agent_plugin). Add the invocation to the agent configuration file and restart the agent:

module_plugin /usr/bin/pandora-plugin_exec -t /etc/pandora/templates/disk_load.yml

The agent runs it at the interval configured for the plugin, and ingests the module fragments it prints. The agent supplies the agent name, the group and the interval: anything the template declares in an agents: block is ignored in this mode (see What reaches Pandora FMS).

From cron or the server (tentacle or local). The crontab line is the schedule:

*/5 * * * * pandora-plugin_exec -t /etc/pandora/templates/myapp.yml

In tentacle mode the document is sent to the server address in the template. In local mode the document is written into transfer.local.directory; pointing that directory at the Pandora FMS incoming directory (/var/spool/pandora/data_in by default) on the server makes the run self-contained.

docs.title: Pass parameters to a run
docs.text:
Tokens left after the flags feed two reserved variables, seeded before any task runs:

  • args — ordered list of positional tokens: {{ args[0] }}, {{ len(args) }}, for_each: args.
  • params — map of named tokens: {{ params.host }}, {{ params.threshold + 5 }}.

Each token is split on the first unescaped =, and it becomes a named parameter only when the resulting key matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. Every other token is positional. Numeric-looking values become numbers, so arithmetic works on them, and a repeated named key keeps the last value.

Token Becomes sda1 args[0] = "sda1" 90 args[0] = 90 (number) host=db01 params.host = "db01" conn=user=a;pw=b params.conn = "user=a;pw=b" (only the first = splits) 'query\=a=b' positional "query=a=b" (the key would contain = and is not an identifier) k=1 k=2 params.k = 2 (the last one wins)

Two rules decide whether a run works at all:

  • Flags go before the arguments. Flag parsing stops at the first token that is not a flag, and an argument that starts with - is rejected with an error instead of being silently taken as positional.
  • Bash eats the escape. To pass a literal = that must not split, quote the token so the backslash survives: 'query\=a=b', or double it: query\\=a=b.

Referencing an undefined variable does not render an empty string: the affected module is skipped, and the notice reaches standard error only with -v. A parameter is optional only when the template says so explicitly. The three documented patterns are:

Pattern Effect {{ params.missing ?? "default" }} Renders a default when the key is absent when: "'k' in params" Includes the module only when the key was passed {{ len(args) > 1 ? args[1] : "all" }} Guards a positional access by count

Task variables cannot be named args or params; for_each: args is valid.

docs.title: Write a template
docs.text:
A template is a YAML file with three sections: tasks, agents (or top-level modules), and transfer. Parsing is strict: an unknown field name is an error, so a typo stops the run with exit code 1 instead of being ignored.

  • tasks run in declared order. Each one has a unique name, a type (request or local), the matching block, an optional filter and an optional variable that stores the filtered result. Without variable the task still runs and its output is discarded. A task only uses variables produced by tasks declared before it.
  • A request task needs url, and accepts method (default GET), headers, body, timeout (seconds, default 30) and skip_tls_verify (default false). A status outside 2xx is a task failure.
  • A local task needs command, executed through /bin/sh -c, and accepts timeout (seconds, default 30). A non-zero exit status is a task failure. Shell $ is untouched, so awk '{print $5}' works as written; only {{ }} is substituted.
  • A filter declares type: jq or type: regexp and an expression. Without a filter, the trimmed raw output of the task is the value.
  • agents holds one block per agent with its modules; top-level modules is the alternative, valid only with transfer.mode: agent_plugin. The two are mutually exclusive.
  • transfer declares the mode and its options.

The complete field tables are in Reference. The rest of this page uses this longer example, which turns one regexp result into two modules per element:

tasks:
  - name: df
    type: local
    local:
      command: "df -kTP"
    filter:
      type: regexp
      expression: '(?m)^(?P<fs>\S+)\s+(?P<fstype>\S+)\s+(?P<total>\d+)\s+(?P<used>\d+)\s+\d+\s+(?P<pct>\d+)%\s+(?P<mount>.+)$'
    variable: filesystems

modules:
  - for_each: filesystems
    when: 'value.fstype != "tmpfs"'
    name: "DiskUsed_{{ value.mount }}"
    type: generic_data
    data: "{{ value.pct }}"
    unit: "%"

  - for_each: filesystems
    when: 'value.fstype != "tmpfs"'
    name: "DiskUsed_{{ value.mount }} bytes"
    type: generic_data
    data: "{{ value.used }}"
    unit: "KB"

transfer:
  mode: agent_plugin

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Validate a template without delivering anything. For tentacle and local mode, --dry-run prints the agent document on standard output and does not transfer or write it:

pandora-plugin_exec -t <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --dry-run

Add -v to see, on standard error, which variables were stored and which modules were skipped:

pandora-plugin_exec -t <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --dry-run -v

A successful run exits with status 0. Check it explicitly when you script it:

pandora-plugin_exec -t <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --dry-run; echo "exit=$?"

In tentacle and local mode the document starts with an XML declaration and one agent_data element whose attributes are the agent fields of the template:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<agent_data agent_name="myapp" timestamp="2026/10/27 08:00:00" group="Applications" interval="300" agent_mode="1">
  <module>
    <name><![CDATA[Active users]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[42]]></data>
  </module>
</agent_data>

In agent_plugin mode there is nothing to dry-run: the executor only prints module fragments, so a plain execution is already the verification. --dry-run changes nothing in this mode.

pandora-plugin_exec -t /etc/pandora/templates/disk_load.yml

<module>
  <name><![CDATA[Root disk used]]></name>
  <type>generic_data</type>
  <data><![CDATA[81]]></data>
  <unit><![CDATA[%]]></unit>
  <min_warning><![CDATA[80]]></min_warning>
  <min_critical><![CDATA[90]]></min_critical>
</module>

For the final check, deliver for real and look at the result in Pandora FMS: in agent_plugin mode the modules appear under the agent that runs the plugin, and in tentacle or local mode the agent named in the template appears with its modules after the next data ingestion.

docs.title: Variables and module values
docs.text:
Each task with a variable stores exactly one value, and its shape comes from the filter:

Filter result Stored value 0 matches Nothing: the variable stays unset and the task is treated as failed 1 match A scalar N matches An array, one element per match

A task without a filter always produces one element: the trimmed output.

Every captured string that looks numeric becomes a number, recursively inside objects and arrays. Module values are then rendered from numbers, which keeps arithmetic working but drops the original text:

  • a captured 1.0 is published as 1, and 007 as 7;
  • a captured version such as 2.30 is published as 2.3;
  • a counter longer than the precision of a floating-point number loses its last digits.

When a value must keep its exact text, make it non-numeric on purpose (for example with a prefix in the regexp capture) or publish it as generic_data_string.

A jq expression that emits null counts as one match, and a reference to that value is undefined, so the module is skipped like any other unresolved reference. Where the module must publish anyway, give the default inside the expression, as in {{ value ?? "n/a" }}.

docs.title: Module fan-out and conditions
docs.text:
for_each names an array variable and expands the block into one module per element. Inside the block, {{ value }} is the current element and {{ index }} its 0-based position, which is what allows lockstep access to two parallel arrays. Writing several blocks with the same for_each is how one element produces several modules.

  • A scalar variable iterates as a one-element array.
  • An unset for_each variable skips the whole block; the notice is written only with -v.
  • Regexp filters with named capture groups make every element an object, so fields are read as {{ value.mount }}; two or more unnamed groups make every element a positional array, read as {{ value[0] }}.

when holds a boolean expression without {{ }}. It is evaluated per element inside a for_each block and against the whole variable store outside it. A false condition skips that element without an error; a condition that fails to evaluate, or that does not return a boolean, is reported and the module is skipped.

The executor does not deduplicate module names. Two elements that render the same name produce two modules with that name in the same document, so make the name unique with the element itself — as the example above does with {{ value.mount }}.

docs.title: What reaches Pandora FMS
docs.text:
In tentacle and local mode the executor builds one <agent_data> document per agent of the template. The agent attributes come from the template: agent_name, agent_alias, parent_agent_name, description, version, os_name, os_version, timestamp, address, group, interval and agent_mode. When timestamp is omitted the run time is used, and when interval is omitted the document carries 300.

Each module becomes a <module> element with <name>, <type> and <data>; description, unit, the thresholds and the rest of the supported fields are added when the template sets them. A module whose data field is empty or absent publishes the value 0.

In agent_plugin mode none of that header is emitted: only the <module> elements are printed, concatenated, with no XML declaration and no root element. The agent fields of the template — group, interval, alias, description, os_*, address — are therefore not applied, because the real agent supplies its own identity and interval. When the template declares more than one agent, each module name is prefixed with <agent name> + transfer.module_prefix_separator (default -) so the modules cannot collide under that single agent.

A module whose value cannot be resolved is absent from the document. Pandora FMS receives no data for it in that run: the executor sends no explicit unknown state, so the module simply stops receiving values. That is the behaviour to expect when a task fails, a filter matches nothing or a condition is false.

docs.title: Everyday operation
docs.text:
• One-shot and stateless. Every run reads its template, executes it and exits. Nothing is cached, so a manual run at any time is equivalent to a scheduled one.
  • Logging. Errors are always written to standard error with the pandora-plugin_exec: prefix and a timestamp. -v adds the debug stream there — stored variables, skips and delivery results — and leaves standard output clean for the XML. There is no log file and no log level.
  • local mode file names. The document is written as <md5 of the agent name>.<epoch seconds>.data inside transfer.local.directory, which is created with mode 0755 if it does not exist. Two runs of the same agent within the same second wait for the next second before writing, so a fast loop does not overwrite data.
  • tentacle mode staging. The document is written to a temporary directory under the system temporary directory, sent with the Tentacle client, and removed when the run ends.
  • Templates are executable content. A template decides which commands run on the host. Keep template files writable only by the user that runs the executor, and treat a template received from someone else as code you are about to execute.
  • Credentials. There is no secret store: a credential is written in the template, passed as a runtime parameter, or read by the command itself. A credential passed as a parameter is visible in the process list and in the shell history of whoever typed it, so keep templates at mode 0600 and prefer the credential-reading command pattern when the target supports it.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Two task types only: HTTP requests and local commands. There is no SNMP or database task, and the template has no conditional task execution.
  • No scheduling and no daemon mode: the run happens when the agent, cron or an operator starts it.
  • Tasks are sequential. A slow request delays every later task in the same run, and the run has no global timeout — only the per-task one.
  • HTTP responses are read up to 10 MiB. A larger body is truncated silently, and the truncation usually surfaces later as a JSON parse error in the filter.
  • A local task timeout terminates the /bin/sh process that runs the command; a command that starts its own children is responsible for stopping them.
  • No retries. A failed task leaves its variable unset, and only --strict turns that into a non-zero exit status; without it the reason is visible only with -v.
  • webhook delivery, per-template scheduling and additional task types are announced as not yet available in the addon's own documentation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• error: argument "--dry-run" looks like a flag; flags must come before the arguments — the flags were written after a positional token. Move every flag before the arguments.
  • Exit code 1 with invalid template: ... — the template failed to parse. The message names the offending field or line: an unknown field, a duplicated task name, a type that does not match its block, an invalid filter type, an invalid variable name, agents together with top-level modules, top-level modules without agent_plugin mode, a missing tentacle.address or a missing transfer.mode.
  • Exit code 1 with a template is required — -t was not passed, or the value was consumed by a preceding flag.
  • Exit code 2 — a task failed under --strict. Run again with -v to see which task and why.
  • A module is missing from the console — its value was never resolved. Run with -v and look for left unset, skipped or filter matched nothing; the usual causes are a task that failed, a filter that matched nothing, and a parameter that was not passed.
  • A module publishes 0 — the template does not set data, or the captured value was the empty string.
  • A number arrives with digits missing or without its decimals — numeric coercion (see Variables and module values). Publish the value as text when its exact form matters.
  • Exit code 3 with tentacle send failed — the Tentacle client could not deliver. Check that tentacle_client is in PATH or set transfer.tentacle.binary, the address and port in the template, and network access to the server. With several agents, the agents already sent in that run are delivered and the remaining ones are not.
  • local mode writes files but no agent appears — the documents were written into a directory the server does not ingest. Confirm transfer.local.directory character by character: a wrong path is created silently instead of reported.
  • task output is not valid JSON — the jq filter received something that is not JSON: an HTML error page, an empty body, a truncated body above 10 MiB, or a local command that printed a warning before the JSON.
  • unexpected status 401 / 403 / 500 — the request failed. The message carries the status and the first 200 characters of the response body, which is usually enough to tell authentication from a server error.
  • A request fails on a certificate — the endpoint presents a certificate the host does not trust. skip_tls_verify: true accepts invalid certificates for that task and disables the protection, so use it only for a target you control.
  • A local command hangs until the timeout — the task timeout expired and the shell was killed. Raise timeout for that task if the command legitimately needs longer, and check whether the child process that was left behind still holds a lock or a port.
  • when is ignored or the module never appears — when is a raw expression, so {{ }} around it is an error; inside a for_each block it sees value and index, not the array variable.

docs.title: Command-line flags
docs.text:
pandora-plugin_exec -t <template.yml> [flags] [args...] [key=value...]
Flag Effect -t, --template <path> Template to execute. Required --dry-run Prints the generated document on standard output and does not transfer or write it. Has no effect in agent_plugin mode, which always prints --strict Aborts on the first task failure or unresolved module instead of skipping it -v, --verbose Debug logging on standard error: task results, skips, warnings, delivery --version Prints the version and exits

Flags must precede the arguments, and an argument that begins with - is rejected with exit code 1.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Template parse or validation error, and usage errors such as a missing -t 2 Task failure under --strict, and any error while building an agent document 3 Transfer error: the Tentacle delivery or the local write failed

Without --strict, a failed task or an unresolved module does not change the exit status: the run delivers the modules that resolved and exits with 0, and the reason is written to standard error only with -v.

docs.title: Runtime parameter classification
docs.text:
Token Key Value Stored as sda1 — sda1 args[0] 90 — 90 args[0], number host=db01 host db01 params.host threshold=90 threshold 90 params.threshold, number conn=user=a;pw=b conn user=a;pw=b params.conn 'query\=a=b' — query=a=b positional, because the key is not an identifier =foo — =foo positional, because the key is empty k=1 k=2 k 2 params.k, the last value wins

args is always a list, even when empty, so for_each: args and len(args) are safe. params is always a map. Both are reserved: a task variable cannot use those names.

docs.title: Template: tasks
docs.text:
Field Required Description name Yes Unique task identifier, used in log lines type Yes request or local, and it must match the block that is present request When type: request HTTP request specification local When type: local Command specification filter No Extraction filter. Without it the trimmed raw output is the value variable No Name that stores the result, matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. Without it the output is discarded

Tasks support {{ }} in their string fields — URL, body, header values and command. Task name, variable and filter.expression are not rendered.

docs.title: request
docs.text:
Field Required Default Description url Yes — Target URL. Supports {{ }} method No GET GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH or HEAD. Not rendered headers No — Header name to value. Values support {{ }} body No — Request body. Supports {{ }} timeout No 30 Seconds, applied to the whole request skip_tls_verify No false Accepts invalid TLS certificates

A status outside 2xx fails the task, and the error carries the status and the first 200 characters of the body. The response body is read up to 10 MiB.

docs.title: local
docs.text:
Field Required Default Description command Yes — Executed with /bin/sh -c. Supports {{ }}; shell $ is untouched timeout No 30 Seconds; the shell process is terminated on expiry

A non-zero exit status fails the task, and the error carries the first 200 characters of standard error.

docs.title: Template: filters
docs.text:
Field Required Description type Yes jq or regexp expression Yes The filter expression. Not rendered

jq — the task output must be valid JSON, and the expression runs in an embedded engine, so no jq executable is needed. Every value the expression emits is one element: .token gives a scalar, .items[].name an array of strings, .items[] an array of objects, and . the whole document as one object.

regexp — RE2 syntax, applied to the raw output: no backtracking and no lookahead, while (?m) and (?i) are available. The shape of each match depends on its capture groups:

Pattern shape Each match becomes No capture group (cpu\d) The full match, as a string One unnamed group ((\d+)%) Capture group 1, as a string Two or more unnamed groups ((a)(b)(c)) A positional array: [[a, b, c], ...] Named groups ((?P<mount>...)) An object: group name to captured text

Named and unnamed groups in the same regexp are not a supported combination for predictable access: as soon as one group is named, each match becomes an object built only from the named groups.

Cardinality is the same for both types: 0 matches leaves the variable unset, 1 match stores a scalar, N matches store an array.

docs.title: Template: agents
docs.text:
Required unless the template uses top-level modules.

Field Required Description name Yes Agent name modules Yes At least one module block alias No Agent alias parent_agent_name No Parent agent description No Description version No Agent version string os_name, os_version No Operating system identification timestamp No Overrides the document timestamp. Defaults to the run time address No IP address or host name group No Target group interval No Seconds. The document carries 300 when omitted agent_mode No Agent mode. The document carries 1 when omitted

Every string field supports {{ }}. These fields are only used in tentacle and local mode.

docs.title: Control fields
docs.text:
These are executor semantics and are not sent to Pandora FMS.

Field Description for_each Name of an array variable. The block expands to one module per element, with {{ value }} and {{ index }} available. A scalar variable iterates as one element, and a named-group element is read as {{ value.field }} while a positional one is read as {{ value[0] }} when Raw boolean expression, without {{ }}. False skips the module, or that element inside a for_each block

docs.title: Data fields
docs.text:
name and type are required; the rest are optional. Values may be numbers or strings in YAML, and all of them support {{ }}. The executor passes every field to the data document; only interval changes its name, to module_interval.

Field Description name Module name type Module type: generic_data, generic_proc, generic_data_string, generic_data_inc, async_data, ... data Module value. An empty or absent data publishes 0 description Description unit Unit label interval Module interval, sent as module_interval tags Tags module_group Module group module_parent, module_parent_unlink Parent module relation min_warning, max_warning, min_critical, max_critical Numeric thresholds min_warning_forced, max_warning_forced, min_critical_forced, max_critical_forced Forced threshold variants str_warning, str_critical String-match thresholds str_warning_forced, str_critical_forced Forced string thresholds warning_inverse, critical_inverse Invert the threshold logic min, max Valid data range post_process Multiplier applied by the server disabled Create the module disabled status Force the module status timestamp Overrides the data timestamp custom_id Custom identifier critical_instructions, warning_instructions, unknown_instructions Operator instructions quiet Quiet mode min_ff_event, min_ff_event_normal, min_ff_event_warning, min_ff_event_critical FlipFlop thresholds module_ff_interval, ff_type, ff_timeout, each_ff FlipFlop behaviour crontab Cron-style module scheduling extra_data Extra payload alert_templates List of alert template names to bind

docs.title: Template: transfer
docs.text: Field Required Description mode Yes tentacle, local or agent_plugin tentacle.address For tentacle Pandora FMS server address tentacle.port No Tentacle port, 41121 by default tentacle.binary No Path to the Tentacle client when it is not in PATH tentacle.extra_args No Extra Tentacle client arguments, as a list local.directory For local Directory where the .data document is written module_prefix_separator No Separator for the multi-agent prefix in agent_plugin mode, " - " by default Mode Output Use case tentacle Complete <agent_data> document sent with the Tentacle client Remote execution from cron or the server local Complete <agent_data> document written as a .data file Running on the Pandora FMS server itself agent_plugin <module> fragments on standard output Running as the module_plugin of a software agent

docs.title: Expression language
docs.text:
{{ }} placeholders and when conditions are expressions in the syntax documented at expr-lang.org. Useful built-ins for template authors:

Category Built-ins and operators Strings split(s, sep) · join(list, sep) · upper(s) · lower(s) · trim(s) · replace(s, old, new) · contains(s, sub) · startsWith(s, pre) · endsWith(s, suf) · s matches "re2-pattern" Collections x in list · len(list) · list[i] · first(list) · last(list) · filter(list, pred) · map(list, expr) · all/any/none(list, pred) · sort(list) · uniq(list) · concat(a, b) Logic and nil a ?? "default" · obj?.field · cond ? a : b · 'key' in map Numbers + - * / % · abs(x) · min/max(a, b) · sum(list) · avg(list) · int(x) · float(x) · string(x) JSON toJSON(x) · fromJSON(s)

Inside the predicates of filter, map, all, any and none the current element is #, as in filter(filesystems, #.pct > 90).

The expression language is used only in {{ }} and in when. A task's filter.expression is jq or a RE2 regular expression, never an expression of this language. In regular expressions written inside when, double the backslash (\\d), because expression string literals process escapes and the engine must receive a verbatim \d.

docs.title: Bundled templates
docs.text:
Template Purpose templates/df_used.yml Filesystem usage: one percentage module and one size module per filesystem. Replaces pandora_df_used_go, with thresholds at 90 and 95 on the percentage module templates/pandora_mem_used.yml Memory and swap usage in percent and in bytes. Replaces pandora_mem_used templates/pandora_netusage.yml Total bytes received and transmitted from /proc/net/dev, published as an incremental module. Replaces pandora_netusage templates/http_api_example.yml Token authentication chain against a JSON API: login → token → two authenticated requests templates/local_commands_example.yml Local commands as an agent plugin, with the three regexp result shapes

All three replacements end in transfer.mode: agent_plugin and expect the invocation shown in their own header comment, with the template at /etc/pandora/templates/.

Copy these templates from the package if it carries a templates/ directory: the executor never installs a template and never reads one you did not pass with -t.

Template Parameter Default Effect df_used.yml include — Force monitoring of a mount whose fstype is outside the default list. Comma-separated, exact mount matches df_used.yml exclude — Never monitor a mount. Comma-separated, exact mount matches. Exclude wins over include pandora_netusage.yml include — Monitor only these interfaces. Comma-separated, exact names pandora_netusage.yml exclude — Never monitor an interface. Comma-separated, exact names. Exclude wins over include pandora_mem_used.yml mem_critical 95 Critical threshold of the Memory_Used percentage module pandora_mem_used.yml swap_critical 95 Critical threshold of the Swap_Used percentage module

The two byte modules of pandora_mem_used.yml compute their critical threshold inside the command, at 95 % of the corresponding total, and ignore those parameters.

The size module of df_used.yml publishes the Used column of df -kTP, which df reports in 1K blocks, while the template declares unit: "bytes". A filesystem whose df reports 1000000 in that column is published as 1000000 bytes, a value 1024 times smaller than the real usage. If you rely on that module, convert the value in the template or correct the unit.

docs.title: PostgreSQL monitoring plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use PostgreSQL Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path. The Marketplace entry states that this addon is no longer actively maintained.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The PostgreSQL monitoring plugin turns your own SQL queries into Pandora FMS modules. Each run connects to a PostgreSQL server, executes every query listed in a configuration file and builds one module per query. It is a server plugin: Pandora FMS executes it on a server, or you run it manually from a terminal.

The plugin is query-driven. It does not ship a fixed PostgreSQL metric model: the example configuration supplied with the addon queries connections, roles, version, locks, commits, rollbacks and tuple counters, and you can replace those queries with your own SELECT statements.

A run executes every query in the file once, then delivers the result in one of three ways:

  • Agent data file (default): the plugin writes an agent data XML file into the Pandora FMS data directory and prints 1.
  • Tentacle: with --tentacle_address, the plugin writes the same file, sends it with tentacle_client and then prints 1.
  • Module XML on standard output: with --as_agent_plugin 1, the plugin prints one <module> block per query on standard output and writes no file.

The plugin keeps no state between runs, so the values it publishes are the values PostgreSQL returns at execution time.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text:
Scope State Evidence Network access from the machine that runs the plugin to the PostgreSQL listener (TCP, --port, 5432 by default) Required The connection parameters -i and --port A PostgreSQL role able to read pg_stat_activity, pg_roles, pg_locks, pg_stat_database and pg_database Required The example queries shipped with the addon PostgreSQL 9.6 or later while the shipped wait_event queries are kept Required pg_stat_activity.wait_event exists from PostgreSQL 9.6; on older servers those two queries fail and their modules are skipped Pandora FMS Plugin Server enabled with the plugin_exec helper installed, when the plugin is registered in Pandora FMS Required Pandora FMS runs plugin modules through the Plugin Server A Pandora FMS data directory writable by the user that runs the plugin, for file and Tentacle delivery Required --data_dir, /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ by default Operating system and distribution of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for version 1.1 PostgreSQL server releases Not validated No PostgreSQL version matrix has been recorded for this addon Specific Pandora FMS versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded for this addon Tentacle delivery Not validated --tentacle_address needs a reachable tentacle_client; no such run has been recorded

The Marketplace record states that this plugin is no longer actively maintained and recommends an alternative plugin for new deployments. The record also limits the download to licensed users; see Addon identity.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Connectivity between the machine that runs the plugin and the PostgreSQL server. When the plugin runs as a server plugin, that machine is the Pandora FMS server that executes the module, which may be a remote server.
  2. A PostgreSQL role and password for monitoring. The shipped queries read cluster-wide views, so a role that only sees its own sessions undercounts the connection modules: to see every session, use a superuser or, in PostgreSQL 10 and later, a role with pg_read_all_stats.
  3. A Pandora FMS installation with the Plugin Server enabled, the console to register the plugin and create the module, and a writable data directory for the delivery mode you choose.
  4. The query file. The addon supplies an example; you can edit it or write your own. See Query configuration file.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the .pspz2 package from the Marketplace entry, which is limited to licensed users:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.postgresql_plugin

Register it in the console:

  1. Open Servers → Register plugin and upload the .pspz2 file with Upload file.
  2. Pandora FMS unpacks the package into the console's plugin attachment store, registers the plugin Pandora PostgreSQL with a maximum timeout of 20 seconds and 10 macros, and points the plugin command at the installed executable.
  3. A package whose plugin name is already registered is rejected with Plugin already registered. Aborting!.

The executable is named pandora_postgresql. If you prefer to register the plugin by hand instead of importing the package, place the executable on the Pandora FMS server and enter its absolute path as the plugin command; the parameters and macros are the ones in Register the server plugin.

docs.title: Register the server plugin
docs.text:
A plugin registered this way is available when creating plugin modules, and each module fills the macros individually. The packaged definition uses this parameter string:

-d _field1_ -u _field2_ -p _field3_ -i _field4_ --port _field5_ --conf _field6_ --agent_name _field7_ --prefix_module _field8_ -g _field9_ _field10_

The packaged definition wraps every macro in quotes. When you register the plugin manually, use the unquoted form above so each value reaches the executable without surrounding spaces.

Field Description Example value _field1_ Database name <DB_NAME> _field2_ PostgreSQL user <USERNAME> _field3_ Password for that user <PASSWORD> _field4_ PostgreSQL host or IP address <TARGET_HOST> _field5_ Database port; 5432 by default 5432 _field6_ Absolute path to the query file <PATH_TO_CONFIG> _field7_ Agent name; _agentname_ by default _agentname_ _field8_ Module name prefix <DB_NAME> _field9_ Destination group; Postgres by default <GROUP_NAME> _field10_ Extra raw arguments, appended at the end --data_dir /var/spool/pandora/data_in/

Two packaged defaults need attention before the first run:

  • The password macro is not hidden. The package imports _field3_ as a visible macro, so the password you enter is stored unencrypted and shown in the macro list. Enable the macro's Hide value option, which stores the value as a hidden, encrypted macro, and set the password afterwards.
  • The prefix default is a single dot. The plugin joins the prefix to the module name with an underscore, so leaving the packaged . produces names such as ._number_connections. Replace it with a meaningful prefix such as the database name, or clear it.

docs.title: Query configuration file
docs.text:
The file is plain text with one query per line and four colon-separated fields:

module_name:SELECT ...:module_type:description
  • The description is optional. A line with fewer than three fields stops the run before any module is produced, with It is mandatory to specify name, query and type!.
  • Any line containing # is ignored, and empty lines are ignored. Use comments on their own line.
  • The module name is written as the Pandora FMS module name, with the prefix from --prefix_module in front of it.
  • The module type is written into the module definition as it appears. Use Pandora FMS module types: generic_data, generic_data_inc, generic_data_string or generic_proc.
  • _database_ in a query is replaced by the database name given with -d, quoted with single quotes, so WHERE db.datname = _database_ becomes WHERE db.datname = '<DB_NAME>'.
  • The whole line is split on every colon. Do not use : inside the statement, including :: casts and time literals: the query is truncated and the module fails.

Minimal example:

number_connections:SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;:generic_data:Number of sessions
database_size_mb:SELECT ROUND(pg_database_size(current_database())/1024/1024);:generic_data:Database size in MB
db_version:SELECT version();:generic_data_string:PostgreSQL version
commits:SELECT sum(xact_commit) FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = _database_;:generic_data:Commits in the monitored database

Put the file where the user that runs the plugin can read it. The packaged default macro points to /var/www/html/pandora_console/attachment/plugin/pandora_postgresql.conf, next to the executable in a standard installation; change it to the path you actually use.

The addon executes every statement it finds. Keep the file to read-only SELECT statements, and verify each query manually before adding it to a production file.

docs.title: Create the plugin module
docs.text:
1. Open the agent that will hold the modules and create a module of type plugin.
  2. Select the registered Pandora PostgreSQL plugin and fill the macros for the target database.
  3. Save the module.

Every execution of a plugin module runs the whole query file and publishes all its modules. Create one plugin module per query file and database; several modules pointing at the same file repeat the same queries on every interval.

_agentname_ resolves to the agent that owns the module, so in this mode the generated modules land in that agent instead of creating a separate one. Replace it with a literal name only when you want a different agent.

A plugin module stores the plugin's standard output as its value. Keep the default delivery mode, which writes the agent data file and prints 1, so the module records 1 and the agent data file carries the metrics. Add --as_agent_plugin 1 only when the module is meant to receive module XML.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The password is part of the plugin parameters. In a plugin module it lives in the stored macro; with a hidden macro value it is stored encrypted. Avoid passing -p <PASSWORD> in an interactive command line: the shell history and the process list can expose it while the plugin runs.
  • The addon exposes no TLS parameters. Encryption and authentication of the database connection follow the PostgreSQL server and client configuration of the machine that runs the plugin.
  • Use a dedicated PostgreSQL role for Pandora FMS and grant only what its queries need.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually on the Pandora FMS server, under the same user that executes plugin modules:

./pandora_postgresql -d <DB_NAME> -u <USERNAME> -p <PASSWORD> -i <TARGET_HOST> \
    --port 5432 --conf <PATH_TO_CONFIG> --agent_name PostgreSQL

The default mode writes an agent data file into --data_dir and prints 1. A printed 0 means the run failed; see Operate and troubleshoot.

To inspect the generated modules without writing a file, add --as_agent_plugin 1. The plugin then prints one <module> block per query, for example:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[number_connections]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <datalist>
    <data>
        <value><![CDATA[12]]></value>
    </data>
    </datalist>
    <description><![CDATA[Number of sessions]]></description>
</module>

Values in the sample are illustrative. Once the plugin module runs on its interval, confirm in the console that the agent holds one module per query and that the plugin module itself reports 1.

No live run, database connection or console ingestion was performed while writing this page. The steps above are operator checks, not observed results.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
A successful run produces one agent and one module per query:

Property Value Agent name --agent_name; PostgreSQL by default, _agentname_ in the registered plugin Agent description PostgreSQL agent Group --group; Postgres by default Interval Empty in the agent definition; an agent that already exists keeps its own interval Module name The first field of the query line, prefixed with <prefix>_ when --prefix_module is set Module type The third field of the query line, as written Module description The fourth field of the query line, empty when omitted

Each module is emitted with a <datalist>: one entry per row returned by the query, with the columns of a row joined by ;. A single-row, single-column query — a count(*), for example — produces a list with one entry. Keep monitoring queries to one row and one column when you expect a single value.

The plugin does not set thresholds, units or alert templates. Thresholds and the module interval are configured in Pandora FMS on the generated module.

docs.title: Example queries
docs.text:
The example file supplied with the addon defines these queries:

Module Query Notes number_connections SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity; Sessions in the whole cluster, all databases, including the monitoring session connections_waiting_in_locks SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event = 'Lock'; Sessions waiting on a heavyweight lock connections_idle_in_transaction SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event = 'idle in transaction'; Always 0: idle in transaction is a session state, not a wait event, so the filter matches no row number_users SELECT COUNT(usename) FROM pg_stat_activity; Sessions that have a user name, not distinct roles number_roles SELECT count(*) FROM pg_roles; Roles in the cluster psql_version SELECT version(); Server version string num_blocks SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_locks; Rows in pg_locks, that is current lock entries, not deadlocks number_commits sum(xact_commit) for the monitored database Cumulative counter number_rollbacks sum(xact_rollback) for the monitored database Cumulative counter tuples_returned sum(tup_returned) for the monitored database Cumulative counter tuples_searched sum(tup_fetched) for the monitored database Cumulative counter tuples_inserted sum(tup_inserted) for the monitored database Cumulative counter tuples_updated sum(tup_updated) for the monitored database Cumulative counter tuples_removed sum(tup_deleted) for the monitored database Cumulative counter state SELECT state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = _database_; One row per session of the database number_connections_list SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity; One row per session, columns joined by ; number_databases_list select * from pg_database; One row per database

The counters use generic_data, so Pandora FMS stores the cumulative value returned by PostgreSQL. Define the module as generic_data_inc in the query file when you want the increment between runs instead.

A query that fails does not stop the run: the plugin writes the error to standard error and continues with the next query, so its module is missing for that execution while the others are still published.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
• Every run opens one connection, executes the queries sequentially and closes the connection. There is no parallelism and no debug or verbose flag; the diagnostic channels are standard output, standard error and the exit status.
  • When the plugin runs as a server plugin, Pandora FMS schedules it on the module interval. Run it manually only under the same user and with the same macros as the module.
  • The package registers a maximum timeout of 20 seconds per execution, and Pandora FMS applies the lower of that value and the server's plugin_timeout. A query file with slow statements can hit the limit; keep the queries cheap.
Signal Cause and check the following arguments are required: -d/--database, -u/--user, -p/--password, -i/--ip, --conf A required argument is missing. The parser prints its usage and exits with status 2 Error while creating PostgreSQL table ... followed by Error: ... and 0 The connection failed: unreachable host or port, wrong database, wrong credentials, or pg_hba.conf rejecting the client. The first message is printed on standard output, the rest on standard error Error al conectarse ... The query file could not be opened. Check --conf and the permissions of the file for the user that runs the plugin error with the query:<query>.<error> PostgreSQL rejected one query. The remaining queries still run; fix the statement or the privileges of the role It is mandatory to specify name, query and type! A query line has fewer than three colon-separated fields. The run stops without producing modules A module is missing while the others appear Its query failed, its line is malformed, or it uses a column that does not exist in that PostgreSQL release ERROR - Could not write file: ..., please check directory permissions --data_dir does not exist or is not writable by the user that runs the plugin. The run exits with status 1 Tentacle error or Tentacle error: ... and no 1 Tentacle delivery failed: tentacle_client is missing or --tentacle_address/--tentacle_port are wrong. The data file stays in --data_dir 0 printed instead of 1 The run failed before generating modules; read the preceding messages The module reports 1 but no data reaches Pandora FMS The data file was written somewhere the Data Server does not read. Check --data_dir against the server's incomingdir

The plugin exits with status 0 for a successful run and also for a run that failed after reading its arguments — a connection error, an unreadable query file or a malformed line — because those failures are reported by the printed 0 and the error messages, not by the exit status. Use the printed value and the message text, not the exit status alone, to judge a manual run.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
./pandora_postgresql -d <DB_NAME> -u <USERNAME> -p <PASSWORD> -i <TARGET_HOST> [options]
Name Required Default Description -d, --database Yes — Database to connect to and the value substituted for _database_ -u, --user Yes — PostgreSQL user -p, --password Yes — Password for that user. It is not the port -i, --ip Yes — PostgreSQL host or IP address --conf Yes — Path to the query configuration file --port No 5432 PostgreSQL port --agent_name No PostgreSQL Name of the agent written in the agent data file --prefix_module No Empty Prefix joined to every module name with _ -g, --group No Postgres Group written in the agent definition --data_dir No /var/spool/pandora/data_in/ Directory where the agent data file is written --tentacle_address No Empty Tentacle server address. When set, the data file is sent with tentacle_client --tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port --as_agent_plugin No 0 1 prints the module XML on standard output; any other value writes the agent data file -h, --help No — Print the help and exit

docs.title: Query file fields
docs.text: Position Field Required Description 1 Module name Yes Pandora FMS module name, without the prefix 2 Query Yes SQL statement executed as written, after _database_ substitution 3 Type Yes Pandora FMS module type written into the module definition 4 Description No Module description; empty when omitted
