docs.text: Property Value Marketplace identifier pandorafms.postgresql_plugin Name PostgreSQL monitoring Version 1.1 Marketplace last update 2025-08-20 Package pandorafms.postgresql_plugin.1.1.pspz2 Registered plugin name Pandora PostgreSQL License One; the download is limited to licensed users Maintenance The Marketplace record states the plugin is no longer actively maintained Maximum execution timeout 20 seconds

docs.title: RabbitMQ Local monitoring plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-29.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use RabbitMQ Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The rabbitmq-local plugin monitors the state of a RabbitMQ cluster from Pandora FMS. Each run queries the RabbitMQ management HTTP API and turns the result into Pandora FMS modules: cluster totals, per-node resource metrics, exchange activity, connection counters and an availability check.

The plugin supports two execution models:

This page documents the plugin bundled with the Pandora FMS agent. The Marketplace addon pandorafms.rabbitmq is a different one: see RabbitMQ monitoring plugin.

  • Server plugin mode (default; selected when as_agent_plugin is absent, 0 or empty): each run builds an agent_data document and delivers it to Pandora FMS through Tentacle or through a local data folder.
  • Agent plugin mode (requires an explicit as_agent_plugin=1): each run prints the generated modules as XML on standard output, for the Pandora FMS agent to ingest.

docs.title: Compatibility and availability
docs.text: The plugin has been validated on Rocky Linux 9 against a RabbitMQ broker running 3.13.7 with the management plugin enabled. The broker must expose its management HTTP API on the management port — 15672 by default in RabbitMQ — and the machine that runs the plugin must be able to reach it. The plugin adds no default port: include the management port in host (see Configure).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A RabbitMQ broker with the management plugin enabled.
  2. A RabbitMQ user allowed to query the management API.
  3. A Pandora FMS installation to receive the plugin output: the Pandora FMS server when running in server mode, or the monitored endpoint when running in agent plugin mode.
  4. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) available in PATH, only when the server mode delivers through Tentacle.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text: The plugin is distributed as the rabbitmq-local executable and its rabbitmq-local.conf configuration file. Copy both files to the host that will run the plugin. The configuration file is optional: when it is used, it is passed to the executable as its only positional argument.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin combines three configuration sources, in increasing precedence:

defaults < configuration file < command-line flags

The configuration file is optional. When it is used, it must be the single positional argument: the first command-line argument that does not start with -, and no other. It is a plain-text file with key=value lines. Every key can also be passed as a command-line flag, in any of these four forms:

-key value    --key value    -key=value    --key=value

Flags override the file values, so a shared file can hold the common settings while each execution overrides what it needs. The configuration is validated strictly: an unknown flag, a flag without a value at the end of the command line and a second positional argument are configuration errors reported on standard error with exit status 1.

Server plugin mode is the default and needs an agent name and a delivery target. This is the minimum configuration for a server plugin run with Tentacle:

host=<RABBITMQ_HOST>:<MANAGEMENT_PORT>
user=<RABBITMQ_USER>
pass=<RABBITMQ_PASSWORD>
agent_name=rabbitmq-local
interval=300
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<PANDORA_FMS_SERVER>
tentacle_port=41121

Or copy the generated XML to a local data folder:

host=<RABBITMQ_HOST>:<MANAGEMENT_PORT>
user=<RABBITMQ_USER>
pass=<RABBITMQ_PASSWORD>
agent_name=rabbitmq-local
transfer_mode=local
local_folder=/var/spool/pandora/data_in

Agent plugin mode requires an explicit as_agent_plugin=1. This is the minimum configuration for an agent plugin run:

host=<RABBITMQ_HOST>:<MANAGEMENT_PORT>
user=<RABBITMQ_USER>
pass=<RABBITMQ_PASSWORD>
as_agent_plugin=1

The same agent plugin configuration with flags only, without a configuration file:

./rabbitmq-local -host <RABBITMQ_HOST>:<MANAGEMENT_PORT> -user <RABBITMQ_USER> -pass <RABBITMQ_PASSWORD> -as_agent_plugin 1

The credentials can also be read from a separate file, so neither the user nor the password appears in the command line or in the operating system process list:

# Credentials read from a file (readable only by the plugin user).
./rabbitmq-local -host <RABBITMQ_HOST>:<MANAGEMENT_PORT> \
    -cred_file /etc/pandora/plugins/rabbitmq-local.creds -as_agent_plugin 1

The credentials file uses key=value lines:

user=<RABBITMQ_USER>
pass=<RABBITMQ_PASSWORD>

agent_name, interval, transfer_mode, local_folder and the tentacle_* keys are server mode only: they are ignored while the plugin runs in agent plugin mode. The same server mode run with flags, overriding the file values:

./rabbitmq-local rabbitmq-local.conf -agent_name rabbitmq-local \
    -transfer_mode tentacle -tentacle_ip <PANDORA_FMS_SERVER>

Key points:

  • host accepts host, host:port, http://host:port or https://host:port; when no scheme is given the plugin queries http://<host>. The plugin adds no default port: a host without a port uses the scheme default (80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS), so include the management port — 15672 is RabbitMQ's default — unless a proxy serves the API on the scheme default port.
  • ca_file points to a PEM bundle with the CA that signs the management API certificate. It is only used with an https host; without it, HTTPS verifies against the system trust store.
  • The credentials can be set inline (user and pass) or in a separate key=value file (cred_file) with the user and pass lines. When cred_file is set — in the configuration file or as a flag — it takes precedence over user and pass. An unreadable file, or a file without user or pass, is an error.
  • In server mode, agent_name names the agent created in Pandora FMS, and interval is the agent interval in seconds.
  • The transfer mode is Tentacle only when transfer_mode=tentacle; any other value, including the default, copies the XML into local_folder.
  • Command-line flags replace the file values, for example ./rabbitmq-local rabbitmq-local.conf -interval 60.
  • The shipped rabbitmq-local.conf sets as_agent_plugin=1 and leaves the server mode keys commented out, so it starts in agent plugin mode as it is.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• Prefer HTTPS: with an https:// host the credentials and the collected metrics travel encrypted. With plain HTTP they travel unencrypted, so restrict the management API to a trusted network, or place a TLS proxy in front of it.
  • HTTPS verifies the server certificate against the system trust store, or against the ca_file bundle when one is configured.
  • Inline pass is stored in the configuration file in plain text: restrict the file permissions to the user that runs the plugin.
  • Avoid -pass on the command line: the command is stored in the shell history and the operating system process list can expose it while the plugin runs. Use -cred_file with a credentials file readable only by the plugin user (for example chmod 600).
  • The credentials file is stored in plain text as well: its protection is the file system permission model, so keep it owned by the plugin user and readable by nobody else.

docs.title: Register the plugin in the console
docs.text:
The plugin can also be registered in the Pandora FMS console as a server plugin, so Pandora FMS executes it on the server that runs the modules — the main server or a remote server — instead of in a command line. Registered this way the plugin keeps its server mode: every run builds the agent XML and delivers it, and the agent with its modules appears in the console.

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set the name, the plugin type Standard, an optional maximum timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the path to the rabbitmq-local executable on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/rabbitmq-local.
  4. In Plugin parameters, keep server mode (no as_agent_plugin key) and use the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... as placeholders:
-host _field1_ -user _field2_ -pass _field3_ -agent_name _field4_ -transfer_mode tentacle -tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1
  1. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:
Field Description Example value _field1_ Management API host, including the port http://rabbit.example.com:15672 _field2_ RabbitMQ user allowed to query the management API monitoring _field3_ Password for that user; mark Hide value — _field4_ Name of the agent that will hold the modules in the console RabbitMQ-remote-agent

-transfer_mode tentacle -tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 delivers the agent to the Tentacle server of the machine that runs the plugin, so the agent lands in the Pandora FMS server that executes the module. To copy the XML to a local data folder instead, replace those flags with -transfer_mode local -local_folder /var/spool/pandora/data_in.

Once registered, the plugin is available when creating plugin modules, and each module fills the fields individually. The module is executed on the server selected for it, including a remote Pandora FMS server, so each broker is monitored from the Pandora FMS server closest to it without installing anything on the broker host. The same registered plugin serves several RabbitMQ instances, and the field values can use the Pandora FMS macros documented in the console Plug-in macros help.

The registered parameters can also include -cred_file — with a fixed path or as a field — so the modules read the credentials from a file on the Pandora FMS server instead of holding them in module fields. The parameters can also point to a configuration file on the server — a literal path or a _fieldN_ field — so the file supplies the shared settings.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from a terminal, passing the configuration file as its only positional argument:

./rabbitmq-local /etc/pandora/plugins/rabbitmq-local.conf

The relative form ./rabbitmq-local rabbitmq-local.conf works when the terminal is already in the directory that contains both files. Each run executes once and exits.

The plugin prints its usage summary (every parameter and five examples) with ./rabbitmq-local -h.

In agent plugin mode, a successful run prints one XML <module> block per generated module on standard output. The sample below shows an excerpt of a run against a single-node cluster:

<module>
  <name><![CDATA[Cluster name]]></name>
  <type>generic_data_string</type>
  <data><![CDATA[rabbit@node01]]></data>
</module>
<module>
  <name><![CDATA[Total queue messages]]></name>
  <type>generic_data</type>
  <data><![CDATA[12]]></data>
</module>
<module>
  <name><![CDATA[Availability]]></name>
  <type>generic_proc</type>
  <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
  <description><![CDATA[Rabbit MQ API availability]]></description>
</module>
<module>
  <name><![CDATA[Memory used - rabbit@node01]]></name>
  <type>generic_data</type>
  <data><![CDATA[174895104]]></data>
  <description><![CDATA[Usually in bytes. Represents the total memory that the RabbitMQ node is using at that instant.]]></description>
</module>

In server mode, a successful run prints 1 and the agent configured in agent_name appears in Pandora FMS with its modules. If the run does not generate modules, see Operate and troubleshoot.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The plugin generates the same module catalog in both execution models. The modules cover five groups:

  • Cluster level. Cluster name, Total queue messages, Messages unacknowledged, Total exchanges and the Queue publish rate, Queue deliver get rate and Queue deliver noack rate modules report the totals and rates of the whole cluster.
  • Node level. For every cluster node, Memory used - <node> and Memory rate - <node> report its memory consumption, Proc used - <node> and Proc details - <node> its Erlang processes, and Node status - <node> whether the node is running.
  • Exchange level. Exchanges in rate and Exchanges out rate report the publish-in and publish-out rate of the last exchange that reports activity; when no exchange reports a rate, both modules report 0.
  • Connection level. Total connections, Connections running and Connections blocked count the open connections, and Total received octets and Total sent octets sum their received and sent octet rates.
  • Availability. Availability is 1 when the cluster overview request succeeds and 0 otherwise.

When the management API cannot be reached — wrong credentials, network problem, disabled management plugin — Availability reports 0, the node modules are omitted from the output, and the exchange and connection modules report 0.

docs.title: Operate and troubleshoot
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state between runs: every execution queries the broker at that moment, so it can be executed manually at any time.
  • In server mode, schedule the plugin from Pandora FMS (for example, through the server plugin scheduler or cron) and use interval to match the desired agent interval. In agent plugin mode, the Pandora FMS agent executes it according to the configured plugin schedule.
  • Availability reports 0 — the cluster overview request failed. Check that the management plugin is enabled, that host names the management port and that the credentials can query the management API. With an https host, also check that the server certificate verifies: point ca_file at the CA bundle when the API uses a private certificate.
  • No module XML is printed — running with no arguments at all, or with -h/--help, prints the usage summary and stops instead of generating modules. Run the plugin with the configuration flags or with the path to an existing configuration file. When the configuration is missing a required value (host, user, the password from any of its sources, agent_name in server mode, tentacle_ip for Tentacle delivery or local_folder otherwise), the plugin prints the error and a pointer to -h without generating modules.
  • The plugin exits with cannot read cred_file, cred_file ... is missing user or cred_file ... is missing pass — the credentials file must exist, be readable by the plugin user and define both user and pass. Fix the file or fall back to inline user and pass.
  • No per-node modules appear while Availability reports 1 — the nodes request failed; the rest of the cluster modules are still generated. Repeat the run and check the broker node list.
  • Server mode does not print 1 — the delivery failed. Check that tentacle_client is available and can reach tentacle_ip:tentacle_port, or that local_folder exists and is writable.
  • The data looks stale in Pandora FMS — the plugin always reports the values the broker returns at execution time; check the broker itself and the execution schedule.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The configuration file is optional: without it, the plugin runs from the defaults plus the flags.

Name Required Default Description host Yes — Management API host, in host, host:port, http://host:port or https://host:port form. HTTP is the default. Include the management port: no default port is added. ca_file No — PEM bundle with the CA that signs the management API certificate (only used with an https host). user Yes, unless cred_file is set — RabbitMQ user allowed to query the management API. pass Yes, unless cred_file is set — Password for user. cred_file No — File with the credentials as key=value lines (user and pass), with the same format as the configuration file. When set, it takes precedence over user and pass. Use an absolute path readable only by the plugin user. An unreadable file, or a file without user or pass, is an error. agent_name Required in server mode — Server mode only. Name of the agent created in Pandora FMS. interval No 300 Server mode only. Agent interval in seconds. as_agent_plugin No 0 (server plugin) 1 (or any value other than 0) prints the module XML on standard output; 0 (or an empty value) builds and delivers an agent. tmp No System temporary folder Folder used to write the XML document before delivery. transfer_mode Conditional Empty (local copy) Server mode only. tentacle delivers with the Tentacle client; any other value, including the default, copies the XML into local_folder. local_folder Required when not using Tentacle — Server mode only. Destination folder for the XML copy. tentacle_ip Required when transfer_mode=tentacle — Server mode only. Tentacle server address. tentacle_port No 41121 Server mode only. Tentacle server port. tentacle_opts No Empty Server mode only. Extra options passed to the Tentacle client, separated by whitespace.

The file uses key=value lines. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and the last occurrence of a repeated key wins.

When cred_file is set — in the configuration file or on the command line — the credentials are read from that file and used instead of user and pass.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
./rabbitmq-local [config-file] [ -key value ... ]
Condition Behavior The command line is empty The plugin prints the usage summary and stops No positional argument, but flags are present The plugin runs from the defaults plus the flags The positional argument names an existing file The plugin runs with the file configuration, overridden by the flags The positional argument names a file that does not exist The plugin reports the error on standard error and exits with status 1 -key value, --key value, -key=value or --key=value Each flag replaces the value with the same key from the file or the defaults -h or --help anywhere in the command line The plugin prints the usage summary and stops An unknown flag, a flag without a value, or a second positional argument The plugin reports the error on standard error and exits with status 1

Flags can appear before or after the configuration file path.

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
In the names below, <node> is a cluster node name:

Module name Type Meaning Cluster name generic_data_string Cluster name reported by the broker Total queue messages generic_data Total messages in all queues Messages unacknowledged generic_data Total messages delivered but not acknowledged Total exchanges generic_data Total number of exchanges Queue publish rate generic_data Cluster publish rate Queue deliver get rate generic_data Rate of messages fetched directly from queues Queue deliver noack rate generic_data Rate of messages delivered to consumers without acknowledgement Availability generic_proc 1 when the cluster overview request succeeds, 0 otherwise Memory used - <node> generic_data Memory used by the node, in bytes Memory rate - <node> generic_data Rate at which the node memory is consumed or released Proc used - <node> generic_data Erlang processes used by the node Proc details - <node> generic_data Rate at which the node Erlang processes are created or terminated Node status - <node> generic_proc 1 while the node is running, 0 otherwise Exchanges in rate generic_data Publish-in rate of the last exchange that reports one; 0 when none reports activity Exchanges out rate generic_data Publish-out rate of the last exchange that reports one; 0 when none reports activity Total connections generic_data Number of open client connections Connections running generic_data Connections in the running state Connections blocked generic_data Connections that are not in the running state Total received octets generic_data Sum of the received-octet rate over all connections Total sent octets generic_data Sum of the sent-octet rate over all connections

docs.title: RabbitMQ monitoring plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-29.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use RabbitMQ Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The RabbitMQ monitoring plugin turns the state of a RabbitMQ broker or cluster into Pandora FMS modules. Each run queries the RabbitMQ management HTTP API and builds one module set: cluster totals and message rates, memory and process usage per node, the status of each node, exchange publish rates, connection counters and an availability check.

Nothing is installed on the RabbitMQ nodes. The plugin runs on the host you choose and reads the broker over HTTP with a single credential pair.

The plugin supports two execution models:

  • Server plugin mode (default when as_agent_plugin is absent or disabled): each run builds an agent document and delivers it to Pandora FMS through Tentacle or a local data folder.
  • Agent plugin mode (requires as_agent_plugin=1): each run prints the generated modules as XML on standard output, for the Pandora FMS agent to ingest.

This page documents the Marketplace addon pandorafms.rabbitmq. The RabbitMQ Local plugin that ships with the Pandora FMS agent is a different addon: it reads the same API but has its own configuration keys and generates its own module set. It is documented in RabbitMQ Local monitoring plugin; do not mix the two configurations.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon pandorafms.rabbitmq, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity A RabbitMQ broker with the management plugin enabled Required The plugin reads /api/overview, /api/nodes, /api/exchanges and /api/connections, which the management plugin provides HTTP access from the host that runs the plugin to the management listener (TCP, 15672 by default in RabbitMQ) Required The plugin sends every request to the base URL in host A RabbitMQ user allowed to read node and connection data Required One HTTP Basic credential pair, user and pass; RabbitMQ's own documentation states that the monitoring tag grants node-level data and other users' connections tentacle_client on the host that runs the plugin Required when transfer_mode=tentacle Server plugin delivery RabbitMQ broker versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded. The legacy guide only states that the plugin was developed against RabbitMQ 3.7.18; the plugin itself asks nothing beyond an API that answers the four documented endpoints Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Pandora FMS NG 784 and later Supported The Marketplace states that all its integrations are compatible with Pandora FMS NG 784 and later versions; it is a catalogue-wide statement covering this addon, not a test record for it TLS to the management API Not validated The addon has no TLS, proxy or CA option: the base URL is used as given

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. The RabbitMQ management plugin enabled on at least one node. It is included in the RabbitMQ distribution and is enabled with rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_management; no restart is needed. Any node with the plugin enabled answers for the whole cluster, so one address is enough even in a multi-node deployment.
  2. Network access from the host that runs the plugin to that listener. The management UI and API use port 15672 by default, and 15671 when RabbitMQ serves them over TLS.
  3. A RabbitMQ user that can query the four endpoints. The plugin authenticates with HTTP Basic, so it needs a user name and a password. The monitoring tag is what RabbitMQ documents for node-level data and other users' connections; a monitoring-only user is created with that tag and with empty resource permissions.
  4. Pandora FMS to receive the output: the Pandora FMS server in server plugin mode, or the Pandora FMS agent of the monitored host in agent plugin mode.
  5. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) available in PATH, only when server plugin mode delivers through Tentacle.

The shipped example configuration uses the RabbitMQ guest account. In a standard RabbitMQ installation guest can only connect from localhost, so replace it with the dedicated monitoring user.

docs.title: Install the addon
docs.text:
Download the package from the Marketplace entry (the download is limited to licensed users):

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/pandorafms.rabbitmq

Copy the rabbitmq_monitor executable to the host that will run it — for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/rabbitmq_monitor when it runs on the Pandora FMS server — and place its configuration file next to it or in any directory you can protect. The package also includes an example rabbitmq_monitor.conf; edit a copy of it, because its values are examples.

Nothing is installed on the RabbitMQ nodes, and no RabbitMQ client tools are needed on the monitoring host: all data comes from the management HTTP API.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin combines three sources, in increasing precedence:

defaults < configuration file < command-line arguments

The configuration file is optional. When it is used it must be the first argument of the command line; a path placed after a flag is not read as a configuration file. It is a plain-text file with one key=value pair per line. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and the last occurrence of a repeated key wins. There are no sections: a bracketed header is stored as an unused key.

The file name in the examples, rabbitmq_monitor.conf, is a convention, not a requirement.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Agent plugin mode is the shortest configuration: the Pandora FMS agent runs the plugin and ingests the module XML it prints.

host=http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672
user=<USERNAME>
pass=<PASSWORD>
as_agent_plugin=1

Server plugin mode needs an agent name and a delivery target. With Tentacle:

host=http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672
user=<USERNAME>
pass=<PASSWORD>
agent_name=RabbitMQ
interval=300
transfer_mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<PANDORA_FMS_URL>
tentacle_port=41121

Or copy the agent document into a local data folder instead of using Tentacle:

host=http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672
user=<USERNAME>
pass=<PASSWORD>
agent_name=RabbitMQ
interval=300
transfer_mode=local
local_folder=/var/spool/pandora/data_in

The same agent plugin run with arguments only, without a configuration file:

./rabbitmq_monitor -host http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672 -user <USERNAME> -pass <PASSWORD> -as_agent_plugin 1

Key points:

  • host is the base URL of the management API, including the scheme and the port: http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672. The plugin appends the /api/... paths to this value, so a bare host:port is not a complete request URL. The shipped example (host=192.168.80.20:8080) is a placeholder with a non-default port; replace it.
  • user and pass are sent as HTTP Basic credentials on every request. They must belong to a user that can read the endpoints listed in Prerequisites. There is no token, certificate or alternative authentication surface.
  • as_agent_plugin selects the model. 1 (or any numeric value greater than 0) prints module XML on standard output; 0, an empty value or a non-numeric value keeps server plugin mode. as_server_plugin=0 also selects agent plugin mode when as_agent_plugin is absent, and as_agent_plugin wins when both keys are present.
  • agent_name names the agent created in Pandora FMS, and interval is its interval in seconds. Both are server plugin mode only.
  • transfer_mode selects the delivery. tentacle (case-sensitive) runs the Tentacle client; any other value copies the agent document into local_folder.
  • module_group names the module group assigned to every generated module. module_interval and module_tag_list set the module interval and the module tags in the same way. When they are absent the modules carry no group, no own interval and no tags.
  • One agent per broker. Module names carry no broker prefix, so two brokers delivered to the same agent overwrite each other's modules. Use a different agent_name per broker, or one agent plugin installation per broker.

In agent plugin mode the executable is declared as a plugin of the Pandora FMS agent — in the agent configuration file or through remote configuration — with the configuration file as the first argument of the plugin command and as_agent_plugin=1 inside that file. The agent runs the plugin, reads the module XML from standard output and reports the modules in its own agent, so agent_name, interval and the transfer keys are not used in this mode.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The plugin has no TLS options of its own: it requests the base URL you give it. With an http:// base URL the credentials and the collected metrics travel unencrypted, so keep the management listener on a trusted network or serve it through a TLS terminator. RabbitMQ serves the management API over HTTPS on port 15671 when it is configured for TLS; an https:// base URL depends on the TLS support available to the executable and is not validated here.
  • There is no CA bundle, proxy or certificate-verification key. A private or self-signed certificate therefore has no supported configuration path in this addon.
  • pass is stored in the configuration file in plain text: restrict the file permissions to the user that runs the plugin (for example chmod 600).
  • Avoid -pass on the command line: the command is stored in the shell history and the operating system process list can expose it while the plugin runs. A scheduled server plugin keeps its parameters in the Pandora FMS database, so treat the module definition as sensitive as well.

docs.title: Register the plugin in Pandora FMS
docs.text:
rabbitmq_monitor can also be registered in the Pandora FMS console as a standard server plugin, so Pandora FMS executes it on the server that runs the modules instead of in a command line. Registered this way the plugin keeps server plugin mode: every run builds the agent document and delivers it, and the agent with its modules appears in the console.

  1. Open Servers → Plugins and click Register Plugin.
  2. Set the name, the plugin type Standard, an optional maximum timeout and a description.
  3. In Plugin command, enter the absolute path to rabbitmq_monitor on the Pandora FMS server, for example /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin/rabbitmq_monitor.

  4. In Plugin parameters, pass the documented keys and use the plugin macros _field1_, _field2_, ... as placeholders. For one broker in server plugin mode with Tentacle:

    -host _field1_ -user _field2_ -pass _field3_ -agent_name _field4_ -transfer_mode tentacle -tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 -tentacle_port 41121

  5. In Macro parameters, describe each field. The example uses these values:

    Field Description Example value _field1_ Management API base URL, including scheme and port http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672 _field2_ RabbitMQ user allowed to read the management API <USERNAME> _field3_ Password for that user; mark Hide value — _field4_ Name of the agent that will hold the modules RabbitMQ

-tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 delivers to the Tentacle server of the machine that runs the plugin, so the agent lands in the Pandora FMS server that executes the module. To copy the document into a local data folder instead, replace the Tentacle parameters with -transfer_mode local -local_folder /var/spool/pandora/data_in.

Once registered, the plugin is available when creating plugin modules, and each module fills the fields individually. The module is executed on the server selected for it, including a remote Pandora FMS server, so each broker is monitored from the Pandora FMS server closest to it without installing anything on the broker host.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from a terminal, passing the configuration file as its first argument:

./rabbitmq_monitor /etc/pandora/plugins/rabbitmq_monitor.conf

The relative form ./rabbitmq_monitor rabbitmq_monitor.conf works when the terminal is already in the directory that contains both files. Each run executes once and exits.

An empty command line prints the usage summary:

- Syntax:

./rabbitmq_monitor <plugin_configuration_file_path>

There is no help flag: -h and --help are treated like any other argument.

In agent plugin mode, a successful run prints one XML <module> block per generated module on standard output. This is an excerpt of the document built for a single-node cluster:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Cluster name]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[rabbit@node01]]></data>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Availability]]></name>
    <type>generic_proc</type>
    <data><![CDATA[1]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Rabbit MQ API availability]]></description>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[Memory used - rabbit@node01]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[174895104]]></data>
    <description><![CDATA[Usually in bytes. Represents the total memory that the RabbitMQ node is using at that instant.]]></description>
</module>

Availability is 1 only when the overview request succeeds; a 0 there means the overview request did not return HTTP 200 (see Operate and troubleshoot).

In server plugin mode a run prints 1 and exits. That 1 is printed after the delivery attempt, not as its result: a failed Tentacle transfer or a failed local copy also prints 1. Confirm the agent and its modules in the console.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text:
The module catalog is fixed. A run emits eight modules on every execution, adds six when the overview request succeeds and adds five per node when the nodes request succeeds. A single-node cluster with a healthy API therefore produces 19 modules.

  • Availability and connection counters (always). Availability, Total connections, Connections running, Connections blocked, Total received octets, Total sent octets, Exchanges in rate and Exchanges out rate are generated on every run, even when no request succeeds.
  • Cluster totals (overview request). Cluster name, Total queue messages, Messages unacknowledged, Total exchanges, Queue publish rate, Queue deliver get rate and Queue deliver noack rate are generated only when /api/overview answers with HTTP 200.
  • Per node (nodes request). For every node the API returns, Memory used - <node>, Memory rate, Proc used - <node>, Proc details and `Node status
  • ` are generated. When the nodes request fails, none of these modules is generated, and the rest of the run is unaffected.

How the values are read:

  • Rates are per-second rates taken from the rate fields the management API computes over its own sampling interval. Memory rate and Proc details are the memory and process rates of a node; Exchanges in rate and Exchanges out rate are publish rates of one exchange, not cluster totals: the plugin walks the exchange list and keeps the last exchange that reports a non-zero rate. When no exchange reports one, both modules report 0.
  • Connections blocked is every connection whose state is not exactly running. It is not a count of connections in RabbitMQ's blocked state.
  • Total received octets and Total sent octets are the sum of the per-connection receive and send octet rates, so they are throughput in octets per second, not accumulated totals.
  • Memory rate and Proc details carry no node name, unlike the other three per-node modules. In a cluster with more than one node each node adds its own module with the same name, so these two series cannot be attributed to a node. Use them only on single-node clusters where the name is unambiguous.
  • Queue deliver get rate does not report what its name says. The module reads the publish rate when the get rate is present, so in practice it repeats Queue publish rate or reports 0. Use Queue publish rate for publish activity and do not alert on Queue deliver get rate.

When the management API cannot be reached — wrong credentials, network problem, management plugin disabled — every request fails: Availability reports 0, the six cluster modules and the five per-node modules are not generated, and the seven remaining modules report 0.

The agent document created in server plugin mode carries the name and alias from agent_name and the interval from interval. Its address attribute is derived from host by splitting on :; in this version it holds the number of colon-separated parts (for example 3 for http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672), not the broker address, so do not expect the agent address field to show the broker.

docs.title: Everyday operation
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state between runs: every execution reads the broker at that moment, so it can be run manually at any time.
  • In server plugin mode, schedule it from Pandora FMS (the server plugin scheduler or cron) or from any external scheduler. In agent plugin mode, the Pandora FMS agent executes it according to the configured plugin schedule. interval only sets the interval of the agent created in the console; it does not schedule the plugin.
  • Use debug=1 for diagnostics. The addon writes its own messages to standard error only when debug is enabled: temporary-file write errors, Tentacle output and local-copy errors are silent without it. debug does not write to standard output, so it does not corrupt the module XML in agent plugin mode.
  • The agent document is written to the folder in tmp (default /tmp) as <agent_name>.<epoch>.data, and the file is removed after a successful Tentacle or local delivery. A failed delivery leaves it in place: check that folder when deliveries fail repeatedly, and clear it once the cause is fixed.
  • A run stopped with SIGTERM prints Received SIGTERM, exiting... and exits with status 0, so a timeout looks like a successful run. Set a maximum timeout in the plugin definition only if you can verify the expected run time for your broker size.
  • Create one agent per broker, with a distinct agent_name, and use module_group to separate these modules from others in the same agent.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Availability reports 0 — the overview request did not return HTTP
  • Check that the management plugin is enabled, that host names the management listener of a node that answers for the cluster, and that user and password authenticate. A 401/403 from RabbitMQ, an unreachable host, a wrong port and a disabled plugin all produce the same result: the plugin reads only HTTP 200 responses and reports no error for the others.
  • No per-node modules appear while Availability reports 1 — the nodes request failed. monitoring users see node-level data; a user without that tag is refused. The rest of the run still generates its modules.
  • All values are 0 — the overview request failed while the later requests returned empty lists: this is the same cause as an Availability of 0.
  • The agent never appears in the console in server plugin mode — the delivery failed and the run still printed 1. Re-run once with debug=1 to see the reason, then check that tentacle_client is installed and in PATH, that tentacle_ip:tentacle_port is reachable, or that local_folder exists and is writable by the user that runs the plugin.
  • ERROR: ... lines — the plugin prints its own configuration errors on standard output, before the usage summary, and still exits with status 0. Read the output, not the exit status.
  • A required value is not reported — the required-value checks run only when at least two arguments remain after the configuration file is consumed. With the documented single-file form (./rabbitmq_monitor rabbitmq_monitor.conf) they do not run: a missing host, user, pass, agent_name, tentacle_ip or local_folder is not reported, and the run proceeds with the values it has. Always run once with an explicit flag (debug=1 works) after editing the file, or verify the first result in the console.
  • The modules never update and the broker is healthy — check the execution schedule of the plugin in Pandora FMS and the interval of the agent, and run the plugin manually with debug=1 to confirm that the management API answers from the host that executes it.
  • An https:// base URL with a private certificate — the addon has no CA or verification option, so a private or self-signed certificate has no supported path here. Monitor the plain HTTP listener from a trusted network, or terminate TLS in front of RabbitMQ with a certificate the host trusts.

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description host Yes — Base URL of the RabbitMQ management API, including scheme and port, for example http://<TARGET_HOST>:15672. The plugin appends /api/overview, /api/nodes, /api/exchanges and /api/connections to this value. user Yes — RabbitMQ user sent as HTTP Basic credentials. pass Yes — Password for user. agent_name Required in server plugin mode — Name and alias of the agent created in Pandora FMS. interval No 300 Server plugin mode only. Interval of the created agent, in seconds. as_agent_plugin No 0 (server plugin mode) 1 (or any numeric value greater than 0) prints the module XML on standard output. 0, empty or non-numeric keeps server plugin mode. as_server_plugin No 1 Accepted by the configuration reader. 0 selects agent plugin mode when as_agent_plugin is absent; as_agent_plugin takes precedence when both are present. transfer_mode Required in server plugin mode Empty tentacle delivers with the Tentacle client; any other value copies the document into local_folder. local_folder Required when transfer_mode is not tentacle — Destination folder for the agent document copy. tentacle_ip Required when transfer_mode=tentacle — Tentacle server address. tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port. tentacle_client No tentacle_client Tentacle client executable, resolved in PATH or given as an absolute path. tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options passed to the Tentacle client, separated by whitespace. tmp No /tmp Folder where the agent document is written before delivery. module_group No Empty (no group sent) Module group assigned to every generated module. module_interval No Empty (agent interval) Module interval assigned to every generated module. module_tag_list No Empty (no tags) Module tags assigned to every generated module, passed through as given. debug No 0 1 (or any numeric value greater than 0) writes diagnostic messages, Tentacle output and delivery errors to standard error.

Boolean keys are enabled by any numeric value greater than 0; 0, an empty value or a non-numeric value means disabled. Unknown keys are accepted and ignored: the plugin does not validate the key set.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
./rabbitmq_monitor [config-file] [ -key value ... ]
Condition Behavior The command line is empty The plugin prints the usage summary and exits 0 The first argument names an existing file It is read as the configuration file and removed from the argument list The first argument is not an existing file It is not read as a configuration file; the run continues from the defaults plus the flags -key value Replaces the value of key --key value or -key=value Not recognized: only one leading hyphen is removed, so the pair is stored under a key the plugin ignores and the documented key keeps its file or default value Arguments that do not form a -key value pair Ignored; a trailing argument without a value is not reported -h or --help Not a help option; the flag is ignored and the run continues Configuration error Reported on standard output, followed by the usage summary, with exit status 0

The flags can appear before or after the configuration file path, but only a file in the first position is read as the configuration file.

docs.title: Delivery behavior
docs.text: Situation Result transfer_mode=tentacle and the transfer succeeds The temporary file is removed after the transfer transfer_mode=tentacle and the transfer fails Nothing is delivered; the client message is written to standard error only with debug=1, and the temporary file stays in tmp Any other transfer_mode The document is copied into local_folder and the temporary file is removed; a copy error is written to standard error only with debug=1 transfer_mode empty Nothing is delivered; the reason is written to standard error only with debug=1 Delivery result as seen on standard output A 1 is printed in every case Exit status 0 for configuration errors, failed delivery and SIGTERM

docs.title: Generated modules
docs.text:
<node> is a node name reported by the broker.

Module name Type Meaning Generated when Cluster name generic_data_string Cluster name reported by the broker Overview request succeeds Total queue messages generic_data Total messages in all queues Overview request succeeds Messages unacknowledged generic_data Messages delivered but not acknowledged Overview request succeeds Total exchanges generic_data Number of exchanges Overview request succeeds Queue publish rate generic_data Cluster publish rate Overview request succeeds Queue deliver get rate generic_data Reports the publish rate when a get rate is present (see Understand the results) Overview request succeeds Queue deliver noack rate generic_data Messages delivered to consumers without acknowledgement Overview request succeeds Availability generic_proc 1 when the overview request returns HTTP 200, 0 otherwise Always Memory used - <node> generic_data Memory used by the node, in bytes Nodes request succeeds Memory rate generic_data Rate at which the node memory is consumed or released Nodes request succeeds Proc used - <node> generic_data Erlang processes used by the node Nodes request succeeds Proc details generic_data Rate at which the node Erlang processes are created or terminated Nodes request succeeds Node status - <node> generic_proc 1 while the node is running, 0 otherwise Nodes request succeeds Exchanges in rate generic_data Publish-in rate of the last exchange that reports one; 0 when none reports activity Always Exchanges out rate generic_data Publish-out rate of the last exchange that reports one; 0 when none reports activity Always Total connections generic_data Number of connections returned by the API Always Connections running generic_data Connections whose state is exactly running Always Connections blocked generic_data Connections whose state is not running Always Total received octets generic_data Sum of the per-connection received-octet rates Always Total sent octets generic_data Sum of the per-connection sent-octet rates Always

Module names are created exactly as listed, without any broker or instance prefix. The modules have no thresholds, no units and no alert templates: set them in the console.

docs.title: Redis monitoring plugin
docs.text:
Article last updated: 2026-10-27.

Discovery integration recommended

For new installations use Redis Discovery, which is the recommended integration for this service. This plugin is the legacy path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Redis monitoring plugin turns the statistics of a Redis server into Pandora FMS modules. Each run connects to one Redis instance, reads the INFO sections you select, and publishes every field Redis returns as a module named exactly after that field: server identity and uptime, connected clients, memory, persistence, statistics, replication, CPU, per-command counters, cluster state and keyspace sizes.

Nothing is installed on the Redis server. The plugin connects over TCP from the host that runs it, with an optional password.

The plugin supports two execution models:

  • Server plugin mode (default when neither mode key is set): each run builds an agent document and delivers it to Pandora FMS through Tentacle or a local data folder.
  • Agent plugin mode (requires as_agent_plugin=1): each run prints the generated modules as XML on standard output, for the Pandora FMS agent to ingest.

This page documents the monitoring plugin, which reads the statistics of one instance per run. Discovering Redis instances and generating their agents is a different addon, documented in Redis Discovery.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Scope State Evidence Addon redis, version 1.1 Documented target The version this page describes. See Addon identity Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the Redis listener (TCP, 6379 by default in Redis) Required The plugin opens a client connection to the address in server A Redis password, when the instance requires authentication Required when authentication is enabled Prerequisite of the password key, not a compatibility statement tentacle_client on the host that runs the plugin Required when mode=tentacle Server mode delivery Redis server versions Not validated No version matrix has been recorded. The legacy guide only states the plugin was developed against Redis 3.2.12; the plugin itself requires nothing beyond a server that answers INFO Operating system of the host that runs the plugin Not validated No operating system has been recorded for this version Pandora FMS versions Not validated The Marketplace carries a general banner for all its integrations, not a statement specific to this addon

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Network access from the host that runs the plugin to the Redis host and port.
  2. A Redis password, when the instance has authentication enabled. The plugin sends a password only: it has no user name key, so an instance that requires an ACL user name cannot be monitored with it. Use the default user with requirepass, or an ACL user that authenticates with a password alone.
  3. Pandora FMS to receive the output: the Pandora FMS server in server plugin mode, or the Pandora FMS agent of the monitored host in agent plugin mode.
  4. The Tentacle client (tentacle_client) available in PATH, only when server mode delivers through Tentacle.

The account used by the plugin only reads INFO. No official source identifies a narrower set of Redis permissions; grant only what the instance needs to answer that command.

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
Download the package from the free Marketplace entry:

https://marketplace.pandorafms.com/entries/redis

Copy the redis_monitor executable to the host that will run the plugin, and create its configuration file next to it (see Configure). Nothing is installed on the Redis server, and no Redis client tools are needed on the monitoring host.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
The plugin combines its defaults with two input sources, in increasing precedence:

defaults < configuration file < command-line arguments

The configuration file is optional. When it is used, it must be the first argument of the command line: a file path placed after a flag is not read. It is a plain-text file with one key=value pair per line. Blank lines and lines that start with # are skipped, keys and values are trimmed, and the last occurrence of a repeated key wins.

The file has no sections. The plugin reads only the keys listed in Configuration file keys; a bracketed header such as [THRESHOLDS] is stored as an unused key with an empty value and has no effect.

The two keys that define what is read are:

  • server — the instance to read, as <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>. Include the port: the sample configuration always does.
  • metrics — the INFO sections to read, separated by spaces. all reads every section the server reports.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Agent plugin mode is the shortest configuration: the Pandora FMS agent runs the plugin and ingests the module XML it prints.

server=<REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>
password=<PASSWORD>
metrics=all
module_group=Redis
as_agent_plugin=1
as_server_plugin=0

Server plugin mode needs an agent name and a delivery target. With Tentacle:

server=<REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>
password=<PASSWORD>
metrics=all
module_group=Redis
as_agent_plugin=0
as_server_plugin=1
agent_name=redis-monitoring
temp=/tmp
mode=tentacle
tentacle_ip=<PANDORA_FMS_SERVER>
tentacle_port=41121

Or copy the agent document into a local data folder instead of using Tentacle:

server=<REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>
password=<PASSWORD>
metrics=all
as_agent_plugin=0
as_server_plugin=1
agent_name=redis-monitoring
temp=/tmp
mode=local
local_folder=/var/spool/pandora/data_in

The same agent plugin run with arguments only, without a configuration file:

./redis_monitor -server <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT> -password <PASSWORD> -metrics all -as_agent_plugin 1

Key points:

  • as_agent_plugin and as_server_plugin select the execution model. When neither is set, the plugin runs as a server plugin. When both are set to 1, both models run in the same execution: the module XML is printed and the agent document is delivered.
  • agent_name is required in server mode: it is the name of the agent created in Pandora FMS. The plugin sends that name only; it reads no agent interval, agent group or version key.
  • mode selects the delivery: tentacle uses the Tentacle client, and any other value, including local, copies the agent document into local_folder.
  • module_group is the name of the module group assigned to every generated module. Pandora FMS resolves it case-insensitively against the existing groups; when the name does not match one, the modules are created without that group.
  • temp is the folder where the agent document is written before delivery. On Linux it defaults to /tmp when the key is absent.
  • metrics is a single value: the section names are separated by spaces, so the whole list goes on one line.
  • Module names are the Redis field names, with no prefix. Run one agent per Redis instance: two instances delivered to the same agent overwrite each other's modules.

docs.title: Credentials and transport
docs.text:
• The Redis connection is not encrypted: the plugin has no TLS option, so the password and the statistics travel in clear text. Keep the connection on a trusted network, or place a TLS tunnel in front of Redis.
  • Inline password is stored in the configuration file in plain text: restrict the file permissions to the user that runs the plugin.
  • Avoid -password on the command line: the command is stored in the shell history and the operating system process list can expose it while the plugin runs. Prefer the configuration file with restrictive permissions (for example chmod 600).
  • debug=1 prints diagnostic dumps to standard output, including the full INFO response. Treat that output as sensitive: do not paste it into public tickets, and do not enable debug together with agent plugin mode (see Operate and troubleshoot).

docs.title: Register the plugin in Pandora FMS
docs.text:
redis_monitor can also be registered in the Pandora FMS console as a standard server plugin, so Pandora FMS executes it on the server that runs the modules instead of in a command line. Registered this way the plugin keeps server plugin mode: every run builds the agent document and delivers it, and the agent with its modules appears in the console.

Use the absolute path of the executable as the plugin command, and the documented keys as parameters. The console substitutes its _fieldN_ macros at execution time, so per-module values can be supplied without editing the plugin:

-server _field1_ -password _field2_ -metrics _field3_ -agent_name _field4_ -mode tentacle -tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 -tentacle_port 41121
Field Description Example value _field1_ Redis address, including the port <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT> _field2_ Redis password. It travels in the module command line, so treat the module definition as sensitive — _field3_ INFO sections to read, separated by spaces all _field4_ Name of the agent that will hold the modules redis-monitoring

-tentacle_ip 127.0.0.1 delivers to the Tentacle server of the machine that runs the plugin, so the agent lands in the Pandora FMS server that executes the module. To copy the document into a local data folder instead, replace the Tentacle flags with -mode local -local_folder /var/spool/pandora/data_in.

Once registered, the plugin is available when creating plugin modules, and each module fills the fields individually. The module is executed on the server selected for it, including a remote Pandora FMS server, so each Redis instance is monitored from the Pandora FMS server closest to it without installing anything on the Redis host.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Run the plugin manually from a terminal, passing the configuration file as its first argument:

./redis_monitor /etc/pandora/plugins/redis_config.conf

The relative form ./redis_monitor redis_config.conf works when the terminal is already in the directory that contains both files. Each run executes once and exits.

In agent plugin mode, a successful run prints one XML <module> block per field on standard output, in this form:

<module>
    <name><![CDATA[redis_version]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[7.2.4]]></data>
    <module_group>Redis</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[connected_clients]]></name>
    <type>generic_data</type>
    <data><![CDATA[3]]></data>
    <module_group>Redis</module_group>
</module>
<module>
    <name><![CDATA[db0]]></name>
    <type>generic_data_string</type>
    <data><![CDATA[keys=12,expires=4,avg_ttl=0]]></data>
    <module_group>Redis</module_group>
</module>

<module_group> is present only when module_group is set.

In server plugin mode a successful run prints nothing, and the agent configured in agent_name appears in Pandora FMS with its modules. The plugin does not report the delivery result in its exit status, so confirm the arrival in the console instead of relying on the command.

docs.title: Understand the results
docs.text: Every module is one field of the Redis INFO response. The plugin reads the sections listed in metrics, and for each field it creates a module named after the field, with a group when module_group is set.

docs.title: Module names and types
docs.text:
• The module name is the Redis field name exactly as the server returns it: no prefix, no section prefix. used_memory stays used_memory, and a keyspace line arrives as db0.
  • A value that contains a letter becomes a generic_data_string module: redis_version, role, maxmemory_policy, used_memory_human (1.05M), rdb_last_bgsave_status and db0 (keys=12,expires=4,avg_ttl=0).
  • A value with digits only becomes a generic_data module: connected_clients, used_memory, uptime_in_seconds, maxmemory, mem_fragmentation_ratio, and also the numeric flags redis_git_dirty and aof_enabled.
  • The plugin adds no description, unit or threshold, and no availability module. The module catalog is exactly the set of fields the selected sections return for your Redis version and configuration.

There is no connectivity module: when a run cannot read the instance, it publishes no module at all and the existing modules receive no new data.

docs.title: Sections you can read
docs.text:
metrics accepts any section name the Redis server accepts, separated by spaces; the plugin only passes each name to INFO, so names match case-insensitively as Redis does. all reads every section. The sections commonly used with this plugin are:

metrics value What it reads Representative modules server Identity, version and uptime redis_version, redis_mode, os, arch_bits, process_id, run_id, tcp_port, uptime_in_seconds, uptime_in_days, executable, config_file clients Client connections connected_clients, blocked_clients, client_longest_output_list, client_biggest_input_buf memory Memory used_memory, used_memory_human, used_memory_rss, used_memory_peak, maxmemory, maxmemory_policy, mem_fragmentation_ratio, mem_allocator persistence RDB and AOF state loading, rdb_changes_since_last_save, rdb_last_bgsave_status, rdb_last_save_time, aof_enabled, aof_last_write_status, aof_current_size stats Counters and rates total_connections_received, total_commands_processed, instantaneous_ops_per_sec, keyspace_hits, keyspace_misses, evicted_keys, expired_keys replication Role and replicas role, connected_slaves, master_replid, master_repl_offset; the master_* and slave* fields depend on the instance role cpu CPU consumed by the server used_cpu_sys, used_cpu_user, used_cpu_sys_children, used_cpu_user_children commandstats Per-command counters cmdstat_get, cmdstat_set, with values such as calls=1,usec=2,usec_per_call=2.00 cluster Cluster state cluster_enabled keyspace Keys per database db0, db1, with values such as keys=12,expires=4,avg_ttl=0 all Every section above —

Fields appear or disappear according to the Redis version and the instance configuration (for example, AOF fields exist only when AOF is enabled), so a module that is missing from the output is a field the server did not report in that run.

docs.title: Everyday operation
docs.text:
• The plugin keeps no state: every execution reads the instance at that moment, so it can be run manually at any time.
  • In server plugin mode, schedule it from Pandora FMS, for example through the server plugin scheduler or cron. In agent plugin mode, the Pandora FMS agent executes it according to the configured plugin schedule.
  • Use debug=1 in manual runs to print the connection details, the section list and the complete INFO response. debug writes to standard output, so in agent plugin mode it interleaves with the module XML and the agent cannot parse the output: never enable it in a scheduled agent plugin execution.
  • Because module names carry no instance prefix, keep one agent per instance and use module_group to separate these modules from others in the same agent.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• No module XML is printed in agent plugin mode — check that as_agent_plugin=1 is in effect (when both mode keys are empty the plugin runs as a server plugin), that metrics is not empty, and that the configuration file is the first argument of the command.
  • The agent never appears in Pandora FMS in server mode — the delivery failed silently. Run once with debug=1 to see the reason: a missing mode and a missing local_folder are reported only with debug enabled, and a Tentacle failure prints the client message only with debug enabled.
  • tentacle_client cannot be found or cannot connect — make sure the client is installed and in PATH (or set tentacle_client to its absolute path) and that tentacle_ip and tentacle_port reach the Tentacle server.
  • The local folder delivery fails — check that local_folder exists, is writable by the user that runs the plugin, and names a folder, not a file. The error is printed only with debug=1.
  • NOAUTH or an authentication error from Redis — the instance requires a password and password is empty or wrong. If the instance requires an ACL user name as well, this plugin cannot authenticate (it has no user name key).
  • Connection refused or timeout — the plugin cannot reach server. Check the host, the port, the firewall and that Redis is listening on an address reachable from the monitoring host.
  • Some older modules stop updating after a Redis upgrade or configuration change — the field no longer exists in the INFO output. Adjust metrics or the alerting on that module.
  • The module list is empty — metrics is empty or names sections the instance does not report. Start with metrics=all and narrow it once you see which modules arrive.

docs.title: Configuration file keys
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description server Yes — Redis address, as <REDIS_HOST>:<REDIS_PORT>. Include the port. password No Empty (no authentication) Password sent to Redis. The plugin has no user name key. metrics Yes — INFO sections to read, separated by spaces. all reads every section. as_agent_plugin No 0 1 (or any value greater than 0) prints the module XML on standard output. as_server_plugin No 1 when neither mode key is set 1 (or any value greater than 0) builds and delivers the agent document. When both mode keys are 1, both models run. agent_name Required in server mode — Name of the agent created in Pandora FMS. module_group No Empty (no group sent) Name of an existing module group assigned to every generated module. Resolved case-insensitively; an unknown name leaves the modules without that group. mode Required in server mode Empty tentacle delivers with the Tentacle client; any other value copies the agent document into local_folder. transfer_mode No Empty Alternative key for mode, read only when mode is empty. local_folder Required when mode is not tentacle — Destination folder for the agent document copy. temp No /tmp on Linux Folder where the agent document is written before delivery. tmp is accepted as an alternative key. tentacle_ip Required when mode=tentacle — Tentacle server address. tentacle_port No 41121 Tentacle server port. tentacle_client No tentacle_client Tentacle client executable, resolved in PATH or given as an absolute path. tentacle_opts No Empty Extra options passed to the Tentacle client, separated by whitespace. debug No 0 1 (or any value greater than 0) prints connection details, the section list and diagnostic messages on standard output.

Boolean keys are enabled by any numeric value greater than 0; 0, an empty value or a non-numeric value means disabled.

docs.title: Command-line execution
docs.text:
./redis_monitor [config-file] [ -key value ... ]
Condition Behavior The first argument names an existing file The plugin reads it as the configuration file and applies the remaining arguments over its values The first argument is not a file, or the file path comes after a flag The file is not read; the plugin runs from the defaults plus the arguments -key value Replaces the value of key --key value or -key=value Not recognized: the pair is read as a different key that the plugin ignores, so the documented key keeps its default or file value Arguments that do not form a -key value pair Ignored; a trailing argument without a value is not reported The command line is empty The plugin runs with the default values; no usage text is printed -h or --help No help option exists: it produces no help output and is treated like any other unknown flag

Unknown keys are accepted and ignored: the plugin does not validate the key set.

docs.title: Delivery behavior
docs.text: Situation Result mode=tentacle and the Tentacle transfer succeeds The temporary file is removed after the transfer mode=tentacle and the transfer fails The document is not delivered; the client message is printed only with debug=1 Any other mode The document is copied into local_folder and the temporary file is removed mode empty and no transfer_mode alternative Nothing is delivered; the reason is printed only with debug=1 Delivery result Not reflected in the exit status; verify in the Pandora FMS console
